qs.q:
What is the next number in the series?
2, 10, 50, 250, ?
qs.e:
Each term is 5 times the previous one: 2×5 = 10, 10×5 = 50, 50×5 = 250.
Next term = 250 × 5 = 1250.
Answer: 1250

qs.q: Vegetable prices have suddenly gone up in the market. What is the likely cause?
o: Sellers want to earn high profit margins only now
People have stopped eating other food items now
Prices are always highest in the winter season now
qs.e:
A sudden price rise is best explained by supply falling while demand stays the same.
(a), (b) and (d) are arbitrary or unsupported claims that the statement gives no basis for.
Answer: Vegetable supply has reduced greatly

qs.q:
Directions: Pick the correct options from below.
37, 53, ?, 97, 125
In a certain coded language 'ROOT' is coded as 'MIJN' and 'FANS' is coded as 'AUIM'. How will 'JAMS' be coded in the same code language?
qs.e:
Letters move back alternately by 5 and 6: R−5=M, O−6=I, O−5=J, T−6=N.
FANS: F−5=A, A−6=U (wrapping), N−5=I, S−6=M.
JAMS: J−5=E, A−6=U, M−5=H, S−6=M → EUHM.
Answer: EUHM

qs.q:
The criteria for selecting a candidate for the post of 'Mechanical Engineer' are as follow.
The candidate:
1. must have passed M.Tech in Mechanical Engineering with more than 75% marks.
2. must have secured more than 65% marks in the written test and more than 70% in the interview.
3. must not be less than 30 years and not more than 35 years of age as on 1 January 2019.
However, if a candidate fulfils all the above criteria EXCEPT:
a. no. 2, but has obtained more than 80% marks in M.Tech, his/her case is to be referred to the Chief Engineer.
b. no. 3, but has got more than five years experience of working as a Mechanical Engineer, his/her case is to be referred to the Deputy Director.
Based on the criteria given and without assuming any additional information, you have to a take a decision for the following candidate.
Vijendra completed M.Tech with 76% marks in Mechanical Engineering. He was born on 14th November 1983. He has got 73% marks in both written test and interview. He has worked as Mechanical Engineer for three years.
o: The candidate is to be selected.
The candidate is not to be selected.
The candidate's case is to be referred to the Chief Engineer.
The candidate's case is to be referred to Deputy Director.
qs.e:
Condition 1: 76% > 75% – met. Condition 2: written 73% > 65% and interview 73% > 70% – met.
Born 14 Nov 1983, so on 1 Jan 2019 he is 35 years 1 month – above 35, so condition 3 fails.
Exception (b) needs more than five years of experience; he has only three.
So no route to selection or referral applies.
Answer: The candidate is not to be selected.

qs.q:
Statement:
Online education platforms are increasingly being adopted by students.
Assumptions:
I. Students have access to the internet.
II. Traditional education has become irrelevant.
III. Online platforms offer flexible learning.
o: Only I and III are implicit
Only II and III are implicit
qs.e:
Adopting online platforms presupposes internet access – I is implicit.
Students would choose them for some benefit such as flexibility – III is implicit.
Nothing suggests traditional education is irrelevant; II is an extreme claim.
Answer: Only I and III are implicit

qs.q:
In the question one statement is given, followed by arguments, I and II. You have to decide which of the argument is strong.
Statement: Should male labourers be paid more than female labourers?
Arguments:
I. Yes. Even physiologists confirm that men are physically stronger than women.
II. No. Equal work should be paid equally irrespective of gender.
o: Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
qs.e:
Pay depends on the work done, not on general physical strength, so I is weak.
II rests on the sound principle of equal pay for equal work, so it is strong.
Answer: Only argument II is strong

qs.q:
Select the option exactly similar to:
16th Floor, Alpha Tower, Near City Center Mall, Bangalore, KA 560001
o: 16th Floor, Alpha Tower, Near City Center Mall, Bengalooru, KA- 560001
16 Floor, Alpha Tower, Near City Center Mall, Bangalore, KA 560001
16th Floor, Alpha Tower, Near City Center Mall, Bangalore, KA 560001
16th Floor, Alpha Tower, Near City Center Mall, Bangalore, Karnataka 560001
qs.e:
(a) changes the city name and adds a hyphen; (b) drops 'th'; (d) writes Karnataka in full.
Only (c) matches every character.
Answer: 16th Floor, Alpha Tower, Near City Center Mall, Bangalore, KA 560001

qs.q:
In the question a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statement.
Statement: Should India support all the decisions and policies made by Pakistan.
Arguments:
I. Yes, as this is the only way to maintain peace among both the nations.
II. No, as India should have its own opinion on the decisions and policies made by Pakistan as some may be correct and some may be incorrect.
o: Either argument I or argument II is strong
Neither argument I nor argument II is strong
qs.e:
I claims blanket support is the 'only way' to peace – an exaggerated, unsupported claim, so weak.
II reasons that policies should be judged on merit – a sound, relevant argument.
Answer: Only argument II is strong

qs.q: Pointing to Sakshi, I said, 'She is the daughter of the brother of the son of my wife.' How am I related to Sakshi?
qs.e:
The speaker has a wife, so the speaker is male. Son of my wife = my son.
Brother of my son = also my son; his daughter Sakshi is my granddaughter.
So the speaker is Sakshi's grandfather.
Answer: Grandfather

qs.q:
Find the next element that replace the ? Logically
1, 15, 85, 435, ?

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully and decide which of the conclusions logically follows(s) from the statements.
Statements:
(I) All ships are boats.
(II) All anchors are ships
Conclusions:
I. All anchors are boats.
II. Some ships are anchors.
III. No anchor is a boat.
IV. Some boats are anchors.
o: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I, II, and IV follow
qs.e:
Anchors ⊂ ships ⊂ boats, so all anchors are boats (I follows) and III is false.
Since all anchors are ships, some ships are anchors (II); since all anchors are boats, some boats are anchors (IV).
Answer: Only conclusions I, II, and IV follow

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'GOAT' is coded as '68', 'POLE' is coded as '63'. How will 'FAIL' be coded in that code language?
qs.e:
Use reverse alphabet positions (A=26 … Z=1), add them, then add 3.
GOAT: 20+12+26+7 = 65, +3 = 68. POLE: 11+12+15+22 = 60, +3 = 63.
FAIL: 21+26+18+15 = 80, +3 = 83.
Answer: 83

qs.q: Amrita is the sister of Bablu. Bablu is the brother of Deepak. Deepak is the son of Malti and Malti is the wife of Lakhan. Nehal is the brother of Lakhan. How is Nehal related to Amrita?
qs.e:
Amrita, Bablu and Deepak are siblings; their parents are Malti and Lakhan.
So Lakhan is Amrita's father, and his brother Nehal is her paternal uncle.
Answer: Father's brother

qs.q:
Directions: Select the correct options from the given alternatives
10, 110, 220, 340, ....
qs.e:
Differences are 100, 110, 120, so the next is 130.
340 + 130 = 470.
Answer: 470

qs.q: In a hospital, non-local patients wait longer for appointments compared to local patients with similar conditions. Which inference is valid?
qs.e:
Conditions are similar, so need or severity cannot explain the gap – (a) and (c) are out.
Nothing is said about payment, so (b) is unsupported.
Longer waits for one group with similar needs point to locals being preferred.
Answer: Preference for local patients

qs.q: A Candidate ID is a 13-digit number. The structure is non-standard: The first 3 digits are the Year, the next 2 digits are the Batch. The Center Code is formed by taking the 6th, 9th, and 12th digits of the entire ID. For the Candidate ID 2021543217654, what is the Center Code?

Some conditional data is provided to you in form of statement you have to check which of the following statement are logically inference from given statement.
Statement: No student who fails the midterm exam passes the final course. Sarah passed the final course.
What can we infer about Sarah's midterm performance?
o: Sarah got an A on the midterm
Sarah did not fail the midterm exam
Sarah studied hard for the midterm
qs.e:
'Failing the midterm ⇒ not passing the course'. Its contrapositive: passing the course ⇒ did not fail the midterm.
Sarah passed, so she did not fail the midterm; grade, effort or retakes cannot be inferred.
Answer: Sarah did not fail the midterm exam

qs.q:
Choose the address that is the same as the one given below.
Sample Address: Flat C-3, Phase 2, Golden Homes, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra – 410210
o: Flat C3, Phase 2, Golden Homes, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra - 410210
Flat C-3, Phase 2, Golden Homes, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra - 410210
Flat C-3, Phase II, Golden Homes, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra - 410210
Flat C-3, Phase 2, Golden Home, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra 410210
qs.e:
(a) drops the hyphen in C-3; (c) writes Phase II; (d) has 'Home' and no dash before the PIN.
(b) matches the sample.
Answer: Flat C-3, Phase 2, Golden Homes, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra - 410210

qs.q: If in a certain code language, 'LIFE' is written as '11731', then in that code language, how 'ZONE' may be written?
qs.e:
Subtract 1, 2, 3, 4 from successive letter positions and write the results together.
LIFE: 12−1=11, 9−2=7, 6−3=3, 5−4=1 → 11731.
ZONE: 26−1=25, 15−2=13, 14−3=11, 5−4=1 → 2513111.
Answer: 2513111

qs.q: Identify the assumption: “The company reduced prices to increase sales.”
qs.e:
Cutting prices in order to raise sales only makes sense if lower prices draw more buyers.
(a) is broader than needed, (c) contradicts the aim, (d) is not implied.
Answer: Lower prices attract more buyers

qs.q: In a certain coded language 'COMPS' is coded as 'NKHKY' and 'ABATE' is coded as 'ZOVXW'. How will 'SMOKY' be coded in the same code language?
qs.e:
Write the word in reverse, then shift letters back by 5, 5, 5, 4, 4.
COMPS → SPMOC → S−5=N, P−5=K, M−5=H, O−4=K, C−4=Y → NKHKY; ABATE → ETABA → Z, O, V, X, W ✓.
SMOKY → YKOMS → Y−5=T, K−5=F, O−5=J, M−4=I, S−4=O → TFJIO.
Answer: TFJIO

qs.q:
Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
Figure 1 — top row: C Δ P; bottom row: F D R
Figure 2 — top row: F C Δ; bottom row: J R P
Figure 3 — top row: N C G; bottom row: T S H
Figure 4 — ?
o: Top row: T H G; bottom row: P N C
Top row: T N C; bottom row: P G H
Top row: T N C; bottom row: P H G
Top row: P N C; bottom row: T H G
qs.e:
The six boxes form a ring; every symbol moves one place clockwise: top-left → top-middle → top-right → bottom-right → bottom-middle → bottom-left → top-left.
In figure 1 → 2: C, Δ move right, P drops to bottom-right, R moves to bottom-middle, F rises to top-left, and the letter landing at bottom-left is replaced by a new one.
Figure 3 → 4: top row T N C; bottom-right G, bottom-middle H, bottom-left a new letter.
Only the option with top T N C and bottom _ H G fits.
Answer: Top row: T N C; bottom row: P H G

qs.q:
Eight symbol-number clusters are given below three of which are same. Find the three clusters that are exactly same.
(A) 74* &4%48@23*7^+#
(B) 74* &4%43@23*7$+#
(C) 74* &4%43@23*7^+#
(D) 74* &4%43@23*7^+#
(E) 74* &4$43@23*7^+#
(F) 74* &4%43@33*7^+#
(G) 74* &4&43@23*7^+#
(H) 74* &4%43@23*7^+#
qs.e:
Take C (74* &4%43@23*7^+#) as reference.
A has 48, B has $ for ^, E has $ for %, F has 33 for 23, G has & for %.
D and H match C character for character.
Answer: C, D and H

qs.q: Which of the following sports includes a ball?
qs.e:
Golf is played by striking a small dimpled ball into a series of holes with clubs.
Boxing uses no ball, badminton uses a shuttlecock (feathered cork), and chess is a board game.
Answer: Golf

qs.q: Which of the following countries never hosted the Asian Games till 2022?
qs.e:
Japan hosted in 1958 (Tokyo) and 1994 (Hiroshima); South Korea in 1986, 2002 and 2014; China in 1990, 2010 and 2022 (held in 2023).
Pakistan has never hosted the Asian Games.
Answer: Pakistan

qs.q: Which of the following is not a function of biosphere reserves?
qs.e:
UNESCO's biosphere reserve concept has three functions: conservation (of biodiversity and cultural diversity), development (sustainable, for local people) and logistic support (research, education).
Monoculture farming reduces biodiversity, so it runs against the purpose of a reserve.
Answer: Promotion of monoculture farming

qs.q: The Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh was constitutionalized through which Constitutional Amendment?
qs.e:
The Constitution (100th Amendment) Act, 2015 gave effect to the 1974 India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement and its 2011 Protocol.
It amended the First Schedule to exchange enclaves between the two countries.
The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced GST.
Answer: One Hundredth Amendment

qs.q: On which date did the Gujarat State Assembly make history by passing the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill 2026?
qs.e:
The Gujarat Assembly passed the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 on 24 March 2026 after a debate of over seven hours (news reports appeared on 25 March).
Gujarat became the second state after Uttarakhand to pass a UCC law; it later received the President's assent.
Answer: March 24, 2026

qs.q:
Match the following regarding the host cities of the Asian Games:
List-I (Asian Games) | List-II (Host City)
I. 2022 Asian Games | 1. Riyadh
II. 2026 Asian Games | 2. Hangzhou
III. 2030 Asian Games | 3. Doha
IV. 2034 Asian Games | 4. Aichi-Nagoya
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e:
2022: Hangzhou, China (held in 2023).
2026: Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
2030: Doha, Qatar; 2034: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
So I-2, II-4, III-3, IV-1.
Answer: I-2, II-4, III-3, IV-1

qs.q: Which statement accurately describes the characteristics of protons in an atom?
o: They revolve around the nucleus in fixed orbits.
They have negligible mass compared to electrons.
They are located in the nucleus of an atom.
qs.e:
Protons are positively charged particles found inside the nucleus along with neutrons.
A proton is about 1836 times heavier than an electron; it is electrons that move around the nucleus and carry negative charge.
Answer: They are located in the nucleus of an atom.

qs.q: In 2022, the President pardoned a woman jailed for a minor crime. Which Article of the Indian Constitution allows the President to grant pardons?
qs.e:
Article 72 empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions, and to suspend, remit or commute sentences.
Article 161 gives a similar power to Governors. Art 74 is the Council of Ministers to aid and advise, Art 75 covers ministers' appointment, Art 53 the executive power of the Union.
Answer: Article 72

qs.q: In May 2026, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) Prataprao Jadhav launched which portal under the Ayush Grid initiative to strengthen digital governance and enhance transparency in the AYUSH sector?
qs.e:
On 19 May 2026 the Ministry of Ayush launched the Ayush Anudan Portal, built under the Ayush Grid digital initiative.
It handles online submission, tracking and approval of grant (anudan) proposals under central sector schemes and is linked with NGO Darpan.
Answer: Ayush Anudan Portal

qs.q: In 2026, India will surpass which country to become Sri Lanka's second-largest export destination?
qs.e:
Sri Lanka Export Development Board data for early 2026 showed India overtaking the United Kingdom as Sri Lanka's second-largest export market.
The USA remains Sri Lanka's largest export destination.
Answer: United Kingdom

qs.q: The stringent industrial licensing regime in India (pre-1991) often led to which unintended consequence for established firms, despite aiming to prevent monopolies?
o: Reduced incentive for technological upgradation and efficiency.
qs.e:
Under the 'licence raj', capacity and entry were controlled by licences, so incumbents faced little domestic or foreign competition.
Protected firms had a captive market and little pressure to modernise technology or cut costs, which hurt efficiency and quality.
Answer: Reduced incentive for technological upgradation and efficiency.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding privatization:
(i) Privatization means not transferring ownership of public sector enterprises to private enterprises.
(ii) Privatization involves the transfer of management of public sector enterprises to private enterprises.
Choose the correct answer:
qs.e:
Privatisation means shedding government ownership and/or management of public sector enterprises in favour of the private sector.
Statement (i) denies the ownership transfer, so it is false; statement (ii) correctly includes transfer of management.
Answer: Only (ii) is true

qs.q: Which of the following veto powers is NOT available to the President of India?
qs.e:
The Indian President has an absolute veto (withholding assent), a suspensive veto (returning a non-money bill for reconsideration) and a pocket veto (keeping a bill pending indefinitely).
A qualified veto, which a legislature can override only by a special majority (as in the USA), is not available to the Indian President.
Answer: Qualified Veto

qs.q: Which of the following subjects is NOT included in the Union List, as per allocation between three lists in seventh schedule, given under Article 246 of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e:
Atomic energy, railways and banking are all Union List subjects.
Intoxicating liquors (production, manufacture, sale) fall in the State List (Entry 8, List II), and liquor excise is also a state subject.
Answer: Liquor

qs.q: The 1991 economic reforms in India led to rapid industrialisation and expansion of energy-intensive sectors. Which market-based mechanism has India adopted to balance industrial growth, energy efficiency and emissions?
qs.e:
The Perform, Achieve and Trade scheme (under the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency, run by BEE from 2012) sets energy-intensity targets for large industrial units.
Units that beat their targets earn tradable Energy Saving Certificates, which laggards can buy, making it a market-based mechanism.
Answer: Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme

qs.q: Under which mission was the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) launched?
qs.e:
DDU-GKY, launched in 2014 by the Ministry of Rural Development, is the placement-linked skilling component of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).
It targets rural poor youth aged 15-35.
Answer: National Rural Livelihoods Mission

qs.q: Which of the following industry was emphasized in the second five year plan of India?
qs.e:
The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) followed the Mahalanobis model, which stressed rapid industrialisation through heavy and basic industries.
Steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela were set up in this period. (The First Plan stressed agriculture.)
Answer: Heavy and basic industry

qs.q: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 introduced provisions to replace the Indian Penal Code. What is the primary objective of this reform?
o: To increase the number of criminal courts in India
To modernize criminal laws and align them with contemporary legal needs
To abolish all colonial-era legal provisions immediately
To transfer criminal law powers entirely to state governments
qs.e:
The BNS replaced the IPC of 1860 with effect from 1 July 2024, alongside the BNSS (replacing CrPC) and BSA (replacing the Evidence Act).
Its stated aim is to modernise substantive criminal law, e.g. adding organised crime, terrorism and community service, to suit present-day needs. It does not create courts or shift criminal law to states.
Answer: To modernize criminal laws and align them with contemporary legal needs

qs.q: What is the public capital expenditure proposed by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman for FY 2026-27 in Union Budget 2026-27?
qs.e:
In the Union Budget presented on 1 February 2026, capital expenditure for FY27 was set at a record ₹12.2 lakh crore (about 3.1% of GDP).
The FY26 budget estimate had been about ₹11.21 lakh crore.
Answer: ₹12.2 lakh crore

qs.q: What was the intended flight profile and duration of the Artemis II mission?
o: 3-day mission; Lunar landing at the South Pole
10-day mission; Lunar flyby and return to Earth
30-day mission; Orbiting the Moon and docking with Gateway
6-month mission; Rotation at the International Space Station
qs.e:
Artemis II is NASA's first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft on the SLS rocket, carrying four astronauts.
It was planned as a roughly 10-day mission that loops around the Moon (a free-return lunar flyby) and returns to Earth, with no landing; landing is left to later Artemis flights.
Answer: 10-day mission; Lunar flyby and return to Earth

qs.q: In June 2026, which of the following products from Assam was granted a Geographical Indication (GI) tag?
qs.e:
The Pepa is the buffalo-horn pipe played during Assam's Bihu festival, so Bihu Pepa is the only Assamese product listed.
Pochampally Ikat is from Telangana, Channapatna Toys from Karnataka and Kullu Shawl from Himachal Pradesh, all of which already held GI tags.
Answer: Bihu Pepa

qs.q: Which of the following symbols is a correct representation for air mass above a hot and dry desert region?
qs.e:
Air masses are coded by moisture (c = continental/dry, m = maritime/moist) and temperature (T = tropical, P = polar, A = arctic).
A hot, dry desert source region gives continental tropical air: cT.
Answer: cT

qs.q: Which of the following is a shallow desert depression formed by wind erosion?
qs.e:
Deflation is the lifting and removal of loose sand and dust by wind; it scoops out shallow basins called deflation hollows (blowouts).
A pediment is a gentle rock slope at a mountain foot, a playa is a basin floor left by evaporating water, and an inselberg is an isolated residual hill.
Answer: Deflation hollow

qs.q: In early 2026, which individual from Chhattisgarh was recognized for outstanding contributions in Social Work with the Padma Shri award?
qs.e:
The Padma awards list announced on the eve of Republic Day 2026 named Budhri Tati of Geedam, Dantewada (Chhattisgarh) for social work.
Known as Bastar's 'Badi Didi', she has worked for decades on education and empowerment of tribal girls and women.
Answer: Dr. Budhri Tati

qs.q: 'Tamu Lochar' is one of the traditional festivals of the ____________ of Sikkim. It is celebrated to mark the beginning of their new year, which falls on the 15th day of Pusa, according to the Hindu calendar Vikram Samvat and 30th December in the English calendar.
qs.e:
The Gurungs call themselves Tamu, and Tamu Lochar (Lhosar) is their new-year festival, observed around 30 December.
Bhutias celebrate Losar, and Lepchas observe Namsoong as their new year.
Answer: Gurung community

qs.q: A man sold two articles for ₹ 850 each. On one article, he earns a profit of 25% and on the other article, he suffers a loss of 15%. What is his overall profit ?
qs.e:
Cost of the first article = 850 ÷ 1.25 = ₹680, so profit = ₹170.
Cost of the second article = 850 ÷ 0.85 = ₹1000, so loss = ₹150.
Net result = 170 − 150 = ₹20 profit.
Answer: ₹ 20

qs.q: The perimeter of a rectangular field is 52 meters, and the difference between its length and its breadth is 10 meters. What is the side length of a square whose area is exactly equal to the area of this rectangular field?
qs.e:
L + B = 52/2 = 26 and L − B = 10, so L = 18 m and B = 8 m.
Area = 18 × 8 = 144 m².
Square side = √144 = 12 m.
Answer: 12 meters

qs.q: What is the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 10,000 at 14% p.a. for 2 5/7 years where the interest is compounded yearly? (nearest to Rs. 1)
The base of a right prism is an equilateral triangle with each side measuring 8 cm . Given that the height of the prism is 10 cm , what is its volume?
qs.e:
Base area = (√3/4) × 8² = 16√3 cm².
Volume = base area × height = 16√3 × 10 = 160√3 cm³ (≈ 277.1).
Answer: 160√3 cubic cm

qs.q: Two right prisms have the same height, but their bases are triangles with areas in the ratio 3:5. What is the ratio of their volumes?
qs.e:
Volume of a prism = base area × height.
With equal heights, the volumes are in the ratio of the base areas = 3 : 5.
Answer: 3:5

qs.q: A right-angled triangle has its angles in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3, and the length of the side opposite to the 60° angle is 6√3 cm. A geometry student needs to find the length of the hypotenuse of this triangle without using any trigonometric table, purely by the property of a 30°-60°-90° triangle. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
qs.e:
Angles 1 : 2 : 3 give 30°, 60°, 90°; sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.
Side opposite 60° = √3k = 6√3, so k = 6.
Hypotenuse = 2k = 12 cm.
Answer: 12 cm

qs.q: The ratio of men to women in a hall is 5 : 3. If 24 more women join and 12 men leave, the ratio becomes 3 : 2. Find the number of men originally present.
qs.e:
Let men = 5x, women = 3x. Then (5x − 12)/(3x + 24) = 3/2.
10x − 24 = 9x + 72, so x = 96.
Men originally = 5 × 96 = 480.
Answer: 480

Let a = 5.75, b = 3.25. Numerator = a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).
Denominator = 100² × (a² + b² − ab) = 10⁴(a² − ab + b²).
Value = (a + b)/10⁴ = 9/10000 = 0.0009.
Answer: 0.0009

qs.q: If 1/(cosec θ + cot θ) = p, then 1/(cosec θ − cot θ) is equal to:
qs.e:
Since cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1, (cosec θ + cot θ)(cosec θ − cot θ) = 1.
So 1/(cosec θ − cot θ) = cosec θ + cot θ = 1/p.
Answer: 1/p

qs.q: Find the ratio of volumes of a sphere to its hemisphere of same radius.
qs.e:
Sphere = (4/3)πr³, hemisphere = (2/3)πr³.
Ratio = 4/3 : 2/3 = 2 : 1.
Answer: 2 : 1

qs.q: The diameter of a circular garden is 140 m. Its area is equal to a rectangular field whose sides are in the ratio 11 : 7. The perimeter (in m) of the rectangular field is (take π = 22/7):
qs.e:
Radius 70 m, area = (22/7) × 70² = 15,400 m².
Sides 11x and 7x: 77x² = 15,400, so x² = 200 and x = 10√2.
Perimeter = 2(11x + 7x) = 36x = 360√2 m.
Answer: 360 √2

qs.q: Alloy A contains metals x and y only in the ratio 3:2, while alloy B contains them in the ratio 5:6. Alloy C is prepared by mixing alloys A and B in the ratio 4:3. The percentage of x in alloy C is:
The chord of a circle is 30 cm long, and the height of the minor segment cut off by this chord is 5 cm. What is the diameter of the circle?
qs.e:
Half-chord = 15 cm; the centre is (r − 5) from the chord.
r² = 15² + (r − 5)² gives 10r = 250, so r = 25 cm.
Diameter = 50 cm.
Answer: 50 cm

qs.q: 3 liters of lime syrup are mixed with m liters of water. If the lime syrup is 5% of the mixture, find the value of m.
qs.e:
Syrup is 5% of the total, so total = 3 ÷ 0.05 = 60 litres.
Water m = 60 − 3 = 57 litres.
Answer: 57 litres

qs.q: Three candidates contested an election. The first candidate got 40% votes and the second got 30% votes. If the total number of votes polled were 36,000, find the number of votes obtained by the third candidate.
If sin A = 3/5, and A is acute, find the value of sec² A − tan² A.
qs.e:
sec²A − tan²A = 1 is an identity for every A where both are defined.
(Check: cos A = 4/5, sec²A = 25/16, tan²A = 9/16, difference = 16/16 = 1.)
Answer: 1

qs.q: Two trains leave the same station and travel in the same direction. If the faster train moves at 54 km/h and the distance between them becomes 42 km after 6 hours, what is the speed of the slower train?
qs.e:
Gap grows at the relative speed: 42/6 = 7 km/h.
Slower train = 54 − 7 = 47 km/h.
Answer: 47 km/h

qs.q: If the length of a rectangular field is increased by 25%, then by what percentage should its breadth be reduced so that the area of the field remains constant?
qs.e:
Length becomes 5/4 of the original, so breadth must become 4/5 to keep the area.
Reduction = 1/5 = 20%.
Answer: 20%

qs.q: During a sale, 52% of the goods are sold at 32% profit, 25% of the remaining goods are sold at 42% profit and the still remaining goods are sold at a loss of 11%. If there is an overall profit of x%, then what is the value of x?
qs.e:
Take total cost 100. 52 units at +32% give +16.64.
Remaining 48; a quarter of it = 12 at +42% gives +5.04.
Last 36 at −11% gives −3.96. Net = 16.64 + 5.04 − 3.96 = 17.72, so x = 17.72.
Answer: 17.72

qs.q: A group of 12 students appeared for a physics test. The average of the top 6 scores was 84.5, and the average of the bottom 6 scores was 72.75. Later, it was found that a decimal error had occurred, and one of the scores from the bottom half was mistakenly recorded as 58.2 instead of 85.2. What is the corrected overall average of the group?
qs.e:
Recorded total = 6 × 84.5 + 6 × 72.75 = 507 + 436.5 = 943.5.
Correction adds 85.2 − 58.2 = 27, so true total = 970.5.
Corrected average = 970.5 ÷ 12 = 80.875.
Answer: 80.875

qs.q: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
o: Rational and irrational numbers are real
qs.e:
Real numbers consist of the rationals and irrationals, so (a) and (b) are true.
Any integer n can be written as n/1, so it is rational, never irrational; (d) is false.
Answer: Every integer is irrational

qs.q:
On a certain sum of money, Neha received a compound interest (interest compounded annually) of ₹308 in 2 years.
She received a simple interest of ₹280 on the same amount for the same time period. What is the rate of interest per annum?
qs.e:
SI for one year = 280/2 = ₹140.
CI − SI = 308 − 280 = ₹28, which is the interest earned on one year's interest.
Rate = 28/140 × 100 = 20%.
Answer: 20%

qs.q: Two completely distinct geometric circles possess radii measuring precisely 15 cm and 10 cm respectively. The straight linear distance spanning perfectly between their two central anchor points is officially measured as 35 cm. What is the mathematical length of the direct common tangent connecting these two circular boundaries?
qs.e:
Direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²).
= √(35² − 5²) = √(1225 − 25) = √1200 = 20√3 cm.
Answer: 20√3 cm

qs.q: If a + 1/a = 3, then find the value of a⁶ + 1/a⁶
Fill in the Blank 1.
qs.e:
Evidence that disturbs a settled belief gets brushed aside as if it were a petty, nit-picking objection.
'Cavil' means exactly that: a trivial or carping objection.
Exculpation (clearing of blame), imputation (accusation) and salience (prominence) do not describe something dismissed as an annoyance.
Answer: cavil
qs.p:
Directions (76-80): Read the following passage carefully and fill in the blanks with the most appropriate word from the given alternatives.
In an age increasingly enamored of instantaneous information, intellectual restraint has become an almost antiquated virtue. The contemporary reader is perpetually assailed by a prodigious volume of claims, conjectures, and polemics, many of which acquire an unwarranted aura of credibility merely through repetition. What is particularly disquieting is not the sheer abundance of information but the gradual erosion of the cognitive habits required to interrogate it. A proposition that ought to invite scrutiny is instead accepted with remarkable alacrity, while evidence that complicates an established conviction is frequently dismissed as an inconvenient (1)________.
This tendency is exacerbated by digital platforms whose algorithms are designed less to cultivate discernment than to maximise engagement. By continuously presenting users with material consonant with their pre-existing preferences, such systems can create an epistemic environment that is deceptively (2)________. Within such an environment, disagreement is no longer perceived as an opportunity for intellectual refinement but as an affront to one’s identity. Consequently, individuals become increasingly (3)________ to information that unsettles their assumptions, even when such information is supported by cogent evidence.
The predicament is further complicated by the proliferation of ostensibly authoritative voices whose expertise is difficult to verify. Eloquence, confidence, and rhetorical dexterity are often mistaken for substantive knowledge, allowing specious arguments to acquire an appearance of legitimacy. The resulting confusion is not merely (4)________; it can have tangible consequences when poorly examined claims influence public policy, medical decisions, or collective perceptions of social reality.
The remedy, therefore, cannot consist simply in accumulating more information. What is required is a deliberate cultivation of intellectual habits that enable individuals to distinguish the plausible from the demonstrable, the persuasive from the (5)________, and the familiar from the genuinely verifiable. In an informational ecosystem increasingly saturated with noise, scepticism—properly understood not as cynical disbelief but as disciplined inquiry—may be among the most indispensable forms of intellectual hygiene.

qs.q: Fill in the Blank 2.
qs.e:
Algorithms keep feeding material 'consonant with' users' preferences, so the environment feels deceptively harmonious and agreeable.
'Congruous' = in agreement, harmonious; it echoes 'consonant'.
Refractory (stubborn), pellucid (transparently clear) and censorious (severely critical) break the logic of an echo chamber.
Answer: congruous

qs.q: Fill in the Blank 3.
qs.e:
Because disagreement feels like an attack on identity, people stop letting unsettling information affect them.
'Impervious to' = not influenced or affected by, which fits 'even when such information is supported by cogent evidence'.
Receptive is the opposite; obsequious (servile) does not fit; inimical means harmful/hostile and describes a thing that damages, not a closed mind.
Answer: impervious

qs.q: Fill in the Blank 4.
qs.e:
The structure 'not merely ___; it can have tangible consequences' needs a word for something harmless that the sentence then contradicts.
'Innocuous' = harmless, so the confusion is not just harmless—it has real effects on policy and health.
Pernicious (harmful) would make the contrast pointless; recondite (obscure) and desultory (random) do not set up the contrast.

qs.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Suave
qs.e:
Suave = smoothly polite, charming and sophisticated.
Urbane carries the same sense of courteous refinement.
Prodigal = wasteful, lament = mourn, nippy = chilly/quick.
Answer: Urbane

qs.q:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.
Be up to the minute.
o: At the last possible instant or opportunity
To be as current as is possible
qs.e:
'Up to the minute' describes the very latest information or fashion.
So 'be up to the minute' means to be fully current.
'At the last possible instant' is the meaning of 'at the last minute', a different idiom.
Answer: To be as current as is possible

qs.q:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?
Eagerly, with great enthusiasm, or ready to enjoy oneself.
qs.e:
'With bells on' = eagerly and enthusiastically (e.g. 'I'll be there with bells on').
Bear the bell = take the lead; passing bell = a bell tolled at a death; sound as a bell = in perfect condition.
Answer: With bells on

qs.q: What is the antonym of "Irascible"?
qs.e:
Irascible = easily angered, hot-tempered.
Petulant, hostile and fractious all point to bad temper (near-synonyms).
Tranquil = calm and peaceful, the opposite.
Answer: Tranquil

qs.q:
Choose the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The librarian requested us to maintain silence in the reading room.
o: The librarian said to us, "Maintain silence in the reading room."
The librarian said, "Please maintain silence in the reading room."
The librarian told us, "Silence should be maintained in the reading room."
The librarian requested, "You can maintain silence in the reading room."
qs.e:
'Requested' in reported speech signals a polite imperative, which in direct speech is shown with 'Please'.
(a) drops the politeness and reads as an order; (c) changes it to passive; (d) keeps 'requested' as the reporting verb and turns it into a statement of ability.
(b) gives the polite imperative correctly.
Answer: The librarian said, "Please maintain silence in the reading room."

qs.q:
From the given alternatives, select the correct direct narration of the given indirect narration.
Shivi told Rahul that he had realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog.
o: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."
Shivi said to Rahul, "He realizes that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."
Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow had been actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."
Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made from a very large neighborhood dog."
qs.e:
Going back to direct speech, 'told' becomes 'said to' and the past perfect 'had realized' moves back one step to simple past 'realized'.
The 'were made' clause stays as it is; (c) wrongly makes it past perfect, (b) uses present 'realizes', (d) changes 'by' to 'from'.
All options keep 'He', so 'he' is taken as a third person here.
Answer: Shivi said to Rahul, "He realized that the mysterious footprints in the snow were actually made by a very large neighborhood dog."

qs.q:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the highlighted word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option "No replacement required".
His actions were considered an anathima to the entire community, leading to his exile.
qs.e:
The word meaning something intensely disliked or cursed is spelt a-n-a-t-h-e-m-a.
'anathima' in the sentence is wrong, and (a) and (b) are also misspelt.
Answer: anathema

qs.q:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice.
The victims were provided food and shelter by the volunteers.
o: The volunteers were providing food and shelter to the victims.
The volunteers have provided food and shelter to the victims.
The volunteers provide food and shelter to the victims.
The volunteers provided food and shelter to the victims
qs.e:
'were provided' is simple past passive, so the active verb must be simple past 'provided'.
The agent 'the volunteers' becomes the subject.
(a) past continuous, (b) present perfect and (c) simple present all change the tense.
Answer: The volunteers provided food and shelter to the victims

qs.q:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
1. In today's fast-paced world, it can be easy to feel disconnected from others.
2. That's why it's important to make time for face-to-face interactions with friends and loved ones.
3. Social media and technology have made it easier than ever to stay in touch, but they can also contribute to feelings of isolation.
4. By prioritizing these connections, we can improve our mental health and overall well-being.
qs.e:
1 states the problem (feeling disconnected); 3 explains a cause (technology can isolate).
2 ('That's why...') draws the remedy from 3; 4 ('these connections') refers back to the face-to-face interactions in 2.
Order: 1-3-2-4.
Answer: 1324

qs.q:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. One of the earliest known vacuum cleaners was so large that it had to be hauled from house to house.
B. Its giant hoses were popped through the windows of customers.
C. Vacuum cleaners were originally horse-drawn.
D. A gas-powered motor generated the suction that pulled the dirt and debris into a glass container where onlookers could gawk at the volume of filth coming from their neighbours' homes.
qs.e:
C opens with the general fact; A introduces one specific early machine.
B's 'Its giant hoses' must follow A, which names that machine.
D then explains how the suction worked and ends the description. Order: C-A-B-D.
Answer: CABD

qs.q:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The usher must have made the guests sit by the time the dinner was ready.
o: The guests must have been made sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.
The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.
The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready.
The guests must have made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner had been ready.
qs.e:
'must have made' becomes 'must have been made' in the passive.
After passive 'make', the bare infinitive changes to the to-infinitive: 'made to sit'.
The time clause 'by the time the dinner was ready' is not changed. (a) lacks 'to', (c) and (d) alter the time clause and (d) also drops 'been'.
Answer: The guests must have been made to sit by the usher by the time the dinner was ready.

qs.q: What is the term for a government controlled by monopolists?
qs.e:
Plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, the class that includes big monopoly holders.
Oligarchy is rule by a small group in general; autocracy is rule by one person.
Plutonomy refers to an economy driven by the rich, not a form of government.
Answer: Plutocracy

qs.q:
Directions: Identify the part containing a GRAMMATICAL ERROR.
The investigative committee / decided to look into / the irregularities and eventually / looked them over carefully.
qs.e:
'Look over' means to inspect quickly or superficially, which clashes with 'carefully' and with the committee's investigation.
The intended phrasal verb is 'look into' (investigate): '...and eventually looked into them carefully'.
The first three parts are correct, so the error is in the last part.
Answer: looked them over carefully

qs.q:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in their fixed positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.
S1 Two days and two nights did Peter sleep without once awakening.
A. He looked; there were two bags of gold.
B. When he came to himself, on the third day, he looked long at all the corners of his hut but in vain did he endeavour to recollect what had taken place; his memory was like a miser's pocket from which you cannot entice a quarter of a kopek.
C. Stretching himself, he heard something clash at his feet.
D. Then only, as if in a dream, he recollected that he had been seeking for treasure and that something had frightened him in the woods.
S2 But at what price he had obtained it, and how, he could by no means tell.
qs.e:
After S1 (he slept two days), B tells us he woke on the third day unable to remember anything.
C: stretching, he hears something clash; A: he looks and finds two bags of gold.
D: the gold jogs his memory of seeking treasure; S2 ('obtained it') refers to that treasure. Order: B-C-A-D.
Answer: BCAD

qs.q:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. The Voynich Manuscript is a 240-page medieval tome written in an unknown language that has baffled scholars and code-breakers for years.
B. All attempts to translate the book’s text or identify the plants depicted in it have failed.
C. The manuscript is believed to have originated sometime between 1404 and 1438.
D. It is filled with enigmatic illustrations and diagrams that seem to depict everything from unusual plants to women with swollen bellies bathing in green pools.
qs.e:
A introduces the manuscript by name; C ('The manuscript') gives its date.
D describes its contents, including plants; B's 'the plants depicted in it' needs D before it.
Order: A-C-D-B.
Answer: ACDB

qs.q: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
qs.e:
A writer of plays is a 'playwright'. It comes from 'wright' (a maker, as in shipwright), not from 'write'.
The other three are common misspellings.
Answer: Playwright

qs.q:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
He warned that if we did not act immediately, the consequences would be irreversible.
o: He said, "If you didn't act immediately, the consequences will be irreversible."
He said, "If you don't act immediately, the consequences will be irreversible."
He said, "If you hadn't act immediately, the consequences would be irreversible."
He said, "If you haven't act immediately, the consequences would be irreversible."
qs.e:
In direct speech, 'did not act' goes back to 'don't act' and 'would be' goes back to 'will be'. This is a first conditional.
'we' in the report becomes 'you' when he addresses them.
(a) mixes past and future; (c) and (d) are ungrammatical ('hadn't act', 'haven't act').
Answer: He said, "If you don't act immediately, the consequences will be irreversible."

qs.q:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
The trainer said to the trainees, "Go on writing this paragraph till you understand it very clearly."
o: The trainer asked the trainees going on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.
The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.
The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understand it very clearly.
The trainer asked the trainees to went on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.
qs.e:
An imperative is reported as 'asked + object + to-infinitive': 'asked the trainees to go on'.
'this' becomes 'that', 'you' becomes 'they', and 'understand' moves back to 'understood'.
(a) uses 'going', (c) keeps present 'understand', and (d) has 'to went'.
Answer: The trainer asked the trainees to go on writing that paragraph till they understood it very clearly.

qs.q:
Choose the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
She said that she had started attending yoga classes because she wanted to lose weight.
o: She said, "I started attending yoga classes because I wants to lose weight."
She said, "I have started attending yoga classes because I want to lose weight."
She said, "I started attending yoga classes because I wanted to lose weight."
She said, "I had started attending yoga classes because I want lose weight."
qs.e:
Reversing the backshift turns past perfect 'had started' into present perfect 'have started' and past 'wanted' into present 'want'.
The pronoun 'she' becomes 'I'.
(a) has 'I wants', (c) leaves 'wanted' in the past, and (d) keeps 'had' and drops 'to'.
Answer: She said, "I have started attending yoga classes because I want to lose weight."

qs.q:
Choose the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
He asked her whether she wanted tea or coffee with her breakfast.
o: He asked her, "You want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"
He said, "Whether you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"
He asked, "Did you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"
He said to her, "Do you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"
qs.e:
'asked her whether...' becomes 'said to her' + a yes/no question starting with an auxiliary: 'Do you want...?'
'wanted' moves back to present 'want', and 'she/her' become 'you/your'.
(a) has no question order, (b) keeps 'whether', and (c) leaves the verb in the past.
Answer: He said to her, "Do you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?"

qs.q: In a sports club, men get full-time coaches but women get part-time coaches despite equal membership fees. Which inference is valid?
o: Possible gender bias in coaching allocation
qs.e:
Both groups pay the same fee, yet women receive a lesser coaching arrangement.
Nothing is said about training needs, coaches' hours or team strength, so (a)-(c) are unsupported guesses.
Unequal service for equal payment based on gender points to a possible bias in allocation.
Answer: Possible gender bias in coaching allocation

qs.q: If 12 March 2024 is a Tuesday, then what day will 21 September 2024 be?
qs.e:
Days after 12 March up to 21 September: March 19 + April 30 + May 31 + June 30 + July 31 + August 31 + September 21 = 193.
193 = 27 × 7 + 4, so 4 odd days.
Tuesday + 4 days = Saturday.
Answer: Saturday

qs.q:
In each of the following questions, a statement is given followed by 2 conclusions. Read the statements carefully and answer the following questions:
Statement: Mr. X is one of the probable candidates short-listed for the post of Director of R.L.M. Institute.
Conclusions:
I. Mr. X will be selected as Director of R.L.M. Institute.
II. Mr. X will not be selected as Director of R.L.M. Institute.
qs.e:
Being short-listed means the outcome is still open: he will either be selected or not.
Neither conclusion alone is certain, but I and II are complementary, so exactly one of them must be true.
Answer: either I or II follows.

qs.q:
Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of ? will logically complete the series?
[Box 1: 3 smiley faces in a column; Box 2: 4 '%' signs; Box 3: 5 '#' signs; Box 4: 6 '@' signs; Box 5: ?]
qs.e:
The symbol changes each step and the count rises by one: 3, 4, 5, 6.
The next box must hold 7 symbols; all options use triangles, so pick the one with 7.
Answer: 7 triangles (Δ) in a column

qs.q:
In the question below there are three statements followed by two conclusions I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the three statements disregarding commonly known facts.
Statements:
Only Car are Vehicle.
Some Car are Bulky.
All Metal are Bulky.
Conclusions:
I. Some Vehicle are not Metal.
II. Some Metal are Car.
qs.e:
SSC/Adda convention: 'Only Car are Vehicle' means every Vehicle is a Car and Vehicle is linked to nothing except Car, so no Vehicle is Metal.
Hence some (indeed all) Vehicles are not Metal: I follows.
Metal lies inside Bulky and Bulky only partly overlaps Car, so Metal may or may not meet Car: II does not follow.
Answer: Only I
Note: B overrules A, agrees with key (c). In SSC/bank reasoning 'Only A are B' is read as 'All B are A' with B restricted to A, i.e. B has no overlap with any other set; that makes Vehicle and Metal disjoint, so I is definite. A's (d) comes from pure Venn logic, where Vehicle could sit inside the Car-Bulky-Metal overlap; that reading is not the exam convention. Marked check: plain set logic gives "Neither"; the exam convention for "Only A are B" gives "Only I" (key).

qs.q: Pointing to a lady, a man said, "The son of her only brother is the brother of my wife." How is the lady related to the man?
qs.e:
The son of the lady's brother is the man's wife's brother, so the lady's brother is the wife's father.
The wife's father is the man's father-in-law, and the lady is his sister.
Answer: Sister of father-in-law

qs.q: In a certain coded language 'COMPS' is coded as 'NKHKY' and 'ABATE' is coded as 'ZOVXW'. How will 'SMOKY' be coded in the same code language?
qs.e:
Write the word in reverse, then shift letters back by 5, 5, 5, 4, 4.
COMPS → SPMOC → S−5=N, P−5=K, M−5=H, O−4=K, C−4=Y → NKHKY; ABATE → ETABA → Z, O, V, X, W ✓.
SMOKY → YKOMS → Y−5=T, K−5=F, O−5=J, M−4=I, S−4=O → TFJIO.
Answer: TFJIO

qs.q:
Which of the following option, if true, would most undermine the conclusion?
Observation: A large number of street vendors moved from the city market area to the main railway station area. Conclusion: The City Market Authority must have enforced stricter regulations, causing the vendors to relocate.
o: Rent in the railway station area is significantly higher than in the city market area.
The City Market Authority recently increased the daily fee for vendors by 50%.
A major new office complex recently opened near the railway station, significantly increasing foot traffic there.
Street vendors typically prefer locations with easy access to public transportation.
qs.e:
The conclusion blames a push from the market authority.
Option (b) supports that push; (a) makes the move harder to explain but gives no other cause; (d) is a general preference, not a new change.
Option (c) gives a fresh pull factor (new customers at the station), an alternative reason that weakens the conclusion most.
Answer: A major new office complex recently opened near the railway station, significantly increasing foot traffic there.

qs.q:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.
Statement:
No chair is a stool.
All stools are wooden.
Conclusions:
I. No chair is wooden.
II. Some wooden are not chairs.
o: Either conclusion I or II follows.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
qs.e:
Chairs are kept apart from stools, but chairs may still overlap the wooden set outside the stools, so I is not certain.
Every stool is wooden and no stool is a chair, so those wooden things (the stools) are not chairs: II follows.
Answer: Only conclusion II follows.

qs.q:
What would be the number on the opposite side of '8' if the given sheet is folded to form a cube?
[Net: a vertical column of four squares 6, 8, 5, 7 (top to bottom); 9 is attached to the left of 8; 10 is attached to the right of 5]
qs.e:
In a straight column of four faces, alternate faces are opposite: 6 opposite 5 and 8 opposite 7.
The two side flaps 9 and 10 are then opposite each other.
Answer: 7

qs.q:
Examine the statement and determine which assumptions are logically implied or necessary for the statement to hold true.
Statement:
Companies should adopt flexible work policies to improve employee productivity.
Assumption:
I. Flexible work arrangements can enhance employee productivity.
II. Employees prefer flexible work policies.
III. All companies currently have low employee productivity.
o: Only I and II are implicit
Only II and III are implicit
qs.e:
The advice only makes sense if flexibility can raise productivity, so I is implicit.
The statement is about productivity, not what employees like, so II is not needed.
'All companies' having low productivity is an extreme claim; improvement can be sought from any level, so III is not implicit.
Answer: Only I is implicit

qs.q:
Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?
27, 55, 99, 165, 260, ?
qs.e:
First differences: 28, 44, 66, 95.
Second differences: 16, 22, 29, which themselves grow by 6 and 7; the next grows by 8, giving 37.
Next first difference = 95 + 37 = 132, so the term = 260 + 132 = 392.
Answer: 392

qs.q: In a line of 33 bicycles, Bicycle R is 10th from the left and Bicycle S is 17th from the right. How many bicycles are there between R and S?
qs.e:
S from the left = 33 − 17 + 1 = 17th.
R is 10th from the left, so bicycles between = 17 − 10 − 1 = 6.
Answer: 6

qs.q:
Statement: "The education board will now conduct teacher training every quarter".
Which conclusion follows?
o: Teachers are unhappy with current conditions
qs.e:
Holding training every quarter shows the board wants teachers' skills refreshed regularly.
Nothing in the statement concerns online classes, student failure or teacher satisfaction.
Answer: Teacher skills need regular updates

qs.q: Find the next letter in the series: M, L, J, G, ?
qs.e:
Positions: M=13, L=12, J=10, G=7.
Gaps are −1, −2, −3, so the next gap is −4: 7 − 4 = 3 = C.
Answer: C

qs.q:
In the question below one statement is given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true, then consider the two conclusions together and decide which of them logically follows beyond a reasonable doubt from the information given in the statement.
Statement: Morning walks are good for health.
Conclusions:
I. All healthy people go for morning walks.
II. Evening walks are harmful.
qs.e:
Saying morning walks help health does not mean every healthy person walks in the morning, so I fails.
The statement says nothing about evening walks, so II fails.
Answer: Neither I nor II follows

qs.q:
In each question below is given a statement followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. You have to consider the statement and the following assumptions and decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.
Statement:
The Parent Teacher Association (PTA) of a school has informed the Principal that they will not send their children to the school unless the school authority reduces the fees with immediate effect.
Assumptions:
I. Majority of the parents may agree with the PTA and may not send their wards to the school.
II. The school authority may accede to the demand of the PTA and reduce the fees.
o: If only assumption I is implicit
If only assumption II is implicit
If both I and II are implicit.
If neither I nor II is implicit
qs.e:
The PTA's threat works only if most parents will actually keep their children home, so I is assumed.
The PTA issues the demand expecting the school may give in, so II is assumed too.
Answer: If both I and II are implicit.

qs.q:
In the figure given below the triangle represents balls, the circle represents chairs and the rectangle represents wickets. The number in each area represents the number of items in that area.
Which of the following statement is correct?
I. Number of wickets which are only chairs are 10.
II. Total number of balls are 14 less than the total number of wickets.
[Diagram regions: wickets only = 13; wickets and chairs only = 10; wickets, chairs and balls = 8; wickets and balls only = 11; chairs only = 9; chairs and balls only = 7; balls only = 12]
qs.e:
I: the part of the rectangle inside the circle but outside the triangle is 10, so wickets that are chairs only (not balls) = 10: true.
Balls = 8 + 11 + 7 + 12 = 38; wickets = 13 + 10 + 8 + 11 = 42.
Balls are 42 − 38 = 4 fewer, not 14, so II is false.
Answer: Only I

qs.q:
The following question consists of a Statement followed by two Arguments I and II.
Give answer :
Statement: Should a total ban be put on trapping wild animals?
Arguments:
I. Yes. Trappers are making a lot of money.
II. No. Bans on hunting and trapping are not effective.
o: if only argument I is strong
if only argument II is strong
if both I and II are strong
if neither I nor II is strong
qs.e:
I: trappers' earnings are not a reason to ban trapping; the real issue is harm to wildlife, so I is weak.
II: a law being hard to enforce is no reason to drop it; the answer is better enforcement, so II is weak.
Answer: if neither I nor II is strong

qs.q:
In making decisions about important questions, it is desirable to be able to distinguish between strong arguments and weak arguments. Strong arguments are those which are both important and directly related to the question. Weak arguments are those which are of minor importance and also may not be directly related to the question or may be related to a trivial aspect of the question. Each question below is followed by two arguments numbered I and II. You have to decide which of the arguments is a strong argument and which is a weak argument.
Statement: Should so much money be spent on advertisements?
Arguments:
I. Yes. It is an essential concomitant in a capitalist economy.
II. No. It leads to wastage of resources.
o: if only argument I is strong
if only argument II is strong
if both I and II are strong
if neither I nor II is strong
qs.e:
I: in a competitive market economy firms must advertise to reach buyers, so heavy ad spending is a built-in need: strong.
II: advertising informs consumers and drives sales; calling it pure waste is a sweeping, unsupported claim: weak.
Answer: if only argument I is strong

qs.q: Which of the following is the most effective step for mitigating the impact of an earthquake?
qs.e:
Most earthquake deaths and losses come from collapsing structures, not the shaking itself.
Mapping seismic zones and enforcing earthquake-resistant building codes directly cuts that damage.
Water harvesting and flood barriers address other hazards; deforestation worsens disaster risk.
Answer: Seismic zoning and earthquake-resistant buildings

qs.q: India’s support for which of the following missions aligns most closely with IMEC’s purpose?
o: One Sun One World One Grid initiative
qs.e:
IMEC (India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor) plans rail, shipping, digital and electricity-grid links across regions.
One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG) aims to interconnect power grids across countries for cross-border clean energy flow.
That cross-border grid connectivity is the closest match to IMEC's connectivity purpose.
Answer: One Sun One World One Grid initiative

qs.q: Which of the following is a subject under the State List?
qs.e:
Public order is Entry 1 of the State List (List II, Seventh Schedule).
Banking and Defence are Union List subjects.
Education moved to the Concurrent List through the 42nd Amendment (1976).
Answer: Public Order

qs.q: Which of the following programmes is NOT a part of the Tenth Five-Year Plan?
qs.e:
The Tenth Plan ran from 2002 to 2007.
The National Horticulture Mission (2005-06), the Micro Irrigation scheme (2006) and the Jute Technology Mission (2006-07) were all launched in that period.
The Drought Prone Area Programme is much older; it began in 1973-74 during the Fourth/Fifth Plan era.
Answer: Drought Prone Area Programme

qs.q: The phase difference between the instantaneous velocity and acceleration of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is:
qs.e:
In SHM, x = A sin ωt, so v = Aω cos ωt = Aω sin(ωt + π/2).
Then a = -Aω² sin ωt = Aω² sin(ωt + π).
Velocity leads displacement by π/2 and acceleration leads it by π, so velocity and acceleration differ by π/2.
Answer: π/2

qs.q: In cricket, ________ is called by the umpire when the bowler doesn’t deliver the ball within reach of the batter.
qs.e:
If a delivery passes so far from the batter that it cannot be reached with a normal stroke, the umpire signals a wide.
A no ball is about illegal actions such as overstepping the crease, and a yorker is just a type of delivery.
Answer: wide

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the District Planning Committee?
qs.e:
Part IXA (Municipalities), added by the 74th Amendment, contains Articles 243P to 243ZG.
Article 243ZD requires a District Planning Committee in every district to consolidate panchayat and municipal plans.
Article 243ZE covers the Metropolitan Planning Committee.
Answer: 243-ZD

qs.q: How many players are there on each side of the Kabaddi Team in the field?
qs.e:
A kabaddi team has 12 registered players, but only 7 take the field at a time.
The other 5 are substitutes.
Answer: 7

qs.q: Who was the great general responsible for executing Alauddin Khilji's Deccan campaigns successfully?
qs.e:
Malik Kafur, Alauddin Khilji's slave-general, led the southern expeditions against Devagiri, Warangal, the Hoysalas (Dwarasamudra) and Madurai between about 1307 and 1311.
Aibak and Balban belong to the earlier Slave dynasty, and Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq founded the Tughlaq dynasty.
Answer: Malik Kafur

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding BRICS:
1. BRICS represents 49.5% of the global population.
2. BRICS represents 40% of global GDP.
3. BRICS represents 26% of global trade.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
qs.e:
For the expanded BRICS grouping, Indian government statements give these shares: about 49.5% of the world's population, about 40% of global GDP and about 26% of global trade.
All three statements match these figures.
Answer: 1, 2 and 3

qs.q: Who among the following is the writer of ‘Train to Pakistan’, ‘Good, Bad and Ridiculous’ and ‘Delhi: A Novel’?
qs.e:
Khushwant Singh wrote Train to Pakistan (1956), about the Partition, and Delhi: A Novel (1990).
'The Good, the Bad and the Ridiculous' is his book of profiles.
Answer: Khushwant Singh

qs.q: Gangaur Festival, Pushkar Fair, Nagaur Fair and Urs Fair are the popular fairs and festivals of which state?
qs.e:
All four are held in Rajasthan.
Gangaur is a major festival of the state, the Pushkar camel fair takes place near Ajmer, the Nagaur cattle fair in Nagaur, and the Urs is held at the Ajmer Sharif dargah.
Answer: Rajasthan

qs.q: Banking reforms were part of the 1991 economic reforms. Which of the following committees recommended banking sector liberalisation in 1991?
qs.e:
In 1991 the M. Narasimham Committee on the Financial System recommended banking reforms, including lower SLR/CRR, interest-rate deregulation and the entry of private banks.
The Kelkar committee dealt with tax reform, and the Tendulkar committee with poverty estimation.
Answer: Narasimham Committee

qs.q: Who was the first Indian Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) after independence?
qs.e:
H.K. Kripalani became chairman in April 1947 and was the first Indian to head the Commission.
He stayed in office through independence until January 1949.
R.N. Banerjee followed him and was in office when the body was renamed UPSC in 1950.
Answer: H.K. Kripalani

qs.q:
Find out the chronological order of the following British Authorities/Persons who took interest in higher education in India:
A. Lord Curzon B. Lord Ripon C. Lord Canning D. Lord Dalhousie
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
qs.e:
Dalhousie: Wood's Despatch (1854).
Canning: universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (1857).
Ripon: Hunter Education Commission (1882).
Curzon: Indian Universities Act (1904).
Answer: D, C, B, A

qs.q: Apart from India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana', Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore composed the national anthem of which of the following countries?
qs.e:
Tagore wrote 'Amar Shonar Bangla' (1905), which Bangladesh adopted as its national anthem.
Sri Lanka's anthem was written by Ananda Samarakoon, though Tagore is said to have influenced it.
Answer: Bangladesh

qs.q: According to the 2011 Census, which of the following religions has the lowest population in the state of Punjab?
qs.e:
Punjab, Census 2011: Islam about 1.93%, Christianity about 1.26%, Jainism about 0.16% (about 45,000) and Buddhism about 0.12% (about 33,000).
Buddhists are the smallest of the four groups.
Answer: Buddhism

qs.q: Work done by a constant force depends on which of the following?
o: Both force and displacement, and the angle between them
qs.e:
For a constant force, W = F·s = F s cos θ.
The work depends on the size of the force, the size of the displacement and the angle between them, and it is zero when θ = 90°.
Answer: Both force and displacement, and the angle between them

qs.q:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
(a) Article 269A of the Constitution of India empowers the Government of India to collect the Goods and services Tax in course of inter-state trade and commerce.
(B) The amount apportioned to a state under the Goods and Services Tax shall form part of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e:
Article 269A(1): the Government of India levies and collects GST on supplies made in inter-state trade or commerce, so (a) is correct.
Article 269A(2): the amount apportioned to a State does NOT form part of the Consolidated Fund of India, so (B) is wrong.
Answer: (a) only

qs.q: Who among the following was part of the gold medal winning Indian hockey team of 1928 Summer Olympics?
qs.e:
Dhyan Chand was India's top scorer at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, where India won its first hockey gold.
Balbir Singh Sr. won his golds from 1948 onwards, and K.D. Jadhav was a wrestler (bronze in 1952).
Answer: Major Dhyan Chand

qs.q: Who supported the king’s judicial authority in the Gupta Empire and played a key role in the judicial system?
qs.e:
In Gupta administration the Mahadandanayaka was the chief judicial (and military) officer who carried out the king's justice.
The Mahapratihara was the chief of the palace guards, Uparikas governed provinces (bhuktis), and Vishayapatis ran districts (vishayas).
Answer: Mahadandanayaka

qs.q: Which of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution is regarded as a major milestone in the country's taxation system for introducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
qs.e:
The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 introduced GST by adding Articles 246A, 269A and 279A (GST Council).
The 97th covered cooperative societies, the 100th the India-Bangladesh land boundary and the 86th the right to education.
Answer: 101st Amendment, 2016

qs.q: Under the Pitt’s India Act of 1784, the Board of Control supervised:
o: Civil and Military government and Revenues
qs.e:
Pitt's India Act set up dual control.
The Court of Directors kept the Company's commercial affairs.
The new Board of Control supervised and directed civil and military government and revenues in the Company's Indian possessions.
Answer: Civil and Military government and Revenues

qs.q: What is the weight of the shot put for the men's category?
qs.e:
The senior men's shot weighs 7.26 kg, which is 16 lb.
The women's shot weighs 4 kg (about 8.8 lb).
Answer: 16 pounds

qs.q: What term describes the region of rapidly increasing density with increasing depth in the ocean?
qs.e:
The pycnocline is the layer where water density rises sharply with depth.
The thermocline is the corresponding layer for temperature (falling sharply) and the halocline for salinity; an isotherm is just a line of equal temperature.
Answer: Pycnocline

qs.q: A boat travels a certain distance. The ratio of the time taken by the boat to travel downstream to the time taken to travel upstream is 5:7. If the downstream speed is 21 km/h, find the speed of the boat in still water.
qs.e:
Same distance both ways, so speeds are in the inverse ratio of times: downstream : upstream = 7 : 5.
Downstream = 21 km/h, so upstream = 21 × 5/7 = 15 km/h.
Still-water speed = (21 + 15)/2 = 18 km/h.
Answer: 18 km/h

qs.q: Two parallel chords are drawn in a circle of radius 25 cm. The distance between the two chords is 27 cm. If the length of one chord is 48 cm, then length of the other chord is equal to:
qs.e:
Chord of 48 cm has half-length 24, so its distance from the centre = √(25² − 24²) = 7 cm.
27 cm > 25 cm, so the chords lie on opposite sides of the centre; the other is 27 − 7 = 20 cm from the centre.
Its half-length = √(25² − 20²) = 15, so length = 30 cm.
Answer: 30 cm

qs.q:
What is the value of (9x + 2y), if the mean of the following distribution is 68?
Class: 0-20 | 20-40 | 40-60 | 60-80 | 80-100 | Total
Frequency: 4 | 10 | x | 2 | y | 60
Ten observations written in descending order are 45, 34, 32, 30, 2x - 15, x + 3, 17, 15, 14, and 8. If the median is 24, then find the value of x.
qs.e:
With 10 values, the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th terms: (2x − 15 + x + 3)/2 = 24.
3x − 12 = 48, so x = 20.
Check: the terms become 25 and 23, which keep the descending order (30 > 25 > 23 > 17).
Answer: 20

qs.q: If the mean of three values 3x, 2x+6 and 2x+1 is 7, then find x.
qs.e:
Sum of the three values = 3 × 7 = 21.
3x + 2x + 6 + 2x + 1 = 7x + 7 = 21, so x = 2.
Answer: 2

qs.q: If cot x = 5/12, then sec x + cosec x = ?
qs.e:
cot x = 5/12 gives adjacent 5, opposite 12, hypotenuse 13.
sec x = 13/5, cosec x = 13/12.
Sum = 13(1/5 + 1/12) = 13 × 17/60 = 221/60.
Answer: 221/60

qs.q: If x + y = 5 and 1/x + 1/y = 20/9, then the value of x³ + y³ is:
If cot²θ = 1 + cos²θ - sin²θ, 0° < θ < 90°, then find the value of tan²θ + cosec²θ.
qs.e:
1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, so the right side is 2cos²θ.
cos²θ/sin²θ = 2cos²θ, and cos θ ≠ 0 in the range, so sin²θ = 1/2, i.e. θ = 45°.
tan²45° + cosec²45° = 1 + 2 = 3.
Answer: 3

qs.q: The area of four walls of a room is 336 m². The length of the room is thrice its breadth. If the height of the room is 6 m. What is the area of the floor.
qs.e:
Area of four walls = 2h(l + b) = 2 × 6 × (3b + b) = 48b = 336, so b = 7 m.
l = 3 × 7 = 21 m.
Floor area = 21 × 7 = 147 m².
Answer: 147 m²

qs.q: A train running at 63 km/h takes 30 sec to pass a platform. Next it takes 18 sec to pass a man cycling at 9 km/h in the same direction in which the train is going. The ratio of the length of the train to the length of the platform is:
qs.e:
Relative speed past the cyclist = 63 − 9 = 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so train length = 15 × 18 = 270 m.
Train speed = 63 km/h = 17.5 m/s; train + platform = 17.5 × 30 = 525 m, so platform = 255 m.
270 : 255 = 18 : 17.
Answer: 18 : 17

qs.q: In a parallelogram ABCD, the diagonals intersect at O. ∠BCA = 38° and ∠CAB = 27°. Find ∠AOD if ∠ADO : ∠CDO = 2 : 3.
qs.e:
In triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 180° − 38° − 27° = 115°, and opposite angle ∠ADC = 115°.
Splitting 115° in 2 : 3 gives ∠ADO = 46°, ∠CDO = 69°.
AD ∥ BC, so ∠DAO = ∠DAC = ∠BCA = 38° (alternate angles).
In triangle AOD: ∠AOD = 180° − 38° − 46° = 96°.
Answer: 96°

qs.q: The radius of a cylinder is increased by 33 1/3% and its height is decreased by x% such that the volume of the cylinder remains unchanged. Find x.
qs.e:
Volume ∝ r²h. Radius becomes 4/3 times, so r² becomes 16/9 times.
To keep the volume fixed, height must become 9/16 of the original.
Decrease = 7/16 = 43.75%.
Answer: 43.75

qs.q: A cube has a total surface area of 294 cm². A smaller cube is cut from one of its corners such that the edge of the smaller cube is one-third the edge of the original cube. Find the surface area of the remaining solid.
qs.e:
6a² = 294 gives a = 7 cm (small cube edge 7/3 cm).
Removing a corner cube takes away three small square faces from the outside but exposes three equal inner faces.
So the total surface area is unchanged: 294 cm².
Answer: 294 cm²

qs.q: The value of sin²42° + sin²48° + sec²30° − cot²45° is:
qs.e:
sin 48° = cos 42°, so sin²42° + sin²48° = 1.
sec²30° = (2/√3)² = 4/3 and cot²45° = 1.
Total = 1 + 4/3 − 1 = 4/3.
Answer: 4/3

qs.q: The mean and the mode of a set of data are 62 and 43.6, respectively. Find the median of the data, using the empirical formula. (Round off to one decimal place)
qs.e:
Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, so Median = (Mode + 2 Mean)/3.
Median = (43.6 + 124)/3 = 167.6/3 = 55.87.
Rounded to one decimal: 55.9.
Answer: 55.9

qs.q: Manu printed 20 books of 200 pages each. The cost of printing is Rs. 25 per page. After this, he spent Rs. 80 per book on binding. After this, he spent Rs. 2,000 on advertising the books and Rs. 50 per book in supply. If at the end he sold each book for Rs. 7500, then find the amount gained (profit) by Manu.
Anirudh travels 55 km at 11 km/h, 65 km at 13 km/h, and 120 km at 20 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h)?
qs.e:
Times: 55/11 = 5 h, 65/13 = 5 h, 120/20 = 6 h; total 16 h.
Total distance = 55 + 65 + 120 = 240 km.
Average speed = 240/16 = 15 km/h.
Answer: 15

qs.q: A jar contains a mixture of orange juice and water in the ratio of 3 : 1. 70 litres of the mixture were taken out, and 20 litres of water were added to it. If the water was 30% in the resultant mixture, what was the initial quantity of the mixture in the jar?
qs.e:
Let the mixture be 4k litres (water k). Removing 70 L takes out 17.5 L water, leaving k − 17.5 water in 4k − 70.
After adding 20 L water: water k + 2.5 in a total of 4k − 50.
(k + 2.5) = 0.3(4k − 50) gives 0.2k = 17.5, so k = 87.5.
Initial quantity = 4 × 87.5 = 350 litres.
Answer: 350 litres

qs.q: Four litres of paint was required to paint the surface of a solid sphere. If 4 identical pieces were made of this solid sphere, then how many litres of paint would be required to paint all the surfaces of these 4 pieces?
qs.e:
Sphere surface 4πr² needs 4 L. Cutting by two perpendicular planes through a diameter gives 4 identical quarter-spheres.
Each piece: curved part πr² plus two semicircular flat faces of πr²/2 each, so 2πr².
All four pieces: 8πr² = twice the sphere's surface, so 2 × 4 = 8 L.
Answer: 8

qs.q: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 87.5°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 2 : 3, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
qs.e:
In triangle STR: ∠STR = 180° − (∠R + ∠S)/2 = (∠P + ∠Q)/2, since all four angles sum to 360°.
So ∠P + ∠Q = 2 × 87.5° = 175°.
With ∠P : ∠Q = 2 : 3, ∠P = 70° and ∠Q = 105°.
Difference = 35°.
Answer: 35°

qs.q: The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 2 more than twice of one of the sides, while the third side is 13 more than half of the hypotenuse. The length of the median to the hypotenuse is:
qs.e:
Let one side be a: hypotenuse = 2a + 2, third side = (a + 1) + 13 = a + 14.
a² + (a + 14)² = (2a + 2)² gives a² − 10a − 96 = 0, so a = 16.
Sides 16, 30, 34 (256 + 900 = 1156 = 34²).
Median to the hypotenuse = half the hypotenuse = 17.
Answer: 17

qs.q: If cos A = √3/2, A is an acute angle, then find the value of (tanA − cotA)/(√3 − secA).
qs.e:
cos A = √3/2 with A acute gives A = 30°.
tan A − cot A = 1/√3 − √3 = −2/√3.
√3 − sec A = √3 − 2/√3 = 1/√3.
Ratio = −2.
Answer: -2

qs.q: The number of daily active users on an educational app is modeled by a variable X. If the baseline engagement metric satisfies the equation X + 1/X = 3√2, a data analyst needs to calculate a higher-order engagement index given by the expression X³ + 1/X³. What is the precise numerical value of this higher-order index?

Akshat and Shivam start walking together from point P towards point Q, which are located 300 km away from each other. Akshat travels at a speed of 70 km/h, while Shivam travels at a speed of 50 km/h. After reaching point Q, Akshat immediately turns back towards point P and eventually meets Shivam on the way. At what distance from point Q do they meet?
qs.e:
At the meeting, together they have covered 2 × 300 = 600 km.
Time = 600/(70 + 50) = 5 h.
Shivam has walked 50 × 5 = 250 km from P, i.e. 300 − 250 = 50 km short of Q.
Answer: 50 km

qs.q: What will be the compound interest on a sum of ₹10,176 after 3 years at the rate of 25% per annum, interest being compounded annually?

Given below are some jumbled sentences. Pick the one that gives their correct order.
(1) of space scientists of India, which provides platform to the researchers in space sciences

qs.q:
Given below are some jumbled sentences. Pick the one that gives their correct order.

qs.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Zealous
