Answer: 4682D

qs.q:
In a certain code language,
A @ B means 'A is the mother of B',
A × B means 'A is the wife of B',
A + B means 'A is the brother of B' and
A ÷ B means 'A is the father of B'.
How is S related to H if 'S × D ÷ R + Y @ H'?
qs.e:
S × D: S is D's wife. D ÷ R: D is R's father. R + Y: R is Y's brother, so Y is also a child of D and S.
Y @ H: Y is H's mother.
So S is the mother of H's mother.
Answer: Mother's mother

qs.q:
Consider the given statement(s) and decide which of the given assumption(s) is are implicit in the statement;
Children below age of 5 years should not be given any writing home-work.
Assumptions:
I. Their hands are yet to form co-ordination to hold pencil/ writing material for long.
II. They are very young to be introduced to writing skills.
o: Both I and II are implicit.
Neither I nor II is implicit.
qs.e:
The advice bars writing homework for under-fives, so the writer must take for granted a reason why writing work does not suit them.
I (hands not yet able to hold a pencil for long) and II (too young to be introduced to writing) are both such reasons; each, if false, weakens the advice.
On standard SSC logic a recommendation implicitly assumes the plausible grounds behind it, so both are implicit.
Answer: Both I and II are implicit.

qs.q:
Consider the given statement(s) and decide which of the given assumption(s) is/are implicit in the statement.
Statement:
Students should be encouraged to participate in debates.
Assumptions:
I. They will learn convincing skills.
II. Their communication skills will be enhanced.
o: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
qs.e:
Encouraging debate presumes it benefits students.
Debating trains persuasion (I) and speaking/expression (II), both natural reasons behind the advice.
Answer: Both I and II are implicit

qs.q:
In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions. Find out which conclusion is true based on the given statement.
Statement: S = T < U ≤ V > W
Conclusions:
I. T < W
II. S < V
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
qs.e:
I: T < U ≤ V > W — the sign flips at V, so T and W cannot be compared; I is false.
II: S = T < U ≤ V gives S < V; II is true.
Answer: Only II is true

qs.q:
You are given a Master Address (MA) from official records. Your task is to identify the correct candidate address that matches exactly with the master address in terms of formatting, punctuation, spelling, and structure.
Master Address (MA): FL-10, Block C-3, Royal Enclave, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad - 380009
Candidate Addresses
o: FL-10, Block C-3, Royal Enclave, Ashram Rd., Ahmedabad - 380009
F.L.-10, Block C-3, Royal Enclave, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad - 380009
FL-10, Block C 3, Royal Enclave, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad - 380009
FL-10, Block C-3, Royal Enclave, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad - 380009
qs.e:
(a) shortens 'Road' to 'Rd.'; (b) writes 'F.L.' with dots.
(c) drops the hyphen in 'C-3'.
(d) matches the master address exactly.
Answer: FL-10, Block C-3, Royal Enclave, Ashram Road, Ahmedabad - 380009

qs.q:
Find the next term in the following series.
256, 246, 235, 223, 210, ?
qs.e:
Differences are −10, −11, −12, −13, so the next is −14.
210 − 14 = 196.
Answer: 196

qs.q:
Consider the argument and decide which of the given assumptions is/are implicit Argument:
The BEST bus travels company has decided to increase its fare by 10%.
Assumptions:
1. Passengers may opt for other buses costing less than the BEST bus travels company.
2. The demand for the buses by passengers may remain unchanged even after the fare hike.
qs.e:
A company raises fares expecting it will not lose its riders, so 2 is implicit.
1 predicts riders leaving, which runs against the reasoning behind the hike, so it is not assumed.
Answer: Only assumption 2 is implicit.

qs.q: In which Indian state is the Onam festival celebrated, and why is it celebrated?
o: Tamil Nadu - To mark the homecoming of King Ram
Karnataka - To honor the victory of Lord Rama over Ravana
Kerala - To mark the homecoming of King Mahabali, as per local legends
Andhra Pradesh - To mark the arrival of the monsoon season
qs.e:
Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala, held in the Malayalam month of Chingam.
Legend says the benevolent Asura king Mahabali visits his people every year during Onam.
Highlights include Pookalam, Onasadya feast and Vallam Kali boat races.
Answer: Kerala - To mark the homecoming of King Mahabali, as per local legends

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the control of High Courts over subordinate courts?
qs.e:
Article 235 vests control over district courts and subordinate courts in the High Court.
This includes postings, promotions and leave of judicial officers below district judge.
Art 107 deals with passing of Bills, Art 308 defines 'State' for Part XIV, Art 115 covers supplementary grants.
Answer: Article 235

qs.q: How many total jumps are there in a 3000 m steeplechase race?
qs.e:
The 3000 m steeplechase has 28 fixed barrier jumps and 7 water jumps.
28 + 7 = 35 jumps in total over about 7.5 laps.
Answer: 35

qs.q: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi became the most popular artist of which Gharana?
qs.e:
Bhimsen Joshi trained under Sawai Gandharva, a disciple of Abdul Karim Khan, founder of the Kirana gharana.
He became the best-known Kirana vocalist and received the Bharat Ratna in 2008.
Answer: Kirana Gharana

qs.q: India shares a maritime boundary (sea boundary) with which one of the following countries across the Arabian Sea or the Indian Ocean?
qs.e:
India's maritime neighbours include Sri Lanka, Maldives, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia.
The Maldives lies south-west of Lakshadweep across the Eight Degree Channel.
Mongolia and Afghanistan are landlocked; Russia has no sea boundary with India.
Answer: Maldives

qs.q:
Read the following statements carefully and choose the correct option regarding Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The 1991 reforms led to the opening of the Indian economy to foreign investors.
Reason (R): The government wanted to increase domestic savings rate rapidly.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
qs.e:
The LPG reforms of 1991 did open India to FDI and foreign portfolio investment, so A is true.
The reforms were driven by a balance-of-payments crisis and the need for foreign capital and efficiency, not a goal of rapidly raising domestic savings.
So R is not a valid statement of the motive.
Answer: A is true but R is false

qs.q: Why was the Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85) considered successful despite challenges?
o: The economy faced no challenges and grew as expected.
Most targets were met, except agricultural output due to famine.
The plan’s focus was entirely on urban development.
qs.e:
The Sixth Plan (1980–85) targeted 5.2% growth and achieved about 5.7%, so it is rated a success.
Options (a), (c) and (d) are plainly false: there were challenges, industry did not beat targets, and the focus was poverty removal (IRDP, NREP), not urban development.
Option (b) is the only one consistent with 'successful despite challenges', though its 'famine' wording is loose.
Answer: Most targets were met, except agricultural output due to famine.
Note: B agrees with A and key by elimination; growth 5.2% target vs 5.7% actual verified (Wikipedia), but option (b)'s 'famine' premise is not supported by sources.

qs.q: Who among the following administers the oath to the Pro Tem Speaker during the initial sitting of the newly elected Lok Sabha?
qs.e:
The President appoints a senior member as Pro Tem Speaker and personally administers the oath to him/her.
The Pro Tem Speaker then swears in the new members and presides over the Speaker's election.
Answer: President of India

qs.q: Who was the last ruler of the Pallava Dynasty?
qs.e:
Aparajitavarman (c. 880–897 CE) was the last Pallava king.
He was defeated and killed by Aditya I of the Chola dynasty, ending Pallava rule.
Mahendravarman I and Narasimhavarman I were early great rulers; Nandivarman III preceded Nripatunga and Aparajita.
Answer: Aparajitavarman

qs.q: Which of the following is the indirect source to provides information about the interior of the Earth? I. Volcano II. Earthquake
qs.e:
Per NCERT, direct sources are mining, deep drilling and volcanic eruptions (magma reaches the surface).
Indirect sources include seismic waves from earthquakes, gravity, magnetism, meteors and temperature/pressure gradients.
So only earthquake is an indirect source.
Answer: Only II

qs.q: Bundu Khan was a _________ player of Delhi gharana.
qs.e:
Ustad Bundu Khan (1880–1955) was a celebrated sarangi maestro of the Delhi gharana.
He was famed for his virtuosity and later lived in Pakistan.
Answer: sarangi

qs.q: Who is the author of the book 'The Room on the Roof'?
qs.e:
'The Room on the Roof' was Ruskin Bond's first novel, written at 17 and featuring Rusty.
It won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957.
Answer: Ruskin Bond

qs.q: In what ways do Manganiyar and Langas musical traditions reflect the complex interplay of social hierarchy, patronage, and cultural transmission in Rajasthan's folk music landscape?
o: By being independent of any patronage system and performed solely in public festivals

By historically relying on the patronage of Rajput and Muslim elites, these communities preserved and transmitted a rich repertoire of songs praising rulers, deities, and local legends, thus blending diverse cultural influences and sustaining their social identity through music
By exclusively performing classical Hindustani music without any folk elements
By rejecting all traditional instruments and focusing only on vocal performances
qs.e:
Manganiyars and Langas are hereditary Muslim musician communities of western Rajasthan.
They sang for hereditary patrons (jajmans) - Rajputs for Manganiyars, Sindhi Sipahis for Langas.
Their songs mix Hindu and Sufi themes and use kamaicha, sarangi, dholak, khartal, so the other options are false.
Answer: By historically relying on the patronage of Rajput and Muslim elites, these communities preserved and transmitted a rich repertoire of songs praising rulers, deities, and local legends, thus blending diverse cultural influences and sustaining their social identity through music

qs.q: Which traditional dance of Mizoram is performed to celebrate victory in war?
qs.e:
Solakia (Sawlakia) is a Mizoram dance of the Mara and Lai people, originally performed after victory over enemies.
Kodava is from Karnataka (Coorg), Dumhal from Kashmir.
Answer: So Lakia

qs.q: Purulia Chhau dance is associated with which deity?
qs.e:
Chhau (Purulia, Seraikella, Mayurbhanj styles) is performed mainly at the spring Chaitra Parva festival.
Chaitra Parva and the Gajan/Charak celebrations of Chaitra Sankranti are dedicated to Lord Shiva, so the dance is traditionally linked to Shiva worship.
Its stories come from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas, but the festival deity is Shiva.
Answer: Shiva

qs.q: Which of the following is a balcony-like structure in the architecture of Buddhist stupas that represents the abode of Buddha?
qs.e:
The Harmika is the square railed balcony on top of the stupa's dome, seen as the abode of the gods/Buddha.
Anda is the hemispherical dome, Yasti the central mast carrying the chhatras.
Answer: Harmika

qs.q: Fill in the blanks: Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha can empower Parliament to legislate on subjects in the ______ List.
qs.e:
Article 249 lets Rajya Sabha, by a 2/3 resolution of members present and voting, declare a State List matter of national interest.
Parliament can then legislate on it; the resolution lasts one year and can be renewed.
Answer: State

qs.q: Select the correct combination of folk music and its corresponding State/Union Territory.
qs.e:
Chakri is a popular folk music form of Kashmir.
Thumri is a semi-classical form of Uttar Pradesh, Sorathi belongs to Gujarat/Saurashtra, Sohar is a childbirth song of UP/Bihar.
Answer: Chakri – Jammu and Kashmir

qs.q: Boro is a variety of which of the following crops?
qs.e:
Rice in eastern India is grown in three seasons: Aus, Aman and Boro.
Boro is the winter/summer (rabi-season) rice crop of Assam, West Bengal and Bangladesh.
Answer: Rice

qs.q: In any tennis game, any game starts at 0-0 and the zero point in tennis is called ______________.
qs.e:
In tennis scoring, zero is called 'love' (0, 15, 30, 40, game).
A score of 0-0 is read as 'love-all'.
Answer: love

qs.q:
What was the reason for the disruption in the Third five year Plan?
I. Indo-Pakistan Conflict
II. Two successive years of drought
qs.e:
The Third Plan (1961–66) was derailed by the 1962 war with China and the 1965 Indo-Pak war, which diverted resources to defence.
Severe droughts in the mid-1960s (1965 and 1966) crippled farm output and fuelled inflation.
Growth was about 2.4% against a 5.6% target, leading to the Plan Holiday (1966–69).
Answer: Both I and II

qs.q: In a fluid, the buoyant force acting on a submerged or floating object always acts
o: along the direction of motion of the object
in a direction depending on the shape of the object
qs.e:
Buoyancy arises because fluid pressure increases with depth, so the bottom face is pushed harder than the top.
The net force therefore acts vertically upward through the centre of buoyancy, equal to the weight of fluid displaced (Archimedes).
Answer: vertically upward

qs.q: India approached which of the following international financial institutions for balance of payments assistance during the 1991 economic crisis?
o: International Monetary Fund and World Bank
qs.e:
Facing a severe BoP crisis in 1991, India took a loan from the IMF and the World Bank (IBRD).
In return it accepted conditions leading to the New Economic Policy (LPG reforms).
Answer: International Monetary Fund and World Bank

qs.q: In which state is the “Myoko” festival, based on rotating village responsibility for rituals, celebrated?
qs.e:
Myoko is a spring festival of the Apatani tribe of Ziro Valley, Arunachal Pradesh, held in March.
Hosting duties rotate among clusters of Apatani villages each year, celebrating friendship and prosperity.
Answer: Arunachal Pradesh

qs.q: Which of the following correctly matches the sector with the method used to calculate its contribution to national income in India?
qs.e:
India uses a mix of methods sector-wise.
Agriculture, manufacturing and other commodity sectors: product (value-added) method.
Government and services: income method. Construction: expenditure (commodity-flow) method.
Answer: Construction - Expenditure Method

qs.q: Four prime numbers are listed in order. If the product of the first three is 105 and the product of the last three is 385, what is the largest prime number?
qs.e:
105 = 3 × 5 × 7, so the first three primes are 3, 5, 7.
385 = 5 × 7 × 11, so the last three are 5, 7, 11.
The list is 3, 5, 7, 11 and the largest is 11.
Answer: 11

qs.q: A train, (x + 40) m long, passes a pole in 10 seconds and crosses a bridge, (x - 10) m long, in 15 seconds. Find the value of x.
qs.e:
Speed from the pole = (x + 40)/10; speed over the bridge = (x + 40 + x − 10)/15 = (2x + 30)/15.
Equate: 15(x + 40) = 10(2x + 30) → 15x + 600 = 20x + 300 → x = 60.
Check: train 100 m, speed 10 m/s; bridge 50 m, 150 m in 15 s.
Answer: 60

qs.q: In a triangle, if one angle measures twice the smallest angle and the third one measures three times the smallest angle, then the measure of the greatest angle is ______.
qs.e:
Let the smallest angle be x; the angles are x, 2x, 3x.
6x = 180° → x = 30°.
Greatest angle = 3x = 90°.
Answer: 90°

qs.q: Given is the data on the ages of the students of a class. What is the mean age of all the students taken together?
qs.p:
No of Students | Age of the Students
8 | 8
6 | 8
10 | 7
9 | 7
7 | 5

qs.q: An amount of ₹120 is paid using ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2 coins. If the number of coins of ₹10 and ₹2 are interchanged, then the amount becomes ₹304. If the number of ₹5 and ₹2 coins are interchanged, then the amount is ₹165. How many ₹2 coins are used in the payment of ₹120?
qs.e:
Let the counts of ₹10, ₹5, ₹2 coins be a, b, c: 10a + 5b + 2c = 120.
Swap ₹10/₹2: 2a + 5b + 10c = 304; difference gives 8(c − a) = 184 → c = a + 23.
Swap ₹5/₹2: 10a + 2b + 5c = 165; difference gives 3(c − b) = 45 → c = b + 15.
Substitute: 10(c − 23) + 5(c − 15) + 2c = 120 → 17c = 425 → c = 25 (a = 2, b = 10; all three totals check).
Answer: 25

qs.q: There are two circles touching each other externally. The radius of the first circle with centre O is 12 cm. The radius of the second circle with centre A is 5 cm. Find the length of their common tangent touching the two circles at points P and Q.
qs.e:
Externally touching circles: distance between centres = 12 + 5 = 17 cm.
Direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²) = √(289 − 49) = √240 = 4√15 cm.
Answer: 4√15 cm

qs.q: During a sale, 50% of the goods are sold at 37% profit, 30% of the remaining goods are sold at 26% profit and the still remaining goods are sold at a loss of 24%. If there is an overall profit of x%, then what is the value of x?
qs.e:
Take 100 units of cost. 50 units at +37% give profit 18.5.
30% of the remaining 50 = 15 units at +26% give profit 3.9.
The last 35 units at −24% give loss 8.4.
Net profit = 18.5 + 3.9 − 8.4 = 14 on 100, so x = 14.
Answer: 14

qs.q:
Study the pie charts and answer the question that follows. The charts below show the distribution of students in a school.
What is the number of girls in Class 8?
qs.e:
Class 8 = 30% of 600 = 180 students (matches the second chart's total).
Girls = 40% of 180 = 72.
Answer: 72
qs.p:
Pie chart 1 – Class-wise Distribution of Students (Total 600): Class 6 – 20%, Class 7 – 25%, Class 8 – 30%, Class 9 – 15%.
Pie chart 2 – Gender Distribution in Class 8 (Total 180): Boys – 60%, Girls – 40%.

qs.q: In an isosceles triangle ABC, AB=AC. D is a point inside the triangle such that ∠BAD = 20°, ∠DCB= 20°, ∠CAD = 80°. The value of ∠ABC is:
qs.e:
Since D is inside the triangle, ∠BAC = ∠BAD + ∠CAD = 20° + 80° = 100°.
AB = AC, so the base angles are equal: ∠ABC = (180° − 100°)/2 = 40°.
(∠DCB = 20° is not needed.)
Answer: 40°

qs.q:
The given graph represents the data on the ages of various children.
Study the given graph and answer the question that follows.
What is the difference between the mean and mode of the ages?
qs.e:
Total children = 20 + 50 + 70 + 50 + 20 = 210; age sum = 20 + 100 + 210 + 200 + 100 = 630.
Mean = 630/210 = 3 years; mode (highest bar) = 3 years.
Difference = 0 (the distribution is symmetric).
Answer: 0
qs.p: Bar graph – Age distribution of children (Age in years : Number of children): 1 : 20, 2 : 50, 3 : 70, 4 : 50, 5 : 20

qs.q:
Solve the given equations for (x, y, z):
x + y + z = 2
6x - 4y + 5z = 31
5x + 2y + 2z = 13
In the given histogram, what is the mean marks of the students, correct to one decimal place?
qs.p: Histogram – Marks of Students : Number of Students: 0-15 : 8, 15-30 : 14, 30-45 : 28, 45-60 : 30, 60-75 : 32, 75-90 : 16

qs.q: A vertical communication tower stands on a building 30 meters high. From a point 70 meters from the building, the angles of elevation to the top and bottom of the tower are 60° and 30°, respectively. What is the height of the tower (in m)?
qs.e:
Use the stated building height (30 m) and the 60° angle to the tower top from 70 m.
Top of tower above ground = 70 tan 60° = 70√3 m.
Tower height = 70√3 − 30 ≈ 91.2 m.
Note: the 30° angle to the tower foot does not fit (it would make the building 70/√3 ≈ 40.4 m and the tower 140/√3 ≈ 80.8 m, which is not an option), so it is set aside.
Answer: 70√3 - 30
Note: B agrees with A and key (a) but downgrades to check: recalled data self-inconsistent (30° from 70 m gives building ≈40.4 m, not 30 m). Only the reading 'building = 30 m, top at 60°' reaches an option; the 30°-based reading gives 140/√3 ≈ 80.8 m, matching none. Kept (a) with the 30° datum treated as contradictory.

qs.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are in the ratio 3 : 4, and the length of each side of the rhombus is 25 cm. The tiler covering the rhombus-shaped floor needs its area before ordering the tiles. Find the area of the rhombus.
qs.e:
Let the diagonals be 3k and 4k; half-diagonals 1.5k and 2k are legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse 25.
√(2.25k² + 4k²) = 2.5k = 25 → k = 10, diagonals 30 and 40 cm.
Area = ½ × 30 × 40 = 600 cm².
Answer: 600 cm²

qs.q: A regular octagonal fountain has a circumradius of 10 m. Find the approximate length of each side.
qs.e:
Each side subtends 360°/8 = 45° at the centre.
Side = 2R sin 22.5° = 20 × 0.3827 ≈ 7.65 m.
Answer: 7.65 m

qs.q: If sin P = 5/13 and cos Q = 12/13, find sin P cos Q + cos P sin Q :
qs.e:
Taking acute angles: cos P = 12/13 and sin Q = 5/13.
sin P cos Q = 60/169 and cos P sin Q = 60/169.
Sum = 120/169.
Answer: 120/169

qs.q: Find the value of m which satisfies (23/8)¹² × (8/23)¹⁵ × (23/8)⁹ = (8/23)^(8m+8)
If tan A = 3, find the values of sin A and cos A.
qs.e:
tan A = 3/1: opposite 3, adjacent 1, hypotenuse √(9 + 1) = √10.
sin A = 3/√10, cos A = 1/√10 (their ratio is 3, as required).
Answer: sin A = 3/√10, cos A = 1/√10

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers a fixed discount of 15% on rice and 100 gm rice free with every purchase of 1.9 kg rice. Find the overall discount percent offered by him on rice.
qs.e:
Let the marked price be ₹1 per kg. The customer gets 2 kg (worth ₹2) but pays for 1.9 kg at 85%: 1.9 × 0.85 = ₹1.615.
Discount = (2 − 1.615)/2 × 100 = 19.25%.
(Equivalently, successive discounts of 15% and 5%: 15 + 5 − 0.75 = 19.25%.)
Answer: 19.25%

qs.q: A solid hemispherical block is melted and recast into a cone of the same radius. The height of the cone is what fraction of the radius of the hemisphere?
qs.e:
Volumes are equal: (2/3)πr³ = (1/3)πr²h.
So h = 2r, i.e. the height is 2/1 of the radius.
Answer: 2/1

qs.q: Amit is standing on the ground and flying a kite using a 100 m long string at an angle of elevation of 30°. Nitin is standing on the roof of a building that is 10 m high and flying his kite at an angle of elevation of 45°. The two boys are standing on opposite sides of the point where the kites meet. Find the length (in m) of the string that Nitin must use so that both kites meet at the same point.
qs.e:
Kite height = 100 sin 30° = 50 m above the ground.
Nitin is at 10 m, so the kite is 40 m above him.
String = 40/sin 45° = 40√2 m.
Answer: 40√2

qs.q: If a + 1/a = 3, then find the value of a⁶ + 1/a⁶
Find the area of a minor sector of a circle whose circumference is 88 cm and the length of its minor arc is 22 cm (use π = 22/7).
qs.e:
2πr = 88 → r = 14 cm; circle area = (22/7) × 196 = 616 cm².
Arc is 22/88 = 1/4 of the circumference, so the sector is 1/4 of the area.
Sector area = 616/4 = 154 cm².
Answer: 154 cm²

qs.q: If the number of sides of a regular polygon is 12, then the measure of each exterior angle is:
qs.e:
Exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°.
Each exterior angle = 360°/12 = 30°.
Answer: 30°

qs.q:
Which of the following pairs of words can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?
The ____ sorcerer upturned the ____ of poison into the goblet, his lips curling into a smirk.
qs.e:
The first blank needs an adjective describing the sorcerer: 'vile' means wicked or evil.
The second blank needs a container for poison: a 'vial' is a small glass bottle.
'Veil' (a covering) and 'vail' (to lower) do not fit either slot.
Answer: vile, vial

qs.q:
Out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.
Ensconce
qs.e:
'Ensconce' means to settle somewhere snugly or to hide something away securely.
The opposite idea is to expose or bring into view, which is 'unveil'.
'Establish' is close in meaning; 'impudence' and 'request' are unrelated.
Answer: Unveil

qs.q:
Examine the given sentence and pick out the error.
In order to overcome the mental depression and stress (1) adapting meditation, yoga or (2) similar other methods (3) can be helped
o: in order to overcome the mental depression and stress
qs.e:
The subject 'adopting meditation, yoga or similar methods' is what does the helping, so the verb must be active.
'Can be helped' wrongly makes the subject the receiver of help; it should read 'can help'.
This is the error the question targets.
Answer: can be helped
Note: B agrees with A and key (b). Kept check: part (a) also has 'adapting' (should be 'adopting') and 'similar other' is redundant; (b) is the intended error.

qs.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
qs.e:
The word is built as sub + compartment + al + ization.
(b) adds an extra 'e', (c) swaps 'ar' to 'ra' in 'compartment', and (d) drops the 'a' in '-ization'.
Only (a) is spelt correctly.
Answer: subcompartmentalization

qs.q:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The professor admitted that he had never delivered a lecture on that particular topic in any of his classes.
o: The professor said, "I've never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes."
The professor admitted, "I'd never delivered a lecture on that particular topic in any class."
The professor admitted, "I have not deliver a lecture on that particular topic in any of my classes."
The professor said, "I have never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in none of my classes."
qs.e:
Going back to direct speech, the past perfect 'had never delivered' becomes present perfect 'have never delivered'.
'That' becomes 'this' and 'his' becomes 'my'.
(b) keeps past perfect and 'that'; (c) has 'have not deliver'; (d) uses a double negative 'never ... none'.
Answer: The professor said, "I've never delivered a lecture on this particular topic in any of my classes."

qs.q:
From the given alternatives, select the correct direct narration of the given indirect narration.
Sanvi told Prakash that the coach had announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields.
o: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach is announcing that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would have been cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelling for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."
qs.e:
'Told' becomes 'said to', and the past perfect 'had announced' moves back to simple past 'announced'.
The inner clause 'practice would be cancelled' stays as it is inside the quoted report.
(a) uses a continuous tense, (b) wrongly adds 'have been', (d) uses the active 'cancelling'.
Answer: Sanvi said to Prakash, "The coach announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week due to the flooded condition of the playing fields."

qs.q:
Find the word most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to the given word:
Prolific
qs.e:
'Prolific' means producing a great deal, highly productive.
'Fruitful' carries the same sense of abundant output.
'Barren' is the opposite; 'furtive' means secretive and 'amiable' means friendly.
Answer: Fruitful

qs.q:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:
'A speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly'.
qs.e:
An 'encomium' is a formal expression of high praise in speech or writing.
An elegy mourns the dead, a sermon is a religious talk, and a soliloquy is speaking one's thoughts alone.
Answer: Encomium

qs.q:
Find the word most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to the given word:
Obstreperous
qs.e:
'Obstreperous' describes someone noisy and hard to control.
'Unruly' means disorderly and difficult to manage, so it matches.
'Docile' is the opposite; 'prudent' means careful and 'ambivalent' means having mixed feelings.
Answer: Unruly

qs.q:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. This shift is driven by the fact that electric vehicles produce lower emissions compared to conventional cars.
B. Moreover, advances in battery technology have improved driving range and reduced costs.
C. Therefore, governments are incentivizing EV adoption through subsidies and tax benefits.
D. Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming a major component of sustainable transportation worldwide.
qs.e:
D introduces the topic and spells out the abbreviation EVs, so it opens.
A refers to 'this shift' described in D and gives the first reason.
B adds a further reason with 'Moreover'.
C draws the conclusion with 'Therefore'.
Answer: D – A – B – C

qs.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank 1.
qs.e:
The passage says misinformation threatens informed discourse, so it must exist in huge quantity.
'Deluge' means a flood or overwhelming amount.
'Dearth', 'paucity' and 'modicum' all suggest scarcity, which contradicts the context.
Answer: deluge
qs.p:
Directions (86-90): In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
The digital revolution, for all its emancipatory promise, has spawned a (1)________ of misinformation that threatens the very foundations of informed discourse. Algorithms engineered to maximise engagement tend to privilege sensational content over sober analysis, thereby creating echo chambers in which pre-existing prejudices are relentlessly reinforced. Falsehoods, often cloaked in a veneer of authority, propagate with a speed that verified facts can seldom match.
What makes this phenomenon particularly (2)________ is its subtlety. Unlike overt propaganda, which audiences can readily identify and resist, modern disinformation masquerades as ordinary opinion, insinuating itself into conversations with deceptive ease. Even discerning readers occasionally find themselves unwittingly sharing claims that later prove to be entirely (3)________.
Regulators face a formidable dilemma. Heavy-handed censorship risks (4)________ the freedom of expression that democratic societies hold sacrosanct, whereas excessive leniency allows pernicious narratives to flourish unchecked. Technology companies, for their part, have been accused of equivocating, professing a commitment to truth while profiting handsomely from the very outrage they claim to deplore.
A durable solution, experts contend, must be multifaceted. Media literacy should be embedded in school curricula, enabling young citizens to scrutinise sources and detect manipulation. Simultaneously, platforms must be held accountable for the opaque architecture of their algorithms. Ultimately, however, the (5)________ of truth rests with each individual, for no regulatory framework can wholly substitute for a sceptical and inquisitive mind.

qs.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank 2.
qs.e:
The danger lies in the phenomenon's subtlety, i.e. it causes harm gradually and unnoticed.
'Insidious' means exactly that: harmful in a stealthy way.
'Benign', 'innocuous' and 'salubrious' all suggest harmlessness or health.
Answer: insidious

qs.q:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.
The children are playing ______ the garden ______ their friends.
qs.e:
An enclosed area like a garden takes 'in' for location.
Companionship is shown with 'with': playing with their friends.
'Into' shows motion, and 'among' or 'for' do not fit the second slot.
Answer: in, with

qs.q:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
Take a pair of binoculars with you lest you all should miss the chance of looking at the distant scenes.
o: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes would missed by you all.
Let a pair of binoculars taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.
Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you otherwise the chance of looking at the distant scenes would be missed by you all.
Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.
qs.e:
An imperative becomes passive with 'Let + object + be + past participle': 'Let a pair of binoculars be taken'.
The 'lest' clause keeps 'should' and becomes 'should be missed by you all'.
(a) misses 'be' and uses 'would', (b) drops 'be', (c) replaces 'lest' with 'otherwise'.
Answer: Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you lest the chance of looking at the distant scenes should be missed by you all.

qs.q:
Choose the best option to fill in the blank below.
This is ____ biryani I have had in a year. It is almost ____ the one from Nizam's House in Hyderabad.
qs.e:
Comparing with all biryanis eaten in a year needs the superlative 'the best'.
Comparing equality with one other biryani needs 'as good as'.
'Gooder' is not a word and 'the better' needs exactly two items.
Answer: the best, as good as

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom "Open the floodgates."
o: To release something that was previously under control
qs.e:
Opening floodgates lets held-back water pour out.
Figuratively it means suddenly allowing something that was restrained to happen on a large scale.
Answer: To release something that was previously under control

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom "To square the circle."
qs.e:
Constructing a square with exactly the same area as a given circle is a classic geometric impossibility.
So the idiom means trying to do something that cannot be done.
Answer: To attempt something impossible

qs.q:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.
The construction of the skyscraper is scheduled to have been completed by the end of the year.
o: The skyscraper will have completed the construction by the end of the year.
They are scheduling to have completed the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.
The construction of the skyscraper will be completed by the end of the year.
They are scheduled to complete the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.
qs.e:
The agent of the passive is unstated, so 'They' is supplied as subject.
'Is scheduled' stays passive in form ('are scheduled'), and the infinitive becomes active: 'to complete the construction'.
(a) makes the skyscraper the doer, (b) wrongly uses 'are scheduling', and (c) is still passive.
Answer: They are scheduled to complete the construction of the skyscraper by the end of the year.

qs.q:
Identify the incorrectly spelt word in the sentence and rectify it.
During the preliminary reconnnaissance of the floodplain, the geologists catalogued subterranean fissures and recommended immediate remediation.
qs.e:
The sentence spells it 'reconnnaissance', with three n's together.
The correct form is 'reconnaissance' (one c, double n, double s).
The other options are misspellings of words that are already spelt correctly in the sentence.
Answer: reconnaissance

qs.q:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The child requested his mother to gave him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat.
o: The child requested his mother to
gave him a big chocolate because he
had been very good all day
qs.e:
After 'to', the infinitive takes the base form of the verb.
'To gave' should be 'to give'.
The rest of the sentence is grammatical.
Answer: gave him a big chocolate because he

qs.q:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.
Pari said to Nirvaan, "He admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company."
o: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.
Pari told Nirvaan that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.
Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.
Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invested all his money in that risky startup company.
qs.e:
'Said to' becomes 'told', and the simple past 'admitted' shifts to 'had admitted'.
The already past-perfect 'had made' stays unchanged, and 'to invest' keeps its base form.
(b) drops 'admitted', (c) wrongly changes 'had made' to 'made', (d) has 'to invested'.
Answer: Pari told Nirvaan that he had admitted that he had made a huge mistake in judgment when he decided to invest all his money in that risky startup company.

qs.q:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. As part of this transformation, AI-powered tools can now detect diseases like cancer at much earlier stages than traditional methods.
B. Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming the healthcare industry.
C. Because of this ability, the technology also helps doctors personalize treatment plans based on patient data.
D. However, despite these advantages, concerns about data privacy and ethical use remain significant challenges.
qs.e:
B introduces the theme of AI transforming healthcare.
A follows with 'this transformation' and gives early disease detection.
C builds on 'this ability' with personalised treatment.
D closes with 'However' and the challenges.
Answer: BACD

qs.q:
Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid and choose the correct option.
Statement:
Regular meditation and mindfulness practices among corporate employees lead to improved concentration, reduced burnout, and positively affect overall workplace productivity.
Assumptions:
I. Mindfulness practices influence the psychological state of employees.
II. Reduced burnout has no correlation with workplace productivity.
III. Improved concentration contributes to better performance at work.
o: Only I and II are implicit
Only II and III are implicit
Only I and III are implicit
qs.e:
Saying mindfulness improves concentration and reduces burnout presumes it acts on employees' mental state, so I is implicit.
Linking better concentration to higher productivity presumes concentration helps work performance, so III is implicit.
II contradicts the statement, which ties reduced burnout to productivity.
Answer: Only I and III are implicit

qs.q: In how many years will Rs. 8000 grow to Rs. 14400 at 10% Simple Interest?
qs.e:
Interest needed = 14400 − 8000 = Rs. 6400.
Yearly interest = 10% of 8000 = Rs. 800.
Time = 6400 ÷ 800 = 8 years.
Answer: 8 years

qs.q:
After interchanging the given two numbers (not digits), what will be the value of the given equation?
8 and 5
6 × 8 + 5 - 12 ÷ 4 = ?
qs.e:
Swapping 8 and 5 gives 6 × 5 + 8 − 12 ÷ 4.
By BODMAS: 30 + 8 − 3 = 35.
Answer: 35

qs.q:
What should come in place of '?' in the given series?
15, 23, 38, 61, 99, 160, ?
qs.e:
Each term is the sum of the two before it: 15 + 23 = 38, 23 + 38 = 61, 38 + 61 = 99, 61 + 99 = 160.
Next = 99 + 160 = 259.
Answer: 259

qs.q:
You are given a Master Address (MA) from official records. Your task is to identify the correct candidate address that matches exactly with the master address in terms of formatting, punctuation, spelling, and structure.

Flat No 4B, Sunrise Apartments, M.G. Road, Pune - 411001
Flat No. 4B, Sunrise Apartments, M.G. Road, Pune - 411001
qs.e:
(a) adds a space in 'M. G.'.
(b) misspells 'Apartments' as 'Appartment'.
(c) drops the full stop after 'No'.
(d) matches the master address exactly.
Answer: Flat No. 4B, Sunrise Apartments, M.G. Road, Pune - 411001

qs.q: In a certain coded language 'GRASP' is coded as 'ITCUR' and 'LOGIC' is coded as 'NQIKE'. How will 'BRAIN' be coded in the same code language?
qs.e:
Each letter moves forward 2: G→I, R→T, A→C, S→U, P→R; L→N, O→Q, G→I, I→K, C→E.
BRAIN: B→D, R→T, A→C, I→K, N→P.
Answer: DTCKP

qs.q: A person walks 8 km towards the east, then turns to his left and walks 6 km. He then turns to his left again and walks 8 km. In which direction is he now facing?
qs.e:
Start facing East; a left turn makes him face North.
A second left turn makes him face West, and he keeps walking that way.
Answer: West

qs.q: Identify the reference code that does NOT use only prime digits.
qs.e:
The prime digits are 2, 3, 5 and 7.
2357, 7532 and 5723 use only these.
3957 contains 9, which is not prime.
Answer: 3957W

qs.q:
In a certain code language,
P # Q means 'P is the daughter of Q',
P $ Q means 'P is the husband of Q',
P * Q means 'P is the brother of Q' and
P % Q means 'P is the mother of Q'.
How is A related to E if 'A * B # C $ D % E'?
qs.e:
A * B: A is B's brother. B # C: B is C's daughter. C $ D: C is D's husband.
D % E: D is E's mother, so E is also a child of C and D.
A is a male child of the same parents, so A is E's brother.
Answer: Brother

qs.q:
Consider the given statement(s) and decide which of the given assumption(s) is/are implicit in the statement;
Statement: "Drinking at least 2 liters of water daily is essential for maintaining good health and proper kidney function."
Assumptions:
I. People are generally concerned about maintaining good health.
II. Water consumption has a direct biological effect on kidney function.
o: Both I and II are implicit.
Neither I nor II is implicit.
qs.e:
Calling water intake essential for kidney function takes for granted that water directly affects the kidneys, so II is implicit.
The statement is advice aimed at people, made on the premise that they care about staying healthy, so I is implicit too.
Answer: Both I and II are implicit.
Note: Agrees with key (a). I is the softer of the two (the statement could be read as a bare health fact), but in SSC statement-assumption items the premise that the audience cares about the stated benefit is treated as implicit in advice like this.

qs.q:
Consider the given statement(s) and decide which of the given assumption(s) is/are implicit in the statement.
Statement:
The company has decided to offer flexible working hours to all its employees starting next month.
Assumptions:
I. Employees prefer having control over their work schedules.
II. Flexible working hours will lead to a decrease in overall productivity.
o: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
qs.e:
A company offers flexible hours expecting employees to value control over their schedules, so I is implicit.
No company would adopt a policy it assumes will cut productivity, so II is not implicit.
Answer: Only I is implicit

qs.q:
Statement: P > Q ≥ R = S < T ≤ U
Conclusions:
I. P > S
II. Q < U
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
qs.e:
I: P > Q ≥ R = S gives P > S; I is true.
II: Q ≥ R = S < T ≤ U — the sign flips at S, so Q and U cannot be compared; II is false.
Answer: Only I is true
qs.p: In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions. Find out which conclusion is true based on the given statement.

qs.q:
Find the next term in the following series.
144, 133, 120, 105, 88, ?
qs.e:
Differences are −11, −13, −15, −17, so the next is −19.
88 − 19 = 69.
Answer: 69

qs.q:
Consider the argument and decide which of the given assumptions is/are implicit Argument:
The municipal corporation has decided to double the parking fees in the city center to reduce traffic congestion.
Assumptions:
1. People may prefer to use public transport or carpool due to higher parking fees.
2. The number of vehicles entering the city center will remain entirely unaffected by the fee hike.
qs.e:
Raising fees to cut congestion presumes some drivers will switch to public transport or carpooling, so 1 is implicit.
If vehicle numbers stayed unaffected, the move could not reduce congestion, so 2 contradicts the decision.
Answer: Only assumption 1 is implicit.

qs.q:
In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions. Find out which conclusion is true based on the given statement.
Statement: S = T < U ≤ V > W
Conclusions:
I. T < W
II. S < V
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
qs.e:
I: T < U ≤ V > W — the sign flips at V, so T and W cannot be compared; I is false.
II: S = T < U ≤ V gives S < V; II is true.
Answer: Only II is true

qs.q: In which Indian state is the Bihu festival celebrated, and what does it primarily mark?
o: Punjab - To mark the beginning of the winter harvest
Assam - To mark the change of seasons and agricultural cycles
Odisha - To celebrate the chariot festival of Lord Jagannath
Kerala - To celebrate the boat races and harvest season
qs.e:
Bihu is the main festival of Assam, celebrated three times a year.
Rongali (Bohag) Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and sowing season, Kongali (Kati) Bihu the growing crop, and Bhogali (Magh) Bihu the harvest.
So it is tied to the change of seasons and the farming cycle. Lohri is Punjab's, Rath Yatra Odisha's, Onam/boat races Kerala's.
Answer: Assam - To mark the change of seasons and agricultural cycles

qs.q: In a standard marathon race, what is the official distance covered by the athletes?
qs.e:
The official marathon distance, fixed by World Athletics, is 42.195 km (about 26.2 miles).
13.1 miles (21.0975 km) is a half marathon.
Answer: 26.2 miles (42.195 km)

qs.q: Legendary musician Ustad Bismillah Khan was famously associated with which musical instrument?
qs.e:
Ustad Bismillah Khan of Varanasi made the shehnai a concert instrument.
He played the shehnai at the Red Fort on 15 August 1947 and received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.
Answer: Shehnai

qs.q: India shares a maritime boundary with which one of the following countries across the Indian Ocean (southwest of India)?
qs.e:
India's maritime neighbours are Pakistan, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia.
The Maldives lies south-west of India, beyond Lakshadweep across the Eight Degree Channel.
Myanmar and Thailand border India's sea area on the east (Andaman Sea), not the south-west; Oman has no maritime boundary with India.
Answer: Maldives

qs.q:
Read the following statements carefully and choose the correct option regarding Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Green Revolution in India significantly increased the production of food grains, especially wheat and rice.
Reason (R): It involved the introduction of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, improved irrigation, and extensive use of fertilizers.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
qs.e:
The Green Revolution (from the mid-1960s) sharply raised foodgrain output, mainly wheat and later rice, so A is true.
Its package was HYV seeds plus assured irrigation, chemical fertilisers and pesticides, so R is true.
That package is exactly what raised yields, so R explains A.
Answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

qs.q: What was the primary focus of the First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) in India?
qs.e:
The First Plan (1951–56), based on the Harrod–Domar model, gave top priority to agriculture, irrigation and power (e.g. Bhakra-Nangal, Hirakud).
Heavy industry was the focus of the Second Plan (Mahalanobis model); poverty removal and self-reliance were themes of the Fifth Plan.
Answer: Agriculture, irrigation, and power projects

qs.q: Who among the following administers the oath of office to the President of India?
qs.e:
Under Article 60, the President takes the oath before the Chief Justice of India.
In the CJI's absence, the senior-most available judge of the Supreme Court administers it.
Answer: Chief Justice of India

qs.q: Who is considered the founder of the Mauryan Empire?
qs.e:
Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya (Kautilya), overthrew the Nanda dynasty around 322 BCE and founded the Mauryan Empire.
Bindusara was his son and Ashoka his grandson; Bimbisara was a Haryanka king of Magadha.
Answer: Chandragupta Maurya

qs.q:
Which of the following is a direct source of information about the interior of the Earth?
I. Volcanic eruptions
II. Seismic waves (Earthquakes)
qs.e:
Per NCERT, direct sources are surface rocks, mining, deep drilling and volcanic eruptions (magma brought up from inside).
Seismic waves from earthquakes are an indirect source, studied along with gravity, magnetism and meteors.
So only volcanic eruptions are a direct source.
Answer: Only I

qs.q: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a globally renowned maestro of which Indian classical instrument?
qs.e:
Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is India's best-known bansuri (bamboo flute) player in the Hindustani tradition.
He received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000.
Answer: Flute (Bansuri)

qs.q: Who is the author of the famous collection of short stories titled 'Malgudi Days'?
qs.e:
'Malgudi Days' (1943) is a collection of short stories by R. K. Narayan, set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi.
Ruskin Bond wrote 'The Room on the Roof', Mulk Raj Anand 'Untouchable', Khushwant Singh 'Train to Pakistan'.
Answer: R. K. Narayan

qs.q: The Baul tradition, known for its mystic minstrelsy and soulful philosophy blending Vaishnavism and Sufism, is prominently found in which region?
qs.e:
The Bauls are wandering mystic singers of Bengal (West Bengal and Bangladesh); Lalon Fakir is the best-known Baul.
Their songs mix Vaishnava bhakti and Sufi ideas, and UNESCO listed Baul songs as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2005 (inscribed 2008).
Answer: Bengal

qs.q: Cheraw, a traditional cultural dance featuring the rhythmic clapping of bamboo staves, is performed in which Indian state?
qs.e:
Cheraw, the 'bamboo dance', is a traditional dance of Mizoram.
Men clap pairs of long bamboo staves in rhythm while women dance in and out between them.
Answer: Mizoram

qs.q: The classical dance form 'Sattriya' was introduced by the great Vaishnava saint Sankaradeva. This dance form is deeply associated with devotion to which deity?
qs.e:
Sattriya was created by Srimanta Sankaradeva in 15th–16th century Assam and kept alive in the Vaishnava monasteries (sattras).
Its themes come from the life and stories of Krishna, an avatar of Vishnu.
Answer: Krishna (Vishnu)

qs.q: In the architecture of Buddhist stupas, what is the term used for the umbrella-like structure placed at the very top, representing the Three Jewels of Buddhism?
qs.e:
The chhatra (often a triple umbrella, chhatravali) on the central mast (yasti) crowns the stupa; its three tiers are read as the Three Jewels: Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha.
Anda is the dome, Harmika the railed balcony on top of the dome, Vedika the railing around the stupa.
Answer: Chhatra

qs.q: Fill in the blanks: Under Article 312 of the Indian Constitution, the Rajya Sabha has the exclusive power to authorize the Parliament to create new ______.
qs.e:
Article 312 lets Parliament create new All-India Services if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting.
This is a special power of the Rajya Sabha (like Article 249 for State List subjects).
Answer: All-India Services

qs.q: Select the correct combination of folk dance/music and its corresponding State.
qs.e:
Rouf is a folk dance performed by Kashmiri women, especially at Eid and harvest time.
Lavani belongs to Maharashtra, Garba to Gujarat, and Bihu to Assam.
Answer: Rouf - Jammu and Kashmir

qs.q: Which of the following is primarily a Kharif crop in India?
qs.e:
Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon (June–July) and harvested in autumn: rice, maize, cotton, jowar, groundnut, etc.
Wheat, mustard and barley are rabi (winter) crops.
Answer: Cotton

qs.q: In cricket, what does the term "LBW" stand for?
qs.e:
LBW = Leg Before Wicket: a batter is out if the ball, which would have hit the stumps, is stopped by the body (usually the leg) rather than the bat, subject to the line rules.
Answer: Leg Before Wicket

qs.q: What was the main reason behind the declaration of 'Plan Holiday' (1966-1969) in India?
o: Severe drought and the aftermath of the Indo-Pak war (1965)
qs.e:
The Third Plan (1961–66) failed after the 1962 China war, the 1965 Indo-Pak war and the severe droughts of 1965–66.
With prices rising and resources drained, the Fourth Plan was postponed and three Annual Plans (1966–69) were run instead: the 'Plan Holiday'.
Answer: Severe drought and the aftermath of the Indo-Pak war (1965)

qs.q: Frictional force always acts:
o: perpendicular to the direction of motion
opposite to the direction of relative motion
qs.e:
Friction acts along the contact surface and opposes the relative motion (or tendency of relative motion) between the two surfaces in contact.
Answer: opposite to the direction of relative motion

qs.q: Which international institution is primarily known as the "lender of last resort" for countries facing severe balance of payments crises?
qs.e:
The IMF lends to member countries facing balance-of-payments crises, acting as the international lender of last resort (e.g. India in 1991).
The World Bank and ADB fund development projects; the WTO regulates trade.
Answer: International Monetary Fund (IMF)

qs.q: In which state is the famous "Hornbill Festival" celebrated annually to showcase the rich cultural heritage of its indigenous tribes?
qs.e:
The Hornbill Festival is held every year from 1 to 10 December at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, Nagaland.
It brings together all of Nagaland's tribes and is called the 'Festival of Festivals'.
Answer: Nagaland

qs.q: Which method is NOT typically used to calculate the National Income of a country?
qs.e:
National income is measured by three methods: the product (value added) method, the income method and the expenditure method.
Subsidies are only an adjustment (e.g. moving between market price and factor cost), not a method.
Answer: Subsidies Method

qs.q: Four distinct prime numbers are listed in ascending order. If the product of the first three is 385 and the product of the last three is 1001, what is the largest prime number among them?
qs.e:
385 = 5 × 7 × 11 and 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13.
The common middle primes are 7 and 11, so the four primes are 5, 7, 11, 13.
Largest prime = 13.
Answer: 13

qs.q: In a triangle, if the angles are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4, what is the measure of the largest angle?
qs.e:
Angles are 2k, 3k, 4k with 9k = 180°, so k = 20°.
Largest angle = 4 × 20° = 80°.
Answer: 80°

qs.q: Given is the data on the ages of the students in a club. What is the mean age of all the students taken together?
qs.p:
No of Students | Age of the Students
5 | 12
8 | 13
4 | 14
3 | 15

qs.q: There are two circles touching each other externally. The radius of the first circle is 16 cm and the radius of the second circle is 9 cm. Find the length of their direct common tangent.
qs.e:
For circles touching externally, d = r₁ + r₂ = 25 cm.
Direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²) = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 cm (also 2√(r₁r₂) = 2√144).
Answer: 24 cm

qs.q: A shopkeeper buys an article. He sells one-third of it at a 15% profit, one-fourth at a 20% profit, and the rest at a 24% profit. What is his overall profit percentage?

Study the pie charts and answer the question that follows. The charts below show the distribution of employees in a company across various departments and the gender distribution in the IT department.
What is the number of female employees in the IT department?
qs.e:
IT employees = 25% of 800 = 200.
Female in IT = 40% of 200 = 80.
Answer: 80
qs.p:
Pie chart 1 – Department Distribution (Total: 800): IT 25%, HR 30%, Sales 20%, Ops 25%.
Pie chart 2 – Gender Distribution in IT Dept: Male 60%, Female 40%.

qs.q: In an isosceles triangle ABC, AB = AC. The vertex angle ∠A is 40°. What is the measure of the base angle ∠B?

The given graph represents the data on the ages of various children in a community program. Study the graph and answer the question that follows.
What is the difference between the mean and mode of the ages? (Total children = 20)
qs.p: Bar graph – Age (in years) : Number of children: 10 : 2, 11 : 4, 12 : 7, 13 : 5, 14 : 2

qs.q: In the given histogram, what is the mean marks of the students, correct to one decimal place?
qs.p: Histogram – Marks of Students : Number of Students: 0-10 : 5, 10-20 : 10, 20-30 : 20, 30-40 : 15

qs.q:
Study the information given in the graph below and answer the following question based on it.
If the net availability of food grains is only 80% of the total food production of the country, then what was the population of the country in the year 2010? [Correct your answer to the nearest 10 million]
qs.e:
2010: production = 144 million tonnes; availability per person = 144 kg.
Net availability = 80% of 144 = 115.2 million tonnes = 115.2 × 10⁹ kg.
Population = 115.2 × 10⁹ / 144 = 0.8 × 10⁹ = 800 million.
Answer: 800 million
qs.p:
Line graph – Food production (million tonnes): 1990 : 100, 2000 : 122, 2010 : 144, 2020 : 166.
Annual food availability per person (kg): 1990 : 110, 2000 : 120, 2010 : 144, 2020 : 160.

qs.q: A vertical communication tower stands on top of a building 40 meters high. From a point 40 meters from the base of the building, the angle of elevation to the top of the tower is 60°. What is the height of the tower (in m)?
qs.e:
Height of tower top = 40 × tan 60° = 40√3 m.
Tower height = 40√3 − 40 = 40(√3 − 1) m.
Answer: 40(√3 − 1)

qs.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are in the ratio 3 : 4, and its perimeter is 40 cm. Find the area of the rhombus.
qs.e:
Side = 40/4 = 10 cm. Let diagonals be 6k and 8k; half-diagonals 3k and 4k.
(3k)² + (4k)² = 10² → 5k = 10 → k = 2, so diagonals are 12 cm and 16 cm.
Area = (12 × 16)/2 = 96 cm².
Answer: 96 cm²

qs.q: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 14 cm. Find the perimeter of the hexagon.
qs.e:
A regular hexagon inscribed in a circle has side equal to the radius = 14 cm.
Perimeter = 6 × 14 = 84 cm.
Answer: 84 cm

qs.q: If sin θ = 8/17 and cos φ = 15/17, both in the first quadrant, find the value of sin(θ + φ).
qs.e:
cos θ = 15/17 and sin φ = 8/17 (first quadrant).
sin(θ + φ) = sin θ cos φ + cos θ sin φ = (8×15 + 15×8)/289 = 240/289.
Answer: 240/289

qs.q: Find the value of x which satisfies 2ˣ⁺³ + 2ˣ⁺¹ = 320.
If cot A = 2, find the value of (5 sin A + 3 cos A)/(5 sin A − 3 cos A).
qs.e:
Divide numerator and denominator by sin A: (5 + 3 cot A)/(5 − 3 cot A).
= (5 + 6)/(5 − 6) = 11/(−1) = −11.
Answer: −11

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers a discount of 20% on the marked price of a shirt and still makes a profit of 25%. If the cost price of the shirt is ₹640, what is the marked price?
A solid metallic cylinder of base radius 6 cm and height 12 cm is melted and recast into a solid cone of the same base radius. Find the height of the cone.
qs.e:
Volumes equal: πr² × 12 = (1/3)πr² × h.
h = 3 × 12 = 36 cm.
Answer: 36 cm

qs.q: Two vertical poles of heights 15 m and 25 m are standing on a level ground. If the distance between their bases is 24 m, find the distance between their tops.
qs.e:
Difference in heights = 25 − 15 = 10 m; horizontal gap = 24 m.
Distance between tops = √(24² + 10²) = √676 = 26 m.
Answer: 26 m

qs.q: If x/y + y/x = 2, find the value of x³ + y³.
qs.e:
x/y + y/x = 2 → x² + y² = 2xy → (x − y)² = 0, so x = y.
x³ + y³ = x³ + x³ = 2x³.
Answer: 2x³

qs.q: Find the area of a sector of a circle with a radius of 7 cm if the angle of the sector is 120°. (use π = 22/7).
The sum of interior angles of a regular polygon is 1440°. Find the number of sides of the polygon.
qs.e:
Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180° = 1440°.
n − 2 = 8, so n = 10.
Answer: 10

qs.q:
Which of the following pairs of words can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?
The knight engaged in a fierce ______ to defend his honor, knowing it would serve a ______ purpose for his king.
qs.e:
'Duel' is a fight between two people, so a knight engages in a fierce duel.
'Dual' means double or two-fold, so the fight serves a dual purpose.
Answer: duel, dual

qs.q:
Out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.
ALLEVIATE
qs.e:
Alleviate means to make pain or a problem less severe.
Lessen, mitigate and pacify all point the same way (synonyms).
Aggravate means to make worse, the opposite.
Answer: Aggravate

qs.q:
Examine the given sentence and pick out the error.
He is looking forward (1) to meet his old friends (2) at the college reunion (3) this weekend. (4)
qs.e:
In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it takes a gerund (-ing form).
Correct: 'to meeting his old friends'.
Answer: to meet his old friends

qs.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
qs.e:
The word is built on 'precedent' (p-r-e-c-e-d-e-n-t) with un- and -ed.
The other options add an extra n, double the e, or use s for c.
Answer: Unprecedented

qs.q:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The manager ordered the staff to submit the reports by noon.
o: The manager says to the staff, "Submit the reports by noon."
The manager said to the staff, "Please submit the reports by noon."
The manager said to the staff, "Submit the reports by noon!"
The manager ordered, "The staff must submit the reports by noon."
qs.e:
'Ordered ... to submit' is an indirect command, so the direct form is an imperative in past reporting: said to the staff, "Submit ...".
(a) uses present 'says'; (b) adds 'Please', which signals a request, not an order; (d) is not an imperative addressed to the staff.
The exclamation mark carries the force of the order.
Answer: The manager said to the staff, "Submit the reports by noon!"

qs.q:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.
Rahul said to me, "Are you going to the market today?"
o: Rahul asked me if I was going to the market that day.
Rahul asked me if you were going to the market today.
Rahul told me whether I am going to the market today.
Rahul asked me if I am going to the market that day.
qs.e:
A yes/no question becomes 'asked ... if' in assertive order.
'You' (said to me) becomes 'I'; 'are going' becomes 'was going'; 'today' becomes 'that day'.
Answer: Rahul asked me if I was going to the market that day.

qs.q:
Find the word most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to the given word:
SAGACIOUS
qs.e:
Sagacious means having keen judgement and good sense.
Foolish and ignorant are opposites; bitter is unrelated.
Answer: Wise

qs.q:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:
'A place where coins, medals, or tokens are made'.
qs.e:
A mint is where coins, medals and tokens are struck.
A vault stores valuables, a treasury holds public funds, a repository stores things in general.
Answer: Mint

qs.q:
Find the word most nearly SIMILAR in meaning to the given word:
PERNICIOUS
qs.e:
Pernicious means having a harmful effect, especially gradually or subtly.
Beneficial, healthy and innocent are all opposite in sense.
Answer: Harmful

qs.q:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. Solar and wind power are becoming increasingly cost-competitive with fossil fuels.
B. The transition to renewable energy is critical for combating global warming.
C. Despite this progress, storing energy from these intermittent sources remains a major hurdle.
D. Consequently, many countries are investing heavily in upgrading their energy infrastructure.
qs.e:
B introduces the topic: the transition to renewable energy.
A gives the progress (solar and wind are cost-competitive); C follows with 'Despite this progress' and names the storage hurdle for 'these intermittent sources'.
D ('Consequently ... upgrading their energy infrastructure') is the response to that hurdle and closes the paragraph.
Answer: B - A - C - D
Note: B-check: solved independently; B-A-C-D and B-A-D-C both readable. Kept key (b): C's storage hurdle motivates D's infrastructure upgrade. Memory-based item.

qs.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank 1.
qs.e:
Telemedicine is described as growing rapidly and giving remote access to doctors, so it is an important part of healthcare.
Trivial, obsolete and detrimental are all negative and contradict the passage.
Answer: pivotal
qs.p:
Directions (86-90): In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Telemedicine has emerged as a (1)________ component of modern healthcare, accelerating rapidly due to global health crises. It provides patients with remote access to medical professionals, drastically reducing the (2)________ of travel and physical waiting times. However, the system is not without flaws. A significant (3)________ exists between urban areas with high-speed internet and rural regions where connectivity is scarce. This digital divide threatens to (4)________ existing healthcare inequalities if left unaddressed. To ensure equitable access, policymakers must focus on expanding digital infrastructure, (5)________ telehealth platforms, and training both doctors and patients in using these new tools effectively.

qs.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank 2.
qs.e:
The blank pairs with 'physical waiting times' as something telemedicine drastically reduces.
Only a negative noun fits: reducing the burden of travel.
Answer: burden
qs.p:
Directions (86-90): In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Telemedicine has emerged as a (1)________ component of modern healthcare, accelerating rapidly due to global health crises. It provides patients with remote access to medical professionals, drastically reducing the (2)________ of travel and physical waiting times. However, the system is not without flaws. A significant (3)________ exists between urban areas with high-speed internet and rural regions where connectivity is scarce. This digital divide threatens to (4)________ existing healthcare inequalities if left unaddressed. To ensure equitable access, policymakers must focus on expanding digital infrastructure, (5)________ telehealth platforms, and training both doctors and patients in using these new tools effectively.

qs.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank 3.
qs.e:
The sentence contrasts urban areas with fast internet and rural areas with scarce connectivity, later called a 'digital divide'.
That gap is a disparity.
Answer: disparity
qs.p:
Directions (86-90): In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Telemedicine has emerged as a (1)________ component of modern healthcare, accelerating rapidly due to global health crises. It provides patients with remote access to medical professionals, drastically reducing the (2)________ of travel and physical waiting times. However, the system is not without flaws. A significant (3)________ exists between urban areas with high-speed internet and rural regions where connectivity is scarce. This digital divide threatens to (4)________ existing healthcare inequalities if left unaddressed. To ensure equitable access, policymakers must focus on expanding digital infrastructure, (5)________ telehealth platforms, and training both doctors and patients in using these new tools effectively.

qs.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank 4.
qs.e:
'Threatens to ... if left unaddressed' needs a verb meaning to make worse.
Exacerbate means to worsen; diminish and resolve would be good outcomes, not threats.
Answer: exacerbate
qs.p:
Directions (86-90): In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Telemedicine has emerged as a (1)________ component of modern healthcare, accelerating rapidly due to global health crises. It provides patients with remote access to medical professionals, drastically reducing the (2)________ of travel and physical waiting times. However, the system is not without flaws. To ensure equitable access, policymakers must focus on expanding digital infrastructure, (5)________ telehealth platforms, and training both doctors and patients in using these new tools effectively.

qs.q: Select the correct option to fill in the blank 5.
qs.e:
The blank lists positive steps policymakers must take, alongside expanding infrastructure and training users.
Streamlining (making simpler and more efficient) telehealth platforms fits; the others are harmful.
Answer: streamlining

qs.q:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.
He is sitting ______ the desk, working diligently ______ his new laptop.
qs.e:
One sits 'at' a desk (at a point of activity), not 'in' or 'on' it.
One works 'on' a computer or laptop.
Answer: at, on

qs.q:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct active voice of the following sentence.
The instructions must be followed carefully lest mistakes should be made by the team.
o: The team must follow the instructions carefully lest they should make mistakes.
The team must follow the instructions carefully otherwise they will make mistakes.
Follow the instructions carefully lest mistakes should make by the team.
The team must follow the instructions carefully lest mistakes they should make.
qs.e:
The doer 'the team' becomes the subject of both clauses: must be followed -> must follow, should be made -> should make.
'Lest' must be kept and is followed by 'should'; (b) drops 'lest', (c) is still half passive and ungrammatical, (d) has wrong word order.
Answer: The team must follow the instructions carefully lest they should make mistakes.

qs.q:
Choose the best option to fill in the blank below.
This is ______ book I have read this month. It is easily ______ the previous one.
qs.e:
Comparing with every book read this month needs the superlative with 'the': the best.
Comparing with one other book needs the comparative: better than (and 'easily' goes with a comparative).
'A best' and 'as best as' are incorrect.
Answer: the best, better than

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom "Burn the midnight oil."
o: To read a book in the dark
To work or study late into the night
To set fire to something valuable
qs.e:
The idiom comes from working by an oil lamp after dark.
It means to work or study late at night.
Answer: To work or study late into the night

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom "A wild goose chase."
qs.e:
A wild goose chase is a search or pursuit that is pointless because what is sought cannot be found or reached.
Answer: A foolish and hopeless pursuit

qs.q:
Change the following sentence into the Passive form.
The board has approved the new marketing strategy.
o: The new marketing strategy was approved by the board.
The new marketing strategy has been approved by the board.
The new marketing strategy is approved by the board.
The new marketing strategy had been approved by the board.
qs.e:
The active verb 'has approved' is present perfect.
Present perfect passive is has/have + been + past participle: has been approved.
The other options change the tense.
Answer: The new marketing strategy has been approved by the board.

qs.q:
Identify the incorrectly spelt word in the sentence and rectify it.
The hotel offered excellent accomodation to all the guests attending the international conference.
qs.e:
'Accomodation' is misspelt; the correct form has double c and double m: accommodation.
Excellent, conference and international are spelt correctly in the sentence; options (b)-(d) are misspellings.
Answer: accommodation

qs.q:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
Although he worked very hard, he did not went to the office on time.
qs.e:
After the auxiliary 'did' (and 'did not'), the main verb is in the base form.
Correct: 'did not go'.
Answer: did not went

qs.q:
From the given alternatives, select the correct indirect narration of the given direct narration.
She said to him, "Please help me carry these heavy boxes."
o: She requested him to help her carry those heavy boxes.
She ordered him to help her carry these heavy boxes.
She asked him that he should help her carry those heavy boxes.
She requested him please help her carry those heavy boxes.
qs.e:
'Please' marks a request, so 'said to' becomes 'requested' + to-infinitive, and 'please' is dropped.
'Me' becomes 'her' and 'these' becomes 'those'.
Answer: She requested him to help her carry those heavy boxes.

qs.q:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. Many professionals are now able to perform their duties from the comfort of their homes.
B. The pandemic fundamentally changed how companies operate.
C. However, this shift has also introduced challenges such as blurred lines between work and personal life.
D. Remote working emerged as a widespread necessity rather than a rare privilege.
qs.e:
B opens with the general change caused by the pandemic.
D names the change (remote working became a necessity), and A gives its result (professionals work from home).
C, starting 'However, this shift', adds the downside and closes.
Answer: B - D - A - C
