qs.q:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The English teacher was instructing his trainees that they should write the sentences clearly on the notebook.
o: His trainees were instructed by the English teacher that the sentences should be written clearly on the notebook by them.
His trainees were being instructed by the English teacher that the sentences be written clearly on the notebook by them.
His trainees were being instructed by the English teacher that the sentences should be written clearly on the notebook by them.
His trainees are being instructed by the English teacher that the sentences would be written clearly on the notebook by them.
qs.e:
Past continuous 'was instructing' becomes 'were being instructed' (subject: his trainees).
The reported clause 'they should write the sentences' becomes 'the sentences should be written ... by them'.
Option 1 loses the continuous aspect; option 2 drops 'should'; option 4 changes the tense to present and 'should' to 'would'.
Right option: His trainees were being instructed by the English teacher that the sentences should be written clearly on the notebook by them.

qs.q:
Select the correct option:
The principal investigator insisted ___ conducting a peer-reviewed replication prior to dissemination.
qs.e:
The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' (insist on + noun/gerund).
'Insisted on conducting' = firmly demanded that it be done.
Right option: on

qs.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Incipient
qs.e:
'Incipient' means just beginning to develop.
Embryonic, rudimentary and germinal all mean early-stage, so they are synonyms.
The opposite is fully developed.
Right option: Mature

qs.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The vaccine is said to have been developed by a team of Indian researchers long before the pandemic began.
o: People say that a team of Indian researchers develops the vaccine long before the pandemic began.
People say that a team of Indian researchers had developed the vaccine long before the pandemic began.
It says that a team of Indian researchers has been developing the vaccine long before the pandemic began.
People said that a team of Indian researchers have developed the vaccine long before the pandemic began.
qs.e:
'is said' (present) → 'People say that ...'.
The perfect infinitive 'to have been developed' shows an earlier completed action; since it happened before 'the pandemic began' (past), the clause becomes 'had developed'.
Option 1 uses present 'develops', option 3 changes the meaning with 'It says ... has been developing', option 4 changes 'say' to 'said' and uses 'have developed' with a past time marker.
Right option: People say that a team of Indian researchers had developed the vaccine long before the pandemic began.

qs.q: In the following question, four spellings are given. Select the correctly spelt word.
qs.e:
Correct spelling: L-O-G-O-R-R-H-E-A (British variant: logorrhoea).
It means excessive, often incoherent talkativeness.
The other options double the h, double the r three times, or drop the 'e'.
Right option: Logorrhea

qs.q:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The speed with which the markets collapsed (1)/ caught not only the regulators but also the investors (2)/ off guard who had been predicting (3)/ a period of sustained growth. (4)
qs.e:
A relative clause should come right after the noun it describes.
Here 'who had been predicting' refers to 'the investors', but 'off guard' separates them.
Correct: '...caught not only the regulators but also the investors who had been predicting a period of sustained growth off guard.'
Right option: (3)

qs.q:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The organising committee decided to _____ the annual conference due to unforeseen circumstances.
qs.e:
Unforeseen circumstances suggest the conference was postponed.
'Put off' = postpone; 'put on' = stage/wear; 'put up' = erect/accommodate; 'put by' = save.
Right option: put off

qs.q:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:
Sairam said, "She has to come to Delhi to me within the next couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she mentioned."
o: Sairam said that she had to come to Delhi to her within the following couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she had mentioned.
Sairam said that she had to go to Delhi to him within the next couple of hours to bring help to solve the problem she had mentioned
Sairam said that she has to go to Delhi to him within the next couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she mentioned.
Sairam said that she had to go to Delhi to him within the following couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she had mentioned.
qs.e:
Changes: has → had; come → go (speaker no longer at that place); me → him (Sairam); next → following; mentioned → had mentioned.
Option 1 uses 'come' and 'her'; option 2 changes 'take help' to 'bring help' and keeps 'next'; option 3 keeps 'has' and 'mentioned'.
Right option: Sairam said that she had to go to Delhi to him within the following couple of hours to take help to solve the problem she had mentioned.

qs.q: In the following question, four spellings are given. Select the correctly spelt word.
qs.e:
Correct spelling: E-Q-U-A-N-I-M-I-T-Y.
It means calmness and composure, especially in difficult situations.
Right option: Equanimity

qs.q:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given below.
Excoriate
qs.e:
'Excoriate' means to criticise very severely.
Praise, encourage and appreciate are opposite in sense.
Right option: Condemn

qs.q:
The given sentence contains an error. Identify the error and select the option that rectifies the error.
By the time we arrived, the film has already started.
o: By the time we have arrived, the film had already started.
By the time we arrived, the film had already started.
By the time we arrived, the film have already started.
By the time we will arrive, the film has already started.
qs.e:
With 'by the time + past simple', the earlier action takes the past perfect.
So 'has already started' must become 'had already started'.
Option 1 wrongly makes 'arrived' present perfect; option 3 has 'have' with a singular subject; option 4 mixes future and present perfect.
Right option: By the time we arrived, the film had already started.

qs.q:
Directions: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in PASSIVE VOICE.
Who vandalised the marble plaques that adorn the memorial's eastern colonnade?
o: Who were the marble plaques that adorn the memorial's eastern colonnade vandalised by?
By whom the marble plaques that adorn the memorial's eastern colonnade were vandalised?
By whom were the marble plaques that adorn the memorial's eastern colonnade vandalised?
Whom were the marble plaques that adorn the memorial's eastern colonnade vandalised by?
qs.e:
An active 'Who + V2 + object?' becomes 'By whom + was/were + object + V3?'.
The object 'the marble plaques' is plural, so 'were'; question order needs the auxiliary before the subject.
Option 2 lacks the question inversion; options 1 and 4 leave 'by' dangling at the end, which is informal and not the standard form.
Right option: By whom were the marble plaques that adorn the memorial's eastern colonnade vandalised?

qs.q:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The merger was announced so abruptly (1)/ that it shocked not only the board members (2)/ but also to the investors (3)/ who had been expecting a gradual transition. (4)
qs.e:
'Not only ... but also' must join parallel items.
'Shocked not only the board members' takes a direct object, so the second item must also be a plain object: 'but also the investors'.
The extra 'to' in part 3 breaks the parallelism.
Right option: (3)

qs.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: Impecunious
qs.e:
'Impecunious' means having little or no money.
Destitute, bankrupt and penurious are synonyms.
The opposite is very rich.
Right option: Opulent

qs.q:
Select the correct meaning of the idiom used in the given sentence.
Despite the challenges, Priya managed to keep her head above water.
o: To remain calm in a stressful situation
To barely manage to survive or cope
qs.e:
'Keep one's head above water' means to just about manage to survive, especially financially or under pressure.
It does not mean staying calm, avoiding help or keeping quiet.
Right option: To barely manage to survive or cope

qs.q: Pointing to a photograph, Amit said, "She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather." How is the person in the photograph related to Amit?
qs.e:
The only son of Amit's grandfather is Amit's father.
The daughter of Amit's father is Amit's sister.
Answer: Sister

qs.q: Choose the set where the pattern of vowels and consonants differs.
qs.e:
Mark consonant = C, vowel = V.
BEAT = CVVC, SOUR = CVVC, COIN = CVVC.
PLAY = CCVC (P, L consonants; A vowel; Y consonant), so it differs.
Answer: PLAY

qs.q:
If × means +, ÷ means -, + means ÷, and - means ×, find the value of:
120 + 15 - 4 × 10 ÷ 5 = ?

Instructions: For the question below, carefully examine the Reference Statement. Then, identify the single option among the four alternatives (a, b, c, d) that is an EXACT AND COMPLETE REPLICATION of the Reference Statement. Pay exceptionally close attention to every character, number, symbol, space, and punctuation mark.
Reference: Reykjavik, ISL: 17th August 1985.
qs.e:

qs.q:
In the question below there are three statements followed by two conclusions I and II. You have to take the three given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the three statements disregarding commonly known facts.
Statements:
All Laptops are Computers.
Some Computers are Tablets.
No Tablet is a Smartphone.
Conclusions:
I. Some Laptops are Tablets.
II. No Smartphone is a Computer.
o: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
qs.e:
The Tablets that are Computers need not include any Laptop, so I is not certain.
Smartphones are only kept away from Tablets; they may still be Computers (outside the Tablet part), so II is not certain.
Answer: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

qs.q:
Select the option which is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term.
PNDR : SMKU : : GKPT : JNSW : : VQMD : ?
qs.e:
GKPT → JNSW: G+3 = J, K+3 = N, P+3 = S, T+3 = W (each letter +3).
Apply +3 to VQMD: V→Y, Q→T, M→P, D→G.
Answer: YTPG
Note: The first pair as printed does not fit: PNDR → SMKU is +3, −1, +7, +3 (a +3 rule would give SQGU), so it is likely a memory/typo error. The second pair gives a clean +3 rule, and only YTPG fits it; the first pair's shifts would give YPTG, which is not an option. Agrees with PDF key (a).

qs.q: 18th of a month is Friday. This month has 31 days. What will be the 14th of next month?
qs.e:
From the 18th to the 31st is 13 days; the 14th of next month is 13 + 14 = 27 days after the 18th.
27 = 3 weeks + 6 days, so move 6 days on from Friday.
Friday + 6 = Thursday.
Answer: Thursday

qs.q: One evening, Rekha started walking towards the sun for 60m. She took a right turn and walked 40m. Finally, she turned right again and walked 90m to reach the park. What is the minimum distance and in which direction is the park from her starting point?
qs.e:
In the evening the sun is in the West, so she walks 60 m West.
Right turn from West = North: 40 m North. Right again = East: 90 m East.
Net: 90 − 60 = 30 m East and 40 m North.
Distance = √(30² + 40²) = 50 m, towards the North-East.
Answer: 50 m North - East

qs.q: In a certain code language, MACHINE is written as NBDIJOF. How will PROBLEM be written in that code?
qs.e:
Each letter moves one step forward: M→N, A→B, C→D, H→I, I→J, N→O, E→F.
PROBLEM: P→Q, R→S, O→P, B→C, L→M, E→F, M→N.
Answer: QSPCMFN

qs.q:
You are given a Master Address (MA) from official records. Your task is to identify the correct candidate address that matches exactly with the master address in terms of formatting, punctuation, spelling, and structure.
Master Address (MA): 45/A, Lotus Tower, Phase-2, New Rajendra Nagar, Delhi - 110060
Candidate Addresses:
o: 45/A, Lotus Tower, Phase-2, New Rajendra Nagar, Delhi - 110060
45/A, Lotus Towers, Phase-2, New Rajendra Nagar, Delhi - 110060
45/A, Lotus Tower, Phase 2, New Rajendra Nagar, Delhi - 110060
45/A, Lotus Tower, Phase-2, New Rajender Nagar, Delhi - 110060
qs.e:
(b) writes Towers; (c) drops the hyphen in Phase-2.
(d) spells Rajender instead of Rajendra.
(a) matches character for character.
Answer: 45/A, Lotus Tower, Phase-2, New Rajendra Nagar, Delhi - 110060

qs.q:
Statements:
(i) All athletes who train properly win a medal.
(ii) Rajesh is an athlete.
Conclusions:
(i) Rajesh won a medal.
(ii) If Rajesh trained properly, he will win a medal.

The medal is promised only to athletes who train properly.
We are not told Rajesh trained properly, so (i) does not follow.
(ii) restates the rule for Rajesh, so it follows.

qs.e:

qs.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.
2, 10, 30, 68, 130, ?

What comes next in the following series?
Z26, Y24, X22, W20, V18, ?
qs.e:
Letters go back one step: Z, Y, X, W, V, U.
Numbers fall by 2: 26, 24, 22, 20, 18, 16.

qs.q:
In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions. Find out which conclusion is true based on the given statement.
Statement: A > B = C ≥ D < E ≤ F
Conclusions:
I. A > D
II. B < F
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
qs.e:
I: A > B = C ≥ D gives A > D. True.
II: B = C ≥ D < E ≤ F; the signs ≥ and < point opposite ways at D, so B and F cannot be compared. Not true.
Answer: Only I is true

qs.q: 8 friends P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, and W are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. P is third to the right of W and third to the left of Q. S is second to the right of T. V is second to the left of R. T is not an immediate neighbour of Q. Who is to the immediate right of U?
qs.e:
Facing the centre, number seats so that left = +1, and put W at 0. P = 0 − 3 = 5, and P = Q + 3 gives Q = 2.
T is not next to Q (seats 1, 3), and S = T − 2 must be free, so T = 6, S = 4.
V = R + 2 on seats 1, 3, 7: R = 1, V = 3, U = 7, or R = 7, V = 1, U = 3.
U's immediate right (seat U − 1) is T in the first case and Q in the second.
Only Q is among the options.
Answer: Q
Note: The clues allow two seatings (W, R, Q, V, S, P, T, U or W, V, Q, U, S, P, T, R going leftwards), giving T or Q as U's immediate right; checked by brute force with either handedness. W is never possible, so the PDF key (b) W is wrong. Only Q appears among the options, so (d).

qs.q:
The criteria for selecting a candidate for a Bank Probationary Officer are as follows. The candidate:
1. must hold a Bachelor's degree with at least 60% marks.
2. must have secured at least 65% in the preliminary exam and 70% in the mains exam.
3. must be between 21 and 30 years of age as on 1 April 2023.
However, if a candidate fulfils all criteria EXCEPT:
a. no. 1, but has a Master's degree with at least 55% marks, the case is to be referred to the HR Manager.
b. no. 3, but belongs to a reserved category, the case is to be referred to the Zonal Head.
Rahul completed his B.Sc. with 58% and M.Sc. with 62%. He was born on 12th May 1995. He scored 68% in prelims and 72% in mains. He does not belong to any reserved category.
What decision should be taken?
o: The candidate is to be selected.
The candidate is not to be selected.
The case is to be referred to the HR Manager.
The case is to be referred to the Zonal Head.
qs.e:
1: B.Sc. 58% is below 60%, so criterion 1 fails.
2: 68% ≥ 65% and 72% ≥ 70%, satisfied. 3: on 1 April 2023 he is 27, satisfied.
Only 1 fails, and his M.Sc. 62% is at least 55%, so exception (a) applies.
Answer: The case is to be referred to the HR Manager.

qs.q: In the following question, four number pairs are given. In each pair the number on left side of (-) is related to the number of the right side of (-) with some logic/Rule/Relation. Three pairs are similar on the basis of same Logic/Rule/Relation. Select the odd one out from the given alternatives.
qs.e:
Rule: right number = square of left number.
15² = 225, 12² = 144, 14² = 196.
13² = 169, not 171.
Answer: 13 - 171

qs.q: In a certain code, MONKEY is coded as XDJMNL, how is TIGER coded?
qs.e:
Write MONKEY backwards: YEKNOM. Move each letter back one: X D J M N L.
TIGER backwards: REGIT. Back one each: R→Q, E→D, G→F, I→H, T→S.
Answer: QDFHS

qs.q:
Statement:
Should a total ban be put on the use of plastic bags?
Arguments:
I. Yes. It will reduce the massive environmental pollution caused by plastic waste.
II. No. It will result in the loss of jobs for millions working in the plastic manufacturing industry.
o: if only argument I is strong
if only argument II is strong
if neither I nor II is strong
qs.e:
I is strong: it gives a major, direct benefit of the ban (less plastic pollution).
II is also strong: losing the livelihood of millions is a serious, direct cost of a total ban.
Both arguments are relevant and weighty.
Answer: if both arguments are strong

qs.q: Which layer of the Earth is composed primarily of liquid iron and nickel and is responsible for creating the Earth's magnetic field?
qs.e:
The outer core (about 2,900–5,100 km deep) is a liquid layer of iron and nickel.
Convection currents in this molten metal act like a dynamo and generate the Earth's magnetic field.
The inner core is solid; the mantle is rocky silicate; the crust is the thin solid outer shell.
Right option: Outer Core

qs.q: The New Economic Policy of 1991 in India is commonly referred to by which acronym?
qs.e:
The 1991 reforms under PM P. V. Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh rested on three pillars: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation.
Hence the policy is known as the LPG model.
PURA is a rural-amenities scheme, NITI is the 2015 policy think tank, and GST is the 2017 indirect tax.
Right option: LPG

qs.q: Which of the following is India’s indigenous Beyond Visual Range (BVR) air-to-air missile?
qs.e:
Astra is a DRDO-developed beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile carried by fighters such as the Su-30MKI and Tejas.
BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile (Indo-Russian), while Prithvi and Agni are surface-to-surface ballistic missiles.
Right option: Astra

qs.q: The classical dance form 'Sattriya' originated in which of the following Indian states?
qs.e:
Sattriya was created in the 15th century by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardeva and grew in the sattras (monasteries) of Assam.
It was recognised as a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.
Odisha has Odissi, Manipur has Manipuri, and Kerala has Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.
Right option: Assam

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding an Indian festival:
i. It marks the harvest of the winter crop.
ii. It is traditionally celebrated by lighting bonfires and dancing around them, primarily in North India.
Which festival is being talked about?
qs.e:
Lohri, celebrated on 13 January mainly in Punjab and neighbouring North Indian states, is linked with the harvest of the winter (rabi) crops such as sugarcane.
Its central ritual is a bonfire, around which people sing and dance (bhangra, gidda) and offer til, rewri and popcorn.
Onam (Kerala) and Pongal (Tamil Nadu) are South Indian, and Makar Sankranti is pan-Indian without the bonfire as its defining feature.
Right option: Lohri

qs.q:
With reference to the Finance Commission of India, consider the following:
1. It is a constitutional body established under Article 280.
2. It is constituted every five years by the Prime Minister of India.
3. Its primary function is to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, so it is a constitutional body; true.
Statement 2: it is constituted every fifth year (or earlier) by the President, not the Prime Minister; false.
Statement 3: its main job is to recommend how the net proceeds of taxes are shared between the Union and the States; true.
Right option: 1 and 3 only

qs.q: During the Delhi Sultanate period, the department of 'Diwan-i-Arz' was related to:
qs.e:
Diwan-i-Arz was the military department set up by Balban, headed by the Ariz-i-Mumalik.
It recruited, paid and inspected the army.
Agriculture was Diwan-i-Kohi (Muhammad bin Tughlaq), revenue was Diwan-i-Wizarat, and charity was Diwan-i-Khairat (Firoz Shah Tughlaq).
Right option: Military Affairs

qs.q: Which of the following greenhouse gases has the highest global warming potential (GWP) per molecule?
qs.e:
GWP compares a gas's heating effect with that of CO₂ (GWP = 1) over 100 years.
Methane is about 28, nitrous oxide about 265, while sulfur hexafluoride is about 23,500 — the highest of any gas assessed by the IPCC.
Right option: Sulfur Hexafluoride (SF₆)

qs.q: Neeraj Chopra made history by winning the Gold Medal in Javelin Throw at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics. What was his winning throw distance?
qs.e:
Neeraj Chopra won gold at Tokyo on 7 August 2021 with his second-round throw of 87.58 m.
It was India's first Olympic gold in athletics.
86.65 m was his qualification-round throw at Tokyo; 89.94 m was his later national record set in Stockholm in 2022.
Right option: 87.58 m

qs.q:
Read the below statements:
Statement I: The 'Nathu La pass' connects the Indian state of Sikkim with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
Statement II: The 'Rohtang Pass' is located in the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas and connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys.
o: Neither Statement I nor II is correct
Both Statement I and II are correct
qs.e:
Statement I: Nathu La, in the Dongkya range of East Sikkim, links Sikkim with Tibet (China) and is an India–China border trade post; true.
Statement II: Rohtang Pass (about 3,980 m) lies on the eastern Pir Panjal range in Himachal Pradesh and joins the Kullu valley with Lahaul and Spiti; true.
Right option: Both Statement I and II are correct

qs.q: Which committee in India is prominently known for recommending the estimation of poverty line based on nutritional requirements (calories)?
qs.e:
The 1979 Task Force headed by Y. K. Alagh fixed the poverty line by calorie norms: 2,400 kcal per person per day in rural areas and 2,100 kcal in urban areas.
The Kelkar Committee dealt with fiscal/tax reform, Raja Chelliah with tax reforms, and Narasimham with banking sector reforms.
Right option: Alagh Committee

qs.q:
Read the following statements regarding ancient Indian History:
1. The Mauryan Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
2. Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador in the court of Ashoka.
3. The Arthashastra was authored by Chanakya (Kautilya).
Which of the above statement/s is/are true?
qs.e:
Statement 1: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 321 BCE; true.
Statement 2: Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya, not Ashoka; false.
Statement 3: the Arthashastra is credited to Kautilya (Chanakya), Chandragupta's minister; true.
Right option: Statement 1 and 3 only

qs.q: The famous 'Red Fort' in Delhi was commissioned to be built by which Mughal Emperor?
qs.e:
Shah Jahan ordered the Red Fort (Qila-i-Mubarak) in 1638 when he shifted the capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad (Delhi); it was completed in 1648.
Akbar built the Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri; Aurangzeb only added the Moti Masjid inside the Red Fort.
Right option: Shah Jahan

qs.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
Statement I: 'Onam' is celebrated primarily in Kerala as a major harvest festival.
Statement II: 'Bihu' is the traditional harvest festival marking the Assamese New Year.
o: Both Statement I and II are correct
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct
qs.e:
Statement I: Onam, in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August–September), is Kerala's main harvest festival, linked with King Mahabali; true.
Statement II: Rongali (Bohag) Bihu in mid-April is Assam's harvest festival and marks the Assamese New Year; true.
Right option: Both Statement I and II are correct

qs.q: Which of the following Harappan sites is renowned for having an artificial brick dockyard?
qs.e:
Lothal, on the Bhogavo river in Gujarat, has a large baked-brick basin identified as the world's earliest known dockyard.
Kalibangan is known for fire altars and a ploughed field, Mohenjo-Daro for the Great Bath, and Banawali for a toy plough.
Right option: Lothal

qs.q:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
I. They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
II. They are justiciable in nature, meaning they can be enforced by courts.
qs.e:
Statement I: the 42nd Amendment (1976), on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice, added Part IV-A (Article 51A) with ten duties; true.
Statement II: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — no court can directly enforce them; false.
Right option: Only I

qs.q: Who became the first Indian author to win the International Booker Prize for the novel 'Tomb of Sand' in 2022?
qs.e:
Geetanjali Shree's Hindi novel 'Ret Samadhi', translated as 'Tomb of Sand' by Daisy Rockwell, won the International Booker Prize in 2022.
It was the first book in any Indian language to win the prize.
Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006) and Salman Rushdie (1981) won the Booker Prize for English novels, not the International Booker.
Right option: Geetanjali Shree

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Paris Agreement:
1. It is a legally binding international treaty on climate change.
2. Its overarching goal is to hold the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels.
3. It was adopted in 2015 at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP21).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: the UNFCCC describes the Paris Agreement as a legally binding international treaty on climate change; true.
Statement 2: its goal is to keep warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue 1.5°C; true.
Statement 3: it was adopted at COP21 in Paris on 12 December 2015 (in force from November 2016); true.
Right option: 1, 2 and 3

qs.q:
Read the below statements:
Statement I: NITI Aayog was established on January 1, 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
Statement II: The President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.
o: Both statements I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
Both statements I and II are correct
qs.e:
Statement I: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission; true.
Statement II: the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog is the Prime Minister, not the President; false.
Right option: Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect

qs.q: Which country hosted the FIFA Men's World Cup in 2022 where Argentina emerged victorious?
qs.e:
The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in Qatar (November–December 2022), the first in the Arab world.
Argentina beat France on penalties in the final at Lusail.
Brazil hosted in 2014 and Russia in 2018.
Right option: Qatar

qs.q: Which of the following is true about "Fiscal Deficit"?
o: It is the difference between total revenue and total expenditure of the government.
It represents the total borrowings required by the government.
It only accounts for capital expenditures.
It is independent of the interest payments on past debts.
qs.e:
Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings, so it equals the government's total borrowing requirement.
It covers both revenue and capital expenditure, and interest payments are part of the expenditure it includes.
Option (a) loosely describes the budget/overall deficit, not the fiscal deficit.
Right option: It represents the total borrowings required by the government.

qs.q: What is INS Vikrant, which was commissioned into the Indian Navy recently?
o: India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier
qs.e:
INS Vikrant (IAC-1), built by Cochin Shipyard, was commissioned on 2 September 2022 at Kochi.
It is the first aircraft carrier designed and built in India.
India's nuclear submarine is INS Arihant, not Vikrant.
Right option: India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier

qs.q: Which young Indian chess prodigy reached the finals of the FIDE Chess World Cup 2023?
qs.e:
At the FIDE World Cup 2023 in Baku, 18-year-old R Praggnanandhaa reached the final, beating Fabiano Caruana in the semi-final.
He lost the final to Magnus Carlsen in tie-breaks and finished runner-up.
Gukesh and Vidit Gujrathi went out in the quarter-finals.
Right option: R Praggnanandhaa

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Commonwealth Games:
1. India hosted the Commonwealth Games for the first time in 2010.
2. The 2010 Commonwealth Games were held in Mumbai.
3. Australia has hosted the Commonwealth Games the maximum number of times.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: the 2010 Games were the first Commonwealth Games held in India; true.
Statement 2: they were held in New Delhi, not Mumbai; false.
Statement 3: Australia has hosted five times (1938, 1962, 1982, 2006, 2018), more than any other country; true.
Right option: 1 and 3 only

qs.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can Parliament amend the Constitution and its procedures?
qs.e:
Article 368 in Part XX gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and lays down the procedure for doing so.
Article 352 is national emergency, 356 is President's rule in a state, and 370 was the special provision for Jammu & Kashmir.
Right option: Article 368

qs.q: The height of a right circular cylinder is 14 cm and its curved surface area is 264 cm². Find the volume of the cylinder. (Take π = 22/7)
qs.e:
Curved surface area = 2πrh: 2 × 22/7 × r × 14 = 88r = 264, so r = 3 cm.
Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 9 × 14 = 22 × 9 × 2 = 396 cm³.
396 cm³

qs.q: Consider two similar triangles, △ABC and △PQR. The ratio of their corresponding perimeters is 4:5. If the area of △ABC is 64 cm², what is the area of △PQR?
qs.e:
For similar triangles the perimeter ratio equals the side ratio, 4 : 5.
Areas are in the ratio of squares of sides: 16 : 25.
Area of △PQR = 64 × 25/16 = 100 cm².
100 cm²

qs.q: If p = 3 + √2 and q = 3 − √2, which of the following is true?
qs.e:
p + q = 6 is rational, so (a) is false; p − q = 2√2 is irrational.
p × q = (3 + √2)(3 − √2) = 9 − 2 = 7, which is rational.
p/q = (3 + √2)²/7 = (11 + 6√2)/7 is irrational.
p × q is rational

qs.q: If (x − 1/x) = 4, then what is the value of x³ − 1/x³?
A shopkeeper bought 4 kg of sugar and 5 kg of rice for ₹ 320. Next time, he bought 6 kg of sugar and 3 kg of rice for ₹ 300. Find the cost of 1 kg of sugar and 1 kg of rice respectively.
qs.e:
Let sugar = s and rice = r per kg: 4s + 5r = 320 and 6s + 3r = 300 (i.e. 2s + r = 100).
From the second, r = 100 − 2s; substitute: 4s + 500 − 10s = 320, so s = 30 and r = 40.
Check: 120 + 200 = 320 and 180 + 120 = 300.
₹ 30, ₹ 40

qs.q: The difference between the simple interest and compound interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 5% per annum is ₹ 15. Find the sum.
A solid metallic cylinder of base radius 3 cm and height 5 cm is melted to form cones, each of height 1 cm and base radius 1 mm. Find the number of cones so formed.
qs.e:
Cylinder volume = π × 3² × 5 = 45π cm³.
Cone: radius 1 mm = 0.1 cm, so volume = (1/3) × π × 0.01 × 1 = π/300 cm³.
Number of cones = 45π ÷ (π/300) = 45 × 300 = 13,500.
13500

qs.q: The price of a commodity increases by 20%. By what percentage should a consumer reduce their consumption so that the expenditure on the commodity remains unchanged?
qs.e:
Reduction needed = increase/(100 + increase) × 100.
= 20/120 × 100 = 16.66%.
Check: 1.2 × (5/6) = 1, so expenditure is unchanged.
16.66%

qs.q: If tan θ = 4/3 and θ is acute, find the value of (sin θ + cos θ)/(sin θ − cos θ).
qs.e:
Divide numerator and denominator by cos θ: (tan θ + 1)/(tan θ − 1).
= (4/3 + 1)/(4/3 − 1) = (7/3)/(1/3) = 7.
7

qs.q: In a company, the average salary of 15 managers is ₹ 60,000, and the average salary of 35 employees is ₹ 20,000. What is the overall average salary of all the staff members combined?

qs.e:
With a = 0.04 and b = 0.02 the expression is (a³ + b³)/(a² − ab + b²).
Since a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²), it equals a + b = 0.04 + 0.02 = 0.06.
0.06

qs.q: If the radii of two circles are 5 cm and 3 cm, and the distance between their centers is 10 cm, find the length of the direct common tangent.
qs.e:
Direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²).
= √(10² − (5 − 3)²) = √(100 − 4) = √96 cm.
√96 cm

qs.q: A grocer mixes two varieties of tea costing ₹ 80 per kg and ₹ 120 per kg. In what ratio should he mix them so that the mixture costs ₹ 110 per kg?
From an external point P, two tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with center O. If the radius of the circle is 5 cm and OP = 13 cm, find the area of quadrilateral PAOB.
qs.e:
Radius ⟂ tangent, so PA = √(OP² − OA²) = √(169 − 25) = 12 cm.
PAOB is two congruent right triangles OAP and OBP.
Area = 2 × ½ × 5 × 12 = 60 cm².
60 cm²

qs.q: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B can do the same work in 30 days. They start working together, but after 5 days, B leaves. In how many more days will A finish the remaining work?
qs.e:
Together per day = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12; in 5 days they do 5/12.
Remaining = 7/12, which A alone finishes in 7/12 × 20 = 35/3 ≈ 11.67 days.
11.67 days

qs.q: The marked price of an article is ₹ 2,500. A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is the selling price of the article?
A train traveling at 72 km/h crosses a 250 m long platform in 26 seconds. What is the length of the train?
qs.e:
Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s.
Distance in 26 s = 20 × 26 = 520 m = train + platform.
Train = 520 − 250 = 270 m.
270 m

qs.q: A certain sum triples itself in 10 years at a certain rate of simple interest. In how many years will it become 5 times of itself at the same rate of interest?
qs.e:
Tripling means interest = 2P in 10 years, so the rate is 20% per annum.
To become 5 times, interest = 4P, which takes 4P ÷ (0.2P) = 20 years.
20 years

qs.q: If the cost price of 15 articles is equal to the selling price of 12 articles, find the profit percentage.
qs.e:
Let each CP = ₹ 1; then CP of 15 = ₹ 15 = SP of 12, so each SP = 15/12 = ₹ 1.25.
Profit % = 0.25/1 × 100 = 25%.
25%

qs.q: An article is sold at a 15% profit. If its cost price was ₹ 20 less and selling price was ₹ 20 less, the profit would have been 20%. Find the original cost price.
qs.e:
Let CP = x, so SP = 1.15x. New CP = x − 20, new SP = 1.15x − 20.
1.2(x − 20) = 1.15x − 20 gives 0.05x = 4, so x = 80.
Check: CP 80, SP 92; new CP 60, new SP 72, and 72/60 = 1.2 (20% profit).
₹ 80

qs.q:

A homonym has the same spelling/sound but a different meaning.
Only option 2 uses 'bark' again, meaning the outer covering of a tree.

qs.q:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.
The manager informed the team that the client had accepted their proposal the previous day.
o: The manager said to the team, "The client has accepted our proposal yesterday."
The manager said to the team, "The client accepted our proposal the previous day."
The manager said to the team, "The client accepts our proposal yesterday."
The manager said to the team, "The client had accepted our proposal the previous day."
qs.e:
Going back to direct speech we reverse the reported-speech changes.
'had accepted' becomes 'has accepted', 'the previous day' becomes 'yesterday', 'their' becomes 'our'.
Options 2 and 4 keep 'the previous day', and option 3 uses the wrong tense.
Right option: The manager said to the team, "The client has accepted our proposal yesterday."
Note: Checker B: transcription verified; agrees with key (a) but keeps conf=check. (a) reverses every reported-speech change (had accepted -> has accepted, the previous day -> yesterday, their -> our), though 'has accepted ... yesterday' is ungrammatical; the ideal direct form 'The client accepted our proposal yesterday' is not offered. (b) has the right tense but keeps 'the previous day', so it is not a true reversal. (a) is the intended exam answer.

qs.e:

The other options drop a 'c', an 'm', or the 'i'.

qs.q: Which of the following is the correct tense used in the phrase: "regulatory frameworks are evolving to ensure that AI applications are transparent"?
qs.e:
'are evolving' = is/am/are + verb-ing.
That is the present continuous tense: an action in progress now.
Right option: Present Continuous
qs.p:
Directions (81-85): Read the passage and answer the questions:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare is rapidly transitioning from a theoretical concept to a ubiquitous reality. The integration of machine learning algorithms in diagnostics has demonstrated unprecedented accuracy, often matching or even surpassing human experts in interpreting radiological images and pathology slides. Beyond diagnostics, AI is instrumental in predictive analytics, helping hospitals anticipate patient admissions and allocate resources effectively. However, this technological leap is not without challenges. Data privacy remains a paramount concern, as training these algorithms requires vast amounts of sensitive patient data. Furthermore, the "black box" nature of some AI models raises ethical questions about accountability when a misdiagnosis occurs. To ameliorate these issues, regulatory frameworks are evolving to ensure that AI applications are transparent, unbiased, and subject to rigorous clinical validation. Ultimately, the successful adoption of AI in medicine will depend on fostering a symbiotic relationship between human clinicians and intelligent machines, leveraging technology to augment rather than replace human judgment.

qs.q: Identify the grammatical function of the word "unprecedented" as used in the passage.
qs.e:
In 'demonstrated unprecedented accuracy', the word describes the noun 'accuracy'.
A word that qualifies a noun is an adjective.
Right option: Adjective

qs.q:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.
The mechanic is repairing my car right now.
o: My car is repaired by the mechanic right now.
My car is being repaired by the mechanic right now.
My car was being repaired by the mechanic right now.
My car has been repaired by the mechanic right now.
qs.e:
Present continuous active (is repairing) becomes is/are + being + V3 in the passive.
Object 'my car' becomes the subject: 'My car is being repaired by the mechanic'.
Right option: My car is being repaired by the mechanic right now.

qs.q:
Select the correct option:
The Principal congratulated the student ___ his outstanding performance in the board exams.
qs.e:
The standard collocation is 'congratulate someone on something'.
So the student is congratulated on his performance.
Right option: on

qs.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: Ephemeral
qs.e:
Ephemeral = lasting a very short time.
Transient, fleeting and short-lived are synonyms; the opposite is permanent.

The IT department installed the new software across all computers.
The IT department has installed the new software across all computers.
The IT department had installed the new software across all computers.

'has been installed' is present perfect passive.

qs.q:
Statement: Students these days aspire to study at top international universities for having a dream career.
Course of action:
I.Students should research and shortlist the universities and the courses offered.
II.Students must first enroll in English language learning programs.
qs.e:
Course I is the natural first step: to get into a top foreign university you must first research and shortlist universities and courses.
Course II says students 'must first' join English programmes. Not every student needs this (many already know English, and many top universities teach in other languages), so it is not a necessary step.

qs.p: Directions: In the question below is given a statement followed by two courses of action numbered I and II. qs.q:
Statement: L ≥ Q = R ≤ S ≥ D > U
Conclusions:
I. R ≤ L
II. U < S
o: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
qs.e:
Conclusion I: L ≥ Q = R gives L ≥ R, i.e. R ≤ L. True.
Conclusion II: S ≥ D > U gives S > U, i.e. U < S. True.
Answer: Both I and II are true

The missing term is B U S.

qs.q:
Read the Scenario and give appropriate answer:
You're a police officer. Your partner uses excessive force during an arrest. They ask you not to report it, saying it would ruin their career and reputation.
What should you do?
o: Justify the force in your report to protect them.
Confront your partner privately and demand accountability.
Report the incident to internal affairs.
qs.e:
Excessive force is misconduct. As a police officer you have a duty to report it, whatever your loyalty to your partner.
Justifying it in your report or staying silent makes you part of the misconduct. A private talk alone does not create any official accountability.
The proper channel is internal affairs.
Answer: Report the incident to internal affairs.

qs.q: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd letter-cluster.
qs.e:
Rule: the 2nd letter is the opposite of the 1st (their positions add up to 27), 3rd = 1st + 3, and 4th = 3rd + 6.
AZDJ: A(1)+Z(26)=27, A+3=D, D+6=J ✓
EVHN: E(5)+V(22)=27, E+3=H, H+6=N ✓
CXFL: C(3)+X(24)=27, C+3=F, F+6=L ✓
JPMS: J(10)+P(16)=26, so P is not the opposite of J (the opposite of J is Q). This is the odd one.
Answer: JPMS

qs.q:

35, 54, 77, 106, 137, ?

These are consecutive prime numbers: 19, 23, 29, 31. The next prime is 37.
137 + 37 = 174.

qs.q: A family consisting of D, P, W, Y and M is travelling to meet one another. W is travelling with his daughters, D and P. M is travelling with his maternal grandmother, Y. D is the mother of M. How is Y related to P?
qs.e:
W is the father of D and P, so D and P are sisters.
Y is M's maternal grandmother, and D is M's mother, so Y is D's mother.
Y is therefore W's wife and the mother of both daughters, D and P.
