Statement: Should children be allowed to use smartphones?
Argument I: No, Smartphones are addictive, they reduce study time and play time.
Argument II: Yes, the future is about technology. The sooner the children learn how to use technology the better for their and society's future.
o: if neither argument I nor II is strong
if only argument II is strong.
if only argument I is strong.
If both argument I and II are strong
qs.e:
Argument I gives a concrete, directly relevant harm: smartphones are addictive and take time away from study and play. It is strong.
Argument II is a broad generalisation. Children can learn technology through computers and school without having their own smartphone, so 'the future is technology' does not by itself show that smartphones should be allowed. It is weak.
Answer: if only argument I is strong.
Note: Statement-and-argument questions are partly subjective. Both earlier solvers also chose 'only I'; some keys may treat II as strong too.
qs.p: In the question a statement is given, followed by two arguments, I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given arguments, if any, is a strong argument.

qs.q:
What will come in the place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '-' are interchanged with '×' and '÷', respectively?
18 × 17 + 4 ÷ 22 - 2 = ?
qs.e:
Swap + with × and − with ÷.
18 × 17 + 4 ÷ 22 − 2 becomes 18 + 17 × 4 − 22 ÷ 2.
With BODMAS: 17 × 4 = 68 and 22 ÷ 2 = 11.
18 + 68 − 11 = 75.
Answer: 75

qs.q:
Compare the following two addresses.
Address 1: Ms. Neha Verma, Flat No. 204, Tower B, Green Acres, Pune 411045
Address 2: Mrs. Neha Verma, Flat No. 204, Tower B, Green Acres Society, Pune - 411045
Are these likely to be the same?
o: No, city codes do not match
Yes, all details match except name titles
No, the flat numbers are different
No, the name titles are different
qs.e:
Name (Neha Verma), flat number (204), tower (B), society (Green Acres), city (Pune) and PIN code (411045) all agree.
The only differences are the title (Ms. vs Mrs.) and small formatting ('Society', the dash before the PIN), which do not change the location.
So the two addresses most likely refer to the same place.
Answer: Yes, all details match except name titles
Note: Address 2 also adds the word 'Society', which the chosen option does not mention; it is still clearly the best of the four options.

qs.q:
What will come in the place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '-' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?
109 - 55 × 605 ÷ 77 + 93 = ?
If 19th January 2023 falls on Thursday, what will be the week day on 06 July 2024?
qs.e:
From 19 Jan 2023 to 19 Jan 2024 is 365 days (2023 is not a leap year).
19 Jan 2024 to 6 Jul 2024: 12 (rest of Jan) + 29 (Feb, leap year) + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 6 = 169 days.
Total = 534 days = 76 weeks + 2 days.
Thursday + 2 days = Saturday.
Answer: Saturday

qs.q: Select the odd word from the given alternatives.
qs.e:
Magnalium (aluminium + magnesium), nichrome (nickel + chromium) and Muntz metal (copper + zinc) are all alloys.
Sodium is a pure chemical element, not an alloy.
Answer: Sodium

qs.q: In a certain coded language if "MONSOON" is coded as "PMQQPMO", and "WINTERS" is coded as "UPGRPGY" then how is "SUMMERS" coded ?
qs.e:
Write the word backwards, then add +2 and −2 to the letters by turns.
MONSOON → NOOSNOM → N+2=P, O−2=M, O+2=Q, S−2=Q, N+2=P, O−2=M, M+2=O = PMQQPMO ✓
WINTERS → SRETNIW → UPGRPGY ✓
SUMMERS → SREMMUS → S+2=U, R−2=P, E+2=G, M−2=K, M+2=O, U−2=S, S+2=U.
Answer: UPGKOSU

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'INHALE' is written as 'REEDIH'. How will 'MIGHTY' be written in that language?
qs.e:
Swap each pair of letters, then add +4 and −4 by turns.
INHALE → NI AH EL → N+4=R, I−4=E, A+4=E, H−4=D, E+4=I, L−4=H = REEDIH ✓
MIGHTY → IM HG YT → I+4=M, M−4=I, H+4=L, G−4=C, Y+4=C (wraps round), T−4=P.
Answer: MILCCP

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'FLORENCE' is coded as '86' and 'GRATITUDE' is coded as '114'. How is 'FOREIGN' coded in the given language?
qs.e:
Code = sum of the letters' positions in the alphabet + number of letters.
FLORENCE: 6+12+15+18+5+14+3+5 = 78; 78 + 8 = 86 ✓
GRATITUDE: 7+18+1+20+9+20+21+4+5 = 105; 105 + 9 = 114 ✓
FOREIGN: 6+15+18+5+9+7+14 = 74; 74 + 7 = 81.
Answer: 81

qs.q: Pawan bought 4 dozen apples and 3 kg grapes. A dozen apples cost twice as much as 1 kg of grapes. If 5 kg grapes cost Rs 450, what is the amount spent by Pawan on buying apples and grapes as mentioned above?
qs.e:
1 kg grapes = 450 ÷ 5 = Rs 90.
1 dozen apples = 2 × 90 = Rs 180.
Apples: 4 × 180 = Rs 720. Grapes: 3 × 90 = Rs 270.
Total = 720 + 270 = Rs 990.
Answer: Rs. 990

qs.q: You and your friend decided to go swimming in a nearby river. So on reaching there, you heard the crying sound of the drowning child. You would:
o: dive into the river to save him.
wait to see if some other person is there to help
qs.e:
A child's life is in immediate danger and every second counts. You came to swim, so you can swim.
Waiting for someone else or searching for professional divers wastes time the child does not have, and just watching is unacceptable.
The right response is to act at once and rescue the child.
Answer: dive into the river to save him.

qs.q:
Statement: Government permitted private colleges to increase their fees.
Assumption I: Government colleges do not need to increase fees.
Assumption II: Private colleges are in financial difficulties.
o: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
qs.e:
A government lets private colleges raise fees only if it accepts that they need more money to run, so II (they are in financial difficulty) is implicit.
The statement says nothing about government colleges, so I is not implied.
Answer: Only assumption II is implicit
qs.p: In each question below is given one/more statements that followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. Consider the statement and decide which of the given assumptions is implicit.

qs.q: Rogerio, in search of an internet café, walked 30 m due North. He turned right and walked 18 m. He again turned right and walked 30 m. Finally, he turned left and walked 22 m to reach the internet café. How far and in which direction is the internet café from his starting point?
qs.e:
Start at (0,0). 30 m north → (0,30).
Turn right (now facing east), 18 m → (18,30).
Turn right (now facing south), 30 m → (18,0).
Turn left (now facing east), 22 m → (40,0).
The café is 40 m from the start, due east.
Answer: 40 m due East

qs.q:
Consider the given statement true and decide which of the given assumptions is (are) implicit.
Statement:
A teacher tells a student, “if you don’t finish your homework, you will not be allowed into the class”.
Assumptions:
1. Discipline is a way to create effective learning.
2. The teacher will be happy not to have a student who is not punctual in his work.
o: Neither assumption I nor II is implicit.
Both assumptions I and II are implicit.
qs.e:
The teacher uses a rule (no homework, no class) to enforce discipline, which assumes that discipline helps learning. So I is implicit.
The statement does not suggest the teacher would be happy to lose a student. The aim is to make the student finish the work, not to keep them out. So II is not implicit.
Answer: Only assumption I is implicit.

qs.q:
Select the word that CANNOT be formed using the letters of the given word, using each letter only as many times as it appears in the given word.
METAPHORICAL
qs.e:
METAPHORICAL has M, E, T, A, P, H, O, R, I, C, A, L, so A appears twice and T only once.
MORAL, METAL and HOTEL can all be formed.
TOTAL needs two T's, but there is only one.
Answer: TOTAL

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Supreme Court of India?
qs.e:
Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution covers the Union Judiciary.
Its first Article, 124, says there shall be a Supreme Court of India with a Chief Justice and other judges.
Article 121 bars Parliament from discussing a judge's conduct, 122 bars courts from questioning Parliament's proceedings, and 123 is the President's ordinance power.
Right option: Article 124.

qs.q: Which Buddhist text mentions the 16 Mahajanapadas?
qs.e:
The standard list of sixteen Mahajanapadas (Kashi, Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara, Kamboja) comes from the Anguttara Nikaya of the Sutta Pitaka.
The Vinaya Pitaka deals with monastic rules; the Jain Bhagavati Sutra gives a separate list.
Right option: Anguttara Nikaya.

qs.q: Bihu dance is primarily associated with which state?
qs.e:
Bihu is the folk dance of Assam, performed mainly during Rongali (Bohag) Bihu in mid-April, the Assamese new year.
Manipur is known for Manipuri/Ras Leela, Tripura for Hojagiri, and Meghalaya for Nongkrem and Shad Suk Mynsiem.
Right option: Assam.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the 16 Mahajanapadas:
1. They are mentioned in both Buddhist and Jain literature.
2. The Mahajanapada of Magadha was located between the Ganga and Yamuna rivers.
3. Anguttara Nikaya is a Buddhist text that mentions them.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: true. Buddhist texts (Anguttara Nikaya) and Jain texts (Bhagavati Sutra) both name sixteen Mahajanapadas.
Statement 2: false. Magadha lay in south Bihar, between the Ganga and the Son; the Ganga-Yamuna Doab held Kuru, Panchala and Vatsa.
Statement 3: true. The Anguttara Nikaya is the Buddhist source of the list.
Right option: 1 and 3 only.

qs.q: Which famous Indian playback singer received the Bharat Ratna in 2001?
qs.e:
Lata Mangeshkar, the 'Nightingale of India', was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001 (along with Ustad Bismillah Khan).
Asha Bhosle, Shreya Ghoshal and Alka Yagnik have not received the Bharat Ratna.
Right option: Lata Mangeshkar.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bharatanatyam dance form:
1. It originates from the state of Tamil Nadu.
2. It primarily uses hand gestures and facial expressions to narrate stories.
3. Bharatanatyam was recognized as a classical dance form of India after independence.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: true. Bharatanatyam grew out of the temple dance tradition of Tamil Nadu.
Statement 2: true. It tells stories through mudras (hand gestures) and abhinaya (facial expression).
Statement 3: true in the formal sense. Classical status is conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, set up in 1952, so its recognition as a classical form came after independence, although the dance itself is ancient.
Right option: 1, 2, and 3.
Note: Solver 1 chose '1 and 2 only', solver 2 '1, 2, and 3'. Kept '1, 2, and 3': the list of classical dances is the Sangeet Natak Akademi's (founded 1952), so statement 3 is literally true. Statement 3 is still loosely worded (the dance is ancient), so the official key could treat it as false; marked check.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about National Sports Day in India:
1. It is celebrated on 12 August every year.
2. It is observed to honor Major Dhyan Chand, a legendary hockey player.
3. It marks the anniversary of India's first hockey gold medal in the Olympics.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: false. National Sports Day is on 29 August, not 12 August (12 August is International Youth Day).
Statement 2: true. It honours hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.
Statement 3: false. 29 August is his birth anniversary (born 1905), not the date of India's first Olympic hockey gold (1928).
Right option: 2 only.

qs.q:
Assertion (A): The Mahajanapada of Magadha was located in the present-day state of Bihar.
Reason (R): Magadha was situated between the Ganga and Son rivers, providing fertile land and strategic advantages.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
qs.e:
A: true. Magadha covered the Patna-Gaya region of present-day south Bihar.
R: true. Magadha lay between the Ganga (north) and the Son (west), giving fertile alluvial land, iron ores nearby and river defences.
The Ganga-Son region is exactly where Bihar lies today, so R explains A.
Right option: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Note: Both solvers agree. R describes Magadha's geography and advantages rather than strictly why it is in Bihar, so 'R is not the correct explanation' is arguable; marked check.

qs.q: Kuchipudi is a classical dance form primarily associated with which state?
qs.e:
Kuchipudi takes its name from Kuchipudi village in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.
Kerala has Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, Karnataka has Yakshagana (theatre), and Tamil Nadu has Bharatanatyam.
Right option: Andhra Pradesh.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. It led to the formation of the state of Telangana.
2. It was passed in the year 2014.
3. Chhattisgarh was also formed as part of this act.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: true. The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 carved Telangana out of Andhra Pradesh (formed 2 June 2014).
Statement 2: true. Parliament passed it in February 2014 and it got assent in March 2014.
Statement 3: false. Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November 2000 under the Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000.
Right option: 1 and 2 only.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Padma Awards:
1. They were instituted in 1954.
2. The Padma Vibhushan is the highest civilian award in India.
3. They are conferred in three categories: Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: true. The Padma Awards were instituted in 1954.
Statement 2: false. The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award; the Padma Vibhushan is the second highest.
Statement 3: true. They are given in three grades: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.
Right option: 1 and 3 only.

qs.q: In which year was the Padma Awards instituted in India?
qs.e:
The Padma Awards were instituted by the Government of India in 1954, the same year as the Bharat Ratna.
They are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day.
Right option: 1954.

qs.q: The Mahajanapada of Magadha was primarily located between which two rivers?
qs.e:
Magadha (south Bihar) was bounded by the Ganga to the north, the Son to the west and the Champa to the east, with hills to the south.
The Ganga-Yamuna Doab was Kuru-Panchala land, the Narmada is far to the south, and the Gandak region belonged to Vajji and Malla.
Right option: Ganga and Son.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985:
1. It introduced the Anti-Defection Law in India.
2. It amended the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
3. It applies only to Members of Parliament and not to State Legislatures.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: true. The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 brought in the Anti-Defection Law.
Statement 2: accepted as true. It did this by adding the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution (strictly it inserted, not amended, the Schedule).
Statement 3: false. The law applies to members of both Parliament and State Legislatures.
Right option: 1 and 2 only.

qs.q: Which Article contains provisions for the establishment of High Courts in India?
qs.e:
Article 214 states that there shall be a High Court for each State; this is the provision establishing High Courts.
Article 216 deals with the constitution (composition) of High Courts, 226 with their power to issue writs, and 231 with a common High Court for two or more States.
Right option: Article 214.

qs.q: Which great Indian sportsperson's birth anniversary is celebrated as National Sports Day?
qs.e:
National Sports Day (29 August) marks the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand, winner of Olympic gold in 1928, 1932 and 1936.
Milkha Singh was a sprinter and Kapil Dev a cricketer; 'Dhyan Singh' was Dhyan Chand's original name, used here as a distractor.
Right option: Major Dhyan Chand.

qs.q: When is National Sports Day celebrated in India every year?
qs.e:
National Sports Day is celebrated on 29 August every year, the birthday of Major Dhyan Chand (born 1905).
12 August is International Youth Day, 15 August is Independence Day and 5 September is Teachers' Day.
Right option: 29 August.

qs.q: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985 introduced which provision in India?
qs.e:
The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 added the Tenth Schedule, which contains the Anti-Defection Law.
Panchayati Raj came with the 73rd Amendment (1992), Fundamental Duties with the 42nd (1976), and GST with the 101st (2016).
Right option: Anti-Defection Law.

qs.q:
Match the following Mahajanapadas with their modern-day locations:
Mahajanapada | Modern-Day Location
1. Magadha | A. Bihar
2. Kashi | B. Uttar Pradesh
3. Avanti | C. Madhya Pradesh
4. Gandhara | D. Pakistan
qs.e:
Magadha (capital Rajagriha, later Pataliputra) lies in Bihar: 1-A.
Kashi (capital Varanasi) lies in Uttar Pradesh: 2-B.
Avanti (capital Ujjain) lies in Madhya Pradesh: 3-C.
Gandhara (capital Taxila) lies in present-day Pakistan: 4-D.
Right option: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D.

qs.q: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
qs.e:
The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885.
Its first session met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, on 28 December 1885, with A. O. Hume as a founder.
Right option: 1885.

qs.q: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
qs.e:
The first INC session (Bombay, December 1885) was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.
Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the second session (Calcutta, 1886); A. O. Hume was a founder and general secretary; Surendranath Banerjee led the Indian National Conference.
Right option: W. C. Bonnerjee.

qs.q: How many Mahajanapadas are mentioned in the Buddhist and Jain literature?
qs.e:
Buddhist (Anguttara Nikaya) and Jain (Bhagavati Sutra) texts speak of sixteen Mahajanapadas in the 6th century BCE.
Right option: 16.

qs.q:
Assertion (A): The first session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.
Reason (R): The Indian National Congress was founded in 1887 by A. O. Hume.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
qs.e:
A: true. W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session of the INC in 1885.
R: false. The INC was founded in 1885, not 1887 (though A. O. Hume was indeed a founder).
Right option: A is true, but R is false.

qs.q:
Match the following classical dance forms with their states:
Dance Form | State
1. Kuchipudi | A. Andhra Pradesh
2. Mohiniyattam | B. Kerala
3. Yakshagana | C. Karnataka
4. Bharatanatyam | D. Tamil Nadu
qs.e:
Kuchipudi belongs to Andhra Pradesh: 1-A.
Mohiniyattam belongs to Kerala: 2-B.
Yakshagana belongs to coastal Karnataka: 3-C.
Bharatanatyam belongs to Tamil Nadu: 4-D.
Right option: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D.

qs.q: If a + 1/a = 7, then a⁵ + 1/a⁵ is equal to:
There are two identical circles of radius 10 cm each. If the length of the direct common tangent is 26 cm, then what is the length (in cm) of the transverse common tangent?
qs.e:
Equal radii, so direct common tangent = distance between centres: d = 26 cm
Transverse tangent = √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²) = √(26² − 20²)
= √(676 − 400) = √276 = 2√69
Answer: 2√69

qs.q: The base of a right pyramid is a square and the length of the side of square is 32 cm and height of the pyramid is 12 cm, then what is the total surface area of the square pyramid?
qs.e:
Slant height = √(12² + (32/2)²) = √(144 + 256) = 20 cm
Lateral area = ½ × perimeter × slant = ½ × 128 × 20 = 1280 cm²
Base area = 32² = 1024 cm²
TSA = 1280 + 1024 = 2304 cm²
Answer: 2304 sq. cm

qs.q: If Δ ABC ~ Δ QPR, ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔPQR) = 4/9, AC = 12 cm, AB = 18 cm and BC = 10 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
qs.e:
ΔABC ~ ΔQPR matches A↔Q, B↔P, C↔R, so BC corresponds to PR.
Ratio of areas = (ratio of sides)² ⇒ side ratio = √(4/9) = 2/3
BC/PR = 2/3 ⇒ PR = 10 × 3/2 = 15 cm
Answer: 15

qs.q: Two trains are running on opposite tracks between stations A and B. After crossing each other they take 4 hr and 9 hr respectively to reach their destination. If speed of first train is 54 kmph, find the speed of second train.
qs.e:
After meeting: S₁/S₂ = √(t₂/t₁) = √(9/4) = 3/2
S₂ = 54 × 2/3 = 36 km/h
Answer: 36 kmph

qs.q: If AB and CD are two chords of a circle intersected at point O. If CO = 4 cm and OD = 3.75 cm and AB = 8 cm then find the smallest possible length of BO?
qs.e:
Intersecting chords: AO × OB = CO × OD = 4 × 3.75 = 15
Let BO = x, AO = 8 − x ⇒ x(8 − x) = 15 ⇒ x² − 8x + 15 = 0
x = 3 or 5; the smaller value is 3 cm
Answer: 3 cm

qs.q: Find the value of given expression. 3 - (- 6){- 2 - 9 - 3} ÷ 7{1 + (- 2)(- 1)}
Ratio of three number is 2 : 3 : 1 and their product is 162. Sum of the first two numbers is how much more than the third number?
qs.e:
Let numbers be 2k, 3k, k ⇒ 6k³ = 162 ⇒ k³ = 27 ⇒ k = 3
Numbers: 6, 9, 3
(6 + 9) − 3 = 12
Answer: 12

qs.q: Ratio of ages of Namrata and Divya is 4 : 3. The sum of their ages is 28. Ratio of their ages after 4 years will be
qs.e:
Total parts 4 + 3 = 7 ⇒ 1 part = 28/7 = 4
Ages now: 16 and 12
After 4 years: 20 and 16 ⇒ 20 : 16 = 5 : 4
Answer: 5 : 4

qs.q: A sum of money is divided among A, B, C in the ratio 3 : 2 : 5, respectively. If the share of C is Rs. 300 more than B, then how much more money will A get than B?
qs.e:
C − B = 5 − 2 = 3 parts = Rs. 300 ⇒ 1 part = Rs. 100
A − B = 3 − 2 = 1 part = Rs. 100
Answer: Rs. 100

qs.q: The curved surface area of a sphere is 1386 cm². The volume of this sphere is:
A sum of money increases to ₹7,500 after 5 years and ₹9,200 after 7 years respectively at the same rate of simple interest. Find the approximate rate of interest per annum.
If a + b + c = 7 and a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = 301, then ab + bc + ca = ?
qs.e:
a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)[(a + b + c)² − 3(ab + bc + ca)]
301 = 7 × (49 − 3S), where S = ab + bc + ca
43 = 49 − 3S ⇒ S = 2
Answer: 2

qs.q: What is the value of, sin 150° × cos 0° × tan 67° × tan 23° × tan 45°
The length of a room is 5.5 m and the width is 3.75 m. Find the cost of paving the floor with slabs at the rate of Rs. 800 per sq. meter.
ΔABC is right angled at B. If sin A = 3/5, then find the value of tan C.
qs.e:
Right angle at B, so AC is the hypotenuse.
sin A = BC/AC = 3/5 ⇒ take BC = 3, AC = 5, AB = √(25 − 9) = 4
tan C = opposite/adjacent = AB/BC = 4/3
Answer: 4/3

qs.q: P and R started a business together by investing Rs. 20000 and Rs. 15000 respectively. Total profit is Rs. 5600 after 1 year, but P donate 10% of his profit and R donate 15% of his profit. Find the total donated amount?
qs.e:
Profit ratio P : R = 20000 : 15000 = 4 : 3
P's profit = 5600 × 4/7 = 3200; R's profit = 2400
Donations = 10% of 3200 + 15% of 2400 = 320 + 360 = 680
Answer: 680

qs.q: The cost of painting a solid cone at 30 paise per cm² is ₹1056. Find the radius of the cone if its slant height is 36 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
qs.e:
A solid cone is painted all over, so use total surface area.
TSA = 1056 ÷ 0.30 = 3520 cm²
πr(l + r) = 3520 ⇒ r(36 + r) = 3520 × 7/22 = 1120
r = 20 gives 20 × 56 = 1120 ✓
Answer: 20 cm

qs.q: F and M together can do a piece of work in 8 days. F alone can do the same work in 12 days. In how many days can M alone do the same work?
qs.e:
M's one-day work = 1/8 − 1/12 = (3 − 2)/24 = 1/24
M alone takes 24 days
Answer: 24

qs.q: The volume of a prism is 308 cm³ and the height is 11 cm. The base area of the prism is:
qs.e:
Volume of prism = base area × height
Base area = 308 ÷ 11 = 28 cm²
Answer: 28 cm²

qs.q: The monthly income of a person was ₹15,400 and his monthly expenditure was ₹7,200. His income increased by 20% and his expenditure increased by 5%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
A shopkeeper marks the price of his goods at 20% higher than the cost price and allows a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage?
qs.e:
Let CP = 100 ⇒ MP = 120
SP = 120 × 0.9 = 108
Profit = 8%
Answer: 8%

qs.q: On selling 25 shirts, a retailer earns profit equal to the cost price of 8 shirts. What is the profit percentage?
qs.e:
Profit on 25 shirts = CP of 8 shirts
Profit% = 8/25 × 100 = 32%
Answer: 32

qs.q: An article is marked at ₹2,000. A shopkeeper offers a discount of 25% on the article. What is the selling price of the article after the discount?
Pipe C and D alone can fill a tank in 4 and 5 hours, respectively. If pipe C is closed after 3 hours and at the same time pipe D is opened, in how many hours will the tank get filled?
qs.e:
In 3 hours C fills 3/4 of the tank; 1/4 remains
D fills 1/5 per hour ⇒ time = (1/4) ÷ (1/5) = 5/4 = 1.25 hours
Answer: 1.25

qs.q:
Select the correct passive voice of the given sentence.
The police arrested a terrorist and sent him to jail.
o: A terrorist was arrested by police and sent to jail.
A terrorist would have been arrested by police and sent to jail.
A terrorist was arrested by police and were sent to jail.
A terrorist was arrested by police and didn not sent to jail.
qs.e:
Active: The police arrested a terrorist and sent him to jail (simple past, two verbs).
Passive of simple past = was + V3 for both verbs: 'was arrested' and '(was) sent'.
The subject 'a terrorist' is singular, so 'were sent' is wrong; 'would have been' changes the tense; 'didn not sent' is ungrammatical.
Answer: A terrorist was arrested by police and sent to jail.

qs.q:
Select the antonym for the given word.
LANGUID
qs.e:
LANGUID means weak, slow, lacking energy or spirit.
Slow and relaxed are close in meaning to it; acceptable is unrelated.
The opposite is full of energy, i.e. active.
Answer: active

qs.q:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
They said that he is not going to call them.
(Underlined segment: he is not going to call them)
o: he has not gone to call then
they are not going to call them
he was not going to call them
qs.e:
The reporting verb 'said' is in the past tense, so the reported clause must move one tense back.
'is going to' (present continuous form) becomes 'was going to'; the pronoun 'he' stays the same.
'shall', 'has gone' and 'they' either keep the wrong tense or change the meaning.
Answer: he was not going to call them

qs.q:
Complete the phrasal verb in the following sentence:
Please write _________ your name and address here.
qs.e:
'Write down' is a phrasal verb meaning to put something on paper so that it is recorded.
'Write on/in/at your name' are not idiomatic in this sense.
Answer: down

qs.q:
Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the given word.
PUERILE
qs.e:
PUERILE means childishly silly, immature, of little worth or seriousness.
Trivial (silly, unimportant) carries this sense; 'pure' and 'powerful' are unrelated.
'Innocent' is positive (free of guilt), while puerile is a criticism, so it does not fit.
Answer: Trivial

qs.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Had the management anticipated the sudden drop in market demand, they would have postponed the grand launch of the new electric sedan.
o: Had the sudden drop in market demand been anticipated by the management, the grand launch of the new electric sedan would have been postponed.
If the management anticipated the sudden drop in market demand, the grand launch of the new electric sedan would be postponed.
Had the sudden drop in market demand been anticipated by the management, they would have postponed the grand launch of the new electric sedan.
The grand launch of the new electric sedan would have been postponed by the management if they anticipated the sudden drop in demand.
qs.e:
The sentence is a third conditional with inverted 'Had': both clauses have active verbs (anticipated, would have postponed).
If-clause passive: Had the sudden drop in market demand been anticipated by the management.
Main-clause passive: the grand launch ... would have been postponed.
Option C converts only the first clause; B and D change the tense to a second conditional.
Answer: Had the sudden drop in market demand been anticipated by the management, the grand launch of the new electric sedan would have been postponed.

qs.q:
Rewrite the following sentence from active to passive.
You ought to have finished the task.
o: The task ought to have been finished by you.
The task ought to have been finish by you.
The task ought to has finished by you.
The task ought to has been finished by you.
qs.e:
Pattern: ought to have + V3 (active) becomes ought to have been + V3 (passive).
Object 'the task' becomes the subject; 'you' becomes 'by you'.
'finish' (not V3) and 'has' after 'to' are wrong.
Answer: The task ought to have been finished by you.

qs.q:
Choose the idiom from the given alternatives that best matches the following definition:
"An arbitrary and ruthless standard to which exact conformity is forced, often by using violent, unnatural, or distorting methods to alter the original data or situation."
qs.e:
A Procrustean bed comes from the Greek myth of Procrustes, who stretched or cut his guests to fit his bed.
It means an arbitrary standard to which things are forced to conform by violent or distorting means.
Sisyphean task = endless futile work; Gordian knot = intractable problem; Sword of Damocles = constant threat.
Answer: A Procrustean bed

qs.q:
Direction: Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
One to one mentorship is provided to the students by our Academy.
o: Our Academy has provided one to one mentorship to the students.
Our students providing one to one mentorship to the Academy.
Our Academy provides one to one mentorship to the students.
Our Academy is providing one to one mentorship to the students.
qs.e:
'is provided' = simple present passive (is/am/are + V3).
Its active form uses the simple present: Our Academy provides ...
'has provided' is present perfect and 'is providing' is present continuous, so they change the tense; option B reverses the meaning.
Answer: Our Academy provides one to one mentorship to the students.

qs.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.
The historian said, "But for the sudden onset of the monsoon, the army would have captured the fort by sunset."
o: The historian said that but for the sudden onset of the monsoon, the army would have captured the fort by sunset.
The historian remarked that if the monsoon did not set in suddenly, the army would have captured the fort by sunset.
The historian stated that but for the sudden onset of the monsoon, the army would had captured the fort by sunset.
The historian said that for the sudden onset of the monsoon, the army would had captured the fort by sunset.
qs.e:
The reported sentence is a third conditional ('would have captured'), which expresses an unreal past; such clauses do not change tense in indirect speech.
Reporting verb 'said' becomes 'said that'; 'but for' must be kept, since dropping it reverses the meaning.
'would had' is ungrammatical, and 'if the monsoon did not set in' wrongly mixes tenses.
Answer: The historian said that but for the sudden onset of the monsoon, the army would have captured the fort by sunset.

qs.q:
S1:The city is almost a slum and stinks most of the time.
P: The slush on the road did not deter them.
Q: The occasional slips and falls were considered a small price to pay for the trip.
R: They were excited, fascinated by the sight of fresh snow on the roads.
S: Even so, it looked beautiful to tourists of various categories.
S6:But some visitors came away with the unforgettable sight of young labours scantily clad.
qs.e:
S1 calls the city a slum; S ('Even so, it looked beautiful to tourists') contrasts with it, so S comes first.
P ('the slush did not deter them') refers back to the tourists in S.
R says why they were not deterred: they were excited by the fresh snow.
Q ends the sequence: the slips and falls were a small price to pay, which leads to S6's 'But some visitors ...'.
Answer: SPRQ
qs.p: Direction: The following passage consists of six sentences. The first and the sixth sentences are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labelled P, Q, R and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and choose the correct order from the options.

qs.q:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
CAVILLING
qs.e:
CAVILLING means raising petty or trivial objections, finding fault unnecessarily.
Captious, nitpicking and querulous (complaining) are all similar in meaning.
Laudatory means expressing praise, the opposite of fault-finding.
Answer: Laudatory

qs.q:
A. To think that a computer would one day replace a book is indeed unthinkable and far fetched.
B. The thoughts and ideas contained in a book are immortal like Tulsidas’ Ram Charitra Manas, Ved Vyas’ Mahabharata, The Bible and many other religious and literary works like Shakespeare’s plays etc.
C. On the other hand a computer is but a machine, that at best can visually display the contents of a specific book.
D. A good book in the words of John Milton “is the precious lifeblood of a master spirit, embalmed and treasured up to a purpose to a life beyond life."
qs.e:
D opens with a definition of a good book (Milton's quote).
B develops it: the ideas in books are immortal, with examples.
C contrasts with 'On the other hand a computer is but a machine'.
A concludes that a computer replacing a book is unthinkable.
Answer: DBCA
qs.p: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

qs.q:
One word substitution for:
The ability of a system to store an electric charge; the ratio of the change in an electric charge to the corresponding change in its electric potential.
qs.e:
Capacitance is the ability of a system to store electric charge, measured as change in charge ÷ change in potential (C = Q/V).
'Capacitator' is not a word (the device is a capacitor), 'capacitative' is an adjective, and 'capacity' is a general word for volume or ability.
Answer: Capacitance

qs.q: Arrogancy can cause(A)/ a person to underestimate others,(B)/ to believe they are superior and beyond reproach.(C)/ No error(D)
qs.e:
Part (A) uses 'Arrogancy', an archaic form; the standard noun is 'arrogance'.
Correct: Arrogance can cause a person to underestimate others, to believe they are superior and beyond reproach.
Parts (B) and (C) are fine; 'they' for 'a person' is accepted singular usage.
Answer: A
qs.p: Directions: Each item in this section has a sentence with three underlined parts labelled as (a), (b) and (c). Read each sentence to find out whether there is any error in any underlined part and indicate your response. on the Answer Sheet against the corresponding letter i.e., (a) or (b) or (c). If you find no error, your response should be indicated as (d).

qs.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
It is necessary to help the beggars.
o: Beggars are required to be helped.
Beggars is required to be helped.
qs.e:
'It is necessary to help the beggars' expresses obligation; its passive can be written with 'are required to be + V3'.
The plural subject 'beggars' needs 'are', not 'is'.
After 'to be' the main verb must be V3 'helped'; 'to helped' and 'required help' are ungrammatical.
Answer: Beggars are required to be helped.

qs.q: I ______ my work by the time you come back. (Put proper form of 'to finish')
qs.e:
'By the time you come back' points to a moment in the future.
An action that will be complete before a future moment takes the future perfect: will have + V3.
'will be finished' is passive in form, while 'finished' and 'had finished' are past tenses.
Answer: will have finished

qs.q:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.
Bite the bullet
o: Decide to do something that is difficult
qs.e:
'Bite the bullet' means to make yourself do something unpleasant or difficult that cannot be avoided.
It comes from patients biting a bullet to endure pain during surgery.
Answer: Decide to do something that is difficult

qs.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence into an indirect speech.
Ravi said, “My parents and I are going to have ice cream tonight.”
o: Ravi told that he and his parents are going to have ice cream tonight.
Ravi told that he and his parents were going to have ice cream that night.
Ravi told that he and his parents went to have ice cream that night.
Ravi told that he and his parents have been going to have ice cream tonight.
qs.e:
The reporting verb is past ('said'), so 'are going' becomes 'were going'.
'My parents and I' becomes 'he and his parents'; 'tonight' becomes 'that night'.
Option A keeps the tense and 'tonight', C changes the meaning to 'went', D uses the wrong tense.
Answer: Ravi told that he and his parents were going to have ice cream that night.

qs.q:
Directions: Select the option that is the direct form of the given sentence.
Nidhi exclaimed that it was a beautiful painting.
o: Nidhi said to the artist in surprise, “How beautiful you made that painting!”
Nidhi told him in wonder, “How beautiful!”
Nidhi said to the artist, “That looks like a beautiful painting!”
qs.e:
'exclaimed that it was a beautiful painting' reports an exclamation.
Direct form keeps 'exclaimed' and uses an exclamatory sentence: 'What a beautiful painting!'
The other options add details (the artist, 'you made', 'looks like') that are not in the given sentence.
Answer: Nidhi exclaimed, “What a beautiful painting!”

qs.q: What main idea does the passage primarily convey?
o: Bach combined technical precision with creative expression
Baroque composers experimented with new instruments
Musical harmony depends mainly on rhythmic patterns
qs.e:
The passage stresses Bach's control over structure and harmony (technique) and his artistic depth (creativity).
The last line says his music shows disciplined technique and artistic imagination coexisting.
The other options are either not mentioned or are details, not the main idea.
Answer: Bach combined technical precision with creative expression
qs.p:
Comprehension: (Que No. 21 - 25)
Read the passage and answer questions that follow.
Johann Sebastian Bach is widely regarded as one of the most influential composers in the history of Western music. Living in Germany during the Baroque period, Bach produced compositions that demonstrated extraordinary control over musical structure and harmony. His works often combined several independent melodic lines, a technique known as counterpoint, allowing multiple musical ideas to progress simultaneously while remaining harmonically balanced. This approach required careful planning and deep theoretical knowledge. Many of Bach’s compositions were written for church services, yet their complexity and artistic depth extended far beyond religious settings. Musicians and scholars frequently study his works to understand how precise patterns of rhythm and melody can create rich musical textures. Even centuries after his lifetime, Bach’s compositions continue to influence performers, composers, and educators. His music illustrates how disciplined technique and artistic imagination can coexist within a carefully designed musical framework.

qs.q: Which musical technique used by Bach allowed several melodies to progress simultaneously?
qs.e:
The passage says Bach combined several independent melodic lines, 'a technique known as counterpoint', so that musical ideas progress simultaneously.
Improvisation, crescendo and ornamentation are not mentioned.
Answer: Counterpoint

o: A traveller visits several countries to experience different cultures without following a planned route.
A photographer captures spontaneous street scenes without making any changes to the composition.
An architect carefully designs a building so that every structural element supports both strength and visual beauty.
A shopkeeper lowers prices during a festival to attract more customers and increase sales.
