qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 4, ?, ?, 49, 121, 169, 289
qs.e:
The terms are squares of consecutive prime numbers: 2², 3², 5², 7², 11², 13², 17².
So the missing terms are 3² = 9 and 5² = 25.
Answer: 9, 25

qs.q: National Sports University is situated in ________.
qs.e:
The National Sports University is located at Imphal, Manipur.
It was set up under the National Sports University Act, 2018 under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, to teach sports science, coaching and management.
Answer: Manipur

qs.q: Which country has the Republic feature of the Indian Constitution been borrowed from?
qs.e:
The Republic feature, where the head of state is elected and not hereditary, is usually credited to the French Constitution, along with the ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity.
From Ireland India took the DPSPs and the method of electing the President; from Britain the parliamentary system.
Answer: French Constitution

qs.q: When was the Indian Hockey Federation established?
qs.e:
The Indian Hockey Federation (IHF) was formed in 1925 (at Gwalior).
India joined the international body soon after and won its first Olympic hockey gold at Amsterdam 1928. Hockey India replaced the IHF as the governing body in 2009.
Answer: 1925

qs.q: Which of the following options is the legislative organ of the Union government?
qs.e:
The Union government has three organs: Parliament (legislature), the executive (President and Council of Ministers) and the judiciary.
Parliament, consisting of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (Article 79), makes laws for the Union.
A legislative assembly is the legislature of a state, not of the Union.
Answer: Parliament

qs.q: A bronze article having a marked price of ₹1,000 is sold during a festive season sale after three successive discounts of 20% and 30% and 10%. What will be the amount (in ₹) to be paid by a customer if she buys the article during the festival season?

In an election between Sunita and Mamata, 85% of voters cast their votes but 2% of votes were invalid. If Sunita got 64,974 votes which is 78% of valid votes, then the total number of voters enrolled in the election was:
qs.e:
Let N = enrolled voters. Votes cast = 85% of N; valid = 98% of that = 0.833N.
Sunita's 64,974 votes are 78% of valid votes → valid votes = 64974 ÷ 0.78 = 83,300.
N = 83300 ÷ 0.833 = 1,00,000.
Answer: 1,00,000

qs.q: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 20% on the marked price of an item and thus gains 10%. What is the ratio of the cost price to the marked price of the item?
qs.e:
SP = 80% of MP and SP = 110% of CP.
0.8 MP = 1.1 CP → CP/MP = 0.8/1.1 = 8/11.
Answer: 8:11

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Evaluate
qs.e:
Evaluate means to judge the value or quality of something (evaluate answer sheets). 'Assess' matches.
Unity = oneness; Misquote = repeat someone’s words wrongly; Misjudge = judge wrongly.
Answer: Assess

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The media, these days, constructs ________(misleading) narratives on politics and celebrities to increase the viewership.
qs.e:
Misleading means giving a false idea. 'Mendacious' means untruthful, lying (mendacious narratives), so it matches.
Candid = frank; Sincere = genuine; True = factual. All three are opposites of misleading.
Answer: mendacious

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Care a hang
o: Putting an outfit on a hanger
qs.e:
'(Not) care a hang' means not to care at all – to show no interest or concern.
Example: He doesn't care a hang about what the neighbours say.
'Caring too much' is the opposite, and the two options about clothes and hangers take 'hang' literally.
Answer: Showing no interest

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. Solomon’s reputation as an accountant is taintless .
qs.e:
Taintless means without any stain or blemish (a taintless record). 'Faultless' matches.
Dubious = doubtful; Inconsistent = not uniform; Flawed = having faults (the antonym).
Answer: faultless

qs.q: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, if ‘P + Q ÷ R − T × M’, which of the following is true?
o: T is the brother of P.
M is the sister of T.
P is the brother of R.
Q is the mother of M.
qs.e:
Codes: + son, – wife, × brother, ÷ mother.  P + Q ÷ R – T × M.
Generation 1: Q is the mother of P (P is her son) and of R.
Generation 2: P (male) and R are siblings; R is T's wife, and T is M's brother.
So P is the brother of R ✓. T is P's brother-in-law, M's gender is not known, and Q is not M's mother.
Answer: P is the brother of R.

qs.q: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. q p _ r _ r q _ p _ r p _ q _ p r _ p _ q

r p q r r q r p

r p q q r q r p

Other options break it at the end (e.g. …prrppq).
Answer: r p q r r q r r

Third: S, O, K, ?, C → −4 → G.
Fourth: M, O, Q, ?, U → +2 → S.
Answer: UGGS

Step 2→3: top-left→centre, top-right→middle-right, centre→bottom-left, middle-right→bottom-right, bottom-left→top-left, bottom-right→top-right.
From figure 4 (+, ☆; D, 8; N, 2): top-left N, top-right 2, centre +, middle-right ☆, bottom-left D, bottom-right 8.

qs.q: Which Indian marathon event is considered the largest marathon in Asia?
qs.e:
The Mumbai Marathon (Tata Mumbai Marathon), held every January, is the largest marathon in Asia by number of participants.
It started in 2004 and is a World Athletics Gold Label road race.
Answer: Mumbai Marathon

qs.q: In which of the following years did India NOT host the ICC Cricket World Cup Tournament?
qs.e:
India hosted (or co-hosted) the men's ODI World Cup in 1987, 1996, 2011 and 2023.
The 1983 World Cup was held in England, and India won it there under Kapil Dev.
Answer: 1983

qs.q: On which of the following dates does India celebrate its Constitution Day?
qs.e:
India marks Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) on 26 November, because the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949.
It has been observed officially since 2015; the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).
Answer: 26th November

qs.q: The organisation that Comptroller and Auditor General heads is known as ___________.
o: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
qs.e:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (Article 148) heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department (IA&AD).
The CAG audits the accounts of the Union and state governments and bodies they fund.
The Controller General of Accounts is under the Finance Ministry, and ICAI regulates chartered accountants.
Answer: Indian Audit and Accounts Department

qs.q: A dishonest merchant sells his grocery using weights that are 12% less than the true weights and makes a profit of 10%. Find his total gain percentage.
qs.e:
Take the CP of 1000 g = ₹1000. Weights 12% less → he gives only 880 g (cost ₹880).
He charges 10% profit on the claimed 1000 g → SP = ₹1100.
Gain = (1100 − 880)/880 × 100 = 220/880 × 100 = 25%.
Shortcut: (1.1/0.88 − 1) × 100 = 25%.
Answer: 25%

qs.q: In an election between two candidates P and Q, P got 78% of the total valid votes. If the total votes of the electorate were 75,60,000, then what was the number of valid votes that Q got if 10% of the voters did not cast their vote and 15% of the votes polled were declared invalid?
qs.e:
Total electorate = 75,60,000; 90% voted → 68,04,000 votes polled.
Valid = 85% of polled = 68,04,000 × 0.85 = 57,83,400.
P got 78%, so Q got 22% of valid votes = 57,83,400 × 0.22 = 12,72,348.
Answer: 12,72,348

qs.q: A shopkeeper, on the eve of Diwali, allowed a series of discounts on television sets. Find the selling price of a television set, if the marked price of television is ₹1,200 and successive discounts are 15% and 10%.
qs.e:
Successive discounts multiply: 1200 × 0.85 × 0.90.
1200 × 0.85 = 1020; 1020 × 0.9 = 918.
Answer: ₹918

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. She was overstrung before her dance performance.
qs.e:
Overstrung means very tense and anxious (overstrung before an exam). 'Nervous' matches.
Placid and Calm are the opposite; Cheerful = happy.
Answer: Nervous

qs.q: Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom. The doctors tried very hard to save his mother but they were unsuccessful.
qs.e:
'Move heaven and earth' means to make every possible effort: 'The doctors moved heaven and earth to save his mother but they were unsuccessful.'
'Face the music' = accept punishment, 'draw the line' = set a limit, 'run like clockwork' = go smoothly.
Answer: moved heaven and earth

qs.q: Identify the correct synonym of the word given below. FATIGUE
qs.e:
Fatigue means extreme tiredness after effort (fatigue after a long march). 'Tiredness' matches.
Mission = an important task; Obese = very fat; Vigour = energy and strength (the antonym).
Answer: Tiredness

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Adversity
qs.e:
Adversity means difficulty or hard times (courage in adversity). 'Misfortune' matches.
Pleasure, Success and Advantage all mean good fortune, the opposite.
Answer: Misfortune

qs.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Our legal system must frame proper legal rules for juvenile criminals.
qs.e:
'Juvenile' means young (below adult age); juvenile criminals are young offenders. So 'young' keeps the meaning.
'Dotage', 'senile' and 'old' refer to old age – the opposite.
Answer: young

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the nail on the head
o: They hit a nail with a hammer.
They have accurately identified or explained something.
qs.e:
'Hit the nail on the head' means to describe something exactly right or identify the real cause of a problem.
Image: striking the nail squarely, not the wood around it.
Example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the real issue was poor planning.
Hammering, headaches and uncertainty are literal or unrelated readings.
Answer: They have accurately identified or explained something.

Answer: WWCWWWCW

qs.q: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A − B means ‘A is the son of B’. A × B means ‘A is the husband of B’. A ÷ B means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is P related to T if ‘P − Q + R ÷ S × T’?
qs.e:
Codes: + wife, – son, × husband, ÷ father.  P – Q + R ÷ S × T.
Generation 1: Q is R's wife; P is Q's son, so R and Q are P's parents.
Generation 2: R is S's father, so P and S are brothers (S is male, being a husband).
S is T's husband, so P is T's husband's brother.
Answer: Husband’s brother

qs.q: Which figure should replace the question mark (?) if the following series were to be continued?
qs.e:
Two movement rules alternate; step 1→2 equals step 3→4, so step 4→5 repeats step 2→3.
Step 2→3: the top-left item leaves; top-right→top-left, top-middle→centre, centre→bottom-middle, bottom-left→top-right, bottom-middle→top-middle, bottom-right→bottom-left, and a new item comes in at bottom-right.
From figure 4 (= L B; T; V D 3): = leaves; top row B D V, centre L, bottom 3 T and new 4.
Answer: Option 1

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Number the 8 small triangles clockwise. The shaded triangle moves anticlockwise by 1, 2, 3 places in turn.
So the next move is 4 places anticlockwise: from the lower-right triangle beside the bottom edge it reaches the triangle in the top-left quarter that touches the top edge.
Answer: Option 1

qs.q: Which of the following famous Indian athletes won the Zurich Diamond League final 2022 in September 2022?
qs.e:
Neeraj Chopra won the Diamond League Final at Zurich on 8 September 2022 with a javelin throw of 88.44 m.
He became the first Indian to win a Diamond League trophy.
Answer: Neeraj Chopra

qs.q: Which of the following Table Tennis World Championship events was held in India?
qs.e:
India hosted the 19th World Table Tennis Championships in 1952 at Bombay (Mumbai).
India hosted the event again in 1975 (Calcutta). The 1950, 1951 and 1953 championships were held in Europe (Budapest, Vienna, Bucharest).
Answer: 19th World Championships, 1952

qs.q: Who among the following, while praising the amending feature of the Indian Constitution said that ‘This variety in the amending process is wise but is rarely found’?
qs.e:
K. C. Wheare, the British constitutional expert, praised the mix of methods for amending the Indian Constitution (simple majority, special majority, and special majority plus state ratification).
He said such variety in the amending process is wise but rarely found; he also called India "quasi-federal".
Granville Austin called the Constitution "a seamless web" and a "social document".
Answer: K C Wheare

qs.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India expressly provides that the President is eligible for re-election?
qs.e:
Article 57 says a person who holds, or has held, the office of President is eligible for re-election to that office.
There is no limit on terms in India (Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected twice); in the USA the President is limited to two terms.
Article 56 is term of office, 58 qualifications and 59 conditions of office.
Answer: Article 57

qs.q: Which of the following cups/trophies is NOT related to the Indian domestic cricket?
qs.e:
Ranji, Duleep and Deodhar Trophies are domestic cricket competitions in India.
The Durand Cup is a football tournament, started in 1888 at Shimla; it is the oldest football tournament in Asia.
Answer: Durand Cup

qs.q: The cost price of a bat is 75% of the marked price. Calculate the gain percentage after allowing a discount of 15%.
qs.e:
Take MP = 100, so CP = 75.
SP after 15% discount = 85.
Gain = 10/75 × 100 = 13.33%.
Answer: 13.33%

qs.q: The salary of a worker is first increased by 25%, then it is decreased by 12%. The percentage change in his salary is:
qs.e:
Successive change: take salary 100.
100 × 1.25 = 125; 125 × 0.88 = 110.
Net = +10%.
Shortcut: a + b + ab/100 = 25 − 12 − 3 = +10%.
Answer: 10% increase

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Merit
qs.e:
Merit means the quality of being good or deserving praise (selection on merit). 'Virtue' (a good quality) matches.
Fatigue = tiredness; Residue = what is left over; Oblique = slanting, indirect.
Answer: Virtue

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Layla is the Sultan’s consort.
qs.e:
Consort means a wife, husband or companion, especially of a ruler (the queen’s consort). 'Partner' matches.
Alcoholic = addicted to alcohol; Foe and Enemy = opponent, the opposite of a companion.
Answer: Partner

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Jump the gun
o: To do something too soon and too quickly
qs.e:
'Jump the gun' means to act too soon, before the proper time.
Origin: a runner who starts before the starting pistol is fired.
Example: The company jumped the gun by announcing the product before it was tested.
It does not mean starting again, stopping, or using a gun for sport.
Answer: To do something too soon and too quickly

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To read between the lines
o: To understand more than what the words suggest
qs.e:
'To read between the lines' means to understand the hidden meaning beyond what is actually written or said.
Example: Her letter sounded cheerful, but reading between the lines, I knew she was lonely.
Reading aloud, reading differently or underlining are literal readings and miss the 'hidden meaning' idea.
Answer: To understand more than what the words suggest

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Jovial
qs.e:
Jovial means cheerful and friendly (a jovial host). 'Cheerful' matches.
Profane = disrespectful to sacred things; Solemnity = seriousness; Miserable = very unhappy (the antonym).
Answer: Cheerful

qs.q: Select the figure from among the given options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically completethe series.

Next: 2 + 5 = 7, the bottom-left; the grid stays the same.

qs.q: In a certain code language, R + T means ‘R is the sister of T’. R – T means ‘R is the father of T’. R * T means ‘R is the wife of T’. R ÷ T means ‘R is the mother of T’. Based on the above, how is M related to Q if ‘M * N – P + Q ÷ R +T’?
qs.e:
Codes: + sister, – father, * wife, ÷ mother.  M * N – P + Q ÷ R + T.
Generation 1: M is N's wife; N is P's father, so M is P's mother.
Generation 2: P is Q's sister, so Q is also a child of M and N; Q is the mother of R (and R's sister T).
So M is Q's mother.
Answer: Mother

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 12, 25, 49, ?, 197, 395

The last four letters 'YNFJ' stay the same while the first letter goes back 2 each time: B, Z, X, V.
Answer: FZJYN

qs.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state?
qs.e:
Article 166 deals with conduct of business of the Government of a state: all executive action is taken in the Governor's name, and the Governor makes rules for its convenient transaction.
It is the state-level counterpart of Article 77.
Article 164 is about appointment of ministers and Article 167 about the Chief Minister's duty to inform the Governor.
Answer: Article 166

qs.q: In May 2022, Then President Ram Nath Kovind appointed _________ as the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
qs.e:
In May 2022 President Ram Nath Kovind appointed Vinai Kumar Saxena, then Chairman of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, as the 22nd Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
He replaced Anil Baijal, who resigned; Kiran Bedi had been the LG of Puducherry.
Answer: Vinai Kumar Saxena

qs.q: Which of the following Constitutions inspired the law-making process in India?
qs.e:
India borrowed the parliamentary system from Britain, including the law-making procedure, rule of law, single citizenship and cabinet system.
From the USA it took Fundamental Rights and judicial review; from Ireland the DPSPs; from Canada a federation with a strong Centre.
Answer: British Constitution

qs.q: How many players are there on each side of the Kabaddi Team in the field?
qs.e:
A kabaddi team has 7 players on the court at a time (12 in the squad, 5 substitutes).
A raider from one side enters the opponent's half and tries to touch defenders while chanting 'kabaddi' on one breath.
Answer: 7

qs.q: Which of the following terms is NOT related to cricket?
qs.e:
No ball, wide ball and wicket are cricket terms.
Deuce is a tennis (and badminton/table tennis) term for a tie at 40-40 or its equivalent, after which one side must win two points in a row.
Answer: Deuce

qs.q: Naman bought few apples for ₹720 from a shop. He negotiated the price and the shopkeeper reduced it by ₹2 per apple. Due to this Naman could buy four more apples than what he had bought earlier. How many apples did he originally buy?
qs.e:
Let him buy x apples first: price per apple = 720/x.
720/x − 720/(x + 4) = 2 → 720 × 4 = 2x(x + 4) → x² + 4x − 1440 = 0.
(x + 40)(x − 36) = 0 → x = 36.
Check: ₹20 each for 36 apples, ₹18 each for 40 apples.
Answer: 36

qs.q: If Ram purchases a fan, he gets 8% discount, however, if he purchases three fans he gets 6% on the first, 10% on the second and 12% on the third. If the price paid by the Ram for three fans is ₹6,800, then what will be the marked price of each fan?
qs.e:
Let the marked price of one fan be M.
Price for three = 0.94M + 0.90M + 0.88M = 2.72M = 6800.
M = 6800 ÷ 2.72 = ₹2,500.
Answer: ₹2,500

The woman spends 2/3 of her income. Take income = 300: expenditure = 200, savings = 100.
New income = 300 × 1.18 = 354; new expenditure = 200 × 1.24 = 248.
New savings = 354 − 248 = 106.
Increase = 6/100 × 100 = 6%.
Answer: 6%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Expertise
qs.e:
Expertise means expert skill or knowledge (technical expertise). 'Proficiency' matches.
Clumsiness = awkwardness; Lack = absence; Ignorance = lack of knowledge. All three are opposites.
Answer: Proficiency

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. The________(crux) of his argument was that education should continue throughout life.
qs.e:
Crux means the most important or central point (the crux of the matter). 'Essence' matches.
Etiquette = rules of polite behaviour; Proposal = a suggested plan; Draft = a rough version.
Answer: essence

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bold word in the following sentence. His eloquent speech always persuades people to work for their betterment.
qs.e:
Eloquent means fluent and persuasive in speaking (an eloquent speaker). 'Articulate' (expressing oneself clearly and effectively) matches.
Vague = unclear; Inarticulate = unable to speak clearly (the antonym); Short = brief.
Answer: Articulate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Nobody’s fool
qs.e:
'Nobody's fool' describes a sensible person who cannot easily be tricked or deceived.
Example: Don't try to cheat Grandma at cards – she is nobody's fool.
It does not claim the person is 'the wisest' of all, and 'a complete fool' / 'all are fools' are the opposite.
Answer: Not easily deceived

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A dime a dozen
qs.e:
'A dime a dozen' means very common, cheap and nothing special.
Origin: in the US, goods so plentiful that twelve sold for a dime (ten cents).
Example: Coaching ads are a dime a dozen; a good teacher is rare.
It has nothing to do with wealth, amenities or fair trade.
Answer: Something common and not special

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Paramount
qs.e:
Paramount means more important than anything else (safety is paramount). 'Supreme' matches.
Trivial = unimportant; Collateral = secondary, additional; Inferior = lower in rank. These are opposites.
Answer: supreme

qs.q: Select the number from the given options to complete the series. 25, 30, 40, 55, 75, ___
qs.e:
Differences: 5, 10, 15, 20 (multiples of 5).
Next difference = 25: 75 + 25 = 100.

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of ‘?’ will logically complete the series.
qs.e:

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is 4 related to 2 if ‘4 + 3 ÷ 2 ÷ 1 − 5’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, × wife, ÷ father.  4 + 3 ÷ 2 ÷ 1 – 5.
Generation 1: 4 is 3's mother.
Generation 2: 3 is 2's father.
Generation 3: 2 is 1's father, and 1 is 5's brother.
4 is the mother of 2's father.
Answer: Father’s mother

qs.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that ‘there shall be a Vice President of India’?
qs.e:
Article 63 says "There shall be a Vice-President of India".
Article 64 makes the Vice-President ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and Article 65 lets the Vice-President act as President when needed.
Article 61 is impeachment of the President and 62 the time of holding elections.
Answer: Article 63

qs.q: A student, on his school assignment, is taking a session on how to make compost at home for using it at a park. Which fundamental duty is he performing?
o: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
To protect and improve the natural environment
To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
qs.e:
Making compost from kitchen waste reduces garbage and enriches soil, so teaching it protects the environment.
This matches Article 51A(g): to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
Answer: To protect and improve the natural environment

qs.q: India won the ICC Men Cricket World Cup for the first time in which of the following years?
qs.e:
India won the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup for the first time in 1983, beating West Indies in the final at Lord's, England.
The captain was Kapil Dev; India's second title came in 2011 under MS Dhoni.
Answer: 1983

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT an amendment made to the Airport Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) Amendment Act, 2021?
o: The government can call any airport a major airport just by notification.
A major airport is one which has an annual traffic of minimum 35 lakh passengers.
The government will club together profit-making and loss-making airports.
The government can offer airports as a package in PPP mode to the prospective bidders.
qs.e:
The AERA (Amendment) Act, 2021 let the government declare any airport a major airport by notification, and let it club profit-making and loss-making airports and offer them as a package under PPP.
The definition of a major airport as one with annual passenger traffic over 35 lakh was already in the original AERA Act, 2008; the amendment did not introduce it.
Answer: A major airport is one which has an annual traffic of minimum 35 lakh passengers.

qs.q: In which year did India make its Olympic debut in hockey?
qs.e:
India made its Olympic hockey debut at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics and won gold, with Jaipal Singh Munda as captain and Dhyan Chand the top scorer.
It was the first of six straight Olympic hockey golds (1928-1956).
Answer: 1928

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Acquiesce
qs.e:
Acquiesce means to accept or agree quietly, without protest (he acquiesced to their demand). 'Concur' (agree) matches.
Thwart = prevent, block; Cease and Desist = stop.
Answer: Concur

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. In my new office, all employees were different, so I felt like a fish out of water.
qs.e:
'Like a fish out of water' means feeling uncomfortable or awkward in unfamiliar surroundings.
In a new office with very different colleagues, the speaker felt out of place – uncomfortable.
Disappointed and frustrated describe other emotions; homeless is a literal and wrong reading.
Answer: Uncomfortable

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. During Covid times, many organisations made ________(sentimental) appeals to raise funds for migrant workers.
qs.e:
Sentimental means appealing to tender feelings, often excessively. 'Mawkish' means sentimental in an exaggerated way, so it matches.
Practical = realistic; Cynical = distrustful of others’ motives; Sincere = genuine.
Answer: mawkish

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. His ambition in life is to become a happy and satisfied man.
qs.e:
Ambition means a strong desire to achieve something (her ambition is to be a doctor). 'Eagerness' (strong desire) is closest.
Amend = correct, change; Satisfaction = contentment after a desire is met; Apathy = lack of interest (the antonym).
Answer: Eagerness

qs.q: Read the sentence carefully and select the most suitable idiom to fill in the blank. The renowned publisher decided to withdraw a book from the market. No one was interested in the book as the arguments presented were ____________.
qs.e:
'Beside the mark' means irrelevant, not to the point (like an arrow that misses the target).
No one was interested in the book because its arguments were irrelevant, so the publisher withdrew it.
Under the rose = in secret; high and mighty = arrogant; out of the woods = out of danger – none fits arguments that failed to interest readers.
Answer: beside the mark

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. He is an atheist, although he respects everyone’s belief.
o: One who does not believe in God
qs.e:
An atheist is a person who does not believe in God (a- = without, theos = god).
One who believes in God is a theist (the opposite); one who worships nature is a pantheist or naturist; an extremist holds extreme views.
Answer: One who does not believe in God

qs.q: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, how is P related to R if ‘P × S ÷ M − T + R’?

Codes: + son, – wife, × brother, ÷ daughter.  P × S ÷ M – T + R.

Generation 2: M is T's wife; S is M's daughter, and P is S's brother, so P is a son of T.

qs.q: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. E_GHEI_GELK_ _OME

So the blanks are F, I, F, E.
Answer: FIFE

qs.q: Identify the figure from the given options, which when put in place of the question mark (?), will logically complete the series.

From figure 4 (↑, △; $; D, +): top-left D, centre ↑, bottom-left $, top-right +, bottom-right △.

qs.q: Who among the following players is related to table tennis?
qs.e:
Manika Batra is India's leading woman table tennis player; she won four medals, including singles gold, at the 2018 Commonwealth Games.
Pankaj Advani plays billiards/snooker, K Srikanth badminton, and Manish Narwal is a para shooter.
Answer: Manika Batra

qs.q: The Election Laws Amendment Bill passed in the Parliament recently seeks to implement certain electoral reforms. One of them is the eligibility date. Till now, only one date – 1 January was considered for deciding eligibility with respect to age. What reform does the Bill seek in this regard?
o: Eliminating the idea of eligibility date – enrolment throughout the year
Introducing three dates – 1 January, 1 May, 1 September
Introducing four dates – 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October
Introducing two dates – 1 January and 1 June
qs.e:
The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 allows four qualifying dates in a year for voter enrolment: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.
Earlier, someone turning 18 just after 1 January had to wait almost a year to enrol.
The same Act also allowed linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar on a voluntary basis.
Answer: Introducing four dates – 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty of the Indian citizens?
o: To cherish and follow the noble ideas that inspired our national struggle for freedom.
To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
qs.e:
The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) include cherishing the ideals of the freedom struggle, developing scientific temper, and safeguarding public property while abjuring violence.
They include defending the country and rendering national service when called upon, but there is no compulsory national service of any fixed period.
Answer: Mandatory national service of 5 years.

qs.q: In which of the following years was Pro Kabaddi League established in India?
qs.e:
The Pro Kabaddi League began in 2014 (first season July-August 2014), run by Mashal Sports with Star Sports.
Jaipur Pink Panthers won the first season.
Answer: 2014

qs.q: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.
qs.e:
Article 207 says a Money Bill in a state legislature can be introduced only on the recommendation of the Governor, and only in the Legislative Assembly.
It is the state version of Article 117, under which the President's recommendation is needed in Parliament.
Answer: Governor

qs.q: The MP of an article was Rs.180 and it was sold at a discount of 15%, the discount in Rs. is:
qs.e:
Discount = 15% of marked price.
0.15 × 180 = ₹27.
Answer: 27

qs.q: Every month, a man consumes 20 kg of rice and 8 kg of wheat. The price of rice is 20% of the price of wheat, resulting in a total expenditure of ₹300 per month for rice and wheat combined. If the price of wheat is increased by 20%, what percentage reduction in rice consumption is needed to maintain the same expenditure of ₹300? (Given that price of rice and consumption of wheat is constant.)
qs.e:
Let wheat price = w, rice price = 0.2w. 20 × 0.2w + 8w = 300 → 12w = 300 → w = ₹25, rice = ₹5.
Rice costs 20 × 5 = ₹100, wheat 8 × 25 = ₹200.
Wheat rises 20% → 8 × 30 = ₹240, leaving ₹60 for rice → 60 ÷ 5 = 12 kg.
Reduction = (20 − 12)/20 × 100 = 40%.
Answer: 40%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Many people love to visit enchanting hills.
qs.e:
Enchanting means delightfully charming, attractive (an enchanting view). 'Alluring' (attractive, tempting) matches.
Risky = dangerous; Echoing = repeating sound; Cool = slightly cold. None means charming.
Answer: alluring

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. Listening to the same lecture everyday appeared very ___________ to him. (boring)
qs.e:
Boring means dull and uninteresting. 'Monotonous' (dull because unchanging, the same every day) fits the repeated lecture.
Furious = very angry; Monolithic = massive and uniform (like a single block); Nervous = anxious.
Answer: monotonous

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Repulse
qs.e:
Repulse means to drive back or push away (repulse an attack). 'Repel' matches.
Substitute = replace; Recover = get back; Reprove = scold.
Answer: Repel

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the father of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, how is K related to O if ‘K ÷ L − M + N × O’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – husband, × father, ÷ daughter.  K ÷ L – M + N × O.
Generation 1: L is M's husband; K is L's daughter and N is M's child, so K and N are siblings.
Generation 2: N is O's father.
K is the sister of O's father.
Answer: Father’s sister

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 13, ?, 145, 721, 4321
The concept of Public Interest Litigation originated in _______________.
qs.e:
Public Interest Litigation began in the USA in the 1960s, where it was used to give legal representation to poor and unrepresented groups.
In India it was developed in the late 1970s-80s by Justices V. R. Krishna Iyer and P. N. Bhagwati, with relaxed rules on who may file a case.
Answer: USA

qs.q: Which of the following nations won the seven times women’s Asia Cup cricket Championship?
qs.e:
India has won the Women's Asia Cup (cricket) seven times: 2004, 2005-06, 2006, 2008, 2012, 2016 (T20) and 2022.
India dominated the event from its start in 2004; Bangladesh won in 2018 and Sri Lanka won its first title in 2024.
Answer: India

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the State must secure a social order to promote the welfare of people?
qs.e:
Article 38 directs the State to secure a social order in which social, economic and political justice informs all institutions, to promote people's welfare, and to reduce inequalities in income and status.
Article 36 defines "State", 37 says DPSPs are non-justiciable, and 39 lists specific policy principles.
Answer: Article 38

qs.q: When and where did India win its first World Championships medal in Athletics?
qs.e:
Anju Bobby George won bronze in long jump at the 2003 World Athletics Championships in Paris, France.
It was India's first-ever medal at the World Championships in Athletics; Neeraj Chopra later won silver (2022) and gold (2023).
Answer: 2003, France

qs.q: The difference between a discount of 25% and two successive discounts of 15% and 20% on a certain bill was ₹28. Find the amount of the bill.
qs.e:
Successive 15% and 20%: single equivalent = 15 + 20 − 3 = 32%.
Difference from a single 25% discount = 32 − 25 = 7% of the bill.
7% = ₹28 → bill = 28 × 100/7 = ₹400.
Answer: ₹400

qs.q: The profit gained on selling a certain product is 320% of the cost. If the cost increases by 10% but the selling price remains constant, then what percentage of the selling price is the profit (correct to one decimal place)?
qs.e:
Take CP = 100: profit = 320, so SP = 420.
New CP = 110, SP still 420 → profit = 310.
Profit as % of SP = 310/420 × 100 = 73.8%.
Answer: 73.8%

qs.q: A merchant mixes two varieties of sugar of 5 kg and 3 kg, which costs him ₹4 and ₹6 per kg, respectively. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the mixture per kg?
qs.e:
Cost per kg of mixture = total cost ÷ total weight.
= (5 × 4 + 3 × 6)/(5 + 3) = (20 + 18)/8 = 38/8 = ₹4.75.
Answer: 4.75

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Anand personally believes in the motto, “When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.”
o: Earn the maximum out of business
Enjoy the most when the season is favourable
Make the best out of difficult situations
qs.e:
'When life gives you lemons, make lemonade' means to make the best of a bad or difficult situation – turn something sour into something useful.
Example: After losing his job, he started his own bakery – real lemonade from lemons.
It is not about business profits, health or enjoying good seasons.
Answer: Make the best out of difficult situations
qs.u: When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. How did we end up in this rapturous situation?
qs.e:
Rapturous means full of great joy and delight (rapturous applause). 'Ecstatic' matches.
Terrifying = frightening; Misleading = giving a false idea; Disastrous = very harmful. These do not convey joy.
Answer: ecstatic

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Rectify
qs.e:
Rectify means to put right, correct (rectify a mistake). 'Amend' matches.
Mar = spoil; Corrupt = make bad; Upset = disturb. These are opposite in sense.
Answer: amend

qs.q: In a certain code language, X + Y means ‘X is the father of Y’, X − Y means ‘X is the brother of Y’, X × Y means ‘X is the sister of Y’, X ÷ Y means ‘X is the wife of Y’. Based on the above, how is D related to H if ‘D × E ÷ F + G − H’?

qs.q: Which team won the T20 cricket event, Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2022-2023?
qs.e:
Mumbai won the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy 2022-23, beating Himachal Pradesh in the final at Kolkata (November 2022).
It was Mumbai's first title in this domestic T20 competition; Himachal is the tempting option as the runner-up.
Answer: Mumbai

qs.q: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from Irish Constitution?
qs.e:
The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (1937), which in turn took the idea from Spain.
Ireland also gave India the method of electing the President and nominating members to the Rajya Sabha.
Fundamental Rights came from the USA, Rule of Law from Britain and the Concurrent List from Australia.
Answer: Directive Principles of State Policy

qs.q: Who among the following famous Indian women cricketers announced retirement in June 2022?
qs.e:
Mithali Raj announced her retirement from all forms of international cricket on 8 June 2022.
She is the highest run-scorer in women's international cricket and captained India in two ODI World Cup finals (2005, 2017). Jhulan Goswami retired later, in September 2022.
Answer: Mithali Raj

qs.q: The Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice and not more than ______ other Judges appointed by the President of India.
qs.e:
After the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, the Supreme Court has the Chief Justice and not more than 33 other judges, a total strength of 34.
The original Constitution allowed 7 other judges; Parliament has increased the number by law under Article 124(1).
Answer: 33

qs.q: Who won the paralympic bronze medal in archery for India at Tokyo in 2020?
qs.e:
Harvinder Singh won the bronze medal in men's individual recurve archery at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.
It was India's first-ever Paralympic medal in archery. Deepika Kumari, Atanu Das and Pravin Jadhav are Olympic (not para) archers.
Answer: Harvinder Singh

qs.q: For which of the following states was the Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, introduced in the Parliament?
qs.e:
The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced for Uttar Pradesh.
It moved the Gond community in four districts (Chandauli, Kushinagar, Sant Kabir Nagar and Sant Ravidas Nagar) from the SC list to the ST list; it was passed in 2022.
Answer: Uttar Pradesh

qs.q: An article is sold at a profit of 250%. What is the ratio of its cost price to selling price?
qs.e:
Profit 250% → SP = CP + 2.5 CP = 3.5 CP.
CP : SP = 1 : 3.5 = 2 : 7.
Answer: 2 : 7

qs.q: A shopkeeper mixes two types of rice costing ₹250/5 kg and ₹280/5 kg in the ratio 7 : 8. Find the net cost of the resultant mixture (per kg).
In an election between R and S, R gets 110% of the votes of S and beats S by 770 votes. If there were no invalid votes, then the total number of votes polled is:
qs.e:
Let S get x votes; R gets 110% of x = 1.1x.
Margin = 1.1x − x = 0.1x = 770 → x = 7700.
R = 8470; total votes = 7700 + 8470 = 16170.
Shortcut: total = 2.1x = 21 × 770 = 16170.
Answer: 16170

qs.q: If the successive discount by 10%,15%, then the single equivalent rate of discount is:
qs.e:
Single equivalent of a% and b% = a + b − ab/100.
10 + 15 − (10 × 15)/100 = 25 − 1.5 = 23.5%.
Answer: 23.5%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A bad patch
o: A dangerous road to walk on
A person who takes a difficult path
A period of time when a person faces lots of troubles
qs.e:
'A bad patch' is a period of time during which a person faces many difficulties or problems.
Example: The business went through a bad patch after the floods but has now recovered.
'Patch' here means a stretch of time, not a road or path, so the options about paths and roads are literal misreadings.
Answer: A period of time when a person faces lots of troubles

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Turned a deaf ear to
qs.e:
'To turn a deaf ear to' something means to refuse to listen to it – to disregard or ignore it.
Example: He turned a deaf ear to his doctor's warnings.
Rebuked = scolded; 'by any means' and 'at intervals' are unrelated phrases.
Answer: Disregarded

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’, ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’, ‘A / B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A * B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. Which of the following means P is the Son's wife of T? i. T / B – K * P + O ii. T + K * P + B % O iii. K * P + B % T + P iv. P + T * K + B % O
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – father, $ son, % sister, / wife, * husband. We need P to be the wife of T's son.
i. T / B – K * P + O: T is B's wife and B is K's father, so K is T's son; K is P's husband → P is T's son's wife ✓.
ii. T + K * P + B % O: T is K's mother and K is P's husband → P is T's son's wife ✓.
iii. K * P + B % T + P contradicts itself (P is mother of B and child of T); iv. P + T makes P T's mother — both fail.
Answer: Both i and ii

qs.q: Indian Olympic Association was established in which of the following years?
qs.e:
The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was set up in 1927, with Sir Dorabji Tata as its first president and A.G. Noehren as secretary.
It selects and sends Indian teams to the Olympics, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games.
Answer: 1927

qs.q: Which of following is NOT a device of parliamentary proceedings?
qs.e:
Parliamentary devices include Question Hour, Zero Hour, half-an-hour discussion, short duration (two-hour) discussion, calling attention motion and adjournment motion.
There is no device called a full-day discussion in the rules of procedure.
Answer: Full-day discussion

qs.q: Which of the following Articles deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?
qs.e:
Article 80 deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha: up to 250 members, of whom 12 are nominated by the President and up to 238 represent states and UTs.
Article 81 is the composition of Lok Sabha, 84 the qualifications for membership and 92 the Chairman not presiding when a removal motion is pending.
Answer: Article 80

qs.q: Which Article in the fundamental duty applies, when a construction worker takes his 8- year son to the site rather than sending him to school?
qs.e:
Article 51A(k), added by the 86th Amendment (2002), makes it a duty of a parent or guardian to give opportunities for education to their child between 6 and 14 years.
By taking his 8-year-old son to the site instead of school, the worker fails this duty.
51A(h) is about scientific temper, (i) public property and (j) striving for excellence.
Answer: Article 51A (k)

qs.q: P and Q are two fixed points 10 cm apart, and R is a point on PQ such that PR = 6 cm. By what percentage is the length of QR decreased when the length of PR is increased by 5%?
qs.e:
PQ = 10 cm, PR = 6 cm, so QR = 4 cm.
PR increases by 5% → 6.3 cm, so QR = 10 − 6.3 = 3.7 cm.
Decrease in QR = 0.3/4 × 100 = 7.5%.
Answer: 7.5%

qs.q: A discount series of 10% and 16% on an invoice is the same as a single discount of:
qs.e:
Single equivalent of a% and b% = a + b − ab/100.
10 + 16 − (10 × 16)/100 = 26 − 1.6 = 24.4%.
Answer: 24.4%

qs.q: Ramesh sells rice at ₹36 per kg, which he purchased for ₹30 per kg. Moreover, he gives only 800 g of rice instead of 1 kg while selling. Find the actual profit percentage of Ramesh.
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Celebrate
qs.e:
Celebrate means to mark a happy occasion with joy (celebrate a victory). 'Rejoice' matches.
Assure = promise, make certain; Daunt = discourage; 'Bitch' is slang for to complain.
Answer: Rejoice

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. All his friends admired him because he was a straight shooter.
qs.e:
'A straight shooter' is an honest, upright and straightforward person who says what he means.
That is why his friends admired him.
It is not about shooting skill (literal), and 'miserly' or 'complicated' people are the opposite of what is praised.
Answer: A thoroughly upright straightforward person

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. My uncle lives in New York, so I only see him once in a blue moon.
qs.e:
'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely.
Origin: a 'blue moon' is an extra full moon that happens only about once in two to three years.
Since the uncle lives far away in New York, the speaker sees him rarely.
Monthly, weekly and very often all suggest regular meetings, the opposite of the idiom.
Answer: Not very often

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. One of Ram’s leisure activities is tennis.
qs.e:
Leisure means free time spent on enjoyment (leisure activities = hobbies). 'Recreation' (activity done for enjoyment) matches.
Languish = grow weak; Main = chief; Lead = guide.
Answer: Recreation

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'A ? B' means ‘A is the mother of B’, 'A ! B' means ‘A is the wife of B’, 'A & B' means ‘A is the brother of B’ and 'A x B' means ‘A is the father of B’. Which of the following means that Z is the wife's father's mother of L?
o: Z ? B x T & J ! L
Z ? B ! T & J x L
Z ! B x T ? J & L
Z & B ! T x J ? L
qs.e:
Codes: ? mother, ! wife, & brother, x father. Needed chain: L's wife → her father → his mother = Z.
Z ? B x T & J ! L: Generation 1: Z is B's mother.

Generation 3: J is L's wife. So Z is the mother of the father of L's wife ✓.
Answer: Z ? B x T & J ! L

qs.q: In which of the following years will India host the World Badminton Championship?
qs.e:
The Badminton World Federation awarded the 2026 BWF World Championships to India (New Delhi).
India had hosted the World Championships only once before, at Hyderabad in 2009.
Answer: 2026

qs.q: Who was the player of the match in the semi-final of the T20 Women's World Cup 2023 played between India and Australia?
qs.e:
In the 2023 Women's T20 World Cup semi-final at Cape Town, Australia (172/4) beat India (167/8) by 5 runs.
Ashleigh Gardner was Player of the Match for her all-round display (an unbeaten 31 off 18 balls, plus useful overs with the ball); Harmanpreet Kaur's 52 for India was not enough.
Answer: Ashleigh Gardner

qs.q: Who among the following won a Gold Medal at the 2021 World Cadet Wrestling Championship held in Budapest, Hungary?
qs.e:
Priya Malik won the gold medal in the 73 kg category at the 2021 World Cadet Wrestling Championship in Budapest, Hungary.
Vinesh and Geeta Phogat are senior wrestlers, not cadets in 2021.
Answer: Priya Malik

qs.q: How many members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha?
qs.e:
Under Article 80, the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from people with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.
This idea was taken from the Irish Constitution; the Lok Sabha no longer has nominated Anglo-Indian members after the 104th Amendment (2019).
Answer: 12

qs.q: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described Directive Principles of State Policy as __________of the Indian constitution.
o: The mostprecious part of the constitution
a novel feature of the constitution
qs.e:
Dr B. R. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles of State Policy as "novel features" of the Indian Constitution.
He also called Article 32 the "heart and soul" of the Constitution; Granville Austin called DPSPs and Fundamental Rights the "conscience" of the Constitution.
Answer: a novel feature of the constitution

qs.q: As per article 123, the ordinance making power is the most important legislative power of ____________.
qs.e:
Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when either House of Parliament is not in session and immediate action is needed.
An ordinance has the same force as an Act of Parliament but must be approved within six weeks of Parliament reassembling.
The Governor has a similar power for states under Article 213.
Answer: President

qs.q: Kalyan spends 80% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure also increases by 5%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:
qs.e:
Take income = 100: expenditure 80, savings 20.
New income = 115, new expenditure = 80 × 1.05 = 84.
New savings = 115 − 84 = 31.
Increase = 11/20 × 100 = 55%.
Answer: 55%

qs.q: A dishonest fruit-seller sells fruits at 20% profit but he uses 950 gm weight in place of 1 kg. What is the profit per cent?

A manufacturer announces a trade discount of 30% on his products for his dealers. One of the dealers purchased 6 smart phones manufactured by the company at the rate of Rs.25,000 each. What is the amount of trade discount?
qs.e:
List price of 6 phones = 6 × 25000 = ₹1,50,000.
Trade discount = 30% of 1,50,000 = ₹45,000.
Answer: Rs.45,000

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Radhika stood by Monica’s side through thick and thin.
o: Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica’s safety and security
In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time
In the moments when Monica couldn’t complete some simple tasks
Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult
qs.e:
'Through thick and thin' means under all conditions, in good times and bad, however hard things get.
Origin: a hunter riding through thick woods and thin (open) country alike.
Radhika stayed loyal to Monica in every situation.
Options 1–3 restrict her support to easy, happy or trivial moments – the opposite of the idiom.
Answer: Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. His approach was filled with such perseverance that it was difficult to overlook his merit.
qs.e:
Perseverance means continued effort despite difficulty (success through perseverance). 'Doggedness' (tenacious persistence) matches.
Reluctance = unwillingness; Ignorance = lack of knowledge; Monotonous = dull and repetitive (an adjective).
Answer: Doggedness

qs.e:
Each step: the centre number moves to top-left, top-left → top-right, top-right → bottom-right, bottom-right → bottom-left, the old bottom-left number drops out and a new number comes to the centre.
Check figure 1→2: 5 goes to top-left, 2 to top-right, 1 to bottom-right, 0 to bottom-left, 3 drops out.
From figure 4 (6, 4; 7; 2, 5): top-left 7, top-right 6, bottom-right 4, bottom-left 5, new centre.
Answer: Option 2

qs.q: Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. PJ 16, SM 25, VP 36, YS 49, ?
qs.e:
First letters P, S, V, Y go up by 3 → B (wrap past Z).
Second letters J, M, P, S go up by 3 → V.
Numbers 16, 25, 36, 49 are 4², 5², 6², 7² → 8² = 64.
Answer: BV 64

qs.q: G is the brother of F. E is the father of K.. C is the daughter of A. F is the mother of E. C is the sister of E. How is G related to A?
qs.e:
Generation 1: F is the mother of E; C is E's sister, so F is C's mother too. C is the daughter of A, so A is C's father — F's husband.
G is F's brother.
Generation 2: E and C (E is K's father).
So G is the brother of A's wife.
Answer: Wife’s brother

qs.q: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? BKUZ, ENWB, ?, KTAF, NWCH
qs.e:
Check each position (A=1).
First: B, E, ?, K, N → +3 → H.
Second: K, N, ?, T, W → +3 → Q.
Third: U, W, ?, A, C → +2 → Y.
Fourth: Z, B, ?, F, H → +2 → D.
Answer: HQYD

qs.q: Select the figure from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) and logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Lines inside the diamond increase by one each time: 0, 1, 2, 3, so next 4 (both diagonals added, eight parts).
The circle moves clockwise round the diamond: top-left, top, top-right, right, so next bottom-right.
Answer: Option 3

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 96,77,60,47,36, ?
qs.e:
Differences: −19, −17, −13, −11 – the prime numbers in falling order.
Next prime below 11 is 7: 36 − 7 = 29.
Answer: 29

qs.q: When was pro kabaddi league inaugurated for the first time in India?
qs.e:
The Pro Kabaddi League was inaugurated in 2014; its first season ran in July-August 2014 and Jaipur Pink Panthers won it.
It follows the city-franchise model of the IPL and revived interest in the sport.
Answer: 2014

qs.q: Who among the following Indian women boxers was elected as the Chairperson and a voting member of the International Boxing Association in 2022?
qs.e:
Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain was elected Chairperson of the IBA (International Boxing Association) Athletes' Committee in 2022, which also made her a voting member of the IBA Board.
She won bronze in the 69 kg category at Tokyo 2020.
Answer: Lovlina Borgohain

qs.q: In which of the following years was the Election Commission of India founded?
qs.e:
The Election Commission of India was set up on 25 January 1950, a day before the Constitution came into force, under Article 324.
25 January is therefore observed as National Voters' Day (since 2011); the first general elections were held in 1951-52.
Answer: 1950

qs.q: Which of the following numbers best describes the number of white pieces used in chess?
qs.e:
Each side in chess has 16 pieces: 1 king, 1 queen, 2 rooks, 2 bishops, 2 knights and 8 pawns.
So white has 16 pieces (32 on the board in all).
Answer: 16

qs.q: Which of the following duties has been NOT prescribed by the Indian Constitution as Fundamental Duties? 1. To defend the country 2. To pay income tax 3. To cast the vote in election 4. To safeguard the public property
qs.e:
Defending the country (51A(d)) and safeguarding public property (51A(i)) are Fundamental Duties.
Paying income tax and voting in elections are not listed in Article 51A (the Swaran Singh Committee had suggested a duty to pay taxes, but it was not adopted).
So statements 2 and 3 are the ones not prescribed.
Answer: 2 and 3 both

qs.q: A shopkeeper marked the price 20% more than its cost price. If he allows a discount of 30%, then find his loss percent.
qs.e:
Take CP = 100, so MP = 120.
SP after 30% discount = 120 × 0.7 = 84.
Loss = 16 → 16%.
Answer: 16%

Profit on each item = CP × profit%.
Mobile: 10% of 20,000 = ₹2,000. Laptop: 20% of 72,000 = ₹14,400. Mobile cover: 12% of 300 = ₹36.
Total profit = 2000 + 14400 + 36 = ₹16,436.
Answer: 16,436

SP ₹44.8 gives 12% profit → CP = 44.8 ÷ 1.12 = ₹40 per kg.
Take 5 kg: cost ₹200; 1/5 is damaged, leaving 4 kg.
For 5% profit the 4 kg must bring 200 × 1.05 = ₹210 → price = 210 ÷ 4 = ₹52.5 per kg.
Answer: ₹52.5

qs.q: In a company, all employees are getting equal wages. If the number of employees is increased by 20% and their wages per head are decreased by 18%, what is the percentage decrease in total wages?
qs.e:
Total wages = number of employees × wage per head.
New total = 1.20 × 0.82 = 0.984 of the old.
Decrease = 1 − 0.984 = 0.016 → 1.6%.
Shortcut: 20 − 18 − (20 × 18)/100 = −1.6%.
Answer: 1.6%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Labour
qs.e:
Labour means hard physical work (manual labour). 'Toil' matches.
Relaxation = rest (the antonym); Dalliance = casual involvement or idle time; Mesh = net, network.
Answer: Toil

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. In those days, we did not expect luxuries; we were thankful if we could keep the wolf from the door.
qs.e:
'To keep the wolf from the door' means to have just enough money to avoid hunger and poverty.
The wolf stands for starvation waiting outside a poor home.
In hard times they were grateful simply to avoid starvation.
'Wallow in poverty' and 'encourage starvation' say the opposite; 'relish food' means enjoy food.
Answer: Avoid starvation
qs.u: keep the wolf from the door

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bully
qs.e:
A bully is someone who frightens or hurts weaker people. 'Oppressor' (one who treats others cruelly) matches.
Oxen = male cattle (a trap for 'bull'); Coddle = pamper; Plough = farm tool.
Answer: Oppressor

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Thankful
qs.e:
Thankful means grateful (thankful for the help). 'Obliged' (feeling indebted) matches, as in 'much obliged'.
Affirmation = confirmation; Ungrateful = the antonym; Obscure = unclear, unknown.
Answer: Obliged

qs.e:

Third: B, D, ?, H, J → +2 → F.
Fourth: Y, X, ?, V, U → −1 → W.
Answer: IOFW

qs.e:
One triangle and one plus sign are added each time.
Triangles fill the left side of the square (1, 2, 3, 4) and then continue along the bottom; pluses fill the inside of the left edge (1, 2, 3, 4) and then continue along the bottom.
Figure 4 has 4 left triangles + 1 bottom triangle and 4 pluses, so figure 5 has 4 left + 2 bottom triangles and 5 pluses (the fifth along the bottom).
Answer: Option 3

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. M N _ O J K M _ Q O J K _ N Q _ J K M N Q O _ K M N
qs.e:
The block 'MNQOJK' repeats: MNQOJK | MNQOJK | MNQOJK | MNQOJK | MN.
So the blanks are Q, N, M, O, J.
Answer: QNMOJ

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is 5 related to 2 if ‘5 ÷ 1 × 3 ÷ 4 − 2’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, × wife, ÷ father.  5 ÷ 1 × 3 ÷ 4 – 2.
Generation 1: 5 is 1's father.
Generation 2: 1 is 3's wife; 3 is 4's father, so 1 is 4's mother.
Generation 3: 4 is 2's brother, so 1 is 2's mother.
5 is the father of 2's mother.
Answer: Mother’s father

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 949, 1006, 1066, 1129, 1195, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 57, 60, 63, 66 – rising by 3.
Next difference = 69: 1195 + 69 = 1264.
Answer: 1264

qs.q: Which of the following articles from Directive Principles of state policy mentions about organization of Village Panchayats?
qs.e:
Article 40, in Part IV (Directive Principles), asks the State to organise village panchayats and give them powers to function as units of self-government.
The 73rd Amendment (1992) later gave panchayats constitutional status in Part IX.
Article 36 defines "State", 38 deals with social order and welfare, and 42 with just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
Answer: Article 40

qs.q: Who among the following sports persons is designated as brand ambassador for Nikshay Mitra, an initiative under Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan by Ministry of Health and Family welfare of GOI in November 2022?
qs.e:
Paralympic medallist Deepa Malik was made a brand ambassador for Ni-kshay Mitra under the Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (November 2022).
Ni-kshay Mitras are donors who adopt TB patients and support them with nutrition during treatment; Deepa Malik was India's first woman Paralympic medallist (silver, Rio 2016).
Answer: Deepa Malik

qs.q: Which of the following was the mascot of the Khelo India University Games 2022?
qs.e:
Jitu, a swamp deer (barasingha), the state animal of Uttar Pradesh, was the mascot of the Khelo India University Games 2022, held in UP in 2023.
Saavaj (a lion) was the mascot of the 36th National Games in Gujarat, and Moga (an Indian gaur) of the 37th National Games in Goa.
Answer: Jitu

qs.q: Which article of the Constitution of India lays down that it shall be the duty of the Advocate-General to give advice to the Government of the State upon legal matters?
qs.e:
Article 165 provides for the Advocate-General of a State, appointed by the Governor, whose duty is to advise the state government on legal matters.
He is the highest law officer of the state, the counterpart of the Attorney General (Article 76) at the Union level.
Article 168 is about state legislatures and 167 about duties of the Chief Minister.
Answer: Article 165

qs.q: Follow On is related to which of the following cricket formats?
qs.e:
Follow-on applies only to Test (and other multi-innings first-class) matches: a side batting second that trails by 200 runs or more in a five-day Test can be asked to bat again at once.
ODIs and T20s have only one innings per side, so a follow-on cannot occur.
Answer: Only Test Matches

qs.q: What is the tenure of office for the Chief Election Commissioner?
o: 5 years or up to the age of 60 years
6 years or up to the age of 60 years
6 years or up to the age of 65 years
5 years or up to the age of 65 years
qs.e:
Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Conditions of Service) law, the CEC holds office for 6 years or until the age of 65, whichever comes first.
The CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge, which protects the Commission's independence.
Answer: 6 years or up to the age of 65 years

qs.q: An article passing through two hands is sold at a total profit of 40% of the original cost price. If the first dealer makes a profit of 30%, then the profit percentage made by the second dealer is:
qs.e:
Take the original CP = 100. Final price = 140 (40% total profit).
First dealer sells at 30% profit → 130.
Second dealer's profit = (140 − 130)/130 × 100 = 100/13 = 7 9/13 %.
Answer: 7 9/13 %

qs.q: Two candidates contested in an election. 80% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 5% of the polled votes were invalid. The winning candidate got 70% of valid votes and won by a majority of 36,480 votes. Find the total number of voters.
qs.e:
Let N = total voters. Polled = 0.8N; valid = 95% of that = 0.76N.
Winner 70%, loser 30% of valid → margin = 40% of 0.76N = 0.304N.
0.304N = 36480 → N = 1,20,000.
Answer: 1,20,000

qs.q: A shopkeeper allows 40% discount on his goods. He further gives 20% discount. What is the single discount equivalent to these two successive discounts?
qs.e:
Single equivalent of a% and b% = a + b − ab/100.
40 + 20 − (40 × 20)/100 = 60 − 8 = 52%.
Check: 100 × 0.6 × 0.8 = 48 → 52% off.
Answer: 52%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. To bring to light
qs.e:
'To bring to light' means to reveal or disclose something that was hidden.
Example: The audit brought to light several fake accounts.
Disengage = withdraw; engage in conversation = talk; lighten = make lighter – none means reveal.
Answer: To disclose

qs.q: Select the correct meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Rina pulled a long face since her husband had not bought her a diamond necklace on their anniversary.
qs.e:
'To pull a long face' means to look sad, disappointed or sulky.
Rina was unhappy because she did not get the necklace.
Ecstatic, euphoric and electrified all mean extremely happy or excited – the opposite.
Answer: To look saddened

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, if ‘J + K ÷ L − T x R’, then how is J related to L?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, x sister, ÷ daughter.  J + K ÷ L – T x R.
Generation 1: J is K's mother; K is L's daughter, and L is a brother (male), so L is K's father.
So J and L are K's parents — J is L's wife. (T is L's sister, R is T's sibling.)
Answer: Wife

qs.q: Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. YL 93, XK 88, WJ 83, VI 78, ?
qs.e:
First letters Y, X, W, V go back 1 → U.
Second letters L, K, J, I go back 1 → H.
Numbers 93, 88, 83, 78 fall by 5 → 73.
Answer: UH 73

qs.q: Select the figure from among the given option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.
qs.e:
Two movement rules alternate; step 1→2 equals step 3→4, so step 4→5 repeats step 2→3.
Step 2→3 (diagonal places 1–6 from top-left): 1 → top-right, top-right → 6, 6 → bottom-left, bottom-left → 1, and the middle four reverse (2↔5, 3↔4).
From figure 4 (↑ □ S T O P; L top-right; △ bottom-left): diagonal △ O T S □ L, ↑ top-right, P bottom-left.
Answer: Option 1

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ P _ J _ P _ P _ _ P _
qs.e:
With JPPJPJP the series reads JPP | JPP | JPP | JPP – the block 'JPP' repeats four times.
The other options give clusters like JJP or PPP, breaking it.
Answer: JPPJPJP

qs.q: Identify the figure from among the given options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Each figure has one symbol at top-right and one at bottom-left.
The top-right symbol of one figure moves to bottom-left in the next and is mirrored left-to-right (L → ⅃, P → q, 7 → reversed 7); a new symbol appears at top-right.
So figure 5 has the mirrored form of figure 4's top-right symbol at bottom-left and a new symbol (6) at top-right, nothing else.
Option 1 has an extra k; options 2 and 3 have the wrong places or forms.
Answer: Option 4

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 1225, 1184, 1147, 1116, 1087, ?
qs.e:
Differences: −41, −37, −31, −29 – falling prime numbers.
The next prime below 29 is 23: 1087 − 23 = 1064.
Answer: 1064

qs.e:
First letters J, L, N go up by 2 → P.
Second letters K, J, I go back by 1 → H.
Third letters T, R, P go back by 2 → N.
Answer: PHN

qs.q: Which fundamental duty applies on you when you see a few school students, on their educational trip to Humayun’s tomb, writing their names on the walls?
o: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To defend the country and render national service
To protect and improve the natural environment
qs.e:
Humayun's tomb is a protected heritage monument, so writing names on its walls damages public property.
Article 51A(i) makes it a duty to safeguard public property and to abjure violence; it also links with 51A(f) on valuing the country's heritage.
Answer: To safeguard public property

qs.q: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India lays down that ‘The allocation of seats in the Council of States to be filled by representatives of the States and of the Union territories shall be in accordance with the provisions in that behalf contained in the fourth Schedule’?
qs.e:
Article 80(2) says the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to the states and union territories shall follow the Fourth Schedule.
Seats are allotted roughly on the basis of population, so Uttar Pradesh has the most (31).
Article 81 is the composition of the Lok Sabha, 82 readjustment after census and 83 the duration of Houses.
Answer: Article 80

qs.q: Where was the first women’s international test cricket match hosted in India in 1976?
qs.e:
India's first home women's Test match was against West Indies at Bangalore (M. Chinnaswamy Stadium) in October-November 1976.
It was also the first women's Test series played in India.
Answer: Bangalore

qs.q: When was the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award renamed as Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award?
qs.e:
The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award on 6 August 2021.
The change came during the Tokyo Olympics, right after the men's hockey team won bronze. India's National Sports Day (29 August) is Dhyan Chand's birthday.
Answer: 6th August 2021

qs.q: Ajay spends of his income on different household items. If his income increases by 25% and expenditure increase by 20%, then the effect on his savings will be:
qs.e:
Ajay spends 66⅔% = 2/3 of his income. Take income = 300: expenditure 200, savings 100.
New income = 300 × 1.25 = 375; new expenditure = 200 × 1.2 = 240.
New savings = 375 − 240 = 135 → savings rise by 35%.
Answer: 35%

qs.q: The marked price of a TV set is ₹18,500. If the dealer allows two successive discounts of 20% and 5%, for how much is the TV available?
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cut corners
o: Do something in an inexpensive and easy way
qs.e:
'Cut corners' means to do something in the cheapest or easiest way, often skipping proper steps.
Image: walking across a corner instead of going round it, to save effort.
Example: The builder cut corners, and the roof leaked within a year.
Completing work, clearing space and finding a place are not this meaning.
Answer: Do something in an inexpensive and easy way

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I was completely mesmerised by the performance.
qs.e:
Mesmerised means held spellbound, completely captivated (mesmerised by the magician). 'Fascinated' matches.
Bored, Irritated and Annoyed are negative feelings, the opposite of being captivated.
Answer: Fascinated

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Easy does it
o: Used to tell someone to do something horridly
Used to tell someone to do something violently
Used to tell someone to do something rarely
Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully
qs.e:
'Easy does it' is said to tell someone to act slowly, gently and carefully.
Example: Easy does it – lift the glass table slowly.
'Horridly', 'violently' and 'rarely' do not match the gentle care the phrase asks for.
Answer: Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is S related to P if ‘P × Q ÷ R − S × A’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, × wife, ÷ father.  P × Q ÷ R – S × A.
Generation 1: P is Q's wife; Q is R's father.
Generation 2: R is S's brother, so S is also a child of Q and P; S is A's wife, so S is female.
S is P's daughter.
Answer: Daughter

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options, which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Each step three of the five symbols move round a triangle of places while the other two stay put; the two kinds of step alternate.
Steps 1→2 and 3→4: top-left → bottom-right → centre → top-left. Step 2→3: bottom-left → centre → top-right → bottom-left.
So step 4→5 repeats step 2→3: ↓ (bottom-left) goes to the centre, □ (centre) to top-right, ○ (top-right) to bottom-left; ↑ and △ stay.
Result: ↑ top-left, □ top-right, ↓ centre, ○ bottom-left, △ bottom-right.
Answer: Option 2

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ Y Z K X K X _ Z K X _ X Y _ K X K X Y Z _ X K X Y
qs.e:
With XYKZK the series reads XYZKXK | XYZKXK | XYZKXK | XYZKXK | XY – the block 'XYZKXK' repeats.
The other options break a block (e.g. option 1 starts KYZ…).
Answer: XYKZK

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 300, 152, 80, 48, 40, 52, ?
Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of ? will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Each figure has two letters on top and one at the bottom.
The bottom letter moves to top-left in the next figure, the top-right letter moves to the bottom, the old top-left letter drops out and a new letter appears at top-right.
Check: M (bottom of fig 1) is top-left in fig 2, K (top-right) is at the bottom.
From figure 4 (L S / H): top-left H, bottom S, new top-right letter D.
Answer: Option 3

qs.q: The ________ of every state unfurls the flag in its capital on the Republic Day.
qs.e:
On Republic Day (26 January), the Governor of each state unfurls the national flag in the state capital, as the constitutional head of the state.
On Independence Day (15 August), the flag is hoisted by the Chief Minister in the state capital, just as the Prime Minister does at the Red Fort.
Answer: Governor

qs.q: The Upper House of a State Legislature is known as the ____________.
qs.e:
In states that have two Houses, the Upper House is the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) and the Lower House is the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).
Article 169 lets Parliament create or abolish a council; only a few states, such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, have one.
Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are the Houses of Parliament.
Answer: Vidhan Parishad

qs.q: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution was inserted in the Indian Constitution through _____________ Constitutional Amendment Act.
qs.e:
Part IV-A, containing Article 51A (Fundamental Duties), was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
It followed the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee and was inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR.
The 44th Amendment (1978) mainly undid emergency-era changes and removed the right to property as a Fundamental Right.
Answer: 42nd

qs.q: The Parliament passed the Essential Defence Services Bill, 2021 in August 2021. Which of the following is an objective behind passing it?
o: To prohibit strikes, lockouts and layoffs in units engaged in essential defence services
To appoint more women in defence services
To encourage more FDI in defence services
To implement one rank one pension
qs.e:
The Essential Defence Services Act, 2021 lets the government ban strikes, lockouts and lay-offs in units engaged in essential defence services, such as ordnance factories.
It came after employees of the Ordnance Factory Board protested its corporatisation in 2021.
It has nothing to do with women's recruitment, FDI or One Rank One Pension.
Answer: To prohibit strikes, lockouts and layoffs in units engaged in essential defence services

qs.q: Who was the first Indian woman wrestler to represent the country at the 2012 London Olympic Games?
qs.e:
Geeta Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to qualify for and compete at the Olympics, at London 2012 (55 kg freestyle).
Sakshi Malik later won India's first women's wrestling medal (bronze) at Rio 2016.
Answer: Geeta Phogat

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers. I. Two successive discounts of 15% and 20% II. Successive discount of 25 % and 10% III. A discount of 33% The selling price will be minimum under the scheme:
qs.e:
Selling price is lowest where the total discount is highest.
I: 15 + 20 − 3 = 32%. II: 25 + 10 − 2.5 = 32.5%. III: 33%.
Scheme III gives the largest discount, so the lowest SP.
Answer: III

qs.q: In a constituency, 45% of the total number of voters are males and the rest are females. If 60% of the males are illiterate and 60% of the females are literate, then by what per cent is the number of illiterate females more than that of literate males? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
qs.e:
Take 100 voters: 45 males, 55 females.
Literate males = 40% of 45 = 18 (since 60% are illiterate).
Illiterate females = 40% of 55 = 22 (since 60% are literate).
Excess = (22 − 18)/18 × 100 = 22.22%.
Answer: 22.22%

Take 8 articles each costing ₹1 (total ₹8).
5 sold at 20% gain → profit 5 × 0.2 = ₹1; 3 sold at cost → profit 0.
Gain% on whole = 1/8 × 100 = 12.5% = 12½%.
Shortcut: (5/8) × 20% = 12.5%.
Answer: 12½%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Forsake
qs.e:
Forsake means to give up or desert (never forsake a friend). 'Abandon' matches.
Accelerate = speed up; Reveal = disclose; Clutch = hold tightly (nearly the opposite).
Answer: Abandon

qs.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the idiom in the given brackets. His PhD degree seems to be (Penelope’s web).
qs.e:
'Penelope's web' is a task that never gets finished.
Origin: in Homer's Odyssey, Penelope wove a shroud by day and unravelled it each night to put off her suitors.
So his PhD seems endless.
'Difficult', 'important' or 'secret' miss the never-ending sense.
Answer: An endless task

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill the blank in the given situation. I thought Sadhna would always stick by me, but when I got into trouble, she turned out to be a/an ___________.
qs.e:
A 'fair-weather friend' is someone who is your friend only in good times and leaves when you are in trouble.
Sadhna left when the speaker got into trouble, so she was a fair-weather friend.
White elephant = a costly but useless possession; hard nut to crack = a difficult person or problem; open secret = something supposedly secret but known to all.
Answer: fair-weather friend

qs.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. An intense wish to learn something keeps the nerves active.
qs.e:
'Intense' here means strong or very great, so 'powerful' keeps the meaning: a powerful wish to learn keeps the nerves active.
'Lazy' and 'half-hearted' are opposites, and 'fixed' means unchanging, not strong.
Answer: powerful

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exceptional
qs.e:
Exceptional means unusually good, far above average (an exceptional student). 'Outstanding' matches.
Emotional = showing feelings; Trivial = unimportant (the opposite); Total = whole.
Answer: Outstanding
