qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is A related to D if ‘A × B ÷ C + D’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, × wife, ÷ father.  A × B ÷ C + D.
Generation 1: A is B's wife; B is C's father, so A is C's mother.
Generation 2: C is D's mother.
A is the mother of D's mother.
Answer: Mother’s mother

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 20, 25, 25, 35, 30, 45, ?, 55, 40
qs.e:
Two series are mixed alternately.
Odd places: 20, 25, 30, ?, 40 – rising by 5, so ? = 35.
Even places: 25, 35, 45, 55 – rising by 10.
Answer: 35

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of ? will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Each figure holds two numbers: the top number of one figure moves into the lower small region of the next figure, and a new number appears on top (4→bottom in fig 2, 6→bottom in fig 3, 3→ the other part in fig 4).
So figure 5 must have 8 in the lower small triangle and a fresh number on top; the line pattern returns to the shape of figure 1.
Option 1 keeps 8 on top and option 3 reuses 3, so only option 2 (5 on top, 8 below) fits.
Answer: Option 2

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of ? will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
One new symbol is added each time, moving clockwise round the edge: A (top-left), ⊘ (top-middle), S (top-right), T (right-middle).
The next symbol is a new letter in the bottom-right corner (R); the others stay.
Options 1 and 3 repeat a symbol already used, and option 2 puts the new symbols on the left.
Answer: Option 4

qs.q: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? MJPT, PGMW, SDJZ, ? , YXDF
qs.e:
Check each position (A=1).
First: M, P, S, ?, Y → +3 → V.
Second: J, G, D, ?, X → −3 → A (D−3 = A).
Third: P, M, J, ?, D → −3 → G.
Fourth: T, W, Z, ?, F → +3 → C (wrap past Z).
Answer: VAGC

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. L M N _ O L L M _ Q O L L _ N Q O _ L M N Q _ L L M
qs.e:
The block 'LMNQOL' repeats: LMNQOL | LMNQOL | LMNQOL | LMNQOL | LM.
So the blanks are Q, N, M, L, O.
Answer: QNMLO

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
India has single citizenship: every person is a citizen of India only, with no separate state citizenship (unlike the USA, which has dual citizenship).
Independent judiciary, universal adult franchise and a blend of rigidity and flexibility are genuine features of the Indian Constitution.
Answer: Dual Citizenship

qs.q: The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 amended which of the following Acts?
qs.e:
The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 amended the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, during COVID-19.
It made violence against healthcare workers a cognisable, non-bailable offence and widened the Centre's powers; it was replaced by an Act in September 2020.
The 1897 Act was first passed to fight the bubonic plague in Bombay.
Answer: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897

qs.q: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?
o: All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.
A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.
India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.
Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.
qs.e:
India has a multi-party system, and parties are recognised by the Election Commission as national or state parties based on vote share and seats.
Parties register with the Election Commission (not the Supreme Court), symbols are allotted by the Election Commission (not the President), and recognition is not given by Parliament.
Answer: India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.

qs.q: Raja Bhalindra Singh trophy is associated with which of the following national sports events?
qs.e:
The Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy is given at the National Games to the state/team that tops the medal table.
Raja Bhalindra Singh of Patiala was a long-time IOA president and IOC member.
Answer: National Games

qs.q: Sports Authority of India comes under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
qs.e:
The Sports Authority of India (SAI), set up in 1984, works under the Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
It runs training centres and schemes such as TOPS and Khelo India.
Answer: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

qs.q: After offering two successive discounts a toy with a marked price of ₹150 is sold at ₹105. If the value of the first discount is 12.5%, what is the value of the second discount?
In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 88% of the votes is elected by a majority of 684 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (all polled votes are valid)
qs.e:
Winner 88%, loser 12% → majority = 76% of total.
76% = 684 → total = 684 ÷ 0.76 = 900.
Answer: 900

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given group of words. On cloud nine
qs.e:
'On cloud nine' is an idiom meaning extremely happy or delighted.
It has nothing to do with literally flying, anger or physical height.
Answer: Being very delighted

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given group of words. A bitter pill
qs.e:
'A bitter pill (to swallow)' is an unpleasant fact or situation that one has to accept.
Talking nonsense, getting furious and arguing unnecessarily are unrelated meanings.
Answer: Facing a distressing situation

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tendency
qs.e:
Tendency means an inclination to behave in a certain way (a tendency to exaggerate). 'Proneness' matches.
Distaste and Aversion = dislike; Decoy = a lure or trap.
Answer: Proneness

qs.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Bankrupts are those who are incapable to pay their debts.
qs.e:
'Incapable' takes 'of' + -ing ('incapable of paying'), so 'incapable to pay' is wrong. The key's 'incompetent' (unable, lacking means) keeps the meaning in this frame: bankrupts are those incompetent to pay their debts.
'Capable' and 'powerful' are opposites, and 'meagre' (scanty) describes amounts, not people.
Answer: incompetent

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Condone
qs.e:
Condone means to overlook or forgive an offence (we cannot condone cheating). 'Pardon' matches.
Penalty = punishment (the opposite); Solace = comfort in sorrow; Solicitude = care and concern.
Answer: Pardon

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Pugnacious
qs.e:
Pugnacious means quarrelsome, quick to fight or argue. 'Waspish' (irritable, sharp and quick to take offence) is the closest.
Impatient = unable to wait; Good-tempered = the opposite; Arrogant = proud and overbearing.
Answer: Waspish

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Kilter
qs.e:
Kilter means good working order, balance (used in 'out of kilter' = out of order). 'Order' matches.
Anarchy = lawless disorder; Shambles = total mess; Disrepair = poor condition. All three are opposites.
Answer: Order

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘ A is the father of B’; ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’ and ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. Based on the above, how is P related to S if P + Q − R $ S % T?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – father, $ daughter, % sister.  P + Q – R $ S % T.
Generation 1: P is Q's mother.
Generation 2: Q is R's father; R is S's daughter and S is female (a sister), so S is R's mother — Q's wife.
P is the mother of S's husband.
Answer: Husband’s mother

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ _ C _ D C _ _ C C _ _
qs.e:
With CDCCDDC the series reads CDC | CDC | CDC | CDC – the block 'CDC' repeats four times.
The other options give runs like CCCC or DD, which break the block.
Answer: CDCCDDC

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of ? will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Each figure has three numbers: small at top-left, big in the centre, small at bottom-right.
The centre number moves to top-left, the bottom-right number moves to the centre, and a new number comes in at bottom-right (5/9/6 → 9/6/3 → 6/3/2 → 3/2/0).
So figure 5: top-left 2, centre 0 and a new number (1) at bottom-right; option 2 wrongly repeats 2.
Answer: Option 4

qs.q: Select the figure from among the given option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.
qs.e:
Two changes alternate. Steps 1→2 and 3→4: the four corner symbols move one corner clockwise; in the middle row the 2nd and 3rd symbols swap and the 1st and 4th are replaced by new ones.
Step 2→3: corners and middle row exchange – the middle row becomes (bottom-left, top-left, top-right, bottom-right) and the corners take the old middle row (1st → top-left, 4th → top-right, 2nd → bottom-left, 3rd → bottom-right).
Apply step 2→3 to figure 4: middle row I N F O; corners S (top-left), V (top-right), X (bottom-left), △ (bottom-right).
Answer: Option 4

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 3, 6, 9, 18, 21, ?
qs.e:
Alternately multiply by 2 and add 3.
3×2 = 6, 6+3 = 9, 9×2 = 18, 18+3 = 21, 21×2 = 42.
Answer: 42

qs.q: Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. NW17, PY19, RA21, TC23, ?
qs.e:
First letters N, P, R, T go up by 2 → V.
Second letters W, Y, A, C go up by 2 (wrapping after Z) → E.
Numbers 17, 19, 21, 23 go up by 2 → 25.
Answer: VE25

qs.q: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will logically complete the series. QUA_TO_ANT_UAN_KU_NT
qs.e:
With NUMTA the series reads QUANT | OUANT | MUANT | KUANT.
The ending 'UANT' stays the same while the first letter goes back 2 each time: Q, O, M, K.
Answer: NUMTA

qs.q: Who among the following is NOT a member of the National Human Rights Commission?
o: Former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
Former Judge of the Supreme Court
Former Chief Justice of the High Court
qs.e:
Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the NHRC has a Chairperson who was a Chief Justice or Judge of the Supreme Court, plus members including a former Supreme Court judge, a former High Court Chief Justice and experts in human rights.
A serving District Magistrate is not a member of the Commission.
Answer: District Magistrate

qs.q: As of 14 October 2021, which Indian footballer was in the news for breaking Pele's 77 international goals?
qs.e:
Sunil Chhetri passed Pele's 77 international goals at the SAFF Championship in October 2021, scoring his 78th and 79th goals.
He was then the second-highest scorer among active players after Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.
Answer: Sunil Chhetri

qs.q: In which year did the Central Government launch the National Air Sports Policy?
qs.e:
The Central Government (Ministry of Civil Aviation) launched the National Air Sports Policy (NASP) on 8 June 2022.
It covers sports like paragliding, hang gliding, skydiving, ballooning and aerobatics and aims to make India a top air-sports nation by 2030.
Answer: 2022

qs.q: Which committee recommended Constitutional recognition for the local government bodies in 1989?
qs.e:
The P. K. Thungon Committee (1988-89) recommended that local government bodies (panchayats) be given constitutional recognition.
This led towards the 73rd Amendment (1992); Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) proposed the three-tier system, and Ashok Mehta (1977-78) a two-tier system.
Answer: PK Thungon Committee

qs.q: If the selling price of an article is ₹1,792 after a 20% discount, then the marked price of the article is:
qs.e:
SP = 80% of MP (after 20% discount).
MP = 1792 ÷ 0.8 = ₹2,240.
Answer: ₹2,240

qs.q: An investor, invested ₹2,00,000 in shares. The shares rose by 18% on the first day, fell by 15% on the second day, and then fell by 3% on the third day. What is the net percentage increase or decrease in the value of the investor's shares? (Rounded up to one decimal place)
qs.e:
Successive changes multiply (the amount invested does not matter).
1.18 × 0.85 × 0.97 = 1.003 × 0.97 = 0.97291.
Change = 0.97291 − 1 = −0.02709 → decrease of about 2.7%.
(₹2,00,000 becomes ₹1,94,582.)
Answer: decrease by 2.7%

qs.q: A seller sold 19 cookies for ₹95 instead of 20 cookies in one kg, cheating a customer. What is the gain (in ₹) if the seller bought the cookies for ₹76?
qs.e:
One kg should contain 20 cookies, which cost the seller ₹76 → cost per cookie = 76/20 = ₹3.80.
He hands over only 19 cookies as '1 kg' for ₹95; their cost = 19 × 3.80 = ₹72.20.
Gain = 95 − 72.20 = ₹22.80.
Answer: 22.8

The table shows production 9000 in 2018 and 10,800 in 2019, with a constant growth rate.
Growth rate = (10800 − 9000)/9000 × 100 = 20%.
X (2020) = 10800 × 1.2 = 12960.
Answer: 12960

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the roof
qs.e:
'Hit the roof' means to become suddenly very angry.
Example: Dad hit the roof when he saw the phone bill.
Image: someone jumping up in rage hard enough to hit the ceiling.
Destroying buildings, playing or jumping high are literal readings.
Answer: To become very angry

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Creature of habit
o: One who does same thing in the same way
qs.e:
A 'creature of habit' is a person who always does the same things in the same way.
Example: Being a creature of habit, he has the same breakfast at 7 a.m. every day.
It is not about being mean, about a dog, or about a bad habit.
Answer: One who does same thing in the same way

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. A period of free outdoor play can provide a very necessary respite from the hustle and bustle of the day.
qs.e:
Respite means a short rest or relief from something hard (a respite from the heat). 'Break' matches.
Progression = moving forward; Commencement = beginning; Continuation = carrying on. These are the opposite of a pause.
Answer: Break

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Mellifluous
qs.e:
Mellifluous means sweet and smooth-sounding (a mellifluous voice). 'Musical' matches.
Cacophonous = harsh and jarring (the antonym); Loud = high in volume; Distinct = clear, separate.
Answer: Musical

qs.q: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? AWSO, KGCY, UQMI, EAWS, ?
qs.e:
Each letter moves forward 10 places from one term to the next (A=1, wrapping after Z).
First: A, K, U, E → O; second: W, G, Q, A → K; third: S, C, M, W → G; fourth: O, Y, I, S → C.
Check: inside every term the letters also fall by 4 (A, W, S, O), and OKGC fits that too.
Answer: OKGC

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is A related to D if ‘A × B ÷ C × D’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, × wife, ÷ father.  A × B ÷ C × D.
Generation 1: A is B's wife; B is C's father, so A is C's mother.
Generation 2: C is D's wife.
A is the mother of D's wife.
Answer: Wife's mother

qs.q: Identify the figure from among the given options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
Count the items: 16, 15, 14, 13 – one fewer each time, so figure 5 has 12.
At every step one dot disappears and one more dot becomes an X: X's go 0, 1, 2, 3 → 4, dots go 16, 14, 12, 10 → 8.
Option 1 (8 dots + 4 X) fits; option 2 has only 3 X, option 3 has 13 items, option 4 has 11.
Answer: Option 1

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of ? will logically complete the series.
qs.e:
The small corner mark moves anticlockwise round the box: top-right, top-left, bottom-left, bottom-right, and then back to top-right.
Its shape alternates between L and its mirror image ┘: L, ┘, L, ┘, so next is L.
So figure 5 shows L at the top-right.
Answer: Option 4

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. B _ E N B _ C E N B B C _ N B B C E _ B _ C
qs.e:
The block 'BBCEN' repeats: BBCEN | BBCEN | BBCEN | BBCEN | BBC.
So the blanks are C, B, E, N, B.
Answer: CBENB

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, 17, 83, 329, ?, 1961
In which of the following years was the Right of Persons with Disabilities Act passed?
qs.e:
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act was passed in December 2016, replacing the Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995.
It raised the number of recognised disabilities from 7 to 21 and increased the job reservation in government posts to 4%.
Answer: 2016

qs.q: Which of the following Articles states that the Prime Minister should be appointed by the President?
qs.e:
Article 75(1) says the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President, and other ministers by the President on the Prime Minister's advice.
Article 66 deals with election of the Vice-President, 62 with time of presidential elections and 71 with disputes about these elections.
Answer: Article 75

qs.q: In which sport did India win its first individual Olympic medal?
qs.e:
Independent India's first individual Olympic medal was K.D. Jadhav's bronze in freestyle wrestling (bantamweight) at the Helsinki 1952 Olympics.
India's first individual gold came much later from shooter Abhinav Bindra (2008).
Answer: Wrestling

qs.q: The oath of office to the Vice-President is administered by the ________.
qs.e:
Under Article 69, the Vice-President takes the oath of office before the President (or a person appointed by the President).
In contrast, the President's oath (Article 60) is administered by the Chief Justice of India.
Answer: President

qs.q: Vijender Singh has represented India in Olympics for how many times?
qs.e:
Boxer Vijender Singh competed at three Olympics: Athens 2004, Beijing 2008 and London 2012.
At Beijing 2008 he won bronze (middleweight), India's first Olympic boxing medal.
Answer: 3

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
o: To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To value and preserve rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
qs.e:
The Fundamental Duties include safeguarding public property and abjuring violence, upholding the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India, and valuing the country's composite culture.
Prohibiting trade in rare and endangered species is not listed in Article 51A; the related duty is to protect the environment and have compassion for living creatures (51A(g)).
Answer: To prohibit trade in rare and endangered species

qs.q: Successive discounts of 10% and 20% are given on the purchase of a purse. If the marked price of the purse is ₹2,250, find the selling price.
qs.e:
Successive discounts multiply: 2250 × 0.9 × 0.8.
2250 × 0.9 = 2025; × 0.8 = 1620.
Answer: ₹1,620

qs.q: The cost of tomatoes per kg is increased by 300%. A housewife reduces her consumption of tomatoes by 70%. By what percentage does her expenditure on tomatoes increase or decrease?
qs.e:
Expenditure = price × consumption.
Price up 300% → 4 times; consumption down 70% → 0.3 times.
New expenditure = 4 × 0.3 = 1.2 times → 20% increase.
Answer: Increases, 20%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Start from scratch
o: To start or create something from the very beginning
To develop something out of waste material
qs.e:
'Start from scratch' means to begin something from the very beginning, with nothing prepared.
Origin: the starting line once scratched in the ground for a race.
Example: The file got deleted, so I had to write the report from scratch.
Pointing out mistakes, addressing issues and using waste material are not the meaning.
Answer: To start or create something from the very beginning

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Garnish
qs.e:
Garnish means to decorate food or embellish something (garnish with coriander). 'Decorate' matches.
Dwindle = shrink; Blemish and Tarnish = spoil the look, the opposite.
Answer: Decorate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Determined
qs.e:
Determined means firmly decided, not giving up (a determined effort). 'Resolute' matches.
Hesitant and Faltering = unsure, wavering (opposites); Loathe = hate (a verb).
Answer: resolute

qs.q: Select the most appropriate option that has the same meaning as the italicised segment. His illness became a blessing in disguise when he married his nurse.
o: an apparent misfortune that eventually has good results
when someone finds it difficult to choose between two alternatives
deal with a problem if and when it becomes necessary
qs.e:
'A blessing in disguise' is something that seems bad at first but turns out to be good. His illness (bad) led him to marry his nurse (good).
The other options describe a dilemma, 'cross that bridge when you come to it', and a rebuttal.
Answer: an apparent misfortune that eventually has good results

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fallacy
qs.e:
Fallacy means a mistaken belief or faulty reasoning (it is a fallacy that money brings happiness). 'Error' matches.
Veracity = truthfulness; Evidence = proof; Verify = confirm. All are linked to truth, the opposite.
Answer: Error

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 625, 382, 301, 274, 265, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 625−382 = 243, 382−301 = 81, 301−274 = 27, 274−265 = 9 – powers of 3 falling (3⁵, 3⁴, 3³, 3²).
Next difference = 3: 265 − 3 = 262.
Answer: 262

qs.q: Select the figure from among the given option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.
qs.e:
Two movement rules alternate; step 1→2 equals step 3→4, so step 4→5 repeats step 2→3.
Step 2→3: top → bottom-right, bottom-right → bottom-middle, bottom-middle → bottom-left, bottom-left → top; the middle row shifts right with its last item going to the front.
From figure 4 (2; C 1 =; 6 M P): top 6, middle = C 1, bottom M P 2.
Answer: Option 4

qs.q: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ABNI, DAQH, ?, JYWF
qs.e:
Check each position (A=1).
First: A, D, ?, J → +3 → G.
Second: B, A, ?, Y → −1 → Z.
Third: N, Q, ?, W → +3 → T.
Fourth: I, H, ?, F → −1 → G.
Answer: GZTG

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series?
qs.e:
Two changes alternate. Steps 1→2 and 3→4: the symbols swap diagonally (top-left ↔ bottom-right, top-right ↔ bottom-left) without turning.
Step 2→3: every symbol stays in place but turns 90° clockwise (dome up → dome right, ⊢ → T, → → ↓, △ → ▷).
So step 4→5 turns each symbol of figure 4 90° clockwise: ▷ → ▽, ↓ → ←, T → ⊣, right-facing dome → downward dome.
Answer: Option 2

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ B _ _ _ A L _ _ L _ _
qs.e:
With LALBBABA the series reads LBA | LBA | LBA | LBA – the block 'LBA' repeats four times.
The other options give runs like BB or LLL, which break it.
Answer: LALBBABA

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'A ! B' means ‘A is the father of B’, 'A & B' means ‘A is the brother of B’, 'A * B' means ‘A is the wife of B’ and 'A # B' means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Which of the following means that S is the husband's brother's wife of M?
qs.e:
Codes: ! father, & brother, * wife, # daughter. Needed chain: M's husband → his brother → his wife = S.
S * F & J ! I # M: Generation 1: S is F's wife; F is J's brother.
J is I's father and I is M's daughter, so M is J's wife.
Generation 2: I. So S is the wife of M's husband's brother ✓.
Answer: S * F & J ! I # M

qs.q: Which of the following commissions/committees identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
qs.e:
The Justice J. S. Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties (1999) noted that legal provisions already exist to enforce some duties, such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 and laws on wildlife and forests.
The Rajamannar and Sarkaria Commissions dealt with Centre-state relations.
Answer: Justice Verma Committee

qs.q: Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the Indian Constitution deal with the ____________.
o: financial relations between the Centre and the states
legislative relations between the Centre and the states
qs.e:
Part XI covers relations between the Union and states: Articles 245-255 cover legislative relations, and Articles 256-263 cover administrative relations.
Financial relations are in Part XII (Articles 268-293), emergency provisions in Part XVIII and tribunals in Part XIV-A.
Answer: legislative relations between the Centre and the states

qs.q: In chess, which of the following may only move forward to the unoccupied square immediately in front of it?
qs.e:
A pawn moves forward one square into an empty square in front of it (two squares on its first move) and captures diagonally.
Queen, bishop and rook can move several squares along lines and can also move backward.
Answer: The Pawn

qs.q: Agricultural shot is a term used in which of the following sports?
qs.e:
In cricket, an 'agricultural shot' is a wild cross-batted heave across the line, usually towards mid-wicket, like a farmer swinging a scythe.
The term is not used in football or tennis.
Answer: Cricket

qs.e:
Adapt means to adjust to new conditions (adapt to a new school). 'Adjust' matches.
Apply = put to use; Understand = grasp the meaning; Control = direct or restrain. (Do not confuse adapt with adopt = take up.)

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase. I had heard of henpecked husbands and now, I felt that I saw one.
qs.e:
A 'henpecked husband' is one who is bullied or dominated by his wife – an oppressed husband.

Options 2–4 (dominating, bossy, controlling) describe the opposite kind of husband.
Answer: Oppressed husband

qs.q: Identify from the given options the word which is similar in meaning to the following word. Morbid
qs.e:
Morbid means having an unhealthy interest in gloomy things like death (morbid curiosity). 'Gloomy' matches.
Grand = splendid; Bet = a wager; Blithe = carefree and happy (the antonym).

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Roshan, it’s time for you to give your speech to the whole school, wishing you luck to do well.

'Break a leg' is the idiom used to wish someone good luck before a performance, such as a speech.
'Hands down' = easily, 'high five' is a celebratory gesture, and 'down in the dumps' = sad.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. She is a very creative artist and one can see that in her paintings.
qs.e:
Creative means having original ideas, imaginative (a creative designer). 'Innovative' (introducing new ideas) matches.
Likeable = pleasant; Good = of high quality, too general; Pedantic = fussy about small rules and details.
Answer: Innovative

qs.q: In a certain code language, X + Y means ‘X is the sister of Y’, X − Y means ‘X is the wife of Y’, X × Y means ‘X is the mother of Y’, X ÷ Y means ‘X is the father of Y’. Based on the above, how is H related to L if ‘H × I − J ÷ K + L’?

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas’?
qs.e:
Article 43 asks the State to secure a living wage and decent conditions of work, and in particular to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas.
This is a Gandhian principle; Article 42 is about humane conditions of work and maternity relief, 44 the Uniform Civil Code and 49 protection of monuments.
Answer: Article 43

qs.q: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President’s rule in any state?
qs.e:
Article 356 provides for President's Rule when the constitutional machinery in a state fails.
It is considered controversial because it was used over 100 times, often for political reasons; the S. R. Bommai case (1994) set limits on its use.
Article 352 is national emergency, 358 suspension of Article 19, and 360 financial emergency.
Answer: Article 356

qs.q: Bhakti Pradeep Kulkarni is associated with ________.

Answer: chess

qs.q: India hosted the Asian Games in which of the following years?
qs.e:
India hosted the Asian Games twice, both in New Delhi: the 1st Asian Games in 1951 and the 9th in 1982.
The 1982 Games brought colour TV to India and the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium was built for them.
Answer: 1951 and 1982

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution CANNOT be suspended even during an emergency declared on the grounds of war or external aggression?
qs.e:
The 44th Amendment (1978) laid down that the rights under Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a national emergency under Article 359.
Article 20 protects against ex post facto laws, double jeopardy and self-incrimination; Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.
This was a response to the misuse of emergency powers in 1975-77.
Answer: Articles 20 and 21

qs.q: A cooker is marked at ₹12,500. The dealer allows successive discounts of 6%, 6% and 4% on it. What is the net selling price of the cooker?

Three candidates X, Y and Z participated in an election. X got 30% more votes than Y, whereas Z got 25% more votes than Y. X also overtook Z by 5000 votes. If 71% of the voters voted and no invalid votes were cast, then what was the total number of voters in the voting list?
qs.e:
Take Y = 100 parts: X = 130, Z = 125.
X − Z = 5 parts = 5000 → 1 part = 1000.
Total votes = 130 + 100 + 125 = 355 parts = 3,55,000.
These are 71% of voters → total voters = 355000 ÷ 0.71 = 5,00,000.
Answer: 5,00,000

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Magnificent

Answer: Incredible

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Beseech

Impart = give or share (knowledge); Bequeath = leave property by a will; Pamper = indulge, spoil.
Answer: Implore

qs.q: If ‘A & Z’ means ‘A is the brother of Z’, ‘A # Z’ means ‘A is the sister of Z’, ‘A ^ Z’ means ‘A is the brother of Z’s father’, ‘A @ Z’ means ‘A is the wife of Z’, ‘A % Z’ means ‘A is the mother of Z’, ‘A α Z’ means ‘A is the father of Z’, then how is J related to Z in the following expression? qs.q: Which of the following is mentioned in Article 1 of the Indian constitution?

India that is Bharat as federation of states
India that is Bharat shall be a Union of states
India that is Bharat as presidential form of democracy
qs.e:
Article 1(1) says "India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States".
Dr Ambedkar explained that "Union" was used because the federation did not come from an agreement among states, and states have no right to secede.
The words federation, parliamentary democracy and presidential democracy do not appear in Article 1.
Answer: India that is Bharat shall be a Union of states

qs.q: Who holds the record for the longest long jump in India as of 2023?

qs.q: Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with __________.

National emergency is in Part XVIII (Article 352), amendment in Part XX (Article 368) and Finance Commission in Article 280.
Answer: Union Executive

qs.q: Consider the following statements related to the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) handbook. 1.It will be launched by the Ministry of Science and Technology. 2.ODR is the resolution for cases outside courts using digital technology and techniques of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), such as negotiation, mediation and arbitration. 3.The development of ICT and increased use of internet has played a major role for ODR. qs.e:
Statement 1 is wrong: the ODR handbook was released in 2021 by NITI Aayog, not the Ministry of Science and Technology.
Statement 2 is correct: ODR settles disputes outside courts using digital tools and ADR methods like negotiation, mediation and arbitration.
Statement 3 is correct: growth of ICT and internet use made ODR possible.
Answer: Only 2 and 3

qs.q: Which part of the Constitution deals with the Panchayats?

It also added the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects for panchayats; municipalities are in Part IX-A (74th Amendment).
Part IV is DPSP, Part X Scheduled and Tribal Areas, and Part VII (states in Part B) was repealed.
Answer: Part IX

qs.q: Where was the 1st World Cup of Kabaddi organised in 2004?

qs.q: R targets to score 85% marks in exams. He scores 450 marks and misses the target by 35%. How much increment in percentage should be there in his scored marks to meet the target?
qs.e:
'Misses the target by 35%' means he got 85% − 35% = 50% of the maximum marks.
So 450 = 50% → maximum = 900, target = 85% of 900 = 765.
Required increase = (765 − 450)/450 × 100 = 315/450 × 100 = 70%.
Shortcut: (85 − 50)/50 × 100 = 70%.
Answer: 70

qs.q: Amit and Bilal buy goods for ₹1,500 and ₹2,000, respectively. Amit marks his goods up by y%, while Bilal marks his goods up by 2y% and offers a discount of y%. If both make the same profit, then find the value of y.

A trader offers the following discount schemes on the purchase of a refrigerator. ( I ) a discount of 10% followed by a discount of 8% ( ii ) successive discounts of 12% and 10% ( iii ) two successive discounts of 12% ( iv ) a discount of 20% In which scheme is the selling price the lowest?
qs.e:
Lowest selling price = highest effective discount; compare remaining fractions.
(i) 0.90 × 0.92 = 0.828; (ii) 0.88 × 0.90 = 0.792; (iii) 0.88 × 0.88 = 0.7744; (iv) 0.80.
Scheme (iii) leaves the smallest fraction (22.56% total discount).
Answer: (iii)

In an election between two candidates, P received 42% of the valid votes and Q won by 45,360 votes. 20% people did not cast their vote. If 10% of the votes cast were found invalid, what is the total number of votes registered in the poll booth?
qs.e:
Let N = registered votes. Cast = 80% of N; valid = 90% of that = 0.72N.

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series.

The square, triangle and circle sit on three back-to-back places of this path, and all three move one place along it each time (fig 1: top row; fig 2: top-middle, top-right, centre; fig 3: the diagonal; fig 4: centre, bottom-left, bottom-middle).
One more step puts all three in the bottom row: square, triangle, circle.
Answer: Option 4

qs.q: In a certain code language, 'A & B' means ‘ A is the brother of B’, 'A x B' means ‘A is the father of B’, 'A ? B' means ‘A is the mother of B’ and 'A ! B' means ‘A is the wife of B’. Which of the following means that W is the mother's mother of P?
o: W & R ! Y x O ? P
W ? R x Y ! O & P
W ? R ! Y & O x P
W ! R x Y ? O & P
qs.e:
Codes: & brother, x father, ? mother, ! wife. Needed: W is the mother of P's mother.
W ! R x Y ? O & P: Generation 1: W is R's wife; R is Y's father, so W is Y's mother.
Generation 2: Y is O's mother, and O is P's brother, so Y is P's mother.
Generation 3: O and P. W is P's mother's mother ✓.
Answer: W ! R x Y ? O & P

qs.q: Who among the following is known as ‘Captain Cool’ in Indian Cricket?
qs.e:
Mahendra Singh Dhoni is called 'Captain Cool' for his calm temperament under pressure.

Answer: Mahendra Singh Dhoni

qs.q: Which of the following is the first Indian woman Grandmaster in Chess?
qs.e:
S. Vijayalakshmi became India's first Woman Grandmaster (WGM) in 2001; she was also the first Indian woman to earn the International Master title.
Koneru Humpy became the first Indian woman to earn the full Grandmaster title (2002). Harika, Tania and Vaishali came later.

qs.q: The number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall NOT be less than _______.
qs.e:
The 91st Amendment (2003) added Article 164(1A): the number of ministers in a state, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the Assembly's strength, but shall not be less than 12.
This floor of 12 helps small states such as Goa and Sikkim.
Answer: 12

qs.q: ____________ Directive principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
qs.e:
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added four new DPSPs: Article 39(f) (healthy development of children), 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), 43A (workers' participation in management) and 48A (protection of environment).
Answer: Four

qs.q: If an employee's income is ₹72,000, the amount he spends is 40% higher than his savings. Therefore, his savings (in ₹) is:
qs.e:
Let savings = S; spending is 40% higher = 1.4S.
Income = S + 1.4S = 2.4S = 72000 → S = 30000.
Answer: 30000

qs.q: The single discount equivalent to a series discount of 60%, 70% and 80%.
qs.e:
Successive discounts multiply what is left: 0.40 × 0.30 × 0.20 = 0.024.
Only 2.4% of the price remains → single discount = 97.6%.
Answer: 97.6%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Dodge
qs.e:
Dodge means to avoid something by a quick movement or trick (dodge a question). 'Avoid' matches.
Force = compel; Boarding = getting on a vehicle, or lodging; Amount = quantity.
Answer: Avoid

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. This year’s budget is unlikely to pass as law since the president’s proposed budgets typically face a jaundiced eye but this one has gotten even more scepticism.
qs.e:
'A jaundiced eye' is a bitter, resentful or cynical attitude that makes one view something unfavourably.
Origin: jaundice was once thought to make a person see everything yellow (distorted).
The budgets are viewed with resentment and suspicion, matching 'even more scepticism'.
Good will and confidence are the opposite; 'jealousy' is envy of someone's success, which is not the sense here.
Answer: Resentment

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Dissipate
qs.e:
Dissipate means to waste or spend carelessly, or to scatter (dissipate a fortune). 'Spend' is the closest.
Malicious = spiteful; Haste = hurry; Glorious = splendid.
Answer: Spend

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Sejal visits the nearby temple off and on.
qs.e:
'Off and on' means occasionally, at irregular intervals – periodically.
Sejal visits the temple now and then, not all the time.
Constantly, regularly and continuously all suggest a steady, unbroken habit – the opposite.
Answer: Periodically

qs.q: If A is the sister of B, C is the daughter of A, D is the sister of A and E is the brother of C. How is D related to E?

qs.q: Who is considered the highest law officer of the state in India?

The Attorney General (Article 76) is the highest law officer of the Union, not of a state.

qs.q: Which of the following countries will host the ICC men’s Cricket World Cup in the year 2031?

The 2027 edition goes to South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

qs.q: Which of the following terms is related to football?

LBW, overs and third man are cricket terms.

qs.q: Which fundamental duty applies to you when you see your college friends start fighting with the canteen person when he passed a few anti-religious statements?
o: To value and preserve the rich heritage
To promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood
To protect and improve our natural environment
To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry

qs.q: Which Article deals with the election of the President?

Article 66 deals with election of the Vice-President, 74 the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, and 72 the pardoning power.

qs.q: Who among the following Indian cricketers were named the Wisden’s cricketer of the year in the 2022 edition of the Almanack?

qs.q: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Bills is related to the provision of modifying the list of Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu?

qs.q: The marked price of a revolving chair is ₹15,000. It is available on two successive discounts of 20% and 12%. What is its selling price (in ₹)?

In an election between two candidates, 80% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 4% votes were declared invalid. A candidate got 15,360 votes which were 80% of the valid votes. Find the total number of votes.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Maverick

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. This is a clear example of conflict of egos.

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, if M + Q – R + K – Y, then how is M related to Y?

qs.q: Which Article mentions the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

Article 148 provides for a Comptroller and Auditor General of India, appointed by the President and removable only like a Supreme Court judge.

Article 154 is the executive power of the Governor and Article 136 special leave to appeal.

qs.q: N. Rangasamy sworn in as the Chief Minister of Puducherry in May 2021. What is the name of the party he formed?

qs.q: Who among the following is the first Indian to win gold at Junior World Weightlifting Championship in May 2022?

qs.q: Sankalp Gupta is associated with which of the following events?

qs.q: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Fundamental Rights?
o: The Fundamental Rights are mentioned in constitution from article 12 to 35.
Fundamental Rights can be enforced by Law.
Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.
qs.e:
Fundamental Rights (Part III, Articles 12-35) are enforceable in courts, and Article 21 guarantees protection of life and personal liberty.
The idea of Fundamental Rights was borrowed from the US Constitution (Bill of Rights), not the British Constitution, which has no written bill of rights.
Answer: Fundamental rights are derived from the Britain Constitution.

qs.q: Rudrankksh Patil is associated with _________.

qs.q: Which of the following States have enacted the Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 in July- August 2021 to regulate slaughter and transport of cattle and proposed an amendment in December 2021 to allow inter-district transportation of cattle for agricultural and animal husbandry except in districts sharing international border?
qs.e:
The Assam Cattle Preservation Act, 2021 was passed in August 2021; it regulates slaughter, consumption and transport of cattle.

Answer: Assam

qs.q: Vipul spends 30% of his monthly income on rent, 60% of the remaining on groceries, and 40% of the remaining on others. If he saves ₹ 7056 in a month, then how much (in ₹) does he spend on groceries?
qs.e:

Others 40% of 0.28I → left (savings) 0.6 × 0.28I = 0.168I.
0.168I = 7056 → I = 42000.
Groceries = 0.42 × 42000 = ₹17,640.
Answer: 17640

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. At times, David behaves in a very obdurate manner to kids.

qs.q: Which Committee identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?

qs.q: The final match of IPL 2023 was hosted by which of the following cities?

qs.q: Who among the following famous badminton players won Swiss Open 2022?

qs.q: All the six members of a family, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, live together. 2 is the daughter of 3, but 3 is not the mother of 2. 1 and 3 are a married couple. 5 is the sister of 3. 4 is the daughter of 1. 6 is the brother of 2. Who is the mother of 2?
qs.e:
2 is the daughter of 3, but 3 is not her mother, so 3 is her father.
1 and 3 are a married couple, so 1 is 3's wife — the mother of 2.
(4 is 1's daughter, 6 is 2's brother and 5 is 3's sister, i.e. 2's aunt.)
Answer: 1

qs.e:

Step 2→3: top-left → centre, top-middle → top-right, top-right → bottom-right, centre → bottom-left, bottom-left → top-left, bottom-middle → top-middle, bottom-right → bottom-middle.

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 35, 46, 68, 101, 145, ?
qs.e:

Next difference = 55: 145 + 55 = 200.
Answer: 200

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. Z _ A _ Z _ _ Z A _ Z _
qs.e:
With ZZAZZA the series reads ZZA | ZZA | ZZA | ZZA – the block 'ZZA' repeats four times.
The other options give runs like AA or ZZZ, which break it.
Answer: ZZAZZA

Fourth: G, J, ?, P, S → +3 → M.
Answer: GSPM

qs.q: In chess which of the following may move only diagonally?
qs.e:
A bishop moves only diagonally, any number of empty squares, so it always stays on squares of one colour.
The queen moves diagonally as well as straight; the rook moves only straight; the knight moves in an L-shape.
Answer: The Bishop

qs.q: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Election Commission?
qs.e:
Part XV (Articles 324-329) deals with elections; Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.
Part XII deals with finance and property, Part IV with DPSPs and Part XI with Centre-state relations.
Answer: Part XV

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for protecting and improving the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife?
qs.e:
Article 48A, added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), asks the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
Its counterpart duty for citizens is Article 51A(g).
There are no Articles 47-A, 47-B or 49-C in the Constitution.
Answer: Article 48-A

qs.q: Where was the Durand Cup Tournament started in India in 1888?
qs.e:
The Durand Cup was started in 1888 at Shimla (then the summer capital of British India), named after Sir Henry Mortimer Durand, Foreign Secretary of India.
It is Asia's oldest football tournament and the third oldest in the world; it is now held in Kolkata and the North-East.
Answer: Shimla

qs.q: Ramesh purchased 130 books at the rate of ₹200 each and sold half of them at the rate of ₹300 each, one-fifth of them at the rate of ₹350 each and the rest at the cost price. Find his profit percentage.

Rohini buys a Bluetooth headphone set for ₹1,700 from a wholesale shop and marks it at ₹2,000. Later on, she allows a discount of 40% on its sale. What is her loss or gain percentage (correct up to two decimal places)?

Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Leela was in class when the big fight happened. So, if you want to know the details, You should ask her, you will get the truth given by somebody who is directly involved and therefore likely to be accurate.
qs.e:
'Straight from the horse's mouth' means information got directly from the person involved, so it is reliable. Leela was there, so you get it straight from the horse's mouth.
'Off the cuff' = without preparation, 'with kid gloves' = very gently, 'calling a spade a spade' = speaking frankly.
Answer: straight from the horse’s mouth
qs.u: given by somebody who is directly involved and therefore likely to be accurate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Derogatory
qs.e:
Derogatory means showing a disrespectful, critical attitude (derogatory remarks). 'Insulting' matches.
Delegation = a group sent to represent others; Salutary = beneficial; Derivative = copied from something else.
Answer: Insulting

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. We went to a legitimate Mexican restaurant for my birthday, where they served cuisine like you would find in Mexico.
qs.e:
Legitimate here means real, authentic (the restaurant served food like in Mexico). 'Genuine' matches.
Productive = producing a lot; Fictitious = imaginary; Falsified = altered to deceive (both antonyms).
Answer: genuine

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Our university is affiliated with various institutes all over the world.
qs.e:
Affiliated means officially connected or associated (a college affiliated with a university). 'Allied' (joined, connected) matches.
Disparate and Unalike = different; Diverse = varied. None means connected.
Answer: allied

The leaf with its stick turns 45° anticlockwise each time: stick pointing down, down-right, right, up-right, so next it points straight up.
Only option 1 has the arrow on top pointing right and the stick pointing up.
Answer: Option 1

qs.q: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, how is T related to P if ‘P − M + R ÷ T × S’?
qs.e:
Codes: + son, – wife, × brother, ÷ mother.  P – M + R ÷ T × S.
Generation 1: R is the mother of M and of T, so M and T are brothers (T is S's brother, male).
Generation 2 link: P is M's wife.
T is P's husband's brother.
Answer: Husband’s brother

qs.q: In the following series, only one letter-cluster is incorrect. Select the incorrect letter- cluster. ZXU SQN LKI ECZ XVS
qs.e:

LKI falls by 1 and 2 (L→K→I); the right cluster would be LJG.
Answer: LKI

qs.q: Which of the following states is one of those states that have no Panchayati Raj Institution at all?
qs.e:
Nagaland, along with Meghalaya and Mizoram, has no Panchayati Raj Institutions; Part IX does not apply to these states, which have traditional village councils instead.
Assam, Gujarat and Punjab have regular three-tier panchayats.
Answer: Nagaland

qs.q: Jaipal Singh Munda is associated with which of the following sports?
qs.e:
Jaipal Singh Munda captained the Indian hockey team that won the first Olympic hockey gold at Amsterdam 1928.
He later became a tribal leader and a member of the Constituent Assembly.
Answer: Hockey

qs.q: Mirabai Chanu secured a silver medal at which Commonwealth Games?
qs.e:
Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 48 kg weightlifting at the 2014 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
She then won gold at Gold Coast 2018 (48 kg) and Birmingham 2022 (49 kg), so the silver is 2014.
Answer: 2014

qs.q: As per article 158, the Governor shall NOT be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in ________ Schedule.
qs.e:
Article 158(1) says the Governor shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any state specified in the First Schedule.
The First Schedule lists the states and union territories of India.
The Seventh Schedule has the three lists, the Third the oaths, and the Fifth tribal areas.
Answer: First

qs.q: If a 12-year-old is found to be working in a factory manufacturing carpets, which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India will be violated?
qs.e:
Article 24 prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous work.
A 12-year-old in a carpet factory directly violates it.
Article 23 bans trafficking and forced labour, and Articles 25-26 cover freedom of religion.
Answer: Article 24

qs.q: A man loses 28% by selling an article for ₹144. If he sells it for ₹288, what will be his gain/loss percentage?
qs.e:
Loss 28% means SP = 72% of CP: CP = 144 ÷ 0.72 = ₹200.
New SP = 288, gain = 88.
Gain% = 88/200 × 100 = 44%.
Shortcut: 288 is double 144, so new SP = 2 × 72% = 144% of CP, a 44% gain.
Answer: Gain, 44%

qs.q: During a new-year sale, a shopkeeper offers a discount scheme to his customers, ‘Buy 5 Sweaters, Get 2 Sweaters Free’. Find the effective percentage discount given by the shopkeeper.
qs.e:
The customer takes 7 sweaters but pays for only 5.
Discount = free items ÷ total items = 2/7.
2/7 × 100 = 28 4/7 %.
Answer: 28 4/7 %

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. He said that he lacks the ___________ to stand in a queue. (patience)
qs.e:
Patience is the ability to wait or put up with something without getting upset. 'Endurance' (the power to bear something unpleasant) fits waiting in a queue.
Elegance = grace; Acceptance = agreeing to something; Relevance = connection with the matter.
Answer: endurance

qs.q: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the husband of B’, A − B means ‘B is the mother of A’, A × B means ‘B is the sister of A’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, how is Q related to T if ‘P + Q × R − S ÷ T’?
qs.e:
Codes: A + B: A is B's husband; A – B: B is A's mother; A × B: B is A's sister; A ÷ B: A is B's daughter.  P + Q × R – S ÷ T.
Generation 1: S ÷ T: S is T's daughter.
Generation 2: R – S: S is R's mother; Q × R: R is Q's sister, so S is Q's mother too.
P + Q: P is Q's husband, so Q is female — S's daughter, and S is T's daughter.
Answer: Daughter’s daughter

qs.q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts led to formation of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
qs.e:
The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 introduced the Goods and Services Tax and added Article 279A, under which the GST Council was set up.
The Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes state Finance Ministers; GST came into force on 1 July 2017.
The 102nd gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes and the 103rd brought 10% EWS reservation.
Answer: 101st Constitutional Amendment Act

qs.q: The term Blue Line is associated with which of the following games?
qs.e:
The blue lines in ice hockey are the two lines that divide the rink into the defending zone, neutral zone and attacking zone.
They decide offside: an attacker may not enter the attacking zone ahead of the puck.
Answer: Ice Hockey

qs.q: India finished on which of the following positions in overall medals tally at Commonwealth games 2022?
qs.e:
At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, India finished 4th in the medal tally with 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze).
Australia, England and Canada took the top three places.
Answer: 4th

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good’?
qs.e:
Article 39(b) directs the State to ensure that ownership and control of the material resources of the community are distributed to best serve the common good.
39(a) is the right to an adequate means of livelihood, 39(c) prevents concentration of wealth, and 39(d) is equal pay for equal work for men and women.
Answer: Article 39(b)

qs.q: How many athletes were selected to represent India at the 1924 Paris Summer Olympics?
qs.e:
India's athletics team for the 1924 Paris Olympics was picked at the Indian Olympic Games held in Lahore in February 1924; the key counts 8 athletes selected.
India went to Paris with track-and-field athletes plus a tennis team; full Olympic records list 13 competitors in all (7 athletics, 6 tennis).
Answer: 8

qs.q: The monthly income of Ramesh in year 2021 was ₹18,600 and his monthly expenditure was ₹12,400. In year 2022 his income increased by 15% and his expenditure increased by 8%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
The single discount equivalent to the discount series of 15%, 20% and 5% is:
qs.e:
Successive discounts multiply the price: 0.85 × 0.80 × 0.95.
0.85 × 0.80 = 0.68; 0.68 × 0.95 = 0.646.
Price paid = 64.6%, so single discount = 100 − 64.6 = 35.4%.
Answer: 35.4%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold. The choice was judicious as further events proved.
qs.e:
Judicious means showing good judgement, wise (a judicious choice). 'Prudent' (wise and careful) matches.
Hasty = done in a hurry; Ridiculous and Silly = foolish. These are opposites.
Answer: prudent

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. It was his decency that he employed him.
qs.e:
Decency means good, polite and respectable behaviour (the decency to apologise). 'Courtesy' (politeness, kindness) is closest.
Deception = trickery; Rudeness = bad manners; Perversion = a corruption of what is right. All are opposites.
Answer: Courtesy

qs.q: Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. Due to her impoverished state, most of her relatives treated her with contempt.
o: Gave a wide space to her
Turned up their nose at her
qs.e:
'Turn up one's nose at' someone means to treat them as not good enough, i.e. with contempt.
'Turn the corner' means to start improving, 'come in handy' means to be useful, and 'gave a wide space' is not this idiom.
Answer: Turned up their nose at her

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Let the dust settle
o: To wait for a situation to become clear or certain
Wait for the other person to make a move
To make use of a situation
qs.e:
'Let the dust settle' means to wait until a confused or excited situation calms down and becomes clear before acting.
Image: after a fight or a storm, waiting for the dust to fall so you can see clearly.
Example: Let the dust settle after the merger before asking for a raise.
Tidying a space is literal; waiting for the other person's move and making use of a situation are different ideas.
Answer: To wait for a situation to become clear or certain

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the son of B’; ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; and, ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is M related to T if ‘M # N @ L × P + T’?

Numbers 33, 36, 39, 42 go up by 3 → 45.

qs.q: In which of the following games is the ‘Baulk Line’ used?
qs.e:
In kabaddi, the baulk line is the line in each half that a raider must cross for the raid to be valid.
The bonus line lies beyond it. Tennis and badminton use baselines and service lines; kho-kho uses a central lane and cross lanes.
Answer: Kabaddi

qs.q: Nirupama Sanjeev is a famous ______ player of India?
qs.e:
Nirupama Sanjeev (Nirupama Vaidyanathan) is an Indian tennis player.
In 1998 she became the first Indian woman in the Open Era to win a main-draw singles match at a Grand Slam (Australian Open), and she won a mixed-doubles bronze at the 1998 Asian Games.
Answer: tennis

qs.q: Which of the following are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51?
qs.e:
Part IV (Articles 36-51) contains the Directive Principles of State Policy.
Fundamental Rights are in Part III (12-35), Fundamental Duties in Part IV-A (51A), and the Union in Part V.
Answer: Directive Principles of State Policy

qs.q: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the _________ to establish authorities charged with the mandate of preventing environmental pollution in all its forms.
qs.e:
Under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Central Government can take measures to protect the environment and may set up authorities to prevent, control and abate pollution.
The Act was passed after the Bhopal gas tragedy (1984) as an umbrella law for environmental protection.
Answer: Central Government

qs.q: Who among the following famous badminton players won Singapore Open 2022?
qs.e:
PV Sindhu won the Singapore Open 2022 women's singles title in July 2022, beating China's Wang Zhi Yi in the final.
It was her first Super 500 title.
Answer: PV Sindhu

qs.q: Which part of Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President?
qs.e:
Part V (The Union) contains the provisions on the Vice-President, Articles 63-71; Article 66 deals with the election of the Vice-President.
The electoral college consists of all members (elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament.
Part VI is the states, Part IV DPSPs and Part III Fundamental Rights.
Answer: Part V

qs.q: Which of the following Articles and Parts of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature?
qs.e:
Part VI, Chapter III, Articles 168-212, deals with the State Legislature: its composition, officers, procedure and privileges.
Articles 214-231 are about High Courts, 79-122 about Parliament and 243-243O about panchayats.
Answer: Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI

qs.q: Three people, A, B and C, invest in a business in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. It was decided that 9% of the profits will go to charity. If the total profit was ₹2,50,000, then find the share of C in the profit (in ₹).
A person first increases the price of a commodity by 8% and then he announces a discount of 18%. The actual discount (in%) on the original price is:
qs.e:
Take original price 100. After 8% increase: 108.
After 18% discount: 108 × 0.82 = 88.56.
Actual discount on original = 100 − 88.56 = 11.44%.
Shortcut: 8 − 18 − (8×18)/100 = −10 − 1.44 = −11.44%.
Answer: 11.44

qs.q: If books bought at prices ranging from ₹200 to ₹260 are sold at prices ranging from ₹250 to 300, what is the greatest possible profit that might be made in selling 25 books?
qs.e:
The greatest profit comes from buying at the lowest price and selling at the highest.
Profit per book = 300 − 200 = ₹100.
For 25 books: 25 × 100 = ₹2,500.
Answer: ₹2,500

qs.q: Two successive percentage decrease of 25% each is by what percentage less than two successive percentage increase of 25% each? (Round to two decimal places.)
qs.e:
Two decreases of 25%: 0.75 × 0.75 = 0.5625 → net decrease 43.75%.
Two increases of 25%: 1.25 × 1.25 = 1.5625 → net increase 56.25%.
Compare the two percentages: (56.25 − 43.75)/56.25 × 100 = 12.5/56.25 × 100 = 22.22%.
Answer: 22.22%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The company understood that these small protests of employees regarding low wages were just the tip of the iceberg.
o: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater
A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is solvable
A large part of a problem which is really noticeable
A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is non-existent
qs.e:
'The tip of the iceberg' is the small visible part of a problem whose real size is much bigger.
Origin: only about a tenth of an iceberg shows above water.
The small wage protests hinted at much deeper staff unhappiness.
Option 2 ('solvable') and option 4 ('non-existent') change the meaning; option 3 calls it a large part, but the tip is small.
Answer: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Even when he was left with plenty of fortune, he lived a frugal life.

Hardworking = industrious; Purposeless = aimless; Extraordinary = remarkable.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. He was the most honest and good-hearted man that she had ever met.
qs.e:
Honest means truthful and free from deceit (an honest witness). 'Sincere' matches.
Deceptive and Fake = false, the opposite; Biased = unfairly favouring one side.
Answer: Sincere

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is I related to H if ‘B + R × I − T ÷ H’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, × wife, ÷ father.  B + R × I – T ÷ H.
Generation 1: B is R's mother; R is I's wife. I is T's brother.
Generation 2: T is H's father.
I is the brother of H's father.
Answer: Father’s brother

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series?
qs.e:
The four corner symbols move one corner clockwise each step, and the centre arrow turns 45° clockwise each step.
From figure 4 (* , ●; ▲, □; arrow ↘): ▲ top-left, * top-right, □ bottom-left, ● bottom-right, arrow pointing down.
Answer: Option 1

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 176,167,156,147,136, ?
qs.e:
The differences alternate: −9, −11, −9, −11.
Next difference is −9: 136 − 9 = 127.
Answer: 127

qs.q: Which of the four options will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? FX32, EV38, DT44, CR50, ?
qs.e:
First letters F, E, D, C go back 1 → B.
Second letters X, V, T, R go back 2 → P.
Numbers 32, 38, 44, 50 go up by 6 → 56.
Answer: BP56

qs.q: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? QGMW, VCPU, AYSS, ? , KQYO
qs.e:
Check each position (A=1).
First: Q, V, A, ?, K → +5 → F.
Second: G, C, Y, ?, Q → −4 → U.
Third: M, P, S, ?, Y → +3 → V.
Fourth: W, U, S, ?, O → −2 → Q.
Answer: FUVQ

qs.q: At the 36th National Games, Hashika Ramchandra won six gold medals in which of the following sports?
qs.e:
Teenage swimmer Hashika Ramchandra of Karnataka won six gold medals in swimming at the 36th National Games in Gujarat (2022).
She was among the most successful athletes of those Games.
Answer: Swimming

qs.q: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
qs.e:
Gulzarilal Nanda was the acting Prime Minister twice, for 13 days each time: after Nehru's death (1964) and after Shastri's death (1966).
Among full Prime Ministers, Atal Bihari Vajpayee's 1996 term of 16 days was the shortest; Charan Singh and Chandra Shekhar served a few months each.
Answer: Gulzarilal Nanda

qs.q: ‘Castling’ is related to which of the following sports?
qs.e:
Castling is a special chess move in which the king moves two squares towards a rook and that rook jumps to the square the king crossed.
It is the only move in which two pieces move at once, used to make the king safe.
Answer: Chess

qs.q: The concept of ‘Independence of judiciary’ in the Indian Constitution is taken from the Constitution of:
qs.e:
India borrowed the independence of the judiciary, judicial review, Fundamental Rights and the removal procedure for judges from the US Constitution.
From Britain it took the parliamentary system and rule of law; from Ireland the DPSPs; from France the republic and ideals of liberty, equality, fraternity.
Answer: The USA

qs.q: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
qs.e:
The writ of prohibition is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to stop it from acting beyond its jurisdiction.
It is preventive, issued while proceedings are pending; certiorari is curative, used to quash an order already passed without jurisdiction.
Habeas corpus is for unlawful detention and quo warranto challenges a person's right to a public office.
Answer: Prohibition

qs.q: The marked price of an electronic watch in a store is ₹15,620 and it is available at a discount of 27%. What is the price (in ₹, to the nearest tens) that a customer pays if he buys from the store?
qs.e:
Price paid = 73% of 15,620.
15,620 × 0.73 = 11,402.6, which rounds to ₹11,400 (nearest ten).
Answer: 11,400

qs.q: Raman fixes the sale price of his goods at 16% above the cost price. He sells his goods at 12% less than the fixed price. Find the profit percentage correct to two places of decimal.
Identify from the given options the word which is similar in meaning to the following word. Munificent
qs.e:
Munificent means very generous (a munificent donor). 'Magnanimous' (generous, big-hearted) matches.
Miserly = stingy (the antonym); Malicious = spiteful; Underappreciated = not valued enough.
Answer: Magnanimous

qs.q: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Verity is a good virtue for human life.
qs.e:
'Verity' means truth or the quality of being true. So 'Truth is a good virtue for human life.'
Information, knowledge and cooperation are not meanings of verity.
Answer: Truth

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Bincy’s mother kept her cards close to her chest.
o: Kept her plans and thoughts hidden
Informed that all the cards must be kept safe
Kept her purse and money by herself
qs.e:
'To keep one's cards close to one's chest' means to keep one's plans, thoughts or intentions secret.
Origin: card players hold their cards close so others cannot see them.
Example: The coach kept his cards close to his chest and did not reveal the team until match day.
The other options take 'cards' literally or talk about money or affection.
Answer: Kept her plans and thoughts hidden
qs.u: kept her cards close to her chest

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Carcass
qs.e:
A carcass is the dead body of an animal (a deer carcass). 'Corpse' (a dead body) matches.
Scrap = a small piece or waste; Prison = a jail; Gale = a strong wind.
Answer: Corpse

qs.q: Identify the figure given in the options which when put in place of the question mark (?) will logically complete the series?
qs.e:
The four symbols move one step along the cycle top-left → top-right → centre → bottom-right → top-left.
Check figure 1→2: L goes top-left → top-right, * top-right → centre, ! centre → bottom-right, □ bottom-right → top-left.
From figure 4 (*, !; □; L): L top-left, * top-right, ! centre, □ bottom-right – the same as figure 1.
Answer: Option 3

qs.q: Select the figure from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) and logically complete the series.
qs.e:
The pentagon with its T-shaped stick turns 45° clockwise each time: stick down, down-left, left, up-left, so next it points straight up.
The symbol outside (top-left) of one figure goes inside the pentagon in the next (A, ☆, B moved inside), and the outside symbols alternate letter and sign: A, ☆, B, ∞, so next C.
Figure 5: C outside, ∞ inside, stick pointing up.
Answer: Option 2

qs.q: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? FHVQ, IJSO, LLPM, ONMK, ?
qs.e:
Check each position (A=1).
First: F, I, L, O → +3 → R.
Second: H, J, L, N → +2 → P.
Third: V, S, P, M → −3 → J.
Fourth: Q, O, M, K → −2 → I.
Answer: RPJI

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ V D W Y _ D W Y V _ W Y _ D _
qs.e:
With YVDVW the series reads YVDW | YVDW | YVDW | YVDW – the block 'YVDW' repeats four times.
The other options break a block (e.g. option 2 gives YWDW).
Answer: YVDVW

qs.q: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is 4 related to 1 if ‘4 × 3 − 2 − 1’?
qs.e:
Codes: + mother, – brother, × wife, ÷ father.  4 × 3 – 2 – 1.
3 is 2's brother and 2 is 1's brother, so 3, 2 and 1 are siblings (same generation); 3 is male.
4 is 3's wife.
So 4 is the wife of 1's brother.
Answer: Brother’s wife

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 672, 677, 686, 699, 716, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 5, 9, 13, 17 – rising by 4.
Next difference = 21: 716 + 21 = 737.
Answer: 737

qs.q: UPSC is a Constitutional Body to conduct examinations for appointments to the services of the Union and the services of the State, respectively, under Article ________.
qs.e:
Article 320 lays down the functions of the UPSC and state Public Service Commissions, the first of which is to conduct examinations for appointments to Union and state services.
Article 315 sets up these commissions; Article 324 deals with the Election Commission, and 332 with reservation of seats for SC/STs in state assemblies.
Answer: 320

qs.q: The first Indian Olympic Games was hosted by which of the following cities?
qs.e:
The first Indian Olympic Games (forerunner of the National Games) were held at Lahore in 1924.
They were also used to pick India's athletics team for the 1924 Paris Olympics.
Answer: Lahore

qs.q: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as population between the ages of ________ and _________.
qs.e:
The National Youth Policy 2014 defines "youth" as people aged 15 to 29 years.
The earlier National Youth Policy of 2003 had used a wider band of 13–35 years; the 2014 policy narrowed it.
The tempting 15–24 band is the United Nations definition, not India's.
Answer: 15; 29

qs.q: At which Olympic games did Abhinav Bindra win the gold medal?
qs.e:
Abhinav Bindra won gold in the men's 10 m air rifle at Beijing 2008.
It was independent India's first individual Olympic gold medal.
Answer: Beijing 2008

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the ‘Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections’?
qs.e:
Article 46 (a Directive Principle in Part IV) directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and other weaker sections and to protect them from social injustice and exploitation.
Others: Art 45 – early childhood care and education below 6 years; Art 47 – nutrition, public health and prohibition of intoxicants; Art 48 – organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry, ban on cow slaughter.
Answer: Article 46

qs.q: Ram’s income is 2.5% more than Shyam’s income. By what percentage is Shyam’s income less than Ram’s income?
qs.e:
Take Shyam = 100, Ram = 102.5.
Shyam is less than Ram by 2.5/102.5 × 100 = 2.439…%.
Formula: r/(100 + r) × 100 = 2.5/102.5 × 100 ≈ 2.43% (taking two decimals).
Answer: 2.43%

qs.q: A shopkeeper has a fault of 100 g in a 3 kg weight. He sold 3 kg of potatoes to Charu using the same faulty weight for ₹46. The cost price of the potatoes for the seller was ₹12 per kg. How much profit (in ₹) did he earn on the potatoes?
qs.e:
A 3 kg weight short by 100 g actually weighs 2.9 kg.
So Charu gets 2.9 kg for ₹46.
Cost to seller = 2.9 × 12 = ₹34.80.
Profit = 46 − 34.80 = ₹11.20.
Answer: 11.2

qs.q: An article costs₹1,000 for a salesman. He fixes its marked price as₹1,500. He sells it to a customer at a discount of 20%. He gives a furtherdiscount of 10% for each cash payment. Find the percentage of loss or gain that the salesman makes on sale.
Select the correct meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Lucy’s conceited conduct with her colleagues has left her high and dry
qs.e:
'To leave someone high and dry' means to leave them helpless and without support.
Origin: a ship stranded on the shore when the tide goes out.
Lucy's arrogant behaviour made colleagues abandon her, so she is helpless.
Impoverished = poor (money is not mentioned); superseding = replacing; surrounded by people is the opposite.
Answer: Helpless

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. She __________ requested him to pay the bills. (persistently)
qs.e:
Persistently means repeatedly and without giving up (she persistently asked). 'Continuously' (without stopping) is the closest.
Impetuously = rashly, without thinking; Obliviously = unaware; Tremendously = enormously.
Answer: continuously

qs.q: In the following question, select the related word from the given alternatives. Watt:Powert:Pascal:?
qs.e:
Watt is the SI unit of power, so the pair is unit : quantity.
Pascal is the SI unit of pressure (1 Pa = 1 N/m²).
Energy is measured in joule and force in newton, so they do not fit.

qs.q: In the following question, select the related word from the given alternatives. Mekong:Tibet::Amazon:?
qs.e:
The pair is river : where it originates. The Mekong rises on the Tibetan Plateau.
The Amazon rises in the Andes of Peru, so the answer is Peru.

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. c Gk, Gko, kososw,?
qs.e:
Each letter moves +4 from one term to the next: C→G→K→O→S, G→K→O→S→W, K→O→S→W→A.
So after OSW comes S W A.

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. MIN, NJM, OKL, PLK,？
qs.e:
Letter-wise: 1st letter +1 (M,N,O,P→Q), 2nd letter +1 (I,J,K,L→M), 3rd letter −1 (N,M,L,K→J).
Next term = QMJ.

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. BRF, EUH, HXJ, KAL,?
qs.e:
1st letter +3 (B,E,H,K→N), 2nd letter +3 (R,U,X,A→D, wrapping past Z), 3rd letter +2 (F,H,J,L→N).
Next term = NDN.

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series: WZWT, WVOH, WRGV, WNYJ,?
qs.e:
1st letter stays W. 2nd letter −4: Z,V,R,N→J. 3rd letter −8: W,O,G,Y→Q (wrapping). 4th letter −12: T,H,V,J→X (wrapping).
So the next term is WJQX.

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series: MCFI，NEKP, OGPW, PIUD,？

Position-wise gaps: 1st +1 (M,N,O,P→Q), 2nd +2 (C,E,G,I→K), 3rd +5 (F,K,P,U→Z), 4th +7 (I,P,W,D→K, wrapping).
So the next term is QKZK.

qs.q: series between the letter that is second from the left and the one that is fourth from the right in the new letter-cluster formed?
