qs.q: Complete Y2,
qs.e: Letters go backwards (Z, Y, X, W, V) and numbers go forwards (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), so the next term is V5.

qs.q: Ais the daughter of B. B is the son of C. D is the wife of C. How is Drelated to A?
qs.e: B is the son of C, and D is C's wife, so D is B's mother. A is B's daughter, so D is A's grandmother.

qs.q: What is the average of 5 consecutive odd numbers starting from 13?
qs.e: For consecutive odd numbers the average is the middle term: 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, so the average is 17.

qs.q: Pointing to a photograph, a man says, "she is the daughter of the only son of my father's wife". Who is the woman to the man?
qs.e: "My father's wife" is the man's mother, and her only son is the man himself. So the woman is his daughter.

qs.q: Karnam Malleswari became the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal in which sporting discipline?
qs.e: Karnam Malleswari won bronze in weightlifting (69 kg) at the Sydney 2000 Olympics. She was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal.

qs.q: Fill in theblanks: At the 1984 summer olympics, P. T. Usha narrowly missed a bronze medal by._ of a second.
qs.e: At Los Angeles 1984, P.T. Usha finished 4th in the 400 m hurdles, missing the bronze by 1/100th of a second.

qs.q: Consider the following statements: 1) Both the Prime Minister (PM) and Chief Minister (CM) can advise dissolution of the respective Lower House. 2) only the PM can recommend President's Rule under Article 356 of the Constitution. Which ofthe statements is/are correct?
qs.e: Per the key, both are correct. The PM advises the President, and the CM the Governor, to dissolve the Lok Sabha or the Assembly. President's Rule (Art 356) is imposed by the President on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers headed by the PM; a CM has no such role.

qs.q: Article 50 is part of which section of the Constitution?
qs.e: Article 50 (separate the judiciary from the executive) is a Directive Principle, in Part IV (Arts 36-51). Related: Fundamental Duties are in Art 51A, Part IVA.

qs.q: Agrocer purchased 50 kg of rice at 40 perkg and 20 kg of another variety of rice at 55 per kg. He mixed the two varieties and sold the entire mixture at 48 perkg. Find his total profit or loss in this transaction.
A television set has a marked price of 20,000. It is sold after two successive discounts. If the first discount is 15% and the final selling price is15,300, whatisthepercentageofthesecond discount?
qs.e: After 15% off: 20,000 x 0.85 = 17,000. Then 15,300/17,000 = 0.90, so the second discount is 10%.

qs.q: A manufacturer marked a product 30% above its cost price. He provided a discount to a customer, which resulted in him making a profit of 17%. What was the rate of discount given by the manufacturer?
qs.e: Take CP = 100: MP = 130 and SP = 117. Discount = 13/130 = 10%.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:ILLUMINATE
qs.e: Illuminate means to light up, and figuratively to make clear, i.e. explain ("illuminate a point"). Darken and hide are its opposites.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Eat humble pie
o: To accept insult or defeat gracefully
qs.e: "Eat humble pie" means to admit a mistake and accept humiliation or defeat meekly. Option 1 (demand an apology) is the reverse: that is what the other side does.

qs.q: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The architect discussed the vault beneath the cathedral.
o: The gymnast performed a perfect vault over the horse. v
The treasury vault was secured with biometric locks.
The earthquake cracked the stone vault supporting the nave.
The nobles were interred in the family vault.
qs.e: In the given sentence "vault" is an arched stone roof or chamber. Option 1 uses the unrelated meaning "a leap", the same spelling with a different sense. Options 2-4 all refer to a chamber or arched structure.

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series: HDZLGBPJDTMF?
qs.e: Letter 1: H, L, P, T, X (+4). Letter 2: D, G, J, M, P (+3). Letter 3: Z, B, D, F, H (+2, wrapping after Z). Answer XPH.

qs.q: A is the brother of B. B is the daughter of C. How is A related to C?
qs.e: B is C's daughter, and A is B's brother, so A is also C's child. A is male (brother), so A is C's son.

qs.q: B is the sister ofA. A is the brother of C. C is the daughter of D. How is B related to D?
qs.e: B is A's sister, and A is C's brother, so A, B and C are siblings. C is D's daughter, so B (female) is also D's daughter.

Consider the following statements about service rules in table tennis: 1) At 10-10, service alternates every two points. 2) in the final doubles game, receiver order changes when one side reaches 5 points. Which of the above is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1 is wrong: at 10-10 (deuce), service alternates after EACH point, not every two.
Statement 2 is right: in the last possible game of a doubles match, the receiving pair changes order when one side first reaches 5 points.
So only 2 is correct.

qs.q: What is meant by an "own goal" in football?
o: A goal scored from a penalty
A goal scored accidentally into one's own net
A goal scored during injury time
qs.e:
An own goal is when a player accidentally puts the ball into his own team's net; it counts for the opponents.
It is not about who scores (goalkeeper), how (penalty) or when (injury time).

qs.q: Consider the following statements about India's Winter olympics participation: 1) shiva Keshavan competed in six Games and introduced luge to india. 2) Arif Mohammad Khan was the first Indian to qualify for two alpine sking events in 2022. Which ofthe statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1: Shiva Keshavan represented India in luge at six Winter Olympics (1998-2018) - correct.
Statement 2: Arif Mohammad Khan (J&K) was the first Indian to qualify in two alpine events (slalom and giant slalom) at Beijing 2022 - correct.
Both are correct.

qs.q: Fill in the blank:
qs.e:
Neeraj Chopra won India's first World Athletics Championships gold at Budapest 2023 with 88.17 m.
Related: he won silver at Eugene 2022 and Olympic gold at Tokyo 2020 (87.58 m).

qs.q: Which of the following disputes falls under the Supreme Court's exclusive original jurisdiction as per Article 131 of the Indian Constitution?
o: Election disputes of MPs and MLAs
Disputes between Centre and one or more States
qs.e:
Article 131 gives the Supreme Court exclusive original jurisdiction in disputes between the Centre and one or more States (or between States).
Inter-State water disputes are excluded by Article 262; election disputes go to High Courts; appeals are appellate, not original, jurisdiction.

qs.q: Under Bharatiya Nagarik suraksha Samhita(BNss), the period for default bail in minor offences is capped at?
qs.e:
Under BNSS Section 187, if the charge sheet is not filed in time, default bail is due after 60 days for offences punishable with less than 10 years.
Related: for offences punishable with death, life or 10+ years the limit is 90 days.

qs.q: Fill in the Blank: Doctrine of Severability allows the part of a law to be retained. Raa ：
qs.e:
Doctrine of Severability (Art. 13): only the unconstitutional part of a law is struck down, and the valid part is kept if it can stand on its own.
Related: the Doctrine of Eclipse deals with pre-constitutional laws that become dormant, not void.

qs.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Concurrent List allows both Centre and states to legislate. 2. Incase of conflict, State law prevailsover Union law. Which ofthe above is/are correct?
qs.e:
1 is correct: both Parliament and State legislatures can make laws on Concurrent List subjects.
2 is wrong: under Article 254, in a conflict the Union law prevails (unless the State law has Presidential assent).

qs.q: Seventy-five percent of a number is 15 more than two-thirds of that number. Find the number.

A mobile phone retailer sells a phone for P and earns a profit of 20%. For a special festive offer, he marks the same phone at 1.5P. At the offer, he provides a discount of 10%. what will be the percentage profit that he will make during the festive offer?
qs.e:
CP = P/1.2. Festive SP = 1.5P x 0.9 = 1.35P.
SP/CP = 1.35 x 1.2 = 1.62 -> profit 62%.

qs.q: A gadget is sold at a 15% discount on its marked price. This sale leads to a profit of 20% on its cost price. If the profit earned is 450, what would have been the selling price if the gadget was sold at a 25% discount on its marked price?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:GARRULoUS
qs.e:
Garrulous = excessively talkative (about trivial things).
Reserved and Silent are antonyms; 'Listen' is a verb, not a synonym.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Carry coals to Newcastle
o: Provide something where it is already abundant
qs.e:
'Carry coals to Newcastle' = supply something to a place that already has plenty of it (Newcastle was a coal-mining centre).
It is about pointless effort, not complaining or seeking advice.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Toe the line
qs.e:
'Toe the line' = conform to rules or authority; obey exactly what is required.
It has nothing to do with physically following a leader or joining the army.

qs.q: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The artisan engraved a cartouche around the royal name.
o: The papyrus bore a golden cartouche of the pharaoh.
The archaeologist uncovered a silver cartouche.
The sculptor carved a cartouche of floral motifs for the ceiling.
qs.e:
In the question, 'cartouche' is the oval ring enclosing an Egyptian royal name, and A, B, C use that same sense.
In D, 'cartouche' is a scroll-shaped ornamental panel in architecture: same spelling, different meaning, so it is the homonym.

qs.q: A is the brother of B. C is the sister of B. D is the father of C. How is D related to A?
qs.e:
C is the sister of B and A is the brother of B, so A, B and C are siblings.
D is the father of C, so D is also the father of A.

qs.q: Pointing to a boy, a man said,"He is the son of my wife's sister's husband." How is the boy related to the man?
qs.e:
My wife's sister's husband = my brother-in-law (co-brother).
His son is the man's nephew (by marriage). Per the official key the answer is Nephew.

qs.q: Which of the following terms is specifically associated with the javelin throw?
qs.e:
In javelin (like shot put, discus and hammer) the implement must land inside the marked throwing sector (about 29 degrees) for a valid throw.
Related: in javelin the tip must land first; Neeraj Chopra is India's best-known javelin thrower.

qs.q: Who won India's first Paralympic medals in the women's 200mT12 and men'sjavelin throwF41events at Paris 2024?
o: Simran (bronze, 200m T12) and Navdeep Singh (gold, javelin F41)
Navdeep Singh (bronze, 200m T12) and Simran (gold, javelin F41)
Simran (silver, 200m T12) and Navdeep Singh (gold, javelin F41)
Navdeep Singh (gold, 200m T12) and Simran (bronze, javelin F41)
qs.e:
Paris 2024 Paralympics: Simran Sharma won bronze in women's 200 m T12, and Navdeep Singh won gold in men's javelin F41 (upgraded from silver).
Related: India won 29 medals in Paris (7 gold), its best Paralympic tally.

qs.q: What is the minimum age required to contest the Presidential election in India?
qs.e:
Article 58: to be President a person must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a Lok Sabha member.
Related: the Vice-President also needs to be 35 (Art. 66), while a Rajya Sabha MP needs to be 30.

qs.q: Which Article empowers the Parliament to create laws on State List subjects under national interest?
qs.e:
Article 249: if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution (2/3 of members present and voting) that it is in the national interest, Parliament may legislate on a State List subject.
Related: such a resolution is valid for 1 year and can be extended by a year at a time.

qs.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Sixth Schedule is applicable to Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh: 2. Itempowers autonomous district councils to make laws on specified subjects. Which ofthe above is/are correct?
qs.e:
1 is wrong: the Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, not Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh.
2 is correct: it creates Autonomous District Councils that can make laws on listed subjects. So only 2.

qs.q: A vendor purchases7 shirts at the marked price of 6 shirts. If he sells each shirt after giving a 4% discount on its marked price, what is his profit percentage?
qs.e:
CP of 7 shirts = MP of 6, so CP per shirt = 6/7 MP. SP = 0.96 MP.
SP/CP = 0.96 x 7/6 = 1.12 -> profit 12%.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:LUMINo Us
qs.e:
Luminous = giving off light, bright, shining; Radiant is the synonym.
Dull, Dim and Opaque are opposites (or unrelated).

Exiguous = very small in amount; meagre, scanty.
Huge, Excessive and Abundant are antonyms, which is the trap.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: To chewthecud of reflection
qs.e:
'Chew the cud' = think about something slowly and carefully, the way a cow keeps chewing its food.
So 'to chew the cud of reflection' = to ponder deeply, not to eat slowly.

qs.q: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The bishop condemned the act as simony, citing canonical law:
o: The preacher was accused of simonyfor charging for blessings.
The court equated indulgence-selling with simony.
The alchemistfailed to explain the simony in his formulas.
Simony was rampant in medieval ecclesiastical courts.
qs.e:
Official key: C. Simony is the buying or selling of church offices or spiritual benefits; A, B and D all use it in that sense.
Only in C is the word used in a different, unrelated sense (a flaw in an alchemist's formulas), so C is the answer to this 'homonym' question.

qs.q: X is the daughter of Y. Y is the son of Z. W is the wife of Z. How is W related to x?
qs.e:
Chain: X is Y's daughter; Y is Z's son; W is Z's wife, so W is Y's mother.
Mother of X's father = paternal grandmother. Answer: Grandmother.

A − B: A is B's brother. B + C: B is C's mother.
A is the brother of C's mother, so A is C's maternal uncle.

qs.q: Which of the following is true about "en passant" in chess?
o: Only after a pawn moves two squares and waits a turn.
Can be done within two moves after the pawn's advance.
Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares.
Only if the capturing pawn is on a dark square.
qs.e:
En passant must be played immediately, on the very next move after the enemy pawn advances two squares past your pawn. If you wait, the right is lost.
It is the only capture where the capturing pawn does not land on the captured piece's square.

qs.q: In which Olympic Games did Leander Paes make his debut before winning India's first Olympic tennis medal in the following edition?
qs.e:
Leander Paes made his Olympic debut at Barcelona 1992 and won bronze in men's singles at Atlanta 1996.
That was India's first individual Olympic medal since K.D. Jadhav's in 1952.

qs.q: Through which Constitutional Amendment was Article 21A introduced, mandating free and compulsory education as a Fundamental Right forchildren between6and 14 years of age?
qs.e:
The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, inserted Article 21A: free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14.
It also added Fundamental Duty 51A(k) and changed Article 45. The RTE Act followed in 2009.

qs.q: Article312 provides for creation of new_by Parliament.
qs.e:
Article 312 lets Parliament create new All India Services, once the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
The Indian Forest Service (1966) was created under this provision.

qs.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Article 262 empowers Parliament to set up tribunals for river disputes. 2. The Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction in such disputes. Which ofthe above is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1 is true: Article 262 lets Parliament set up tribunals for inter-state river water disputes.
Statement 2 is false: Article 262(2) lets Parliament exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in such disputes. Only 1 is correct.

qs.q: A fruit vendor sells15kg of apples for 750, there by gaining the cost price of5kg of apples. What is his profit percentage?
qs.e:
On 15 kg he gains the CP of 5 kg.
Profit% = 5/15 × 100 = 33.33%.

qs.q: An oven has a marked price of 12,000. Itis sold with two successive discounts. If the second discount is 20% and the final selling price is  8,40o, what is thepercentageofthefirstdiscount?

A furniture store marks its items at 80% above the cost price. They offer a discount of 30% on the marked price. f a customer... receives an additional loyalty discount of 250, and the store stil makes a 12% profit on the cost price, what is the cost price of the furniture item?
qs.e:
Let CP = x. MP = 1.8x, and after a 30% discount SP = 1.26x.
1.26x − 250 = 1.12x, so 0.14x = 250 and x = ₹1,785.71.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:HAPHAZARD
qs.e:
Haphazard means lacking order or plan, so its synonym is random.
Organized, intentional and planned are all antonyms.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Not fit to hold a candle to
qs.e:
'Not fit to hold a candle to' means greatly inferior to someone.
For example: As a batsman he can't hold a candle to his brother.

qs.q: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The ancient sconce held a flickering torch along the corridor.
o: The thief smashed the wall sconce and fled.
The student was sconcedfor violating tradition.
The bronze sconcewas engraved with floral motifs.
The hallwayfeatured a new LED sconce.
qs.e:
Homonyms are the same word with a different meaning. 'Sconce' here is a wall bracket for a torch or candle.
In 'The student was sconced for violating...', sconce is a verb meaning to fine (old Oxford use). The other options all use the bracket meaning.

qs.q: Pis the son of Q. Qis the brother of R. Ris the son of S. How is Prelated to s?
qs.e:
R is S's son, and Q is R's brother, so Q is also S's son.
P is Q's son, so P is S's grandson.

Next = ZAB (the alphabet wraps from Z to A).

qs.q: Introducing a woman, Jay said,"she is the daughter of the only child ofmy grandfather." How is the woman related to Jay?
qs.e:
The only child of Jay's grandfather is Jay's own father or mother.
That parent's daughter is Jay's sister.

qs.q: Find the next number in the series:3,7,15,31, 63, ?

qs.e:
The differences double: +4, +8, +16, +32. So after 53 comes 53 + 32 = 85.
87 is the wrong term.

qs.q: When was the Amateur Athletics Federation of india (AAFi) established?
qs.e:
The Amateur Athletics Federation of India was set up in 1946.
It is now called the Athletics Federation of India (AFI), the national body for athletics.

qs.q: Which of the following statements about India's boxing medals at the 2000 Sydney Olympics is correct?
o: India did not win any boxing medals at Sydney 2000.
India won multiple boxing medals at Sydney 2000.
Karnam Malleswari won a boxing bronze medal at Sydney 2000.
India won its first Olympic boxing medal at Sydney 2000.
qs.e:
India won no boxing medal at Sydney 2000. Its first Olympic boxing medal was Vijender Singh's bronze at Beijing 2008.
Karnam Malleswari won bronze in weightlifting, not boxing, at Sydney. That is the trap.

qs.q: Fill in theblanks: The indian olympic Association (ioA) was officially formed in with sir Dorabji Tata as its founding President and Dr. A. G. Noehren as Secretary.
qs.e:
The Indian Olympic Association was formed in 1927, with Sir Dorabji Tata as President and Dr A.G. Noehren as Secretary.
The IOA is headquartered in New Delhi.

qs.q: Which of the following statements regarding the 56th National Kho Kho Championship 2023-24 is/are correct? 1.) Maharashtra won both the men's and women's titles, becoming overall champions.
qs.e:
At the 56th Senior National Kho Kho Championship (2023-24), held in New Delhi, Maharashtra won both the men's and women's titles.
The matches were held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium and the Karnail Singh Stadium, so per the key both statements are correct.

qs.q: By which Constitutional Amendment was education transferred to the Concurrent List?
qs.e:
The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved education from the State List to the Concurrent List.
Forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice were moved with it.

qs.q: Which major constitutional feature was first introduced by the Government of India Act, 1935 and later adopted in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e:
The GoI Act, 1935 created a federal scheme with provincial autonomy and three lists. The Constitution adopted this federal structure.
Fundamental Duties came through the 42nd Amendment, and universal adult franchise was new in 1950.

qs.q: Arrange the following judicial events chronologically: 1. Berubari Union case 2. Kesavananda Bharati case 3. s. R. Bom mai case
qs.e:
Berubari Union (1960), then Kesavananda Bharati (1973), then S.R. Bommai (1994).
Order: 1-2-3. Kesavananda laid down the basic structure doctrine, and Bommai dealt with Article 356.

qs.q: If A is 25% more than B, and B is 20% more than C, then what is A: C?
The cost price of an article is 500. A shopkeeper sells it at a discount of 20% on the marked price. If the marked price is 600, what is the shopkeeper's profit or loss percentage?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:REBELLIoUS
qs.e:
Rebellious means resisting authority or control, so the synonym is disobedient.
Submissive, obedient and agreeable are all opposites.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:EULoGY
qs.e:
A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing in praise of someone, often after death. Its synonym is tribute.
Criticism, insult and condemnation are opposites.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: To crystinking fish
o: Undervaluing one's own worth or effort
qs.e:
'To cry stinking fish' means to run down your own goods or efforts.
It comes from a fish-seller who calls out that his own fish stinks.

qs.q: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The monk meditated beneath the ancient cor bel protruding from the chapel wall.
o: The cor bel cracked under the weight of the vaulted stone.
Thecorbelwasadorned withgrotesques typical of Gothic style.
The scholar explained the political cor bel in Machiavellian strategy.
The mason restored the damaged stone cor bel last year.
qs.e:
A homonym is the same word used with a different meaning. In every other option, 'corbel' is the stone bracket projecting from a wall, the same sense as the given sentence.
Only the 'political corbel in Machiavellian strategy' sentence uses the word in a different, figurative sense, so the key picks it.

qs.q: Ais the wife of B. B is the son of C. D is the daughter ofA. How is D related to C?
qs.e:
B is C's son and A is B's wife. D is A's daughter, so D is B's daughter.
D is the son's daughter of C, so D is C's granddaughter.

qs.q: What comes next:1,2,6,24,120,?

The terms are factorials: 1!, 2!, 3!, 4!, 5! (multiply by 2, 3, 4, 5).
Next = 120 × 6 = 720.

My wife's brother is my brother-in-law; his son is my wife's nephew, and hence my nephew (by marriage).
Cousin would be my uncle's/aunt's child, so Nephew is correct.

qs.q: The series given below contains a sequence of numbers. Accordingly identify the incorrect combination 4,51414,34,36,74 68
qs.e:
Two interleaved series. Odd places 4,14,34,74: each x2+6 (4x2+6=14, 14x2+6=34, 34x2+6=74).
Even places 5,14,?,68: each x2+4: 5x2+4=14, 14x2+4=32, 32x2+4=68.
So 36 should be 32; 36 is the wrong term.

qs.q: Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1919 is correctly matched with its constitutional implication?
o: Transferred and Reserved subjects-Created functional overlap between central and provincial powers
Creation of bicameralism-Introduced two houses at the central level for the first time
Establishment of Public Service Commission-Gave financial control to Indian members in the Viceroy's Council
Introduction ofdiarchyin provinces-Empowered Indian ministers to control defence and foreign affairs
qs.e:
The Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) made the Central Legislature bicameral for the first time: Central Legislative Assembly and Council of State.
Diarchy was introduced in provinces, but defence and foreign affairs were never given to Indian ministers.

qs.q: Consider the following statements about Judo competition areas and contestants: 1) The competition area is divided into an inner contest area (minimum 8mx8m) and an outer safety area (minimum 3m wide). 2)The blue uniform contestant is called first, followed by the white uniform contestant. Which ofthe statements is/are correct?
qs.e:
Statement 1 is correct: IJF rules need a contest area of at least 8m x 8m and a safety area of at least 3m.
Statement 2 is wrong: the contestant in the WHITE judogi is called first, blue second. Answer: Only 1.

qs.q: Which of the following statements correctly applies the weighted voting mechanism under Article 279A(9) of the Indian Constitution?
o: The Centre holds 75% of the voting power in the GST Council.
A GsT Council decision can be passed solely with the support of the Centre and one State.
The States collectively have twice the voting weight of the Centre in the GST Council.
Each State has equal weight age as the Centre in GST Council voting.
qs.e:
Under Article 279A(9), the Centre has one-third of the weighted votes and all States together two-thirds, so States have twice the Centre's weight.
A decision needs at least three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present, so neither side can pass it alone.

qs.q: In Bharatiya Nagarik suraksha Samhita(BNss), which court may grant default bail after time limit lapses?
qs.e:
Default bail: if the chargesheet is not filed within 60/90 days, the Magistrate must release the accused (Section 187 BNSS, earlier Section 167(2) CrPC).
BNSS replaced CrPC with effect from 1 July 2024.

qs.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The GST Council makes binding recommendations on GST rates: 2. Article246A allows Statestolegislate on intra-state supply of goods and services. Which of the above is/are correct?
qs.e:
1 wrong: GST Council recommendations are only persuasive, not binding (Supreme Court, Mohit Minerals, 2022).
2 correct: Article 246A (101st Amendment, 2016) lets Parliament and State legislatures both make GST laws; inter-State supply is exclusively for Parliament. Answer: Only 2.

qs.q: A shopkeeper marked a watch at 800, He sold it after allowing a 15% discount. if his profit on the sale was 20%, what was the cost price of the watch?
is 300, what would have been the selling price if the product was sold at a 30% discount on its marked price?
qs.e:
Profit 10% of CP = 300, so CP = 3000 and SP = 3300.
SP = 80% of MP, so MP = 3300/0.8 = 4125.
At 30% discount: 0.7 x 4125 = Rs 2887.50.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:coGENT
qs.e:
Cogent = clear, logical and convincing (a cogent argument).
Weak, dubious and unclear are near-opposites.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Wonhislaurels
qs.e:
'Win (one's) laurels' = gain honour or fame for an achievement; laurel wreaths crowned victors in ancient Greece.
Do not confuse it with 'rest on one's laurels' = stop trying after success.

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Came of age
o: Understood morality for the first time
qs.e:
'Come of age' = reach adulthood (legally, e.g. 18) or become mature/fully developed.
The other options add meanings the idiom does not carry.

qs.q: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The nobleman received a ceremonial fief from the sovereign.

qs.q: The concept of"Reasonable Classification" as a limitation to the Right to Equality (Article 14) was established in which case?

qs.q: olive Abookseller purchases5 novels at the marked price of4novels from a distributor. If he then sells these novels to customers, offering a discount of5% on the marked price, what is his profit percentage?

Profit % = 15/80 x 100 = 18.75%.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Golden Raid and card system in Kabaddi?

State Government can, with Union's consent, assign Union functions to its officers

qs.q: Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha and choose the correct option: 1) Rajya Sabha is a continuing house of the Parliament, immune to dissolution under any circumstance. 2) Rajya Sabha members serve staggered six-year terms, with one-third retiring every two years.

o: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,2005
qs.e:
The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. It treats electronic records as primary evidence, in line with the Information Technology Act, 2000.
The BSA took effect on 1 July 2024, along with the BNS and the BNSS.

qs.q: Elite long jumpers typically use how many strides in their approach run?
qs.e: Elite long jumpers usually take an approach run of about 18-22 strides to reach near-maximum controlled speed at take-off.

qs.q: Which of the following statements about India's participation in the 2008 Beijing Olympics is correct? 1) india won medals in Shooting, Boxing, and Wresting, including its first-ever individual olympic Gold. 2) saina Nehwal participated in the women's singles badminton event representing India. Saina Nehwal played women's singles and reached the quarter-finals. She won bronze at London 2012.

qs.q: Fill in theblanks: The Rajya Sabha's special power under Art 249 allows it to authorise Parliament to legislate on a  List subject.
qs.e:
Under Article 249, if the Rajya Sabha resolves by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting that it is in the national interest, Parliament can legislate on a State List subject.
The resolution is valid for 1 year and can be extended by 1 year at a time.

qs.q: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council (isc) is/are correct? A) The Inter-State Council is headed by the Prime Minister of india. B) it functions as a recommend a tory body rather than a tribunal for dispute resolution.
qs.e:
Both statements are correct. The Inter-State Council (Article 263, set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice) is chaired by the Prime Minister.
It is a recommendatory body that investigates and advises on Centre-state and inter-state issues. It is not a dispute tribunal.

qs.q: A bakery produced 5000 cakes at a total cost of 250,000. They gave away 500 cakes for a promotional event. For the remaining cakes, they offered a 20% discount on the market price of 75 per cake. Additionally, they gave one cake free with every 9 cakes bought. If all 5ooo cakes were distributed, what is their overall gain or loss percentage?
qs.e:
Cost = ₹2,50,000. 500 cakes are free, and 4500 go to buyers at ₹75 × 0.8 = ₹60.
With 1 free per 9 bought, 9 of every 10 cakes are paid: 4500 × 9/10 = 4050 paid.
Revenue = 4050 × 60 = ₹2,43,000. Loss = 7000/250000 × 100 = 2.8% loss.

qs.q: Aman spends 80% of his income, His income has increased by 25%, but his expenditure remains the same. By what percent have his savings increased?
qs.e:
Take income = 100: expenditure 80, savings 20.
New income = 125 with expenditure still 80, so savings = 45.
Increase = 25/20 × 100 = 125%.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word:GRUMPY
qs.e:

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Todrawthelongbow

It comes from archers' boastful tales about their shooting.

qs.q: A personal foul in basketball primarily involves:

qs.e:
A personal foul in basketball is illegal physical contact with an opponent during live play (holding, pushing, blocking).
Arguing, delaying the game or bench misconduct are technical fouls, not personal fouls.

The I-League 3 and the Junior Girls National Football Championship (Tier 1 & 2) will both run during the same calendar month.

A Financial Emergency has never been declared in India.

qs.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the borrowing powers of States in India? 1)A state requires the Centre's consent for internal borrowing ifit owes any debt to the Centre. 2) No State can raise loans from foreign sources without prior approval of the Union Government.
qs.e:
Both are correct under Article 293. A state that still owes the Centre a loan needs the Centre's consent for fresh borrowing (293(3)).
States cannot borrow directly from foreign sources; external loans go through the Union.

qs.q: Three numbers are such that the second is 150% of the first, and the third is 80% of the second. What is the ratio of the first to the third?
qs.e:
Take the first number = 100. The second = 150, and the third = 80% of 150 = 120.
First : third = 100 : 120 = 5 : 6.

qs.q: A number was mistakenly increased by 25% instead of decreased by 20%. By what percent is the final result more than the CORRECT value?
qs.e:
Take the number = 100. Wrong result = 125, correct result = 80.
Excess = 45/80 × 100 = 56.25%.

In 'The tailor cut a circular paten from wool fabric', the same word refers to a piece of cloth, a different meaning, so it is the homonym.
The other options all use paten as the liturgical plate.

qs.q: Saloni is the daughter of the only son of Kartik. Nirupama is the mother of Deepak. Yamini’s only son, Ankit, is married to Nirupama. Kartik is the paternal grandfather of Deepak. How is Kartik related to Ankit?
qs.e:
Generation 1: Kartik (and Yamini). Kartik is Deepak's paternal grandfather, i.e. the father of Deepak's father.
Generation 2: Nirupama is Deepak's mother and is married to Ankit, so Ankit is Deepak's father. Ankit is Yamini's only son.
Generation 3: Deepak (and Saloni).
So Kartik is Ankit's father.
Answer: Father

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 5, 18, 70, 278, ?
On which day was the National Emblem of India adopted?
qs.e:
The National Emblem – the Lion Capital of Ashoka from Sarnath – was adopted on 26 January 1950, the day the Constitution came into force.
Its motto "Satyameva Jayate" is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad and is written in Devanagari below the abacus.
Answer: 26th January 1950

qs.q: In which year was the ‘Lotteries Regulation Act’ passed?
qs.e:
The Lotteries (Regulation) Act was passed by Parliament in 1998.
It lets State governments organise lotteries under set conditions and allows a State to ban lotteries within its territory.
Answer: 1998

qs.q: Which of the following teams won the Indian Super League 2020-21?
qs.e:
Mumbai City FC won the Indian Super League 2020-21, beating ATK Mohun Bagan 2-1 in the final at Goa in March 2021.
They also topped the league table, completing the double, under coach Sergio Lobera.
Answer: Mumbai City FC

qs.q: The former Spanish footballer, Antonio Lopez Habas, was the coach at the Hero ISL 2020-21 of which of the following football teams?
qs.e:
Antonio Lopez Habas coached ATK Mohun Bagan in the 2020-21 ISL season, taking them to the final.
He had earlier won ISL titles with Atletico de Kolkata/ATK (2014 and 2019-20).
Answer: ATK Mohun Bagan

qs.q: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India added a new fundamental duty under Article 51-A?
qs.e:
The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(k): a parent or guardian must provide opportunities for education to a child aged 6–14.
The same amendment inserted Article 21A (Right to Education) and changed Article 45.
The original ten duties came with the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
Answer: Eighty-Sixth Amendment Act, 2002

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be hard up
o: Find it very difficult to wake up early
qs.e:
'To be hard up' means to have very little money.
Example: As a student I was so hard up that I walked to college to save bus fare.
It has nothing to do with calculating, climbing stairs or waking early.
Answer: Have very little money

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ostentatious
qs.e:
Ostentatious means showy, designed to impress (an ostentatious wedding). 'Showy' matches.
Tasteful = elegant and modest (the antonym); Sudden = unexpected; Quick = fast.
Answer: showy

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In the same breath
o: Say two contradictory things at the same time
Able to get a foul smell
qs.e:
'In the same breath' means saying two contradictory (opposite) things at almost the same time.
Example: He praised my work and, in the same breath, said it was useless.
Holding breath, smells and breathing exercises are literal readings of 'breath'.
Answer: Say two contradictory things at the same time

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Retaliate
qs.e:
Retaliate means to strike back or respond to an attack (the army retaliated). 'React' (respond) is the closest.
Clap = strike hands together; Facilitate = make easier; Rotate = turn round.
Answer: react

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Avert
qs.e:
Avert means to turn away or prevent (avert a disaster). 'Prevent' matches.
Permit = allow; Confront and Face = meet head-on, the opposite of avoiding.
Answer: Prevent

qs.q: Pamila is the granddaughter of Akun who is married to Nikita. Murali is the brother-in- law of Akun who has two daughters but no son. Rahul is the cousin of Kamal and brother of Pamila. Uday and Vanmay are the sons-in-law of Nikita. Vanmay is married to Yamini and they have two daughters and one son. Uday has one son and one daughter. Tina and Smita are the daughters of Yamini. Murali is unmarried. How is Yamini related to Rahul?
qs.e:
Generation 1: Akun and Nikita, with two daughters and no son.
Generation 2: the daughters are married to Vanmay and Uday. Vanmay's wife Yamini has two daughters (Tina, Smita) and one son; Uday's wife has one son and one daughter.
Generation 3: Pamila (a granddaughter) and her brother Rahul are not Tina/Smita, so they are Uday's son and daughter. Yamini's son (Kamal) is Rahul's cousin.
So Yamini is the sister of Rahul's mother.
Answer: Aunt

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. KYBA, FTEE, AOHI, VJKO, ?, LZQA
qs.e:
Check each position (A=1).
First: K, F, A, V, ?, L → −5 each → Q (Q−5 = L ✓).
Second: Y, T, O, J, ?, Z → −5 each → E (E−5 = Z ✓).
Third: B, E, H, K, ?, Q → +3 → N.
Fourth: A, E, I, O, ?, A → the vowels in order → U.
Answer: QENU

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 10, 14, 31, 35, 73, 77, ?
qs.e:
The terms alternate between two steps: add 4, then double and add 3.
10 + 4 = 14; 14 × 2 + 3 = 31; 31 + 4 = 35; 35 × 2 + 3 = 73; 73 + 4 = 77.
Next comes the ×2 + 3 step: 77 × 2 + 3 = 157.
Answer: 157

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 16, 33, 100, 401, ?
qs.e:
Each term is the previous term multiplied by 2, 3, 4, 5 … and then increased by 1.
16 × 2 + 1 = 33; 33 × 3 + 1 = 100; 100 × 4 + 1 = 401.
Next: 401 × 5 + 1 = 2006.
Answer: 2006

qs.q: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. _ L H _ _ U_ H _ _ U _ H _ N U _ _ E N

The blanks fall on positions 1, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12, 14, 17, 18, which read U, E, N, L, E, N, L, E, L, H.
The other options break the repeating block at some blank.
Answer: U, E, N, L, E, N, L, E, L, H

qs.q: For which of the following teams is the former Indian football captain Sunil Chhetri played in 2021?
qs.e:
Sunil Chhetri played for Bengaluru FC in 2021; he joined the club in 2013 and captained it.
With Bengaluru FC he won the I-League and the ISL (2018-19).
Answer: Bengaluru FC

qs.q: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is the watchdog of free and fair elections in the country and ______ of the Constitution of India provides for its establishment.
qs.e:
Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission.
The Commission was set up on 25 January 1950 (now celebrated as National Voters' Day).
Others: Art 352 – national emergency; Art 356 – President's rule; Art 101 – vacation of seats.
Answer: Article 324

qs.q: Rajeev Ram is a professional tennis player from ______
qs.e:
Rajeev Ram is an American (United States) tennis player of Indian origin, a doubles specialist.
He won the 2021 Australian Open men's doubles with Joe Salisbury and an Olympic mixed-doubles silver at Rio 2016.
Answer: United States of America

qs.q: As per the Hindu Succession Act 1956, who amongst the following has the first right over the property of a Hindu woman who dies intestate?
o: The legal heirs of her father
The legal heirs of her husband
qs.e:
Under Section 15 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the property of a Hindu woman who dies without a will goes first to her sons, daughters (and children of a predeceased child) and her husband.
Only after them come the heirs of the husband, then her parents, then the heirs of her father.
So among the options, the husband has the first right.
Answer: Her husband

qs.q: With reference to the Constituent Assembly, which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Constituent Assembly ratified India’s membership of the Commonwealth in May 1947.
The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem in January 1950.
The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Song in January 1948.
The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag in July 1949.
qs.e:
The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem (Jana Gana Mana) and the National Song (Vande Mataram) on 24 January 1950, its last sitting.
The other statements are wrong: Commonwealth membership was ratified in May 1949 (not 1947), the National Song was adopted in January 1950 (not 1948), and the National Flag was adopted on 22 July 1947 (not 1949).
Answer: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Anthem in January 1950.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Taciturn
qs.e:
Taciturn means saying very little (a taciturn man). 'Reserved' matches.
Verbose = using too many words; Noisy = loud; Lively = full of energy. These are opposites.
Answer: Reserved

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vertical
qs.e:
Vertical means straight up and down, at right angles to the ground (a vertical pole). 'Upright' matches.
Equal = the same; Parallel = side by side, never meeting; Shaky = unsteady.
Answer: Upright

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cake walk
qs.e:
'Cakewalk' (also 'a piece of cake') means something very easy to do.
Origin: the cakewalk was a 19th-century strutting dance contest whose prize was a cake – seen as an easy win.
Example: After all that practice, the test was a cakewalk.
'Tasty', 'sweet' and 'enjoyable' take 'cake' literally.
Answer: Something easy

qs.q: Select the option that gives the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The Chairman of our company takes care of the rank and file in the company.
qs.e:
'The rank and file' means the ordinary members of a group or the ordinary people, not the leaders.
Origin: ordinary soldiers lined up in ranks (rows) and files (columns), as opposed to officers.
The Chairman looks after the ordinary employees.
'Documents and files' is literal; 'top rank people' and 'officers' are the opposite.
Answer: Ordinary people

qs.q: ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. If ‘R % T & Z $ S @ V @ C % Y’, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: C is the paternal grandmother of Z.
V is the father of Z.
T is the daughter of C.
T is the mother of S.
qs.e:
Codes: % sister, $ brother, @ son, & mother.  R % T & Z $ S @ V @ C % Y.
Generation 1: C (female, Y's sister); V is C's son.
Generation 2: T (R's sister) is the mother of Z and S; S is V's son, so V is the father and T is V's wife.
Generation 3: Z and S (brothers).
C is Z's paternal grandmother ✓; V is Z's father ✓; T is S's mother ✓. T is C's daughter-in-law, not daughter.
Answer: T is the daughter of C.

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 17, 16, 32, 29, 116, ?
Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. KMTC, EVOM, OQXG, IZSQ, ?
qs.e:
Compare alternate terms: KMTC → OQXG and EVOM → IZSQ, where every letter moves +4.
So the 5th term is OQXG with each letter +4 (A=1, wrapping after Z).
O(15)+4 = S, Q(17)+4 = U, X(24)+4 = 28−26 = B, G(7)+4 = K.
Answer: SUBK

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 45, 68, 99, ?, 187, 246, 313
qs.e:
Differences: 68−45 = 23, 99−68 = 31, then 187 → 246 is 59 and 246 → 313 is 67.
The differences are alternate prime numbers: 23, 31, 41, 47, 59, 67 (skipping 29, 37, 43, 53, 61).
99 + 41 = 140, and check: 140 + 47 = 187 ✓.
Answer: 140

qs.q: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series, will complete the series. S P _ _ _ P S T S _ _ _ S P S _

The blanks (positions 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, 16) read S, T, S, P, S, T, T.
Answer: S T S P S T T

qs.q: ______ is the first woman hockey player to receive the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award.
qs.e:
Rani Rampal, captain of the Indian women's hockey team, received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2020, becoming the first woman hockey player to get it.
She led India to fourth place at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
Answer: Rani Rampal

qs.q: How many female members were part of the Constituent Assembly that framed the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
The Constituent Assembly had 15 women members, including Sarojini Naidu, Sucheta Kripalani, Hansa Mehta, Durgabai Deshmukh, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur and Ammu Swaminathan.
Dakshayani Velayudhan was the only Dalit woman among them.
Answer: 15

qs.q: The idea of having a provision for a Bicameral Parliament in the Constitution of India was borrowed from the ______ Constitution.
qs.e:
India took the idea of a two-house (bicameral) Parliament from the British Constitution, where Parliament has the House of Commons and House of Lords.
Other British borrowings: parliamentary government, rule of law, single citizenship, cabinet system, writs.
Irish – Directive Principles; Canadian – federation with a strong Centre; French – liberty, equality, fraternity.
Answer: British

qs.q: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 is an Act of Parliament which came into force in:
qs.e:
The RTE Act was passed in August 2009 but came into force on 1 April 2010.
On that day India became one of the countries where education is a fundamental right of every child aged 6–14 (Article 21A).
The tempting option 2009 is the year of enactment, not of coming into force.
Answer: 2010

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Smooth
qs.e:
Smooth means having an even surface without bumps (a smooth road). 'Flat' (level and even) is the closest.
Uneven, Rough and Broken all describe a bumpy or damaged surface, the opposite.
Answer: Flat

qs.q: Select the option that gives the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. I am working on too many projects. I think I have bitten off more than I can chew.
o: To take on more than one can handle
qs.e:
'To bite off more than one can chew' means to take on more work or responsibility than one can handle.
Working on too many projects is exactly this.
Option 1 ('not able to finish') is only a possible result, not the meaning; being happy to multitask and finding work dull are wrong.
Answer: To take on more than one can handle
qs.u: bitten off more than I can chew

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Imminent
qs.e:
Imminent means about to happen very soon (an imminent storm). 'Impending' matches.
Unyielding = firm, not giving way; Ignorant = lacking knowledge; Distant = far off in time (the antonym).
Answer: Impending

qs.q: Select the option that gives the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. It is good to take into account all the important factors before making a decision.
qs.e:
'To take into account' means to consider something when making a decision.
Example: Take into account the traffic when you plan the trip.
Leave = ignore (the opposite); select and control do not mean 'think about'.
Answer: consider

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 16, 35, ?, 217, 653, 1309

‘A # B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. If ‘G # M # T % S @ H & R & W @ U’, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: G is the paternal grandfather of T.
W is the maternal grandmother of H.
R is the husband of T.
M is the maternal grandfather of S.
qs.e:
Codes: # father, % mother, @ sister, & son.  G # M # T % S @ H & R & W @ U.
Generation 1: G is M's father.  Generation 2: M; and W (U's sister), the mother of R.
Generation 3: T is M's child; T is the mother of S and H. H is R's son, so R is the father — T's husband.
Generation 4: S and H.
G is T's paternal grandfather ✓, R is T's husband ✓, M is S's maternal grandfather ✓; W is H's father's mother, i.e. PATERNAL grandmother, so 'maternal grandmother' is wrong.
Answer: W is the maternal grandmother of H.

3rd: M, V, E, N, W (+9 each). 4th: S, I, Y, O, E (−10 each).
So the next cluster is JXWE.
Answer: JXWE

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 62, 74, 80, 86, 95, ?, 158
Which of the following cities won the hosting rights of the 2030 Asian Games in December 2020?

In December 2020 the Olympic Council of Asia gave the 2030 Asian Games to Doha, Qatar, and the 2034 Games to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
Doha had hosted the Asian Games earlier in 2006. Jakarta hosted in 2018 and Hangzhou in 2022 (held 2023).
Answer: Doha

qs.q: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India declared that the Parliament has the power to abridge or take away any of the Fundamental Rights under Article 368 and such an Act, will NOT be a law under the meaning of Article 13?
qs.e:
The 24th Amendment Act, 1971 was passed after the Golaknath case (1967), which had said Parliament cannot take away Fundamental Rights.
It amended Articles 13 and 368 to say Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights, and that such an amendment is not "law" under Article 13.
It also made it compulsory for the President to give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill.
Answer: Twenty-fourth Amendment

qs.q: Who among the following presidents of India gave assent to the 100th Amendment of the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
The 100th Amendment Act, 2015 gave effect to the India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (exchange of enclaves) by amending the First Schedule.
It received assent in May 2015 from President Pranab Mukherjee, who held office from 2012 to 2017.
Ram Nath Kovind became President only in July 2017.
Answer: Pranab Mukherjee

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To take after
qs.e:
'To take after' someone means to resemble an older family member in looks or character.
Example: Riya takes after her mother – same eyes, same smile.
Chasing someone, mocking someone and changing sides are different phrasal meanings ('run after', 'make fun of', 'turn coat').
Answer: To be similar in appearance

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Foul play
o: A bad smelling theatre or playground
A drama which is badly produced
qs.e:
'Foul play' means unfair, dishonest or criminal behaviour (in police use, often murder).
Example: Police suspect foul play in the businessman's death.
The other options take 'foul' (bad smelling / unpleasant) or 'play' (theatre, game) literally.
Answer: Unfair or dishonest behaviour

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DUO
qs.e:
A duo is a pair of people or things (a singing duo). 'Pair' matches.
Bond = a tie or link; Loan = money lent; Debt = money owed.
Answer: Pair

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Paranoid
qs.e:
Paranoid means unreasonably suspicious and distrustful of others (paranoid about being watched). 'Distrustful' matches.
Convinced = certain; Trustful = trusting (the antonym); Committed = dedicated.
Answer: Distrustful

qs.q: There are seven members, B, C, D, E, F, G and H, in a family. H is the only daughter-in- law of D. E is the sister of C. C is the only son of F, who is the wife of D. B and G are the sons of H. How is G related to F?
qs.e:
Generation 1: D and his wife F.
Generation 2: C is F's only son and E his sister. H is D's only daughter-in-law, so H is C's wife.
Generation 3: B and G are H's sons.
G is F's son's son.
Answer: Grandson

57 + 25 = 82.

qs.q: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India gave the status of state to Goa?
qs.e:
The 56th Amendment Act, 1987 made Goa a separate State; Daman and Diu remained a Union Territory.
Goa became the 25th State of India on 30 May 1987.
Answer: 56th Amendment

qs.q: Who among the following female wrestlers won the Ukraine Wrestling Tournament in February 2021?
qs.e:
Vinesh Phogat won gold in the 53 kg category at the Outstanding Ukrainian Wrestlers and Coaches Memorial tournament in Kyiv in February 2021.
It was an important tune-up event before the Tokyo Olympics.
Answer: Vinesh Phogat

qs.q: As of April 2021, who among the following is the only Indian long jumper to have qualified for the Tokyo Olympics 2021?
qs.e:
Murali Sreeshankar qualified for the Tokyo Olympics in long jump with an 8.26 m jump (then a national record) at the Federation Cup in March 2021.
He was the only Indian long jumper to make it to Tokyo.
Answer: Sreeshankar Murali

qs.q: An amendment to the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 was passed in the year ______.
qs.e:
The Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 gave daughters equal rights with sons as coparceners in ancestral (joint family) property.
It amended Section 6 of the 1956 Act and came into force on 9 September 2005.
Answer: 2005

qs.q: In which of the following years was an Act to provide for the reorganisation of the states of India and for matters connected therewith enacted?
qs.e:
The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised Indian states on a linguistic basis, following the report of the Fazl Ali Commission (1955).
It came into effect on 1 November 1956 together with the 7th Constitutional Amendment, creating 14 States and 6 Union Territories.
Answer: 1956

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On the wane
qs.e:
'On the wane' means decreasing or declining in power, size or popularity.
Origin: the moon 'wanes' after full moon as it gets smaller.
Example: Interest in landline phones is on the wane.
'On the rise' is the opposite; 'on the way' and 'on the top' are unrelated.
Answer: On the decline

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A long shot
qs.e:
'A long shot' is an attempt that has very little chance of success.

qs.q: The average score (runs/match) of Mithali before the start of the women’s national series was 45. In the women’s national series of 10 matches, her total score was 500 runs. Find the total number of matches played by her till date, if her new average after the series is 47.5.
qs.e:
This is an average question, not a series. Let n = matches before the series.
Runs before = 45n. After 10 more matches: (45n + 500) ÷ (n + 10) = 47.5.
45n + 500 = 47.5n + 475 → 2.5n = 25 → n = 10.
Total matches = 10 + 10 = 20.
Shortcut: the 10 new matches averaged 50, which is 5 above the old 45; the average rose by 2.5, so old and new match counts are equal (10 and 10).
Answer: 20

qs.q: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. If ‘W @ S % K $ G & U & T @ R + C’, then which of the following statements is correct?
o: G is the maternal grandmother of R.
G is the father of W.
C is the father-in-law of K.
C is the wife of U.
qs.e:
Codes: + daughter, $ husband, @ brother, & mother, % son.  W @ S % K $ G & U & T @ R + C.
Generation 1: K is G's husband (G is female).
Generation 2: W and S are their sons; G is U's mother.
Generation 3: U is the mother of T and R; R is C's daughter, so C is R's father (U's husband).
G is the mother of R's mother → maternal grandmother ✓. G is female (not father), C is K's son-in-law, and C is U's husband, not wife.
Answer: G is the maternal grandmother of R.

qs.q: 'Z + Y' means 'Y is the son of Z'. 'Z $ Y' means 'Y is the father of Z'. 'Y % Z' means 'Y is the son-in-law of Z'. 'Z – Y' means 'Y is the wife of Z'. 'Y * Z' means 'Z is the brother of Y'. 'Y # Z' means 'Z is the only sister of Y'. Which two symbols can sequentially replace the question marks (?) in the following expression to show that ‘D is the wife of W’? W % O – B ? C ? D
qs.e:
Codes: Z + Y: Y is Z's son; Z – Y: Y is Z's wife; Y # Z: Z is Y's only sister; Y % Z: Y is Z's son-in-law.
W % O: W is O's son-in-law. O – B: B is O's wife. So W is married to a daughter of O and B.
With '+ and #': B + C: C is B's son; C # D: D is C's only sister, so D is the daughter of B and O.
So D is the wife of W ✓. ('+ and –' makes D C's wife; '% and –' makes D C's wife; '$ and +' makes D a son.)
Answer: + and #

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the right to equality?
qs.e:
Articles 14 to 18 form the Right to Equality: equality before law (14), no discrimination (15), equal opportunity in public employment (16), abolition of untouchability (17) and abolition of titles (18).
19–22 – Right to Freedom; 23–24 – Right against Exploitation; 25–28 – Freedom of Religion.
Answer: 14 to 18

qs.q: Which of the following events in 2018 holds the Guinness World Record as being the largest annual fundraising event in the world (as of April 2021)?
qs.e:
Guinness World Records lists the London Marathon as the largest annual one-day fundraising event in the world.
In 2018 runners raised over £60 million for charity.
Answer: London Marathon

qs.q: Which of the following Amendment Acts of the Constitution of India abolished the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely states?
qs.e:
The 26th Amendment Act, 1971 abolished the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely states. It removed Articles 291 and 362 and added Article 363A.
It was passed after the Supreme Court struck down the President's 1970 order de-recognising the rulers (Madhav Rao Scindia case).
Answer: 26th Amendment Act 1971

qs.q: GV Mavalankar was the Chairman of the ______ of the Constituent Assembly of India.
o: Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas
Ad hoc Committee on the National Flag
qs.e:
G.V. Mavalankar chaired the Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly. He later became the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights – Sardar Patel; Order of Business Committee – K.M. Munshi; Ad hoc Committee on the National Flag – Rajendra Prasad.
Answer: Committee on the Functions

qs.q: In March 2021, Bhavani Devi became the first Indian ______ to qualify for the Olympics.
qs.e:
In March 2021 Bhavani Devi became the first Indian fencer to qualify for the Olympics (Tokyo 2020, sabre).
She also won the first Olympic fencing bout by an Indian.
Answer: fencer

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Smooth sailing
qs.e:
'Smooth sailing' (plain sailing) means easy progress without problems.
Example: Once the visa came through, the rest of the trip was smooth sailing.
Calm weather is literal; comfortable place and plain dress are unrelated.
Answer: Easy progress

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Saucy
qs.e:
Saucy means boldly disrespectful in a playful way (a saucy reply). 'Cheeky' matches.
Tasty is a trap linked to 'sauce'; Polite = the antonym; Smooth = even.
Answer: Cheeky

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Robust
qs.e:
Robust means strong and healthy, hard to break (a robust structure). 'Sturdy' matches.
Small = little; Round = circular; Weak = the antonym.
Answer: sturdy

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On purpose
qs.e:
'On purpose' means intentionally, deliberately.
Example: He broke the window on purpose, not by mistake.
Accidently is the opposite; luckily and mischievously do not mean deliberately.
Answer: Intentionally

qs.q: 390625 is at which position in the series 5, 25, 125, 625, ______?
qs.e:
The series is the powers of 5: 5¹, 5², 5³, 5⁴ …
390625 = 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 5⁸ (5⁴ = 625 and 625 × 625 = 390625).
The nth term is 5ⁿ, so 390625 is the 8th term.
Answer: 8th

qs.q: Pointing towards a boy, Shalini said, “He is my daughter’s father’s wife’s father’s wife’s only son”. How is Shalini related to the boy?
qs.e:
Work backwards. Shalini's daughter's father is Shalini's husband. The husband's wife is Shalini herself.
Shalini's father's wife is Shalini's mother, and her mother's only son is Shalini's brother.
So the boy is Shalini's brother, which makes Shalini his sister.
The other options would need the boy to be her son or her husband's brother, which the chain does not say.
Answer: Sister

So the missing cluster is DSFQ.
Answer: DSFQ

qs.q: In March 2021, cricketer Kieron Pollard hit six sixes in an over in a match against ______.

In March 2021 West Indies' Kieron Pollard hit six sixes in an over off Akila Dananjaya of Sri Lanka in a T20I at Antigua.
He was the third man to do this in international cricket after Herschelle Gibbs and Yuvraj Singh.
Answer: Sri Lanka

qs.q: An amendment to the Right to Information Act 2005 proposing that the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners be appointed ‘for such term as may be prescribed by the Central Government’ was passed in the year _____.
qs.e:
The Right to Information (Amendment) Act, 2019 removed the fixed 5-year term of the CIC and Information Commissioners. Their term, salary and service conditions are now "as may be prescribed by the Central Government".
Critics said this reduced the independence of the information commissions.
Answer: 2019

qs.q: The salary and allowances of leaders of opposition in parliament are governed by the Act passed for the first time by the parliament in the year ______.
qs.e:
The Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act was passed in 1977.
It gave statutory recognition to the Leader of Opposition in each House; in the Lok Sabha that party must have at least one-tenth of the House's seats.
Answer: 1977

qs.q: In the 2020–21 season, each NBA team played ______ regular-season games.
qs.e:
Due to COVID-19, the NBA cut the 2020-21 regular season to 72 games per team (instead of the usual 82).
Answer: 72

qs.q: With reference to no-confidence motion, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
o: If it is passed in the Lok Sabha, the council of ministers must resign from office.
It is moved for ascertaining the confidence of Lok Sabha in the council of ministers.
It can be moved against the entire council of ministers only.
It should state the reasons for its adoption in the Lok Sabha.
qs.e:
A no-confidence motion does NOT need to state any reason for its adoption in the Lok Sabha. A censure motion must state its reasons.
The other statements are true: it tests the Lok Sabha's confidence in the council of ministers, it is moved against the whole council only, and if passed the ministry must resign.
It needs the support of 50 members to be admitted (Lok Sabha rule 198).
Answer: It should state the reasons for its adoption in the Lok Sabha.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Triumphant
qs.e:
Triumphant means having won, celebrating a victory (a triumphant team). 'Victorious' matches.
Fortunate = lucky; Affluent = wealthy; Pompous = self-important.
Answer: Victorious

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. It was a lavish birthday party and I could see my friend eat like a horse.
qs.e:
'To eat like a horse' means to eat a very large amount.
At the lavish party the friend ate a lot.
'What horses eat' is literal; 'hardly eating' is the opposite; 'eating differently' is unrelated.
Answer: eating excessively

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pay heed to
qs.e:
'To pay heed to' means to listen to or pay careful attention to something.
Example: Pay heed to your teacher's advice.
The other options read 'pay' as paying money (repaying debts, interest, disbursing).
Answer: Listen carefully with attention

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bare
qs.e:
Bare means plain, with nothing extra; as in 'the bare necessities' or 'the bare minimum'. 'Basic' matches.
Earthly = worldly; Hidden = concealed (opposite of bare in the sense of uncovered); Holy = sacred.
Answer: Basic

qs.q: Ranjana said to a woman, “My father is the paternal grandfather of your son Piyush”. How is Piyush related to Ranjana?
qs.e:

Ranjana is a woman, so Piyush's father is Ranjana's brother (the woman addressed is his wife).
The son of one's brother is one's nephew.

qs.q: When was the Tenth Session of the Constituent Assembly held?
qs.e:
The Tenth Session of the Constituent Assembly was held from 6 to 17 October 1949.
The 11th session (14–26 November 1949) followed; the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
Others: 14–31 July 1947 – 4th session; 4 Nov 1948–8 Jan 1949 – 7th session; 16 May–16 June 1949 – 8th session.
Answer: 6-17 October 1949

qs.q: Which of the following countries will host the 2023 AIBA Men's World Boxing Championships?

The 2023 IBA (formerly AIBA) Men's World Boxing Championships were awarded to Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
The championships were held there in May 2023; Uzbekistan is one of the strongest amateur boxing nations.

qs.q: Which of the following Hero Indian Super League teams appointed Sergio Lobera as its head coach in October 2020?

In his first season he won the ISL League Winners Shield and the ISL 2020-21 title.
Answer: Mumbai City FC

qs.q: Which amendment to the Constitution of India added a new subject in the Union List called 'taxes on services’?
qs.e:
The 88th Amendment Act, 2003 added entry 92C "Taxes on services" to the Union List and inserted Article 268A on how service tax is levied and shared.
Service tax had first been levied in 1994 under a Finance Act; this amendment gave it a clear constitutional basis. It was later merged into GST (101st Amendment).
Answer: 88th

qs.q: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India amended Article 19 and inserted provisions fully securing the constitutional validity of zamindari abolition laws in general and certain specified State Acts in particular?
qs.e:
The First Amendment Act, 1951 amended Article 19 (adding new reasonable restrictions such as public order and friendly relations with foreign states).
It also added Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule, fully protecting zamindari-abolition and land reform laws (including specified State Acts) from being challenged in court.
Answer: First Amendment

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Back out
qs.e:
'Back out' means to withdraw from a promise, deal or plan.

Enquire, throw and explode have nothing to do with withdrawing.
Answer: To withdraw

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ravenous
qs.e:
Ravenous means extremely hungry (a ravenous wolf). 'Starved' matches.
Satiated, Full and Content all describe someone who has eaten enough, the opposite.
Answer: Starved

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Lull
qs.e:
A lull is a short period of quiet or calm (a lull in the storm). 'Calm' matches.
Disturbance, Activity and Noise are the opposite.
Answer: Calm

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Have a change of heart
qs.e:
'To have a change of heart' means to change one's opinion or decision.

Surgery is literal; falling in love and expressing happiness are different.
Answer: Change one’s opinion

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 7, 16, 41, 94, 251, ?

Next difference: 157 × 2 + 3 = 317, so 251 + 317 = 568.

qs.q: ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’. ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. Which of the following options means ‘J is the father of R’?
qs.e:
Decode option 3: C @ J → C is J's wife; J $ K → J is K's father; K % M → K is M's brother; M # R → M is R's sister.
So K, M and R are siblings, and J, the father of K, is also the father of R.
Option 1 makes J a brother of K; option 2 makes R the father; option 4 makes J the wife of C, so they fail.
Answer: C @ J $ K % M # R

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 1, 1, 2, 2, 6, 10, 42, ?, 1806
qs.e:
Split into two series.
Odd terms 1, 2, 6, 42, 1806: each is x² + x of the one before (1+1 = 2, 4+2 = 6, 36+6 = 42, 1764+42 = 1806).
Even terms 1, 2, 10, ?: each is x³ + x of the one before (1+1 = 2, 8+2 = 10), so next is 1000 + 10 = 1010.
Answer: 1010

qs.q: Select the letter from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. E, F, I, N, U, ?
qs.e:
Letter positions: E = 5, F = 6, I = 9, N = 14, U = 21.
The gaps are odd numbers +1, +3, +5, +7, so the next gap is +9.
21 + 9 = 30, and 30 − 26 = 4 = D.
Answer: D

qs.q: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. CALI, ZEGO, WIBU, TMWA, ?
qs.e:
1st: C, Z, W, T, Q (−3). 2nd: A, E, I, M, Q (+4). 3rd: L, G, B, W, R (−5).
4th letters I, O, U, A are vowels in cyclic order (A, E, I, O, U), so next comes E.
So the next cluster is QQRE.
Answer: QQRE

qs.q: As of April 2021, ______ held the record for the highest individual Women’s ODI cricket score by an Indian player. She was also the only Indian spinner to take six women’s ODI wickets.
qs.e:
Deepti Sharma scored 188 against Ireland in 2017, the highest individual women's ODI score by an Indian (as of April 2021).
She also took 6/20 against Sri Lanka in 2016, the only Indian spinner with a six-wicket haul in women's ODIs then.
Answer: Deepti Sharma

qs.q: Who was the Australian Open Women’s Singles champion in 2021?

Naomi Osaka of Japan won the 2021 Australian Open women's singles, beating Jennifer Brady of the USA in the final.
It was her fourth Grand Slam title; Brady was the runner-up.

qs.q: Who among the following became a part of the Constituent Assembly from Madras Constituency in 1946?
qs.e:
Ammu Swaminathan was elected to the Constituent Assembly in 1946 from the Madras constituency.
Others: Hansa Mehta came from Bombay; Kamla Chaudhry and Begum Aizaz Rasul came from the United Provinces. Begum Rasul was the only Muslim woman in the Assembly.
Answer: Ammu Swaminathan

qs.q: The ________________ treats a marriage as complete and binding when the Saptapadi ritual is completed.
qs.e:
Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 says that where the ceremonies include the Saptapadi (seven steps around the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.
Answer: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955

qs.q: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India was enacted in 1993 to constitutionally recognise municipal governments?
qs.e:
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional recognition to municipalities (urban local bodies) by adding Part IX-A and the Twelfth Schedule.
Parliament passed it in 1992, and it got the President's assent and came into force in 1993 (1 June 1993), which is why the question says "1993".
Answer: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (CAA), 1992

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit a brick wall

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Honest

Secretive = hiding things; Daring = bold; Strange = unusual.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Imbue
qs.e:
Imbue means to fill or inspire with a feeling or quality (imbued with patriotism). 'Instil' matches.

qs.q: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution of India ______.

reduced the age for voting from 21 to 18 years
exempted Arunachal Pradesh from reservation for Scheduled Castes in Panchayati Raj institutions

qs.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India were borrowed from the ______ Constitution.

qs.q: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in the year ______.

qs.q: Which of the following countries hosted the ITTF (International Table Tennis Federation) Women's World Cup 2020?

Varun's father-in-law's son = his wife's brother.
That brother's only sister = Varun's wife.
Varun's wife's mother-in-law = Varun's mother. So the lady is Varun's mother and Varun is her son.
Answer: Son

qs.q: Realising the importance of maintaining the cleanliness of the water bodies, the Government of India passed the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, ________, to safeguard our water resources.
qs.e:
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was passed in 1974. It was India's first major environmental law.
It created the Central and State Pollution Control Boards. The Air Act followed in 1981 and the Environment (Protection) Act in 1986.
Answer: 1974

qs.q: Who among the following won the 2020 Tour de France?
qs.e:
Tadej Pogačar of Slovenia won the 2020 Tour de France, aged 21, overturning the lead on the penultimate-day time trial.
He was the youngest winner since 1904; Egan Bernal won in 2019.
Answer: Tadej Pogačar

qs.q: How many Schedules did the Constitution of India contain as of April 2021?
qs.e:
The Constitution now has 12 Schedules; it began with 8 in 1950.
The 9th was added by the 1st Amendment (1951), the 10th by the 52nd (1985, anti-defection), the 11th by the 73rd and the 12th by the 74th (1992).
Answer: 12

qs.q: Along with India, which of the following countries was crowned Joint Winner at the 2020 Online FIDE Chess Olympiad?
qs.e:
India and Russia were declared joint winners of the 2020 FIDE Online Chess Olympiad after the final was disrupted by an internet outage.
It was India's first Chess Olympiad title.
Answer: Russia

qs.q: The Constitution (112th Amendment) Bill 2009 provides for ______ reservation for women in Urban Local Bodies was introduced in Lok Sabha on 24th November 2009.
qs.e:
The Constitution (112th Amendment) Bill, 2009 proposed raising women's reservation in Urban Local Bodies from one-third to 50%.
A similar bill (the 110th) proposed 50% for Panchayats. Many States have already given 50% to women by their own laws.
Answer: 50%

qs.q: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was consisted of ______ members.
qs.e:
The Drafting Committee, set up on 29 August 1947, had 7 members with Dr B.R. Ambedkar as chairman.
The members were N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadulla, B.L. Mitter (later replaced by N. Madhava Rau) and D.P. Khaitan (replaced by T.T. Krishnamachari after his death).
Answer: 7

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Retaliate
qs.e:
Retaliate means to strike back in return for an attack or insult. 'React' (respond) is the closest.
Clap = strike hands together; Rotate = turn around; Facilitate = make easier.
Answer: react

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cat’s paw
o: A person used as a tool by another
qs.e:
A 'cat's paw' is a person used by another as a tool to do unpleasant or risky work.
Origin: La Fontaine's fable in which a monkey uses a cat's paw to pull chestnuts out of the fire.
Example: The gang used the boy as a cat's paw to carry the stolen goods.
The other options (attribute, attack, speed) are unrelated.
Answer: A person used as a tool by another

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In the limelight
o: In a well lit up room
qs.e:
'In the limelight' means being the centre of public attention.
Origin: theatres once lit the main actor with limelight (burning lime).
Example: After the award, the young author was in the limelight.
A well-lit room is literal; a secret is the opposite; 'about to be successful' is not the meaning.
Answer: The centre of attraction

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sagacious
qs.e:
Sagacious means wise, with good judgement (a sagacious leader). 'Judicious' matches.
Precious = valuable; Delicious = tasty; Malicious = spiteful. They only rhyme with the right answer.
Answer: Judicious

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Audacity
qs.e:
Audacity means boldness, willingness to take risks (the audacity to challenge the champion). 'Daring' matches.
Meekness = gentle submissiveness; Caution = carefulness (both antonyms); Kindness = goodness.
Answer: Daring
