qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 382, 322, 272, 232, 202, ?
qs.e:
Differences: −60, −50, −40, −30 — each drop is 10 smaller than the last.
The next difference is −20.
202 − 20 = 182.
Answer: 182

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? PK, GT, XC, OL, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: P, G, X, O — each 9 back (16 → 7 → 24 → 15), so next 15 − 9 = 6 = F.
2nd letters: K, T, C, L — each 9 forward (11 → 20 → 3 → 12), so next 12 + 9 = 21 = U.
So the next cluster is FU.
Answer: FU

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NMRQ, NDZG, NUHW, NLPM, ?
qs.e:
1st letter stays N.
2nd: M, D, U, L (−9 each) → L(12) − 9 = 3 = C. 3rd: R, Z, H, P (+8) → P(16) + 8 = 24 = X.
4th: Q, G, W, M (−10) → M(13) − 10 = 3 = C.
So the next cluster is NCXC.
Answer: NCXC

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A & B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A % B means ‘A is the father of B’ If A % B & C # D @ E, then how is B related to E?
qs.e:
A % B: A is B's father. B & C: B is C's husband. C # D: C is D's sister. D @ E: D is E's daughter.
C is D's sister, so C is also E's daughter.
B is the husband of E's daughter, so B is E's son-in-law.
Answer: Son-in-law

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the brother of B, A – B means that A is the sister of B, A + B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal aunt of R?
qs.e:
A paternal aunt is the father's sister, so we need: P is the sister of Q and Q is the father of R.
That is P – Q + R (– = sister, + = father).
P – Q × R makes P a sister of R; P × Q + R makes P a paternal uncle; P + Q – R makes P a grandfather.
Answer: P – Q + R

qs.q: The term ‘Back-stick’ is used in which of the following games/sports?
qs.e:
Back-stick is a field hockey term: hitting or stopping the ball with the rounded (back) side of the stick, which is a foul.
Only the flat face of the stick may be used to play the ball.
Answer: Hockey

qs.q: The term ‘Parliament’ refers to the ____________.
qs.e:
"Parliament" means the national legislature of India. Under Article 79 it consists of the President, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.
A State's legislature is not called Parliament; it is the State Legislature (Article 168).
Answer: National legislature

qs.q: Who among the following Presidents of India was also the deputy chairman of Planning Commission?
qs.e:
Pranab Mukherjee was Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission from 1991 to 1996 and became President of India in 2012.
The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairman of the Commission, so the Deputy Chairman is its working head.
Answer: Pranab Mukherjee

qs.q: The foremost right among rights to freedom is ________.
o: Right to life and personal liberty
Right to freedom of speech and expression
qs.e:
In the NCERT treatment of the Right to Freedom, the foremost right is the right to life and personal liberty (Article 21): no person can be deprived of it except by procedure established by law.
The courts have read many rights into it – livelihood, shelter, privacy, a clean environment.
Preventive detention is an exception to liberty, not a right.
Answer: Right to life and personal liberty

qs.q: A dishonest merchant sells goods at a 12.5% loss on the cost price, but uses 28 g weight instead of 36 g. What is his percentage profit or loss?
qs.e:
Let 1 g cost ₹1. He charges for 36 g at 12.5% loss: SP = 36 × 0.875 = ₹31.5.
He actually hands over only 28 g, which costs him ₹28.
Profit = 31.5 − 28 = 3.5; profit% = 3.5/28 × 100 = 12.5%.
Shortcut: (36/28) × 0.875 = 1.125 → 12.5% gain.
Answer: 12.5% gain

qs.q: Riya could not decide between discount of 30% or two successive discounts of 25% and 5%, both given on shopping of ₹3,840. What is the difference between both the discounts?
qs.e:
Single 30% discount = 30% of 3840 = ₹1,152.
Successive 25% and 5%: equivalent = 25 + 5 − (25×5)/100 = 28.75%; 28.75% of 3840 = ₹1,104.
Difference = 1152 − 1104 = ₹48.
Shortcut: difference = 1.25% of 3840 = ₹48.
Answer: ₹48

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Like a cakewalk
qs.e:
'Like a cakewalk' means very easy to do.
Example: For a seasoned chef, cooking for ten is like a cakewalk.
Smooth surface is literal; 'pleasant experience' and 'active' miss the sense of ease.
Answer: Easy task

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Confusion
qs.e:
Confusion means a state of disorder or uncertainty (confusion in the hall). 'Commotion' (noisy disturbance, disorder) is closest.
Intrepidity = fearlessness; Stagnation = lack of movement; Perusal = careful reading.
Answer: Commotion

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. All eyes
qs.e:
'All eyes' means watching very eagerly and attentively.
Example: The children were all eyes as the magician opened the box.
Anger, no interest and not watching at all do not match eager attention.
Answer: Watching eagerly

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NMQR, NQYD, NUGP, NYOB, ?
qs.e:
1st letter stays N.
2nd: M, Q, U, Y (+4) → Y(25) + 4 = 29 − 26 = 3 = C. 3rd: Q, Y, G, O (+8) → O(15) + 8 = 23 = W.
4th: R, D, P, B (+12) → B(2) + 12 = 14 = N.
So the next cluster is NCWN.
Answer: NCWN

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? DW, FU, GT, IR, JQ, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: D, F, G, I, J — alternately +2, +1, so next +2: L.
2nd letters: W, U, T, R, Q — alternately −2, −1, so next −2: O.
So the next cluster is LO.
Answer: LO

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the father of B, A + B means that A is the mother of B, A ÷ B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the son of P?
qs.e:
Q must be male and P must be Q's parent.
P + Q × R: P is Q's mother and Q is R's father, so Q is male → Q is P's son.
But P + Q ÷ R also works: P is Q's mother and Q is R's brother, so Q is male → Q is P's son.
Q + P × R and R × Q + P make Q the mother, so they fail. The official key takes option 2.
Answer: P + Q × R

qs.q: A @ B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A & B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A ^ B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A + B means ‘A is the father of B’. If A + G & I + R @ S @ T # U & V, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: I is the father-in-law of U.
A is the maternal grandfather of T.
G is the brother of I.
R is the paternal granddaughter of A.
qs.e:
Decode: A is G's father; G is I's brother; I is R's father; R is S's sister; S is T's sister; T is U's wife; U is V's brother.
So A is the father of G and I; I is the father of R, S and T; U is T's husband.
I is U's father-in-law (true); G is I's brother (true); R is A's son's daughter, a paternal granddaughter (true).
T is A's son's daughter, so A is T's PATERNAL grandfather, not maternal. That statement is wrong.
Answer: A is the maternal grandfather of T.

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 4, 6, 12, 14, 28, 30, ?
Which of the following cities hosted the 2019 Military World Games organised by the International Military Sports Council?
qs.e:
The 7th CISM Military World Games were held in Wuhan, China, in October 2019.
The Games are held every four years for athletes from the armed forces; China topped the medal table.
Answer: Wuhan, China

qs.q: Fundamental Duties were added in the Constitution of India under the leadership of which Prime Minister of India?
qs.e:
The Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, when Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister.
They were based on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendations, made during the Emergency. Ten duties were added; the 11th came in 2002.
Answer: Indira Gandhi

qs.q: first edition of the Youth Olympic Games was held at _______.
qs.e:
The first Youth Olympic Games (summer) were held in Singapore in August 2010, for athletes aged 14-18.
The first Winter Youth Olympics followed at Innsbruck in 2012; Nanjing hosted the 2014 summer edition.
Answer: Singapore

qs.q: The Vice President of India is elected for a period of ______ years.
qs.e:
Under Article 67, the Vice-President holds office for 5 years from the date he or she enters office, and can be re-elected.
The Vice-President is also the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Answer: 5

qs.q: A shopkeeper makes a net profit of 44% on selling an article at successive discounts of 10% and 20%. Find the net profit percentage, if the shopkeeper sells the same article at a discount of 15%.
qs.e:
Successive discounts 10% and 20%: SP = MP × 0.9 × 0.8 = 0.72 MP.
This SP = 1.44 CP, so MP = 1.44/0.72 CP = 2 CP.
At 15% discount: SP = 0.85 × 2 CP = 1.70 CP.
Profit = 70%.
Answer: 70%

qs.q: The difference between the cost price and selling price of a pair of shoes is Rs.1,200. If the profit is 15%, the selling price is:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Competent
qs.e:
Competent means having the skill to do something well (a competent doctor). 'Capable' matches.
Complex = complicated; Poor = of low quality; Beginner = a novice, not yet skilled.
Answer: Capable

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom. In weal and woe
qs.e:
'In weal and woe' means in good times and bad – in prosperity (weal = well-being) and adversity (woe = sorrow).
Example: A true friend stands by you in weal and woe.
Options 1, 2 and 4 cover only one side (only bad or only good times).
Answer: In prosperity and adversity

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Announce
qs.e:
Announce means to make something known publicly (announce the results). 'Advertise' (make known publicly) is closest.
Denounce = condemn publicly; Secret = kept hidden; Hide = conceal. The last two are opposites.
Answer: Advertise

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A green horn
qs.e:
A 'greenhorn' is an inexperienced or new person.
Origin: 'green' = young, untrained (like a young animal with new horns).
Example: As a greenhorn in the office, he made many small mistakes.
Uneducated is different from inexperienced; clever and skilled are the opposite.
Answer: Inexperienced person

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The sporadic instructions of the invigilators distracted the examinee.
qs.e:
Sporadic means happening at irregular intervals, now and then (sporadic rain). 'Occasional' matches.
Continuous = without a break (the antonym); Indirect = not straight; Repetitive = repeated again and again.
Answer: Occasional

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1331, 2197, ?, 6859
qs.e:
The terms are cubes of consecutive primes: 1331 = 11³, 2197 = 13³, 6859 = 19³.
The prime between 13 and 19 is 17, and 17³ = 4913.
(15³ = 3375 is tempting, but 15 is not prime and the gap to 19 would not fit.)
Answer: 4913

qs.q: If A + B means that A is the father of B, A – B means that A is the mother of B, A × B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the son of P?
qs.e:
Q must be male and P must be Q's parent.
P – Q + R: P is Q's mother and Q is R's father, so Q is male → Q is P's son.
P – Q × R also works: P is Q's mother and Q is R's brother, so Q is male → Q is P's son.
P + Q – R makes Q a mother (daughter), and P × P – Q is not a valid chain. The official key takes option 4.
Answer: P – Q + R

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’. A & B means ‘A is the father of B’. A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’. If W @ Q # T & Y @ M % K, then how is Q related to K?
qs.e:
W @ Q: W is Q's son. Q # T: Q is T's sister. T & Y: T is Y's father. Y @ M: Y is M's son. M % K: M is K's mother.
T and M are the parents of Y and K, so T is K's father.
Q is T's sister, i.e. the sister of K's father.
Answer: Father’s sister

qs.q: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ABCD, BDFD, CFID, ?, EJOD
qs.e:
1st letters: A, B, C, D, E (+1). 2nd: B, D, F, H, J (+2).
3rd: C, F, I, L, O (+3). 4th letter stays D.
So the missing cluster is DHLD.
Answer: DHLD

qs.q: The Winter Youth Olympic Games 2024 will be held in ________.
qs.e:
The 2024 Winter Youth Olympic Games were held in Gangwon Province, South Korea, in January 2024 (the 4th edition).
Gangwon used venues from the PyeongChang 2018 Winter Olympics. Lausanne hosted in 2020, and Dakar gets the 2026 summer YOG.
Answer: Gangwon

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right?
qs.e:
The right to vote is a constitutional right under Article 326 (adult suffrage) and a statutory right under the Representation of the People Act. It is not a Fundamental Right in Part III.
Freedom of Religion (25–28), Right against Exploitation (23–24) and Right to Equality (14–18) are all Fundamental Rights.
Answer: Right to Vote

qs.q: In AIBA Boxing Junior Boys and Girls Competitions, the bouts must consist of each round of ____ minutes.
qs.e:
Under AIBA technical rules, junior boys' and girls' bouts are three rounds of 2 minutes each.
Youth and elite bouts use 3-minute rounds, with 1 minute of rest between rounds in all categories.
Answer: 2 min

qs.q: Kapil sells a mobile to Sachin at a gain of 15% and Sachin again sells it to Rohit at a profit of 12%. If Rohit pays Rs.322, what is the cost price of the mobile for Kapil?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Transient
qs.e:
Transient means lasting only a short time (transient joy). 'Temporary' matches.
Transform = change; Transmit = send; Trap = catch. These only look alike (trans-).
Answer: Temporary

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom. Bag and baggage
qs.e:
'Bag and baggage' means with all of one's belongings – completely.
Example: The tenant left bag and baggage overnight.
Burden, aimlessness and unhappiness are not the meaning.
Answer: With all of one’s possessions

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. He was murdered in cold blood.
qs.e:
'In cold blood' means deliberately and without pity or emotion.
So he was murdered in a planned, cruel manner, not in a fit of anger.
Cold weather and 'blood was cold' are literal; 'regretfully' is the opposite.
Answer: deliberately

qs.q: ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the daughter of A’. If G # H & I @ J & K, then how is H related to J?
qs.e:
G # H: H is G's daughter. H & I: H is I's mother. I @ J: I is J's husband. J & K: J is K's mother.
H is the mother of I, and I is J's husband.
The husband's mother is the mother-in-law, so H is J's mother-in-law.
Answer: Mother-in-law

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, ?
qs.e:
Each term is n² + 1: 2²+1 = 5, 3²+1 = 10, 4²+1 = 17, 5²+1 = 26, 6²+1 = 37, 7²+1 = 50.
Next: 8² + 1 = 65.
(Differences 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 lead to the same: 50 + 15 = 65.)
Answer: 65

qs.q: If A + B means that A is the brother of B, A × B means that A is the sister of B, A ÷ B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the sister of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's sister. P × Q + R: P is Q's sister and Q is R's brother, so P, Q, R are siblings and P is R's sister.
P + Q × R makes P a brother; P × Q ÷ R makes P a paternal aunt of R.
Options 1 and 4 are printed the same, so both are correct; the official key takes option 4.
Answer: P × Q + R

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? NAME, NEME, ?, NOME, NUME
qs.e:
Only the 2nd letter changes; N_ME stays fixed.
The 2nd letters are the vowels in order: A, E, I, O, U.
So the missing term is NIME.
Answer: NIME

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. RTM, VZX, ZFI, DLT, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: R, V, Z, D, H (+4). 2nd: T, Z, F, L, R (+6). 3rd: M, X, I, T, E (+11).
So the next cluster is HRE.
Answer: HRE

qs.q: The Asian Games 2018 were held in which of the following countries?
qs.e:
The 2018 (18th) Asian Games were held in Indonesia, jointly at Jakarta and Palembang.
India won 70 medals there, then its best at the Asian Games.
Answer: Indonesia

qs.q: Protection of life and liberty is included under which Article of the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
Article 21 says no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
Article 20 – protection in respect of conviction; Articles 23–24 – right against exploitation.
Answer: Article 21

qs.q: Which of the following venues was decided to host the 2022 Asian Games?
qs.e:
Hangzhou, China, was chosen to host the 2022 (19th) Asian Games; they were postponed due to COVID-19 and held in 2023.
Guangzhou hosted in 2010, Incheon in 2014 and Jakarta in 2018.
Answer: Hangzhou, China

qs.q: Raju, Ravi and Ashok contested an election. 5% votes polled were invalid. Raju got 30% of the total votes. Ravi got 32% of the total votes. The winner got 5136 more votes than the person who received the least number of votes. Find the total number of votes polled.
qs.e:
Invalid 5%, Raju 30%, Ravi 32% → Ashok = 100 − 5 − 30 − 32 = 33% of total votes polled.
Winner (Ashok, 33%) − least (Raju, 30%) = 3% of total.
3% = 5136 → total = 5136 × 100/3 = 171200.
Answer: 171200

qs.q: A horse was sold for Rs.60,000 at a profit of 20%. For what price should he have sold to gain a 30% profit?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word to fill in the blank. For Rahul, everything was a _________ (modern) experience until he stepped onto the field.
qs.e:
Modern here means new and unfamiliar to him (everything was a new experience). 'New' matches.
Flashy = showy; Global = worldwide; Asiatic = of Asia.
Answer: new

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Moral
qs.e:
Moral means concerned with right and wrong behaviour (a moral duty). 'Ethical' matches.
Honourable = deserving respect, related but narrower; Godliness = devotion to God (a noun); Symphony = a piece of music.
Answer: Ethical

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom. A skeleton in the cupboard
o: A popular fact which is not hidden
A popular fact to be kept secret
An embarrassing fact not to be kept secret
An embarrassing fact to be kept secret
qs.e:
'A skeleton in the cupboard' (or closet) is an embarrassing or shameful secret that a person or family keeps hidden.
Example: Every family has a skeleton in the cupboard.
Options 1 and 2 call it 'popular'; option 3 says it is 'not to be kept secret' – both wrong.
Answer: An embarrassing fact to be kept secret

qs.q: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. Even though Margaret had already eaten a large meal, she could not resist eating two slices of the delectable pie.
qs.e:
Delectable means delicious, very pleasant to taste (a delectable dessert). 'Delicious' matches; that is why she could not resist it.
Stale = not fresh; Rotten = decayed (both opposites); Nutritious = healthy, but not about taste.
Answer: Delicious

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Fly into a passion
qs.e:
'To fly into a passion' (or rage) means to become angry suddenly.
Example: He flew into a passion when his name was left off the list.
'At times', 'often' and 'always' describe frequency, not a sudden outburst.
Answer: To become angry suddenly

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? abCD, fgHI, ?, stUV, abCD
qs.e:
Each cluster is four consecutive letters (first two small, last two capital).
Starting letters: a(1), f(6), ?, s(19), a(27 → 1) — the jumps are +5, +6, +7, +8.
So the missing cluster starts at 6 + 6 = 12 = l, giving lmNO.
Answer: lmNO

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 4, 10, 28, ?, 244
qs.e:
Each term is three times the previous minus 2.
2 × 3 − 2 = 4; 4 × 3 − 2 = 10; 10 × 3 − 2 = 28.
Next: 28 × 3 − 2 = 82; check 82 × 3 − 2 = 244 ✓.
Answer: 82

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’. A & B means ‘A is the father of B’. A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’. If W @ Q % T & Y @ M % K, then how is Q related to K?
qs.e:
W @ Q: W is Q's son. Q % T: Q is T's mother. T & Y: T is Y's father. Y @ M: Y is M's son. M % K: M is K's mother.
T and M are the parents of Y and K, so T is K's father.
Q is T's mother, i.e. the mother of K's father.
Answer: Father’s mother

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ABCD, HGLO, OLUZ, VQDK, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: A, H, O, V (+7) → 29 − 26 = 3 = C. 2nd: B, G, L, Q (+5) → V.
3rd: C, L, U, D (+9) → D(4) + 9 = 13 = M. 4th: D, O, Z, K (+11) → K(11) + 11 = 22 = V.
So the next cluster is CVMV.
Answer: CVMV

qs.q: If A – B means that A is the mother of B, A + B means that A is the father of B, A ÷ B means that A is the sister of B, then which of the following expression shows that P is the aunt of Q?
qs.e:
An aunt is a parent's sister: P must be the sister of Q's mother or father.
P ÷ R – Q: P is R's sister and R is Q's mother → P is Q's (maternal) aunt.
P ÷ R + Q: P is R's sister and R is Q's father → P is Q's paternal aunt, also an aunt.
P + R ÷ Q makes P Q's father; R ÷ P – Q makes P Q's mother. The official key takes option 3.
Answer: P ÷ R – Q

qs.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is a:
qs.e:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (Article 148) is a single-member constitutional office, appointed by the President for 6 years or until age 65.
The CAG audits the accounts of the Union and the States and is called the guardian of the public purse.
By contrast, the Election Commission is now a three-member body.
Answer: single-member body

qs.q: Who moved the Objective Resolution that was later adapted as the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946. It was adopted on 22 January 1947.
Its ideals – sovereignty, justice, liberty, equality – later took shape as the Preamble.
Answer: Jawaharlal Nehru

qs.q: The Commonwealth Games 2018 were held at which of the following places?
qs.e:
The 2018 (21st) Commonwealth Games were held at Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia.
India finished third with 66 medals, including 26 gold.
Answer: Gold coast

qs.q: A pen was sold for Rs.166.44 with a profit of 14%. If it were sold for Rs.154.76, then what would have been the percentage of profit or loss?

In the election, 8% of the voters did not cast their votes. Two candidates contested the election in which the winning cadidate got 48% of the total votes and won election by 1100 votes. Find the total number of voters in the election, given that all the votes cast were valid?
qs.e:
8% did not vote, so 92% voted (all valid).
Winner 48% of total, loser 92 − 48 = 44% of total.
Margin = 4% of total = 1100 → total voters = 27500.
Answer: 27500

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exaltation
qs.e:
Exaltation means a feeling of great happiness, or the act of raising high (exaltation after the win). 'Ecstasy' matches.
Dejection = sadness (the antonym); Satisfaction = contentment, weaker; Elaboration = adding detail.
Answer: Ecstasy

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break the ice
o: Make people meeting first time feel uncomfortable
Make people meeting first time feel sad
Make people meeting first time feel more detached
Make people meeting first time feel more comfortable
qs.e:
'Break the ice' means to do or say something that makes people meeting for the first time feel more relaxed and comfortable.
Origin: ships breaking ice to clear a path.
Example: A quick game helped break the ice at the orientation.
Uncomfortable, sad and detached are the opposite effect.
Answer: Make people meeting first time feel more comfortable

qs.q: A + B means ‘A is the father of B’ A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A % B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A & B means ‘A is the son of B’ If A + B & C – D + E, then how is A related to E?
qs.e:
A + B: A is B's father. B & C: B is C's son. C – D: C is D's mother. D + E: D is E's father.
A and C are B's parents, and D is C's child, so A is D's father.
D is E's father, so A is E's father's father.
Answer: Father’s father

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? LAT, NDR, PGP, ?, TML
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: L, N, P, R, T (+2). 2nd: A, D, G, J, M (+3). 3rd: T, R, P, N, L (−2).
So the missing cluster is RJN.
Answer: RJN

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 345, 356, 368, 381, 395, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 11, 12, 13, 14 — rising by 1.
The next difference is 15.
395 + 15 = 410.
Answer: 410

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. DMT, JOB, PQJ, VSR, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: D, J, P, V (+6) → 28 − 26 = 2 = B. 2nd: M, O, Q, S (+2) → U.
3rd: T, B, J, R (+8) → R(18) + 8 = 26 = Z.
So the next cluster is BUZ.
Answer: BUZ

qs.q: If A ÷ B means that A is the father of B, A × B means that A is the mother of B, A + B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the daughter of P?
qs.e:
Q must be female and P must be Q's parent.
P ÷ Q × R: P is Q's father and Q is R's mother, so Q is female → Q is P's daughter.
P ÷ Q + R and P × Q ÷ R make Q male (son); P + Q ÷ R makes P Q's brother.
Answer: P ÷Q × R

qs.q: It is the duty of every citizen to uphold and protect the ________, unity and integrity of India.
qs.e:
Fundamental Duty 51A(c) says every citizen must uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
The same three words appear in the oaths of MPs and ministers, and as grounds for reasonable restrictions under Article 19.
Answer: sovereignty

qs.q: Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India is INCORRECT?
o: Members of State legislatures do not take part in his elections.
He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Vice President is elected for five years.
He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
qs.e:
The Vice-President is not removed by the President. Under Article 67(b), removal needs a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
The other statements are true: the electoral college has only MPs (no State MLAs), the VP is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and the term is 5 years.
Answer: He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

qs.q: What is the average circumference of the standard cricket ball in international cricket?
qs.e:
By the Laws of Cricket, a men's ball must have a circumference of 22.4-22.9 cm, i.e. about 8.81-9 inches, and weigh 155.9-163 g.
The other ranges are far too small or too large (a football is about 27-28 inches).
Answer: 8.81 inches - 9 inches

qs.q: In an election between two candidates, the defeated candidate secured 42% of the valid votes polled and lost the election by 7,68,400 votes. If 82,560 votes were declared invalid and 20% people did NOT cast their vote, then the invalid votes were what percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place) of the votes which people did NOT cast?
qs.e:
Defeated 42%, winner 58% → margin 16% of valid = 7,68,400 → valid votes = 48,02,500.
Votes cast = valid + invalid = 48,02,500 + 82,560 = 48,85,060 = 80% of all voters.
All voters = 61,06,325; did not vote = 20% = 12,21,265.
Invalid as % of non-voters = 82560/1221265 × 100 ≈ 6.76% ≈ 6.8%.
Answer: 6.8 Percent

qs.q: The reduction of 20% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 50 kg more for Rs.450. Find the original price of rice per kg.
qs.e:
A 20% price cut saves 20% of ₹450 = ₹90, and that ₹90 buys the extra 50 kg.
Reduced price = 90 ÷ 50 = ₹1.80 per kg.
Original price = 1.80 ÷ 0.8 = ₹2.25 per kg.
Check: 450/2.25 = 200 kg, 450/1.8 = 250 kg (50 more).
Answer: Rs.2.25

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Listening to the news of his father’s illness, Soumen left for home with a heavy heart.
qs.e:
Illness means being unwell, a disease (a long illness). 'Sickness' matches.
Disturbance = interruption; Disintegration = breaking into pieces; Disorder = confusion, or a specific condition, which is less exact here.
Answer: sickness

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The present paper throws light on the nexus between the academic performance and mental health of children.
qs.e:
Nexus means a connection or link between things (the nexus between crime and politics). 'Link' matches.
Dispute = disagreement; Alignment = arrangement in a line; Incongruence = mismatch (the antonym).
Answer: Link

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word to fill in the blank. If we want to progress, we must sometimes embrace __________ (mutate).
qs.e:
Mutate means to change in form or nature (viruses mutate). 'Change' fits; to grow, we must embrace change.
Replicate = copy exactly; Imitate = copy someone; Incise = cut into.
Answer: change

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 111, 222, 444, ?, 1776, 3552
qs.e:
Each term is double the previous: 111 × 2 = 222, 222 × 2 = 444.
444 × 2 = 888; check 888 × 2 = 1776 and 1776 × 2 = 3552 ✓.
Answer: 888

qs.q: R + S means ‘R is the daughter of S’ R = S means ‘R is the father of S’ R ÷ S means ‘R is the wife of S’ R × S means ‘R is the brother of S’ E ÷ F × J + L = M, then how is L related to E?
qs.e:
E ÷ F: E is F's wife. F × J: F is J's brother. J + L: J is L's daughter. L = M: L is M's father.
F is J's brother, so F is also L's son (L is the father, since L = M).
E is the wife of L's son, so L is E's father-in-law.
Answer: Father-in-law

qs.q: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CZNM, FXOL, IVPK, ?, ORRI
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: C, F, I, L, O (+3). 2nd: Z, X, V, T, R (−2).
3rd: N, O, P, Q, R (+1). 4th: M, L, K, J, I (−1).
So the missing cluster is LTQJ.
Answer: LTQJ

qs.q: If A + B means that A is the brother of B, A × B means that A is the sister of B, A ÷ B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the brother of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's brother.
P + Q × R: P is Q's brother and Q is R's sister → P, Q, R are siblings, P is R's brother.
P + R × Q also works directly: P is R's brother (and R is Q's sister).
P + Q ÷ R makes P R's paternal uncle; P × Q + R makes P a sister. The official key takes option 2.
Answer: P + Q × R

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ACC, UZD, OWE, ITF, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: A, U, O, I (−6) → I(9) − 6 = C. 2nd: C, Z, W, T (−3) → Q.
3rd: C, D, E, F (+1) → G.
So the next cluster is CQG.
Answer: CQG

qs.q: Which Part of the Constitution of India reflects the Fundamental Duties?
qs.e:
The Fundamental Duties are in Part IV-A (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
Part IX-B covers co-operative societies, Part X Scheduled and Tribal Areas, and Part XII finance and property.
Answer: Part IV-A

qs.q: Which Article of the Constitution separates the judiciary from the executive?
qs.e:
Article 50, a Directive Principle, asks the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.
Article 143 – advisory opinion of the Supreme Court; Article 74 – Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President; Article 144 – authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court.
Answer: Article 50

qs.q: In which of the following months did the Australian Open take place in 2022?
qs.e:
The 2022 Australian Open was held in January (17-30 January 2022) in Melbourne.
It is always the first Grand Slam of the year; Rafael Nadal and Ashleigh Barty won the singles titles.
Answer: January

qs.q: In Table Tennis, how many lets are allowed in a row on a serve?
qs.e:
In table tennis a let (the serve touches the net and lands correctly) is simply replayed, and there is no limit on the number of lets in a row.
In contrast, a fault (not a let) loses the point at once.
Answer: Unlimited

qs.q: In an election between two candidates, 12% of voters did not cast their votes. The winner by obtaining 68% of the total votes defeated his contestant by 2880 votes. What was the total number of voters who cast their votes in the election?
qs.e:
12% did not vote, so 88% voted.
Winner 68% of total, loser 88 − 68 = 20% of total → margin 48% of total.
48% = 2880 → total voters = 6000.
Votes cast = 88% of 6000 = 5280.
Answer: 5280

qs.q: The price of some wooden furniture increases by 65% when it passes through three hands. If the first and second sellers made a profit of 20% and 25%, respectively, then find the profit percentage of the third seller.
qs.e:
Final price = 1.65 × original = 1.20 × 1.25 × (1 + r).
1.20 × 1.25 = 1.50, so 1 + r = 1.65/1.50 = 1.10.
Third seller's profit = 10%.
Answer: 10%

qs.q: Sunil purchased a fan at a 10% discount on the labelled price. If he had purchased it at a 15% discount, he would have saved ₹400. Find the labelled price of the fan.
qs.e:
The extra 5% discount (15% − 10%) equals the ₹400 saved.
5% of labelled price = 400, so labelled price = 400 × 20 = ₹8,000.
Answer: ₹8,000

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Beat around the bush
o: Avoid the main point by talking in a roundabout way
Avoid saying what you mean, usually because it is not funny
Avoid using foul words to make someone uncomfortable
qs.e:
'Beat around the bush' means to avoid the main point by talking in a roundabout way.
Origin: hunters' beaters hit the bushes around a bird instead of going for it directly.
Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened.
Demeaning, unfunny remarks and foul words are not the meaning.
Answer: Avoid the main point by talking in a roundabout way

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Visiting a book fair always fills my heart with a great satisfaction.
qs.e:
Satisfaction = the pleasant feeling of having what you wanted. E.g. She smiled with satisfaction at her finished painting.
Contentment means the same calm, pleased state of mind, so it fits the sentence exactly.
Refreshment = renewed energy or food/drink; pride = a feeling of self-worth from achievement; bliss = perfect, intense joy (stronger than satisfaction).
Answer: contentment

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Deliberate
qs.e:
Deliberate (adjective) = done on purpose, after careful thought. E.g. It was a deliberate move to save time.
Planned also means thought out in advance, so it is the synonym.
Casual = relaxed, without planning; hasty and rushed = done too quickly without thought - all close to antonyms.
Answer: Planned

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Magnify
qs.e:
Magnify = make something bigger or appear bigger. E.g. A lens magnifies the tiny letters.
Expand = become or make larger, so it matches.
Magnanimous = generous, big-hearted (a sound-alike trap); miniature = very small; underemphasise = give too little importance (opposite idea).
Answer: Expand

qs.q: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? MBTN, KCSP, IDRR, ?, EFPV

3rd: T, S, R, Q, P (−1). 4th: N, P, R, T, V (+2).

Answer: GEQT

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. LMR, PUA, TCJ, XKS, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: L, P, T, X (+4) → 28 − 26 = 2 = B. 2nd: M, U, C, K (+8) → K(11) + 8 = 19 = S.
3rd: R, A, J, S (+9) → S(19) + 9 = 28 − 26 = 2 = B.
So the next cluster is BSB.
Answer: BSB

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the father of B, A –B means that A is the mother of B, A ÷ B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the father of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's father.
P × Q ÷ R: P is Q's father and Q is R's brother → P is R's father.
P × R ÷ Q also works directly: P is R's father (and R is Q's brother).
P ÷ Q × R makes P a paternal uncle; P × Q – R makes P a grandfather. The official key takes option 2.
Answer: P × Q ÷ R

qs.q: ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the son of A’. If K # L & M @ N # P, then how is P related to K?
qs.e:
K # L: L is K's son. L & M: L is M's father. M @ N: M is N's husband. N # P: P is N's son.
N is M's wife, so P is M's son.
Chain: K → son L → son M → son P, so P is K's son's son's son.
Answer: Son’s son’s son

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 29, 33, ?, 113, 369
Which of the following players is associated with boxing?
qs.e:
Lovlina Borgohain is an Indian boxer from Assam; she won bronze in the 69 kg category at Tokyo 2020.
Hima Das is a sprinter; the other names are not boxers.
Answer: Lovlina Borgohain

qs.q: In which year were the 73rd and 74th amendments passed by the Parliament?
qs.e:
Parliament passed both the 73rd (Panchayats) and 74th (Municipalities) Amendments in December 1992.
They came into force in 1993 – the 73rd on 24 April 1993 and the 74th on 1 June 1993.
Answer: 1992

qs.q: Where and when will the fourth edition of the Winter Youth Olympic Games be held?
qs.e:
The Winter Youth Olympics began at Innsbruck 2012, then Lillehammer 2016 and Lausanne 2020; the fourth edition was Gangwon (South Korea) in 2024.
Dakar 2026 is the summer YOG, Nanjing hosted the 2014 summer YOG and Buenos Aires the 2018 summer YOG.
Answer: 2024 Gangwon

qs.q: The ___________ is a set of written rules that are accepted by all people living within a country.
qs.e:
A Constitution is the set of basic written rules that everyone living in a country accepts. It sets up the government, divides power and protects rights.
A Bill is a draft of a proposed law, and a Writ is a court order.
Answer: Constitution

qs.q: By selling a car for Rs.2,78,000, a dealer gains 25%. If the profit is reduced to 18%, then the selling price will be:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Remorse
qs.e:
Remorse = deep regret for a wrong one has done. E.g. The thief showed remorse in court.
Repentance = sincere regret for wrongdoing, so it is the synonym.
Slow = not fast; liberate = set free; affinity = natural liking or closeness - none relate to regret.
Answer: Repentance

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. By the end of the football match, feelings had reached fever pitch.
o: to get so strong that one cannot control them
qs.e:
Idiom: when feelings "reach fever pitch", they become so intense and excited that they are hard to control.
At the end of the football match, the crowd's excitement had become uncontrollable.
The other options (in many places, extremely serious, start well) describe different ideas.
Answer: to get so strong that one cannot control them

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To smell a rat
o: To have reason to know the presence of a rat
To know the smell of a rat
To learn the smell of a rat
qs.e:
'To smell a rat' means to suspect that something is wrong or that someone is cheating.
Image: a cat that smells a hidden rat.
Example: When the 'lottery prize' asked for a fee, I smelt a rat.
The other options take 'smell' and 'rat' literally.
Answer: To have reason to suspect

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 26, 54, 110, 222, ?, 894

26 × 2 + 2 = 54; 54 × 2 + 2 = 110; 110 × 2 + 2 = 222.

Answer: 446

qs.q: If X – Y means that X is the mother of Y, X × Y means that X is the father of Y, X ÷ Y means that X is the sister of Y, then which of the following expression shows that Q is the son of P?
qs.e:
Q must be male and P must be Q's parent.
P – Q × R: P is Q's mother and Q is R's father, so Q is male → Q is P's son.
P – Q ÷ R makes Q a sister (daughter); Q – P × R and R × Q – P make Q a mother.
Answer: P ­– Q × R

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A & B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A % B means ‘A is the wife of B’ If G % M # L @ P & C @ B, then how is L related to B?
qs.e:
G % M: G is M's wife. M # L: M is L's brother. L @ P: L is P's daughter. P & C: P is C's husband. C @ B: C is B's daughter.
P and C are L's parents, and C is B's daughter.
So L is the daughter of B's daughter → B's granddaughter.
Answer: Granddaughter

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. TQT, ZSB, FUJ, LWR, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: T, Z, F, L, R (+6). 2nd: Q, S, U, W, Y (+2). 3rd: T, B, J, R, Z (+8).
So the next cluster is RYZ.
Answer: RYZ

qs.q: In which of the following years was the Fit India Movement launched by Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, GoI?
qs.e:
The Fit India Movement was launched by PM Narendra Modi on 29 August 2019 (National Sports Day), under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
It encourages people to make physical activity a daily habit.
Answer: 2019

qs.q: The system based on individual leadership is a __________ system.
qs.e:
In a presidential system (e.g. the USA), executive power rests with one person – the President – who is elected separately and is not responsible to the legislature. So it rests on individual leadership.
A parliamentary system (e.g. India) rests on collective leadership and collective responsibility of the cabinet.
Answer: presidential

qs.q: The final of the French Open (Roland Garros) Tennis 2021 for men took place on which day?
qs.e:
The 2021 French Open men's singles final was played on 13 June 2021, when Novak Djokovic beat Stefanos Tsitsipas from two sets down.
The 2021 tournament was pushed back a week because of COVID-19.
Answer: 13 June

qs.q: Number p is 15% more than 150. If k is 15% less than p, then k is equal to:
The cost of a piece of diamond varies with the square of its weight. A diamond of Rs.6,084 value is cut into 3 pieces whose weights are in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1. Find the loss involved in the cutting.
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Obligatory
qs.e:
Obligatory = required by rule or law; not a matter of choice. E.g. Wearing a helmet is obligatory for riders.
Compulsory means exactly that - must be done.
Unnecessary = not needed; chosen = picked by choice; optional = left to choice - all are opposites in sense.
Answer: Compulsory

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Being an ardent professional, the lawyer always kept his clients at an arm’s length.
qs.e:
'To keep someone at arm's length' means to keep them at a distance and avoid getting too friendly.
The professional lawyer kept a proper distance from his clients.
'Away from each other' implies separating the clients; 'under wraps' = secret; 'alert and prepared' = on guard.
Answer: At a distance

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Rahul was sharing some of his childhood stories and they were hysterical.
qs.e:
Hysterical has two senses: wildly emotional, and (informally) extremely funny. E.g. The comedian's act was hysterical.
Stories that are shared and 'were hysterical' means they made people laugh a lot, so 'funny' fits.
Emotional is the other sense but doesn't suit amusing childhood stories here; dangerous and scary don't fit.
Answer: Funny

qs.q: A + B means ‘A is the father of B’ A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’ A # B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ If A # B – C @ D + E, then how is A related to E?
qs.e:
A # B: A is B's daughter. B – C: B is C's mother. C @ D: C is D's son. D + E: D is E's father.
B and D are the parents of C and E, and A is B's daughter.
So A, C and E are siblings and A (female) is E's sister.
Answer: Sister

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ?, 11, 35, 107, 323
qs.e:
Each term is three times the previous plus 2.
11 × 3 + 2 = 35; 35 × 3 + 2 = 107; 107 × 3 + 2 = 323.
Working back: (11 − 2) ÷ 3 = 3, so the first term is 3.
Answer: 3

qs.q: If L × M means that L is the mother of M, L – M means that L is the father of M, L ÷ M means that L is the sister of M, then which of the following expression shows that P is the father of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's father (– = father, × = mother, ÷ = sister).
P – Q ÷ R: P is Q's father and Q is R's sister → P is R's father.
Q – P × R makes P R's mother; P – Q × R makes P a grandfather; R – P × Q makes R the father.
Answer: P – Q ÷ R

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? RLV, PNS, NPP, ?, JTJ
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: R, P, N, L, J (−2). 2nd: L, N, P, R, T (+2). 3rd: V, S, P, M, J (−3).
So the missing cluster is LRM.
Answer: LRM

qs.q: Which special knowledge or practical experience is NOT a condition for being nominated to Rajya Sabha by the President of India?
qs.e:
Under Article 80(3), the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha who have special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.
"Eloquence" is not one of these fields.
Answer: Eloquence

qs.q: Which of the following pairs of countries will host the 2023 FIFA Women’s World Cup?
qs.e:
The 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup was co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand, the first with 32 teams.
Spain won it, beating England in the final at Sydney.
Answer: New Zealand and Australia

qs.q: Asiad is regulated by_________.
qs.e:
The Asian Games (Asiad) are governed by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA), headquartered in Kuwait.
The IOC runs the Olympics and the Commonwealth Games Federation runs the CWG.
Answer: Olympic Council of Asia

qs.q: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India pronounce the theory of the ‘Basic Structure’ of the Constitution?
qs.e:
In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), a 13-judge bench ruled that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution but cannot destroy its "basic structure".
Golaknath (1967) had held that Fundamental Rights could not be amended at all. Minerva Mills (1980) later applied the basic structure doctrine.
Answer: Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973

qs.q: A dishonest trader says to customers that he sells his goods at a cost price, but he uses a false weight and gains 12.5% as profit. How many grams does he use to weigh 1 kg?
qs.e:
Selling at cost price but giving less weight: gain% = (true − false)/false × 100.
1000/w = 1.125, so w = 1000 ÷ 1.125 = 888.8 g.
Check: (1000 − 888.8)/888.8 ≈ 12.5%.
Answer: 888.8 g

qs.q: The cost of apples is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net pecentage decrease?
qs.e:
Equal % increase then decrease always gives a net loss of x²/100 %.
1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96 → 4% decrease.
Shortcut: 20²/100 = 4%.
Answer: 4%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Keen
qs.e:
Keen = eager and very interested in doing something. E.g. She is keen to learn French.
Enthusiastic = full of eager interest, so it is the synonym.
Happy = pleased (not necessarily eager); wild = uncontrolled; imitate = copy (a verb, unrelated).
Answer: Enthusiastic

label: CGL 2022, 5 December 2022, shift 1
src: SSC candidate response sheet, official key marked

qs.q: A + B means ‘A is the father of B’ A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A % B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A # B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ If P + Q % R % S # T – U , then how is Q related to U?
qs.e:
P + Q: P is Q's father. Q % R: Q is R's brother. R % S: R is S's brother. S # T: S is T's daughter. T – U: T is U's mother.
S is T's daughter and T is U's mother, so S and U are siblings; Q and R are S's brothers too.
So Q, R, S and U are all children of T, and Q is U's brother.
Answer: Brother

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 41, 54, 67, 80, 93, ?
qs.e:
Each term is 13 more than the one before: 54 − 41 = 67 − 54 = 13.
93 + 13 = 106.
Answer: 106

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? LE, OJ, UO, DT, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: L, O, U, D — gaps +3, +6, +9 (D = 4 after wrapping), so next +12: 4 + 12 = 16 = P.
2nd letters: E, J, O, T (+5 each) → T(20) + 5 = 25 = Y.
So the next cluster is PY.
Answer: PY

qs.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India authorises the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in specific categories of matters?
qs.e:
Article 143 lets the President ask the Supreme Court for its opinion on a question of law or fact of public importance. This is the Court's advisory jurisdiction, and the advice is not binding.
It was used, for example, in the Kerala Education Bill (1958) and Ram Janmabhoomi (1993) references.
Art 142 is about doing complete justice; Art 145 about the rules of court.
Answer: Article 143

qs.q: Pivoting is related to which of the following sports?
qs.e:
Pivoting is a basketball move: a player holding the ball keeps one foot (the pivot foot) fixed and steps in any direction with the other foot.
Lifting the pivot foot before passing or dribbling is travelling.
Answer: Basketball

qs.q: In all AIBA Boxing competitions, the rest time between each round is ________ minutes.
qs.e:
In all AIBA boxing competitions the rest between rounds is 1 minute.
Round length varies by age group (for example 3 minutes for elite and youth, 2 minutes for juniors).
Answer: 1

qs.q: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence is a_______________ in the Indian Constitution.
qs.e:
"To safeguard public property and to abjure violence" is Fundamental Duty 51A(i) in Part IV-A.
Duties cannot be enforced by a court on their own, but they guide citizens and help courts interpret laws.
Answer: fundamental duty

qs.q: 0.5 is what percentage of 20?
qs.e:
Percentage = (part/whole) × 100.
0.5/20 × 100 = 50/20 = 2.5%.
Answer: 2.5%

qs.q: A hotel is giving a discount of 12% on the booking of 2 or more rooms. Additionally, the hotel is offering a 5% discount only on payment using any card of SBI. Rakesh booked 2 rooms in the hotel for a day at the rate of Rs.1,500 per room per day. While checking out, he paid the bill using SBI Silver Card. How much amount did he have to pay?
qs.e:
Bill = 2 rooms × 1500 = ₹3,000.
After 12% discount: 3000 × 0.88 = 2,640.
After 5% card discount: 2640 × 0.95 = ₹2,508.
Answer: Rs.2,508

qs.q: Ram sold a plot for Rs.4,00,000 at a 20% loss. For what price should he sell the plot to gain a 5% profit?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Perseverance
qs.e:
Perseverance = continuing steadily despite difficulty or delay. E.g. Her perseverance helped her clear the exam on the third try.
Steadfastness = firm, unwavering persistence, so it matches.
Discipline = self-control/training; tolerance = putting up with something; humbleness = modesty - related virtues but not the same meaning.
Answer: Steadfastness

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. “Just add a bit of cheese to your pasta and Bob’s your uncle!” Reena suggested to me over dinner last night.
o: It becomes easily and quickly achievable
qs.e:
'And Bob's your uncle' means 'and it's done' – something is easily and quickly achieved.
Here, adding a bit of cheese makes the pasta perfect, just like that.
It does not mean changing appearance, ruining everything or changing nothing.
Answer: It becomes easily and quickly achievable

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. When the District Attorney asked the convict about details of the day of the crime, he started beating about the bush.
o: Speaking in a confusing manner without giving a correct answer
qs.e:
'Beating about the bush' means talking around a topic without coming to the point or giving a clear answer.
The convict avoided giving the true details of the crime day.
Being aggressive, blaming others and seeking sympathy are different behaviours.
Answer: Speaking in a confusing manner without giving a correct answer

label: CGL 2022, 5 December 2022, shift 2
src: SSC candidate response sheet, official key marked

qs.q: A & B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A # B means ‘A is the father of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the son B’ A % B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A + B means ‘A is the mother of B’ If A & B # C & D @ E % F + G, then how is D related to G?
qs.e:
A & B: A is B's wife. B # C: B is C's father. C & D: C is D's wife. D @ E: D is E's son. E % F: E is F's husband. F + G: F is G's mother.
E and F are husband and wife; D is E's son and G is F's child.
So D and G are children of the same couple, and D (son) is G's brother.
Answer: Brother

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 729, 243, ?, 27, 9, 3
qs.e:
Each term is the previous divided by 3.
243 ÷ 3 = 81; check 81 ÷ 3 = 27, 27 ÷ 3 = 9, 9 ÷ 3 = 3 ✓.
Answer: 81

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. TMT, ZOB, FQJ, LSR, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: T, Z, F, L, R (+6). 2nd: M, O, Q, S, U (+2). 3rd: T, B, J, R, Z (+8).
So the next cluster is RUZ.
Answer: RUZ

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? WNM, ULO, SJQ, QHS, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: W, U, S, Q, O (−2). 2nd: N, L, J, H, F (−2). 3rd: M, O, Q, S, U (+2).
So the next cluster is OFU.
Answer: OFU

qs.q: If A ÷ B means that A is the mother of B, A – B means that A is the father of B, A + B means that A is the sister of B, then which of the following expression shows that P is the mother of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's mother (÷ = mother, – = father, + = sister).
P ÷ Q + R: P is Q's mother and Q is R's sister → P is R's mother.
P + Q – R makes P a paternal aunt; P – R + Q makes P the father; Q + P – R makes P the father.
Answer: P ÷ Q + R

qs.q: The Right to Freedom of Religion is contained within which Articles of the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
Articles 25 to 28 make up the Right to Freedom of Religion: freedom of conscience (25), managing religious affairs (26), no tax for promoting a religion (27), and freedom from religious instruction in certain institutions (28).
29–30 are cultural and educational rights; 19–22 the right to freedom; 14–18 the right to equality.
Answer: Article 25 to Article 28

qs.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English?
qs.e:
Article 120 says business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English. The presiding officer may let a member who cannot express himself in either use his mother tongue.
Article 210 is the matching rule for State Legislatures; Art 121 restricts discussion in Parliament on the conduct of judges.
Answer: Article 120

qs.q: The age range for the Youth Boxer category is:
qs.e:
In AIBA's age categories, the Youth boxer category covers ages 17-18.
Juniors are 15-16 years, and Elite boxers are 19-40.
Answer: 17 – 18 years

qs.q: In Tennis which of the following scores is a complete set?
qs.e:
A tennis set is won by the first player to win 6 games with a lead of at least 2 games, so 6-4 completes a set.
5-3 and 6-5 are still unfinished, and 6-6 leads to a tie-break (the set then ends 7-6).
Answer: 6-4

qs.q: A dishonest dealer sells a product at 11% loss on cost price, but uses 22% less weight. What is his percentage profit or loss?
qs.e:
Let 1 unit of weight cost ₹1. He charges for 1 unit at 11% loss: SP = 0.89.
He gives only 0.78 unit (22% less), which costs 0.78.
Profit% = (0.89 − 0.78)/0.78 × 100 = 11/78 × 100 ≈ 14.1% gain.
Answer: 14.1% gain

qs.q: A shopkeeper earns 10% on an investment but loses 20% on another investment. If the ratio of the two investments is 2 : 3, then the combined loss percentage is:
qs.e:
Take investments 2 and 3 (any unit).
Gain on first = 10% of 2 = 0.2; loss on second = 20% of 3 = 0.6.
Net loss = 0.4 on total 5, i.e. 0.4/5 × 100 = 8%.
Answer: 8%

qs.q: A tradesman marks his goods 20% above his cost price. If he allows his customer 20% discount on the marked price, how much profit or loss does he make, if any:
qs.e:
Take CP = 100. MP = 120; SP = 120 × 0.8 = 96.
Loss = 4 on 100 = 4%.
Shortcut: equal % up and down always gives a loss of x²/100 = 400/100 = 4%.
Answer: 4% loss

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word Amend.
qs.e:
Amend = make changes to correct or improve something. E.g. Parliament amended the law.
Rectify = put right, correct, so it is the synonym.
Harm, impair and worsen all mean make worse - the opposite idea.
Answer: Rectify

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Impede
qs.e:
Impede = delay or block the progress of something. E.g. Heavy traffic impeded the ambulance.
Hinder means the same - to obstruct.
Intend = plan to do; prompt = cause or encourage (almost the opposite); respite = a short rest or relief.
Answer: Hinder

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The audience was mesmerised by the speech delivered by the vivacious lady.
qs.e:
Vivacious = lively, full of energy and spirit. E.g. The vivacious host kept the party going.
Energetic carries the same lively sense.
Fearless = brave; prosperous = wealthy, successful; friendly = kind and pleasant - none mean lively.
Answer: Energetic

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Mercy
qs.e:
Mercy = kindness or forgiveness shown to someone you could punish. E.g. The king showed mercy to the prisoner.
Clemency = mercy, especially from a judge or ruler, so it matches.
Legacy = something handed down; clarity = clearness; plurality = being many/more than one.
Answer: Clemency

qs.q: Select the idiom that can correctly replace the underlined part of the given sentence. I know she really wants the promotion, but she really hit me below the hand by telling the boss about my personal problems.
qs.e:
The correct idiom is 'hit (someone) below the belt' – to act unfairly or cruelly.
Origin: in boxing, a punch below the belt is against the rules.
Telling the boss about someone's personal problems to win a promotion is unfair.
'Below the books/bottle' and 'hit me the bricks' are not English idioms.
Answer: hit me below the belt

src: SSC candidate response sheet, official key marked

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’ A & B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’ If X @ Y & Z # U & W @ V, then how is U related to V?
qs.e:
X @ Y: X is Y's son. Y & Z: Y is Z's wife. Z # U: Z is U's brother. U & W: U is W's wife. W @ V: W is V's son.
U is the wife of W, and W is V's son.
A son's wife is a daughter-in-law, so U is V's daughter-in-law.
Answer: Daughter-in-law

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 3, 6, 18, 36, 108, ?
Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? BLJS, FOLT, ?, NUPV, RXRW
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: B, F, J, N, R (+4). 2nd: L, O, R, U, X (+3).
3rd: J, L, N, P, R (+2). 4th: S, T, U, V, W (+1).
So the missing cluster is JRNU.
Answer: JRNU

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the father of B, A + B means that A is the mother of B, A – B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the brother of P?
qs.e:
We need Q to be male and P's sibling (× = father, + = mother, – = brother).
P – Q × R: P is Q's brother and Q is R's father, so Q is male → Q is P's brother.
P + Q – R makes P a mother; P – Q + R makes Q a woman (sister); P × R – Q makes P Q's father.
Answer: P – Q × R

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. CABQ, CEJC, CIRO, CMZA, ?
qs.e:
1st letter stays C.
2nd: A, E, I, M (+4) → Q. 3rd: B, J, R, Z (+8) → 26 + 8 = 34 − 26 = 8 = H.
4th: Q, C, O, A (+12) → A(1) + 12 = 13 = M.
So the next cluster is CQHM.
Answer: CQHM

qs.q: Where was the FIH Men’s Indoor Hockey World Cup 2018 organised?
qs.e:
The 2018 FIH Indoor Hockey World Cup (men's and women's) was held in Berlin, Germany, in February 2018.
Austria won the men's title. Leipzig hosted the 2015 edition.
Answer: Berlin, Germany

qs.q: How many fundamental duties are provided in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e:
There are 11 Fundamental Duties in Article 51A.
Ten were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) and the 11th – a parent's duty to provide education to a child aged 6–14 – by the 86th Amendment (2002).
Answer: 11

qs.q: The Winter Olympics - 2026 will be hosted by _______.
qs.e:
The 2026 Winter Olympics are hosted by Italy, jointly in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo.
Italy earlier hosted the Winter Games at Cortina 1956 and Turin 2006; France gets 2030.
Answer: Italy

qs.q: The elections to the Panchayati Raj institutions are conducted by the ________.
qs.e:
Panchayat elections are conducted by the State Election Commission under Article 243K, added by the 73rd Amendment.
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor. The Election Commission of India handles only Parliament, State legislatures, President and Vice-President.
Answer: State election commission

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers three types of discount schemes for buyers. Which of them has the maximum discount percentage? I. Two successive discounts of 10% each. II. Successive discounts of 15% and 5%. III. 20% discount.
qs.e:
Equivalent discount of a and b = a + b − ab/100.
I: 10 + 10 − 1 = 19%. II: 15 + 5 − 0.75 = 19.25%. III: 20%.
The single 20% discount is the largest.
Answer: Only discount scheme III

qs.q: A businessman cheats by using faulty weights, to the tune of 12% each time, when buying and selling material. What is the rise in his profit percentage using faulty weights only?
qs.e:
Cheating by 12% while buying: he gets 112 units for the price of 100 (a 12% gain).
Cheating by 12% while selling: again 12% more value per sale, so the gains compound.
Overall = 1.12 × 1.12 = 1.2544, a rise of 25.44%.
Shortcut: 12 + 12 + (12×12)/100 = 25.44%.
Answer: 25.44%

qs.q: Mr. X has a monthly income of $26,500 and his monthly expenditure is $20,500. The next year, his salary is increased by 12% and expenditure is increased by 6%. His savings increase by how much percent?
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence. He was sacked from his job because of a grave error on his part.
qs.e:
A 'Himalayan blunder' is a very big, serious mistake – as huge as the Himalayas.
It replaces 'a grave error': He was sacked because of a Himalayan blunder.
Raining cats and dogs = heavy rain; minding one's p's and q's = being careful about manners; picking holes = finding faults.
Answer: Himalayan blunder

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence. I have been a vegetarian for a very long time.
qs.e:
'Donkey's years' means a very long time.
Origin: a pun on donkey's ears, which are long.
So: I have been a vegetarian for donkey's years.
Duck in a thunderstorm = looking dejected; die in harness = die while still working; Damocles' sword = an ever-present danger.
Answer: donkey’s years

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tyranny
qs.e:
Tyranny = cruel, unjust rule by one person with absolute power. E.g. The people rose against the king's tyranny.
Autocracy = rule by one person with unlimited power - the closest synonym.
Compassion = sympathy (opposite in spirit); social = relating to society; discordance = disagreement.
Answer: Autocracy

qs.q: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the underlined word. The president's concern for the homeless people was superficial and ended as soon as the media left the event.
qs.e:
Superficial = on the surface only; not deep or sincere. E.g. He has only a superficial knowledge of physics.
The concern ended when the media left, so it was shallow - not genuine or deep.
Derogatory = insulting; regardless = without paying attention; insubstantial = flimsy, lacking solidity (about things, not feelings).
Answer: Shallow

src: SSC candidate response sheet, official key marked

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. QML, PRC, OWT, NBK, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: Q, P, O, N (−1) → M. 2nd: M, R, W, B (+5) → B(2) + 5 = 7 = G.
3rd: L, C, T, K (−9) → K(11) − 9 = 2 = B.
So the next cluster is MGB.
Answer: MGB

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’. A & B means ‘A is the father of B’. A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’. If W & Q # T & Y @ M % K, then how is W related to K?
qs.e:
W & Q: W is Q's father. Q # T: Q is T's sister. T & Y: T is Y's father. Y @ M: Y is M's son. M % K: M is K's mother.
T and M are the parents of Y and K, so T is K's father.
W is the father of Q and T, so W is K's father's father.
Answer: Father’s father

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 97, 131, 165, 199, 233, ?
qs.e:
Each term is 34 more than the one before: 131 − 97 = 165 − 131 = 34.
233 + 34 = 267.
Answer: 267

qs.q: If K ÷ L means that K is the mother of L, K – L means that K is the father of L, K × L means that K is the sister of L, then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal grandmother of R?
qs.e:
Paternal grandmother = father's mother: P mother of Q, and Q father of R.
That is P ÷ Q – R (÷ = mother, – = father).
P ÷ Q × R makes P R's mother; R – Q ÷ P and Q ÷ P – R put P lower in the tree.
Answer: P ÷ Q – R

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? HFK, KHM, ?, QLQ, TNS
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: H, K, N, Q, T (+3). 2nd: F, H, J, L, N (+2). 3rd: K, M, O, Q, S (+2).
So the missing cluster is NJO.
Answer: NJO

qs.q: Which of the following is a right under Article 300A?
qs.e:
Article 300A says no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law. So the right to property is now a constitutional (legal) right.
It was a Fundamental Right (Art 19(1)(f) and 31) until the 44th Amendment, 1978 removed it from Part III.
Answer: Right to property

qs.q: How many times has India hosted the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup (One Day)?
qs.e:
Up to December 2022, India had hosted or co-hosted the men's ODI World Cup three times: 1987, 1996 and 2011.
India later hosted 2023 alone, making it four.
Answer: 3

qs.q: The first match of IPL 2022 was played in_______.
qs.e:
IPL 2022 opened on 26 March 2022 at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, with Chennai Super Kings against Kolkata Knight Riders.
League matches were held in Mumbai and Pune due to COVID-19.
Answer: Mumbai

qs.q: In which year was the Indian Parliamentary Group established?
qs.e:
The Indian Parliamentary Group was set up in 1949, following a motion adopted by the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) in August 1948.
It is an autonomous body of MPs and works as India's national group in the Inter-Parliamentary Union and the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association.
Answer: 1949

qs.q: During the first year, the population of a town increased by 12%.The next year, due to some contagious disease, it decreased by 8%. At the end of the second year, the population was 64,400. Find the population of the town at beginning of the first year.
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In hot waters
o: To be in a hot climate
qs.e:
'In hot water(s)' means in trouble, usually because of something one has done.
Example: He was in hot water for missing the deadline again.
Dipping in hot water and hot climate are literal; 'feel relaxed' is the opposite.
Answer: To be in trouble

qs.q: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the underlined word. No plausible explanation could be found for her disappearance.
qs.e:
Plausible = seeming reasonable and believable. E.g. He gave a plausible excuse for being late.
Credible = believable, so it fits.
Just = fair; legal = allowed by law; useless = of no use - none mean believable.
Answer: Credible

qs.q: Select the idiom from the given options that gives the most appropriate meaning of the highlighted text in the following sentence. The announcement of the new tourism policy of the government has made some people excited or interested.
qs.e:
'To quicken the pulse' means to make someone excited or interested (excitement makes the heart beat faster).
The new tourism policy has quickened the pulse of some people.
Pull out all the stops = make every possible effort; run around in circles = be busy without progress; reach for the moon = aim very high.
Answer: Quicken the pulse
qs.u: made some people excited or interested

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Wrathful
qs.e:
Wrathful = extremely angry. E.g. The wrathful father shouted at the boys.
Furious = full of intense anger - the synonym.
Pleased = happy; amiable = friendly; cordial = warm and polite - all are opposite moods.
Answer: Furious

src: SSC candidate response sheet, official key marked

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? MU, NE, PX, QF, SA, TG, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: M, N, P, Q, S, T — alternately +1, +2, so next is T + 2 = V.
2nd letters in alternate terms: U, X, A (+3 each, wrapping) and E, F, G (+1 each).
The 7th term continues U, X, A: A(1) + 3 = D. So the next cluster is VD.
Answer: VD

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 67, 78, 71, 82, 75, 86, ?

A & B means ‘A is the son of B’ A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A % B means ‘A is the father of B’ A − B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A * B means ‘A is the wife of B’ If C # D @ E % Z & L # M – N * P, then how is E related to L?
qs.e:
C # D: C is D's sister. D @ E: D is E's brother. E % Z: E is Z's father. Z & L: Z is L's son. L # M: L is M's sister. M – N: M is N's daughter. N * P: N is P's wife.
Z's father is E, and Z is also L's son; L is a woman (a sister).
So E and L are Z's parents, and E is L's husband.
Answer: Husband

qs.q: If A – B means that A is the brother of B, A + B means that A is the sister of B, A × B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the brother of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's brother (– = brother, + = sister, × = father).
P – Q + R: P is Q's brother and Q is R's sister → P is R's brother.
P + Q – R makes P a sister; P × Q + R makes P the father; P – Q × R makes P a paternal uncle.
Answer: P – Q + R

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. QRM, PWD, OBU, NGL, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: Q, P, O, N (−1) → M. 2nd: R, W, B, G (+5) → G(7) + 5 = 12 = L.
3rd: M, D, U, L (−9) → L(12) − 9 = 3 = C.
So the next cluster is MLC.
Answer: MLC

qs.q: Black Card given to a badminton player during the game indicates:
qs.e:
In badminton the umpire shows a yellow card for a warning, a red card for a fault, and a black card for disqualification, given by the referee.
The black card means the player is out of the match or event.
Answer: disqualification

qs.q: Article 19 of the Indian Constitution provides for how many types of freedoms?
qs.e:
Article 19(1) now guarantees six freedoms: speech and expression; assembling peacefully; forming associations; moving freely; residing and settling anywhere in India; and practising any profession or trade.
There were originally seven; the freedom to acquire property (19(1)(f)) was removed by the 44th Amendment, 1978.
Answer: 6

qs.q: Which branch of the government is responsible for implementing laws and policies?
qs.e:
The executive (President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers and civil servants) implements laws and policies.
The legislature makes laws and the judiciary interprets them. NITI Aayog is only a policy think-tank.
Answer: Executive

qs.q: Two candidates P and Q contested in an election. 70% of the registered voters are P supporters. If 60% of the P supporters and 30% of the Q supporters are expected to vote for candidate P, then what percentage of the registered voters are expected to vote for candidate P?
qs.e:
Take 100 registered voters: 70 P supporters, 30 Q supporters.
Votes for P = 60% of 70 + 30% of 30 = 42 + 9 = 51.
So 51% of registered voters are expected to vote for P.
Answer: 51%

qs.q: Successive discounts of 18% and 22% are equal to a single discount of ______.
qs.e:
Equivalent of successive discounts a and b = a + b − ab/100.
18 + 22 − (18×22)/100 = 40 − 3.96 = 36.04%.
Answer: 36.04%

qs.q: A man lost 15% by selling a mobile for Rs.4,675. What will be his gain percentage by selling it for Rs.6,050?
qs.e:
Selling at 15% loss: SP = 85% of CP → CP = 4675 ÷ 0.85 = ₹5,500.
Selling at ₹6,050 gives profit 6050 − 5500 = ₹550.
Gain% = 550/5500 × 100 = 10%.
Answer: 10%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The promises made by the old minister were fulfilled.
qs.e:
Old (for people) = having lived many years. E.g. The old man walked with a stick.
Aged means old in years, so it is the synonym.
Contemporary = of the present time; recent = new, lately happened; vernal = of spring, fresh - all suggest newness, the opposite.
Answer: Aged

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The lecture by the French professor seemed Latin and Greek to the young students.
qs.e:
'Latin and Greek' (also 'Greek to me') means something impossible to understand.
The students could not understand the French professor's lecture at all.
Interesting, lucid (clear) and unbiased do not mean unintelligible; 'lucid' is the opposite.
Answer: Incomprehensible

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘consensus’ from the following sentence. The landowner and the tenant mutually came to an agreement for decisive acceptance of its clause.
qs.e:
Consensus = general agreement among people. E.g. The panel reached a consensus on the new rules.
In the sentence, the landowner and tenant 'came to an agreement' - agreement is the synonym.
Decisive = settling something firmly; acceptance = agreeing to receive; mutually = shared by both - none equals consensus.
Answer: Agreement

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence. Some people still feel that they have very little freedom to be innovative in their work.
o: an old head on young shoulders
qs.e:
'Elbow room' means enough space or freedom to act as one wishes.
So: people feel they have little elbow room to be innovative.
An old lady is not an idiom here; an old head on young shoulders = a young person with mature wisdom; to make a pile = to earn a lot of money.
Answer: elbow room
