qs.q: If X × Y means that X is the father of B, X ÷ B means that X is the mother of B, X – Y means that X is the brother of Y then which of the following expression shows that A is the father of C?
qs.e:
(The symbols mean: × = father, ÷ = mother, – = brother.) We need A to be C's father.
A × B – C: A is B's father and B is C's brother → A is C's father.
A × C – B also works directly: A is C's father (and C is B's brother).
A – B × C makes A a paternal uncle; A × B ÷ C makes A a grandfather. The official key takes option 4.
Answer: A × B – C

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 121, 169, 289, ?, 529, 841
qs.e:
The terms are squares of prime numbers: 121 = 11², 169 = 13², 289 = 17², 529 = 23², 841 = 29².
The prime between 17 and 23 is 19, and 19² = 361.
Answer: 361

qs.q: A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A % B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A $ B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’ If L @ M – N $ O % P, then how is L related to P?
qs.e:
L @ M: L is M's son. M – N: M is N's mother. N $ O: N is O's sister. O % P: O is P's brother.
So L, N, O and P are all children of M.
L is male, so L is P's brother.
Answer: Brother

qs.q: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? MDSA, KERC, ?, GGPG, EHOI
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: M, K, I, G, E (−2). 2nd: D, E, F, G, H (+1).
3rd: S, R, Q, P, O (−1). 4th: A, C, E, G, I (+2).
So the missing cluster is IFQE.
Answer: IFQE

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NDRF, NZJT, NVBH, NRTV, ?
qs.e:
1st letter stays N.
2nd: D, Z, V, R (−4) → R(18) − 4 = 14 = N. 3rd: R, J, B, T (−8) → T(20) − 8 = 12 = L.
4th: F, T, H, V (−12) → V(22) − 12 = 10 = J.
So the next cluster is NNLJ.
Answer: NNLJ

qs.q: How many times did India organise the Commonwealth Games?
qs.e:
India has hosted the Commonwealth Games only once: the 2010 (19th) Games in New Delhi.
India finished second in the medal table with 101 medals.
Answer: Once

qs.q: The real executive power is vested in the Council of Ministers with the _____________ as its head.
qs.e:
In India's parliamentary system, the President is only the nominal head. Real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Article 74).
The Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).
Answer: Prime Minister

qs.q: In football, when the ball strikes the frame of the goal or the referee and remains within the goal and touch lines, it is:
qs.e:
Under football's Laws of the Game, the ball stays in play if it rebounds off the goal frame (posts, crossbar) or the referee and remains inside the field.
It is out of play only when it wholly crosses the goal line or touch line, or play is stopped by the referee.
Answer: still in play

qs.q: A shopkeeper has 2220 kg of rice. A part of which he sells at a 20% profit and the rest at a 12% profit. He gains 18% on the whole. The quantity (in kg) sold at a 12% profit is:
qs.e:
Alligation: 20% and 12% mix to give 18%.
Ratio (20%-part) : (12%-part) = (18 − 12) : (20 − 18) = 6 : 2 = 3 : 1.
Quantity at 12% = 1/4 × 2220 = 555 kg.
Answer: 555

qs.q: Piyush sold a guitar to Anuj at 16% gain and Anuj sold it to Mayank at 32% gain. If Mayank paid Rs.3,828 for the guitar, what amount did Piyush pay for the same?
qs.e:
Successive selling: Mayank's price = Piyush's cost × 1.16 × 1.32.
1.16 × 1.32 = 1.5312 → Piyush's cost = 3828 ÷ 1.5312 = ₹2,500.
Check: 2500 → 2900 → 3828.
Answer: Rs.2,500

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On the ball
qs.e:
'On the ball' means alert, quick to understand and react.
Example: You need to be on the ball in a live quiz.
Doing a bad or average job and being lazy are the opposite.
Answer: To be alert

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The essayist’s sole intention was to baffle his readers.
qs.e:
Baffle = confuse completely; leave someone unable to understand. E.g. The riddle baffled the children.
Puzzle means the same.
Influence = affect; scold = rebuke angrily; annoy = irritate - none mean confuse.
Answer: Puzzle

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. When the war breaks out, all the war mongering social media activists become yellow bellies.
qs.e:
A 'yellow belly' is a coward (yellow is traditionally linked with cowardice).
The loud war supporters become cowards once real war breaks out.
Zealots = fanatics; sceptics = doubters; upset stomachs is literal.
Answer: Cowards

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. REV, UXD, XQL, AJT, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: R, U, X, A (+3) → D. 2nd: E, X, Q, J (−7) → J(10) − 7 = 3 = C.
3rd: V, D, L, T (+8) → T(20) + 8 = 28 − 26 = 2 = B.
So the next cluster is DCB.
Answer: DCB

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZUPK, YTOJ, ?, WRMH, VQLG
qs.e:
Every letter moves back by 1.
ZUPK → YTOJ → XSNI → WRMH → VQLG.
So the missing cluster is XSNI.
Answer: XSNI

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 27, 29, ?, 182, 730, 3652
‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the daughter of A’. If D # E # F & G @ H # I, then how is G related to E?
qs.e:
D # E: E is D's daughter. E # F: F is E's daughter. F & G: F is G's mother. G @ H: G is H's husband. H # I: I is H's daughter.
G is male (a husband) and his mother is F, E's daughter.
So G is E's daughter's son.
Answer: Daughter’s son

qs.q: If A + B means that A is the father of B, A –B means that A is the mother of B, A × B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the son of P?
qs.e:
Q must be male and P must be Q's parent.
P – Q × R: P is Q's mother and Q is R's brother → Q is P's son.
P – Q + R also works: P is Q's mother and Q is R's father (male) → Q is P's son.
P – R × Q makes R the brother; Q – P × R makes Q the mother. The official key takes option 4.
Answer: P – Q × R

qs.q: What is the difference in the number of years between the summer and winter Olympic events?
qs.e:
Since 1994 the Summer and Winter Olympics are held in different years, alternating every two years (e.g. Tokyo 2020/21, Beijing 2022, Paris 2024, Milan-Cortina 2026).
Before that, both were held in the same year; each Games still comes every 4 years.
Answer: 2

qs.q: Which of the following countries hosted the 2022 Asian Wresting Championships where Ravi Dahiya became the first Indian freestyle wrestler to win a hat-trick of gold medals?
qs.e:
The 2022 Asian Wrestling Championships were held in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia (April 2022).
Ravi Dahiya won the 57 kg gold there, his third Asian title in a row (2020, 2021, 2022).
Answer: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia

qs.q: When, for the first time, did the Election Commission of India become a multi-member body?
qs.e:
The Election Commission first became a multi-member body on 16 October 1989, when two more Election Commissioners were appointed. They were removed in January 1990.
It has been a three-member body permanently since October 1993.
Answer: 1989

qs.q: The fundamental duty of a parent or guradian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of 6 and ______.
qs.e:
Fundamental Duty 51A(k), added by the 86th Amendment (2002), requires a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child or ward aged 6 to 14.
It matches Article 21A, which gives free and compulsory education to the same age group.
Answer: 14

qs.q: If the price of petrol is increased by 28%, by what percentage should the consumption be decreased by the consumer, if the expenditure on petrol remains unchanged? (Correct to 2 decimal places)
qs.e:
To keep expenditure fixed when price rises by r%, consumption must fall by r/(100 + r) × 100 %.
28/128 × 100 = 21.875% ≈ 21.88%.
Answer: 21.88%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A rolling stone gathers no moss
o: A person who settles for a short time and runs from place to place, enjoying his freedom
A person who does not settle anywhere for a short time, and is always searching for gold
A person who settles for a long time and leads a boring and useless life
A person who does not settle in one place for a long time, does not gain wealth, name or fame
qs.e:
'A rolling stone gathers no moss' means a person who keeps moving from place to place or job to job does not gain wealth, position or reputation.
Image: moss grows only on stones that stay still.
Option 1 praises freedom, option 2 adds 'gold', option 3 talks about settling – only option 4 gives the real sense.
Answer: A person who does not settle in one place for a long time, does not gain wealth, name or fame

qs.q: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. The students have decided to conspire to steal the test papers.
qs.e:
Conspire = secretly plan with others to do something wrong. E.g. They conspired to cheat the bank.
Plot = make a secret plan, so it matches.
Enact = make into law or perform; moderate = make less extreme; assist = help.
Answer: Plot

qs.q: If L × M means that L is the mother of M, L + M means that L is the father of M, L ÷ M means that L is the sister of M, then which of the following expression shows that P is the father of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's father (× = mother, + = father, ÷ = sister).
P + Q ÷ R: P is Q's father and Q is R's sister → P is R's father.
P ÷ R + Q makes P R's sister; Q + P ÷ R makes Q the father; P + Q × R makes P a grandfather.
Answer: P + Q ÷ R

qs.q: A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A * B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A % B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A $ B means ‘A is the son of B’ If P – Q – R * S $ T, then how is P related to T?
qs.e:
P – Q: P is Q's mother. Q – R: Q is R's mother. R * S: R is S's sister. S $ T: S is T's son.
Q is the mother of R and S, and T is S's other parent, so T is Q's husband.
P is Q's mother, i.e. the mother of T's wife → P is T's mother-in-law.
Answer: Mother-in-law

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ACFD, CFHG, ?, GLLM, IONP
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: A, C, E, G, I (+2). 2nd: C, F, I, L, O (+3).
3rd: F, H, J, L, N (+2). 4th: D, G, J, M, P (+3).
So the missing cluster is EIJJ.
Answer: EIJJ

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 5103, 1701, 567, ?, 63, 21
qs.e:
Each term is the previous divided by 3.
5103 ÷ 3 = 1701; 1701 ÷ 3 = 567; 567 ÷ 3 = 189.
Check: 189 ÷ 3 = 63 and 63 ÷ 3 = 21 ✓.
Answer: 189

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ABCD, FVJV, KPQN, PJXF, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: A, F, K, P (+5) → U. 2nd: B, V, P, J (−6) → J(10) − 6 = 4 = D.
3rd: C, J, Q, X (+7) → 24 + 7 = 31 − 26 = 5 = E. 4th: D, V, N, F (−8) → 6 − 8 + 26 = 24 = X.
So the next cluster is UDEX.
Answer: UDEX

qs.q: The Constitution of India is a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic with a ______________ system of government.
qs.e:
India has a parliamentary system of government: the executive (Council of Ministers) comes from the legislature and is responsible to the Lok Sabha.
This Westminster model was taken from Britain. India is not presidential (like the USA) or monarchical, and has a federal structure with unitary features.
Answer: parliamentary

qs.q: The executive power of the Union is vested in the:
o: Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister
Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
qs.e:
Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President; it is exercised directly or through subordinate officers.
In practice the President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the PM (Art 74). That is why the President is the formal head, while the PM holds real power.
Answer: President

qs.q: Which of the following countries hosted the first edition of the Summer Youth Olympic Games in 2010?
qs.e:
The first Summer Youth Olympic Games were held in Singapore in 2010.
Nanjing (China) hosted 2014, Buenos Aires (Argentina) 2018, and Dakar (Senegal) is set for 2026.
Answer: Singapore

qs.q: The height of stumps in cricket is ____.
qs.e:
By the Laws of Cricket, the stumps are 28 inches (71.1 cm) high above the ground, and the full wicket is 9 inches wide.
Answer: 28 inches

qs.q: Three-fourth of a consignment was sold at a profit of 8% and the rest at a loss of 4%. If there was an overall profit of Rs.600, then find the value of the consignment.
A man loses 20% of his money and after spending 85% of the remainder, he is left with Rs.120. How much did he have at first?
qs.e:
Let the money be x. After losing 20%: 0.8x. He spends 85% of this, leaving 15%.
0.15 × 0.8x = 0.12x = 120 → x = 1000.
Answer: Rs.1,000

qs.q: Rohan sold goods to Ankith worth Rs.55,000 at 15% trade discount. How much money did Ankith pay to Rohan?
qs.e:
Trade discount 15% is deducted from the list price.
Amount paid = 55,000 × 0.85 = ₹46,750.
Answer: Rs.46,750

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. The young boy was born with a silver spoon in his mouth.
o: born with a spoon stuck in his mouth
born with a spoon that was not of gold
born to not so rich parents
qs.e:
'Born with a silver spoon in one's mouth' means born into a rich, privileged family.
Origin: rich godparents gave silver spoons as christening gifts.
Options 1 and 3 are literal; option 4 is the opposite.
Answer: born to riches and luxury
qs.u: born with a silver spoon in his mouth

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fatigue
qs.e:
Fatigue = extreme tiredness after effort. E.g. Fatigue set in after the long march.
Tiredness is the direct synonym.
Feebleness = weakness (lasting lack of strength, not exhaustion); loaf = idle about / a loaf of bread; effort = exertion (the cause, not the state).
Answer: Tiredness

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence. The world needs a global leader who can hold out a gesture of peace
qs.e:
'An olive branch' is an offer or gesture of peace.
Origin: the olive branch has been a peace symbol since ancient Greece and the Bible's flood story.
So: a leader who can hold out an olive branch.
Mother wit = common sense; halcyon days = happy, peaceful past times; a grass widow = a woman whose husband is often away.
Answer: an olive branch

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Belief
qs.e:
Belief = trust or confidence that something is true. E.g. He has a strong belief in hard work.
Faith = firm trust or belief, so it is the synonym.
Promise = an assurance; system = an organised set of parts; religion = a particular set of faith and worship (narrower).
Answer: Faith

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Inherent
qs.e:
Inherent = existing as a natural, permanent part of something. E.g. Risk is inherent in any business.
Inborn = present from birth, natural - the synonym.
Increase = growth; superficial = on the surface only (opposite); conclusion = the end or a judgement.
Answer: Inborn

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NTS, JZF, FFS, BLF, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: N, J, F, B (−4) → 2 − 4 + 26 = 24 = X. 2nd: T, Z, F, L (+6) → L(12) + 6 = 18 = R.
3rd letters alternate S, F, S, F (+13 each), so next is S.
So the next cluster is XRS.
Answer: XRS

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AZBY, BYCX, CXDW, ?, EVFU
qs.e:
Each cluster pairs a letter from the front with one from the back of the alphabet.
1st and 3rd letters move +1 (A, B, C, D, E and B, C, D, E, F); 2nd and 4th move −1 (Z, Y, X, W, V and Y, X, W, V, U).
So the missing cluster is DWEV.
Answer: DWEV

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 480, 240, 120, 60, 30, ?
qs.e:
Each term is half of the previous.
480 ÷ 2 = 240 … 60 ÷ 2 = 30.
Next: 30 ÷ 2 = 15.
Answer: 15

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the brother of B, A ÷ B means that A is the sister of B, A + B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the sister of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's sister (× = brother, ÷ = sister, + = father).
P ÷ Q × R: P is Q's sister and Q is R's brother → P, Q, R are siblings and P is R's sister.
P + Q × R makes P the father; P × Q ÷ R makes P a brother; P ÷ Q + R makes P a paternal aunt.
Answer: P ÷ Q × R

qs.q: A $ B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A # B means ‘A is the father of B’ A * B means ‘A is the mother of B’ If X @ Y $ J * M, then how is X related to M?
qs.e:
X @ Y: X is Y's daughter. Y $ J: Y is J's husband. J * M: J is M's mother.
Y and J are a couple; X is their daughter and M is their child.
So X (female) is M's sister.
Answer: Sister

qs.q: Which of the following countries will be hosting the first edition of ICC Women's Under-19 Cricket World Cup in 2023?
qs.e:
The first ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup was held in South Africa in January 2023.
India, led by Shafali Verma, won it by beating England in the final at Potchefstroom.
Answer: South Africa

qs.q: What is the minimum quorum required in the Lok Sabha so that it can transact any business?
o: One-tenth of the total number of Members of the House
One-fourth of the total number of Members of the House
One-third of the total number of Members of the House
One-fifth of the total number of Members of the House
qs.e:
Article 100(3) fixes the quorum of either House of Parliament at one-tenth of the total number of members, including the presiding officer.
So in the Lok Sabha (543 members) at least 55 must be present; if not, the Speaker adjourns or suspends the sitting.
Answer: One-tenth of the total number of Members of the House

qs.q: In which of the following Olympic games did India NOT win Gold?
qs.e:
India won Olympic hockey gold in 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964 and 1980.
At Rome 1960 India lost the final 0-1 to Pakistan and took silver, ending a run of six straight golds.
Answer: 1960

qs.q: In which of the following years was the voting age reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
qs.e:
The 61st Amendment Act, passed in 1988, lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years by amending Article 326.
It came into force in March 1989 under PM Rajiv Gandhi, so 1989 is the tempting wrong choice.
Answer: 1988

qs.q: The initial profit percentage on the sale of an item was 55%.If the cost price of the item went up by 24% but the selling price remained the same, what would be the new profit percentage?
qs.e:
Take CP = 100, SP = 155.
New CP = 124, SP unchanged at 155.
Profit = 31; profit% = 31/124 × 100 = 25%.
Answer: 25%

qs.q: A mask manufacturing company manufactured ‘X’ number of masks in 2018. It increased its manufacturing capacity by 30% in 2019 and further increased its manufacturing by 15% in 2020. In 2021, due to the machinery breakdown, its manufacturing declined by 40%. What is the value of ‘X’ if it manufactured 179400 masks in 2021?

In a shop, a discount of 5 percent is provided, and if the total payable amount after discount is more than ₹2,000, then an additional discount of 10 percent is provided. Determine the final amount to be paid (in ₹) by a customer, if he buys five products each of price ₹500.
qs.e:
Total price = 5 × 500 = ₹2,500.
After 5% discount: 2500 × 0.95 = 2,375, which is more than 2,000.
Additional 10%: 2375 × 0.90 = ₹2,137.5.
Answer: ₹2,137.5

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The next move of the opponent was anticipated by the team.
qs.e:
Anticipate = expect or foresee something before it happens. E.g. We anticipated heavy traffic and left early.
Predicted = said in advance what would happen, so it fits.
Forgotten = not remembered; suspected = doubted/thought guilty; dreaded = feared - not the same as foreseeing.
Answer: Predicted

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. The way Sheetal imparts knowledge to her students is really praiseworthy.
qs.e:
Impart = pass on information or knowledge. E.g. A good teacher imparts values along with facts.
Transmits = passes on from one to another - the synonym.
Discloses and exposes = reveal something hidden; admits = confesses or lets in - none mean pass on knowledge.
Answer: transmits

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Nobody in the conference seemed to believe the cock and bull story about such a major movie star.
qs.e:
A 'cock and bull story' is an absurd, exaggerated or made-up story.
Nobody believed such a false story about the movie star.
Factual is the opposite; interesting and secretive miss the sense of falsehood.
Answer: Wildly exaggerated or falsified story

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed words to fill in the blank. The lights ________ (lighting up) the artwork on the walls of the museum were looking beautiful.
qs.e:
Lighting up = giving light to something. E.g. Lamps illuminated the stage.
Illuminating means exactly that, so it fills the blank.
Enlightening = giving understanding/knowledge (figurative); trafficking = illegal trading; mesmerising = fascinating.
Answer: illuminating

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. The game is now in full swing.
qs.e:
'In full swing' means at the height of activity – very active and lively.
Example: By 10 p.m. the party was in full swing.
Passive and uninteresting are opposite; 'playing on swings' is literal.
Answer: very active

label: CGL 2022, 7 December 2022, shift 2
src: SSC candidate response sheet, official key marked

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NMTS, SGAK, XAHC, CUOU, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: N, S, X, C (+5) → H. 2nd: M, G, A, U (−6) → U(21) − 6 = 15 = O.
3rd: T, A, H, O (+7) → O(15) + 7 = 22 = V. 4th: S, K, C, U (−8) → U(21) − 8 = 13 = M.
So the next cluster is HOVM.
Answer: HOVM

qs.q: If A ÷ B means that A is the father of B, A – B means that A is the mother of B, A + B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the mother of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's mother (– = mother, ÷ = father, + = brother).
P – Q + R: P is Q's mother and Q is R's brother → P is R's mother.
Q – P + R makes P R's brother; P – Q ÷ R makes P a grandmother; R + P – Q makes P Q's mother.
Answer: P – Q + R

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZYWT, XWUR, VUSP, ?, RQOL
qs.e:
Every letter moves back by 2.
1st: Z, X, V, T, R. 2nd: Y, W, U, S, Q. 3rd: W, U, S, Q, O. 4th: T, R, P, N, L.
So the missing cluster is TSQN.
Answer: TSQN

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 286, 192, 263, 176, 240, 160, 217, 144, ?
qs.e:
Split into two series.
Odd terms: 286, 263, 240, 217 — each 23 less. Even terms: 192, 176, 160, 144 — each 16 less.
The missing term is an odd-position term: 217 − 23 = 194.
Answer: 194

qs.q: ‘A ∞ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. ‘A * B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘B is the father of A’. ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the wife of A’. If V ∞ U @ W # Y * Z, then how is V related to Z?
qs.e:
V ∞ U: V is U's sister. U @ W: W is U's father. W # Y: Y is W's wife. Y * Z: Y is Z's mother.
W and Y are a couple, U (and so V) are W's children, and Z is Y's child.
So V and Z are siblings and V is Z's sister.
Answer: Sister

qs.q: The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to Indian Constitution in which year?
qs.e:
The 11th Fundamental Duty – 51A(k), a parent's or guardian's duty to provide education to a child aged 6–14 – was added by the 86th Amendment Act in 2002.
The first ten duties date from the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
Answer: 2002

qs.q: In India the residuary powers to legislate any matter that is NOT mentioned in the three federal lists lies with the _____________.
qs.e:
Under Article 248 and Entry 97 of the Union List, residuary powers (matters not in any of the three lists) belong to Parliament, the Union legislature.
This follows the Canadian model; in the USA and Australia, residuary powers lie with the states.
Answer: union legislature

qs.q: 'Samvidhan Divas', is celebrated on ________.
qs.e:
Samvidhan Divas (Constitution Day) is celebrated on 26 November. It marks the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution.
It has been observed since 2015, Dr Ambedkar's 125th birth anniversary year. 26 January is Republic Day, when the Constitution came into force.
Answer: 26th November

qs.q: The first edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games was held at __________.
qs.e:
The first Commonwealth Youth Games were held in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 2000.
Later editions: Bendigo 2004, Pune 2008, Isle of Man 2011, Samoa 2015, Bahamas 2017.
Answer: Edinburgh

qs.q: Which of the following strokes in swimming does NOT start with a dive into the pool from outside?
qs.e:
Backstroke is the only competitive stroke that starts in the water: swimmers hold the starting grips facing the wall and push off backward.
Butterfly, breaststroke and freestyle races start with a dive from the starting block.
Answer: Backstroke

qs.q: A discount of 20% is given for the purchase of two books by a bookseller and a discount of 25% is offered if a customer buys more than two books. A 10% discount is being offered to all the customers on purchase of one book. An additional 5% discount will be given to students. Sohan, a student of M.Com. in college, bought a book for Rs.513. What was the marked price of the book?
qs.e:
Buying one book: 10% discount, plus 5% more for a student.
Price paid = MP × 0.90 × 0.95 = 0.855 MP.
MP = 513 ÷ 0.855 = ₹600.
Answer: Rs.600

qs.q: 20% of the inhabitants of a village having died of malaria, a panic set in, during which 30% of the remaining inhabitants left the village. The population was then reduced to 12,000. What was the number of inhabitants initially (Consider integral part only)
qs.e:
Let the initial population be P. After 20% die: 0.8P; after 30% of the rest leave: 0.7 × 0.8P = 0.56P.
0.56P = 12000 → P = 21428.57…
Integral part = 21428.
Answer: 21428

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The MD of the company let the cat out of the bag by telling her secretary, who got the much coveted promotion.
o: To allow a secret to be known, usually without intending to
qs.e:
'To let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret, usually by accident.
Origin: a market trick of selling a cat in a bag as a piglet; opening the bag revealed the cheat.
The MD revealed who got the promotion.
Confessing, inventing stories and confiding secretly do not match 'revealing accidentally'.
Answer: To allow a secret to be known, usually without intending to
qs.u: let the cat out of the bag

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Take something at face value
o: Accept something as it looks without thinking about whether it might, in fact, not be quite what it appears
According to the appearance of something
Not laugh or change your expression even though you want to laugh
Show that you do not like something by making an unpleasant expression
qs.e:
'To take something at face value' means to accept it as it appears without questioning whether it is really true.
Origin: the value printed on a coin or note.
Example: Don't take his promises at face value.
Option 2 is incomplete, option 3 is 'keep a straight face', option 4 is 'make a face'.
Answer: Accept something as it looks without thinking about whether it might, in fact, not be quite what it appears

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’. A & B means ‘A is the father of B’. A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’. If W # Q @ T & Y @ M % K % L, then how is K related to W?
qs.e:
W # Q: W is Q's brother. Q @ T: Q is T's son. T & Y: T is Y's father. Y @ M: Y is M's son. M % K: M is K's mother. K % L: K is L's mother.
T and M are the parents of Q, Y and K; W is Q's brother, so W is their child too.
K is female (mother of L), so K is W's sister.
Answer: Sister

qs.q: If A – B means that A is the father of B, A + B means that A is the mother of B, A × B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the brother of P?
qs.e:
We need Q male and a sibling of P (– = father, + = mother, × = brother).
P × Q – R: P is Q's brother and Q is R's father, so Q is male → Q is P's brother.
Q × P – R also works directly: Q is P's brother.
P × Q + R makes Q a mother (sister); R + P × Q is about R being a mother. The official key takes option 1.
Answer: P × Q – R

qs.q: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? XDNC, VGOE, ?, RMQI, PPRK
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: X, V, T, R, P (−2). 2nd: D, G, J, M, P (+3).
3rd: N, O, P, Q, R (+1). 4th: C, E, G, I, K (+2).
So the missing cluster is TJPG.
Answer: TJPG

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 7, 21, 63, 189, 567, ?
qs.e:
Each term is three times the previous.
7 × 3 = 21, 21 × 3 = 63 … 189 × 3 = 567.
Next: 567 × 3 = 1701.
Answer: 1701

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NTRQ, GOIF, ZJZU, SEQJ, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves back by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: N, G, Z, S (−7) → S(19) − 7 = 12 = L. 2nd: T, O, J, E (−5) → 5 − 5 = 0 → Z.
3rd: R, I, Z, Q (−9) → Q(17) − 9 = 8 = H. 4th: Q, F, U, J (−11) → 10 − 11 + 26 = 25 = Y.
So the next cluster is LZHY.
Answer: LZHY

qs.q: Which of the following bills can be initiated only in the Lok Sabha?
qs.e:
Under Article 109, a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the President's recommendation.
Government bills, private members' bills and Constitution Amendment Bills can be introduced in either House.
Answer: Money bill

qs.q: Who was Player of the Match in the final of U-19 World Cup cricket,2022?
qs.e:
In the 2022 U-19 World Cup final at Antigua, India beat England; all-rounder Raj Bawa was Player of the Match for 5/31 and a useful 35 with the bat.
It was India's record fifth U-19 title, under captain Yash Dhull.
Answer: Raj Bawa

qs.q: In hockey, what is the meaning of the signal if the umpire points both arms horizontally towards the goal?
qs.e:
In field hockey, the umpire signals a penalty corner by pointing both arms horizontally towards the goal.
One arm pointing to the penalty spot means a penalty stroke; both arms pointing towards the centre means a goal.
Answer: Penalty corner

qs.q: In which of the following years was the Citizenship Act passed by the Indian Parliament?
qs.e:
Parliament passed the Citizenship Act in 1955. It sets out how Indian citizenship is acquired (birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory) and lost.
The Constitution (Articles 5–11) covered only citizenship at its start in 1950; Article 11 left the rest to Parliament.
Answer: 1955

qs.q: A shopkeeper bought a cycle for ₹1,200 and sold it for ₹1,500. Find his profit/loss percentage.
What will be the cost price of the goods if a shopkeeper allows a discount of 10% on the marked price of Rs.100 and gains 8%(rounded off to the nearest integer)?
Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom. Turn over a new leaf
qs.e:
'To turn over a new leaf' means to make a fresh start, usually by improving one's behaviour.
'Leaf' here is a page of a book: turning to a clean page.
Example: After the warning he turned over a new leaf and came on time every day.
Stopping, planting trees and taking a break are wrong.
Answer: To begin again

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. A fair-weather friend can never be trusted in the times of exigency.
qs.e:
A 'fair-weather friend' is a selfish friend who is with you only in good times and disappears in difficulty.
That is why such a friend cannot be trusted in an emergency (exigency).
A close friend is the opposite; a pen friend and an old acquaintance are unrelated.
Answer: A selfish friend

qs.q: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the underlined word. He gave a concise explanation of the company’s retirement plan.
qs.e:
Concise = giving much information in few words; brief. E.g. Write a concise summary.
Terse = brief and to the point, so it is the synonym.
Clear = easy to understand (not necessarily short); verbose = using too many words (antonym); sharp = keen or harsh.
Answer: Terse

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 17, 34, 51, ?, 85, 102
qs.e:
The terms are multiples of 17: 17 × 1, 17 × 2, 17 × 3, …
The 4th term is 17 × 4 = 68; check 17 × 5 = 85 ✓.
Answer: 68

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. MOR, SXE, YGR, EPE, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: M, S, Y, E (+6) → E(5) + 6 = 11 = K. 2nd: O, X, G, P (+9) → P(16) + 9 = 25 = Y.
3rd letters alternate R, E, R, E (+13 each), so next is R.
So the next cluster is KYR.
Answer: KYR

qs.q: A + B means ‘A is the father of B’ A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A * B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A % B means ‘A is the husband of B’ If A % B – C + D * E, then how is A related to E?
qs.e:
A % B: A is B's husband. B – C: B is C's mother. C + D: C is D's father. D * E: D is E's sister.
A is C's father; C is the father of D and E.
So A is E's father's father.
Answer: Father’s father

qs.q: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the letter series? J, D, X, R, L, ?
qs.e:
Letter positions: J = 10, D = 4, X = 24, R = 18, L = 12.
Each letter is 6 back (wrapping: 4 − 6 + 26 = 24).
12 − 6 = 6 = F.
Answer: F

qs.q: If A + B means that A is the father of B, A × B means that A is the mother of B, A – B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal grandmother of R?
qs.e:
Paternal grandmother = father's mother: P mother of Q, and Q father of R.
That is P × Q + R (× = mother, + = father).
Q × P + R makes Q the grandmother; P × Q – R makes P R's mother; P + R × Q makes P R's father.
Answer: P × Q + R

qs.q: Which of the following countries was the host of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, 2021?
qs.e:
The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021 was hosted by India (BCCI) but played in the UAE and Oman because of COVID-19.
Australia won, beating New Zealand in the final at Dubai.
Answer: UAE and Oman

qs.q: Which of the following sports was initially known as Poona?
qs.e:
Badminton was earlier called 'Poona' (Poonah), after the city of Pune where British officers played it in the 1860s-70s.
The name 'badminton' came from Badminton House, England, where the game became popular.
Answer: Badminton

qs.q: Every law enacted by the government has to be in conformity with the ________________.
qs.e:
The Constitution is the supreme law. Every law must conform to it, and courts can strike down any law that goes against it (judicial review, Article 13).
Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and the Preamble are all parts of the Constitution, so "Constitution" is the complete answer.
Answer: Constitution

qs.q: Three candidates were participating in an election. The person at third place got 20% of the total votes while the difference between the votes of the winner and the first runner up was 20% of the total votes. If the difference between the votes of the first runner up and the second runner up was 37,000, how many votes did the winner receive?
qs.e:
Third place = 20%, so winner + runner-up = 80% and winner − runner-up = 20%.
Winner = 50%, runner-up = 30% of total votes.
Runner-up − third = 30% − 20% = 10% = 37,000 → total = 3,70,000.
Winner = 50% of 3,70,000 = 1,85,000.
Answer: 1,85,000

qs.q: Ramesh claims that he is selling onions at Rs.36 per kg, which costs him Rs.40 per kg, but he gives 800 grams instead of 1 kg. Find Ramesh’s percentage gain or loss.
qs.e:
He gets ₹36 for 800 g.
Cost of 800 g = 0.8 × 40 = ₹32.
Gain = 4; gain% = 4/32 × 100 = 12.5%.
Answer: Gain 12.5%

qs.q: At a Christmas sale, all the goods in a shop are on sale at 30% discount. If Jasmine buys a skirt marked at ₹800, how much would she need to pay?
qs.e:
Price paid = 70% of 800 = ₹560.
Answer: ₹560

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Never teach your children to flout the rules and regulations of their educational institution.
qs.e:
Flout = openly disregard or show scorn for a rule. E.g. He flouted the traffic rules.
Mock = treat with scorn, ridicule - the closest synonym.
Monitor = watch over; revere = respect deeply (antonym); divulge = reveal a secret.
Answer: Mock

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘obscene’ from the following sentence. Vijay was suspended from duty because he gave dirty and prejudiced remarks to his female colleagues in the office.
qs.e:
Obscene = offensive, indecent, morally disgusting. E.g. The film was banned for obscene scenes.
In the sentence, 'dirty' remarks means indecent ones - the synonym.
Suspended = temporarily removed; prejudice = unfair bias; colleagues = co-workers.
Answer: Dirty

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. PMRF, PDZV, PUHL, PLPB, ?
qs.e:
1st letter stays P.
2nd: M, D, U, L (−9) → L(12) − 9 = 3 = C. 3rd: R, Z, H, P (+8) → P(16) + 8 = 24 = X.
4th: F, V, L, B (−10) → B(2) − 10 + 26 = 18 = R.
So the next cluster is PCXR.
Answer: PCXR

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 10, 15, 25, 45, 85, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 5, 10, 20, 40 — each doubles.
The next difference is 80.
85 + 80 = 165.
Answer: 165

qs.q: If L × M means that L is the mother of M, L – M means that L is the father of M, L ÷ M means that L is the sister of M, then which of the following expression shows that R is the brother of P?
qs.e:
We need R male and P's sibling (× = mother, – = father, ÷ = sister).
P ÷ R – Q: P is R's sister and R is Q's father, so R is male → R is P's brother.
P × R – Q makes P R's mother; P ÷ Q – R makes Q R's father; P ÷ R × Q makes R a mother (P's sister).
Answer: P ÷ R – Q

qs.q: A & B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A # B means ‘A is the father of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the son B’ A % B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A + B means ‘A is the mother of B’ If A & B # C & D @ E % F + G, then how is A related to D?
qs.e:
A & B: A is B's wife. B # C: B is C's father. C & D: C is D's wife. D @ E: D is E's son. (E % F, F + G are not needed.)
A is the wife of C's father, so A is C's mother.
C is D's wife, so A is the mother of D's wife → D's mother-in-law.
Answer: Mother-in-law

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CLPM, FNQN, ?, LRSP, OTTQ
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: C, F, I, L, O (+3). 2nd: L, N, P, R, T (+2).
3rd: P, Q, R, S, T (+1). 4th: M, N, O, P, Q (+1).
So the missing cluster is IPRO.
Answer: IPRO

qs.q: Under the Constitution of India, the Constitutional Head of the Executive of the Union is the _________.
qs.e:
Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President, so the President is the constitutional (nominal) head of the executive.
The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers and is the real executive (Article 74).
Answer: President

qs.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the recognition of the right to education as a Fundamental Right?
qs.e:
Article 21A, added by the 86th Amendment (2002), makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 a Fundamental Right.
It is put into effect by the RTE Act, 2009. Article 300A is the right to property; Art 20 – protection in respect of conviction; Art 33 – Parliament can modify rights for the armed forces.
Answer: Article 21 A

qs.q: The World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2022 was held in_______.
qs.e:
The World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2022 (Fazza) was held in Dubai, UAE, in February-March 2022, with Indian para athletes winning several medals.
Answer: Dubai

qs.q: Which of the following players is associated with badminton?
qs.e:
Kidambi Srikanth is an Indian badminton player who became World No. 1 in 2018 and won silver at the 2021 World Championships.
Sankalp Gupta plays chess; Monica Batra and Archana Kamat are not badminton players (Archana Kamat plays table tennis).
Answer: K Srikanth

qs.q: A dealer marks his goods at 15% above the cost price and allows a discount of 5% for cash payment. His profit percentage is:
A shopkeeper advertises for selling cloth at 7% loss. However, by using a false scale of length 1 metre he actually gains 24%. What will be the actual length he uses instead of 1 metre ?
qs.e:
At 7% loss he charges 0.93 × cost of 1 m but gives only L metres.
0.93/L = 1.24, so L = 0.93/1.24 = 0.75 m = 75 cm.
Answer: 75 cm

qs.q: In an election between two candidates, a candidate who gets 76 % of the total votes polled is elected by a majority of 1480 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (Consider integral part only)
qs.e:
Winner 76%, loser 24% → majority = 52% of votes polled.
52% = 1480 → total = 1480 × 100/52 = 2846.15…
Integral part = 2846.
Answer: 2846

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cudgel one’s brain
qs.e:
'To cudgel one's brain(s)' means to think very hard, especially to remember or solve something.
A cudgel is a heavy stick – beating one's brain for an answer.
Example: I cudgelled my brain but could not recall her name.
'Not to think' is the opposite; 'overthink' adds worry; a debate is unrelated.
Answer: To think hard

qs.q: A & B means ‘A is the son of B’ A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A % B means ‘A is the father of B’ A − B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A * B means ‘A is the wife of B’ If C # D @ E % Z & L # M – N * P, then how is Z related to N?
qs.e:
Z & L: Z is L's son. L # M: L is M's sister. M − N: M is N's daughter. N * P: N is P's wife.
L is M's sister, so L is also N's daughter.
Z is the son of N's daughter, so Z is N's grandson.
Answer: Grandson

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 69, 70, 73, 78, 85, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 1, 3, 5, 7 — consecutive odd numbers.
The next difference is 9.
85 + 9 = 94.
Answer: 94

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the father of B, A + B means that A is the mother of B, A ÷ B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that A is the paternal uncle of C?
qs.e:
A paternal uncle is the father's brother: A brother of B, and B father of C.
That is A ÷ B × C (÷ = brother, × = father).
A ÷ C + B makes A C's brother; A ÷ B + C makes A a maternal uncle; A + B ÷ C makes A C's mother.
Answer: A ÷ B × C

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. TMTQ, WGCE, ZALS, CUUG, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: T, W, Z, C (+3) → F. 2nd: M, G, A, U (−6) → U(21) − 6 = 15 = O.
3rd: T, C, L, U (+9) → 21 + 9 = 30 − 26 = 4 = D. 4th: Q, E, S, G (−12) → 7 − 12 + 26 = 21 = U.
So the next cluster is FODU.
Answer: FODU

qs.q: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? Q, O, M, K, I, G, ?
qs.e:
Letter positions: Q = 17, O = 15, M = 13, K = 11, I = 9, G = 7 — each 2 back.
7 − 2 = 5 = E.
Answer: E

qs.q: The Basketball centre line is part of the:
qs.e:
Under FIBA rules, a team's backcourt includes its own basket, the backboard and the court up to and including the centre line.
So the centre line is part of the backcourt; the frontcourt starts beyond it.
Answer: back court

qs.q: Which of the following can alter the boundary of a state or change its name?
qs.e:
Under Article 3, Parliament can by law form new States, alter the area or boundaries of a State, or change its name.
The bill needs the President's recommendation, and the State legislature's views are sought but are not binding. This shows India is an "indestructible union of destructible states".
Answer: Parliament

qs.q: FIFA U-19 Women's World Cup 2022 will be organised by ______.
qs.e:
India hosted the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in October 2022 (the question says U-19, but there is no such event; the 2022 youth women's World Cup held in India is meant).
Matches were played at Bhubaneswar, Goa and Navi Mumbai, and Spain won.
Answer: India

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with amendment in the Constitution?
qs.e:
Article 368 (Part XX) gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and lays down the procedure.
Others: Art 355 – Union's duty to protect States; Art 360 – financial emergency; Art 365 – effect of failing to follow Union directions.
Answer: Article 368

qs.q: A shopkeeper listed the marked price of a chair at a certain amount. If the shopkeeper declares a 15% discount and sold it at Rs.1,445, then what is the marked price?
A person having bought goods for Rs.400 sells half of it at a gain of 5%. At what gain percentage must he sell the remainder, so as to gain 25% on the whole?
qs.e:
Total cost ₹400; a 25% gain on the whole means total selling price = ₹500.
First half (cost ₹200) sold at 5% gain → ₹210.
The other half must fetch 500 − 210 = ₹290 on a cost of ₹200 → gain = 90/200 × 100 = 45%.
Answer: 45%

qs.q: A and B invested their money in a business in the ratio of 9 : 5. If 10% of the total profit goes for charity and A’s share is Rs.29,840, what is the total profit (in Rs., to the nearest integer)?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. My father took a moment to ponder before signing the deeds of our ancestral home.
qs.e:
Ponder = think about something carefully. E.g. She pondered the offer for a week.
Contemplate = think deeply about, so it fits.
Hesitate = pause from doubt (not the same as thinking it over); sigh = breathe out heavily; brief = short / to inform.
Answer: Contemplate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I bought some extra copies from the stationery shop. These may come in handy during exams.
qs.e:
'To come in handy' means to be useful when needed.
The extra copies may prove useful during exams.
Causing trouble, being sold and bringing luck are not the meaning.
Answer: Be useful

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Play it by ear
o: To do something without special preparation
qs.e:
'Play it by ear' means to act according to the situation without planning in advance.
Origin: a musician playing a tune by hearing it, without written notes.
Example: We have no fixed plan for Sunday; let's play it by ear.
To plan is the opposite; listening carefully and improving are wrong.
Answer: To do something without special preparation

qs.q: F + M means ‘F is the husband of M’ F ÷ M means ‘F is the daughter of M’ F − M means ‘F is the father of M’ F × M means ‘F is the mother of M’ If U + V × K – B, then how is U related to B?
qs.e:
U + V: U is V's husband. V × K: V is K's mother. K – B: K is B's father.
U is the husband of K's mother, so U is K's father.
K is B's father, so U is B's father's father → paternal grandfather.
Answer: Paternal grandfather

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 37, 39, ?, 242, 970, 4852
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? EGJM, GFLN, IENO, ?, MCRQ
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: E, G, I, K, M (+2). 2nd: G, F, E, D, C (−1).
3rd: J, L, N, P, R (+2). 4th: M, N, O, P, Q (+1).
So the missing cluster is KDPP.
Answer: KDPP

qs.q: If A ÷ B means that A is the brother of B, A × B means that A is the sister of B, A – B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the father of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's father (– = father, × = sister, ÷ = brother).
P – Q × R: P is Q's father and Q is R's sister → P is R's father.
P – Q ÷ R also works: P is Q's father and Q is R's brother → P is R's father.
P × Q – R makes P a paternal aunt; P ÷ Q × P is not a valid chain. The official key takes option 1.
Answer: P – Q × R

qs.q: The ICC Women’s cricket World Cup 2022 was held in _________.
qs.e:
The ICC Women's Cricket World Cup 2022 was held in New Zealand (March-April 2022).
Australia won its seventh title, beating England in the final at Christchurch.
Answer: New Zealand

qs.q: The 15th Men’s FIH hockey World Cup will be held in the year ________.
qs.e:
The 15th FIH Men's Hockey World Cup was held in January 2023 at Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, Odisha.
Germany won; the 14th edition (2018) was also in Bhubaneswar.
Answer: 2023

qs.q: Fundamental Rights are mentioned in which part of the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Articles 12–35), called the Magna Carta of India.
Part IV – Directive Principles; Part VI – the States; Part IX – Panchayats.
Answer: Part III

qs.q: The Council of Ministers shall not exceed ___% of the total number of members of the Assembly of States.
qs.e:
The 91st Amendment (2003) caps the total number of ministers, including the PM, at 15% of the total members of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) under Article 75(1A). Article 164(1A) applies the same 15% to State Assemblies.
The question says "Assembly of States", but the intended rule is clearly the 15% cap.
Answer: 15

qs.q: In the first year the population of a town decreased by 5% due to the Corona virus first wave. Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The wrestler retaliated the blow that he received.
qs.e:
Retaliate = attack in return for an attack. E.g. The army retaliated after the border firing.
Reciprocated = gave back in return - the synonym here.
Respected = honoured; welcomed = received gladly; forgave = pardoned - all opposite in spirit.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On cloud nine
qs.e:
'On cloud nine' means extremely happy.
Example: She was on cloud nine after clearing the exam.
Flying, floating and dreaming are literal pictures of being in the clouds, not the meaning.
Answer: Very happy

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The professor refused to comment on the erroneous description of the historical events in the journal.
qs.e:
Erroneous = wrong, containing errors. E.g. The report was based on erroneous data.
Inaccurate means not correct - the synonym.
Suitable = appropriate; lucid = clear; sensitive = easily affected or delicate.
Answer: Inaccurate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Iyadurai Solomon was a great teacher because he instilled in all the children a sense of their own worth.
qs.e:
Instil = gradually fix an idea or feeling in someone's mind. E.g. Parents instil good habits in children.
Inculcate = teach by repetition so it takes root - the synonym.
Stopped = halted; took out = removed (opposite); neglected = ignored.
Answer: inculcate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Someone’s heart is in the right place
o: Suddenly feel so excited or frightened that your heart beats faster
Change your opinion or the way you feel
Share secret worries with someone else
Someone is good even if they sometimes behave in a wrong manner
qs.e:
'Someone's heart is in the right place' means the person is kind and has good intentions, even if their actions are sometimes wrong.
Example: He talks rudely, but his heart is in the right place.
Option 1 = 'heart skips a beat'; option 2 = 'change of heart'; option 3 = 'pour one's heart out'.
Answer: Someone is good even if they sometimes behave in a wrong manner

qs.q: A @ B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A & B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A ^ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A + B means ‘A is the father of B’. If H @ V @ U # W & E ^ X # Z & R ^ S, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: Z is the maternal grandfather of S.
W is the husband of U.
E is the mother-in-law of Z.
U is the sister of H.
qs.e:
Decode: H sister of V; V sister of U; U wife of W; W brother of E; E mother of X; X wife of Z; Z brother of R; R mother of S.
W is U's husband (true); E is the mother of Z's wife X, so E is Z's mother-in-law (true); U is H's sister (true).
Z is the brother of S's mother R, so Z is S's maternal UNCLE, not maternal grandfather. That statement is wrong.
Answer: Z is the maternal grandfather of S.

qs.q: If A – B means that A is the brother of B, A + B means that A is the sister of B, A ÷ B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal uncle of R?
qs.e:
A paternal uncle is the father's brother: P brother of Q, and Q father of R.
That is P – Q ÷ R (– = brother, ÷ = father).
P + Q ÷ R makes P a paternal aunt; P ÷ Q – R makes P a grandfather; P – Q + R makes P R's brother.
Answer: P – Q ÷ R

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? LAFI, MCGL, ?, OGIR, PIJU

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ABNC, HGWN, OLFY, VQOJ, ?

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 98, 70, 42, 14, ?, – 42

14 − 28 = −14; check −14 − 28 = −42 ✓.

qs.q: Which minorities are mentioned in article 30 of the Indian Contituiton?
qs.e:
Article 30 gives all minorities – religious and linguistic – the right to establish and run educational institutions of their choice.
Article 29 protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture; "cultural minority" is not a term used in Article 30.
Answer: Linguistic and religious

qs.q: What is the structure of the Indian judiciary?
qs.e:
The key counts four tiers: Supreme Court at the top, then High Courts in the States, then District Courts, then the subordinate (lower) courts below them.
India has one integrated judiciary: decisions of higher courts bind the lower ones.
Note: NCERT describes three main levels (district courts, High Courts, Supreme Court); four-tier counts the subordinate courts as a separate level.
Answer: Four-tier

qs.q: Where was the FIH Women’s Indoor Hockey World Cup 2015 held?
qs.e:
The 2015 FIH Women's Indoor Hockey World Cup was held in Leipzig, Germany.
The 2018 edition moved to Berlin.
Answer: Leipzig, Germany

qs.q: In which game/sport is the area of bout called a ring?
qs.e:
In boxing, bouts take place in a roped, square area called a ring.
Judo and karate use a mat area (tatami), and taekwondo uses a court/mat.
Answer: Boxing

qs.q: Nihit starts a business with Rs.700. After 5 months Amit and Patel joined him with Rs.300 and Rs.400 respectively. At the end of the year, the business gave a profit of Rs.627. Find the share of Patel in the profit.
qs.e:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
Nihit: 700 × 12 = 8400; Amit: 300 × 7 = 2100; Patel: 400 × 7 = 2800 (they joined after 5 months, so stayed 7).
Ratio 8400 : 2100 : 2800 = 12 : 3 : 4, total 19.
Patel's share = 627 × 4/19 = 33 × 4 = ₹132.
Answer: Rs.132

qs.q: A dealer offers 45% discount on a packet. She offers a further discount of 25% on the reduced price on cash payment. What does a customer has to pay for the packet of ₹2,800, in cash, to avail both discounts?

Price after 45% discount: 2800 × 0.55 = ₹1,540.
Further 25% on cash: 1540 × 0.75 = ₹1,155.
Answer: ₹1,155

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Empty
qs.e:
Empty = containing nothing. E.g. The hall was empty after the show.
Vacant = not occupied, empty - the synonym.
Priceless = very valuable; packed and filled = full - the antonyms.
Answer: Vacant

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Wavering
qs.e:
Wavering = moving unsteadily back and forth; being undecided. E.g. His wavering support worried the party.
Fluctuating = rising and falling irregularly - the synonym.
Sickly = often ill; drenching = soaking; unconvincing = not believable.
Answer: Fluctuating

qs.q: Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom. Down the tubes
qs.e:
'Down the tubes' (down the drain) means failing completely or being wasted.

Minting money is the opposite; being informal and swimming are unrelated.

qs.q: If L + M means that L is the father of M, L × M means that L is the mother of M, L – M means that L is the brother of M then which of the following expression shows that A is the paternal uncle of B?
qs.e:
A paternal uncle is the father's brother: we need A brother of X and X father of B (– = brother, + = father).
A – C + B: A is C's brother and C is B's father → A is B's paternal uncle.
A + B – C makes A the father; A – B × C makes A B's brother.
Answer: A – C + B

qs.q: Which of the following letter clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter cluster series? DW, FU, IR, NM, UF, ?

qs.q: A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A * B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A % B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A $ B means ‘A is the son of B’ If Z * A $ B – C * D % E, then how is Z related to E?
qs.e:
Z * A: Z is A's sister. A $ B: A is B's son. B – C: B is C's mother. C * D: C is D's sister. D % E: D is E's husband.
So Z, A, C and D are all children of B, and Z is D's sister.
D is E's husband, so Z is E's husband's sister.
Answer: Husband’s sister

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NTSM, QNBA, THKO, WBTC, ?

3rd: S, B, K, T (+9) → 20 + 9 = 29 − 26 = 3 = C. 4th: M, A, O, C (−12) → 3 − 12 + 26 = 17 = Q.

qs.q: Which special order of the courts means “arrested person should be presented before the court”?
qs.e:
Habeas corpus ("you may have the body") orders that an arrested or detained person be produced before the court, so the court can check whether the detention is lawful.
Mandamus orders a public official to perform a duty; Certiorari quashes the order of a lower court; Quo warranto asks by what authority a person holds a public office.
Answer: Habeas corpus

qs.q: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only on the grounds of _________.
qs.e:
Under Article 124(4), a Supreme Court judge can be removed only on the ground of proven misbehaviour or incapacity.
Removal needs a President's order after each House of Parliament passes an address with a special majority. No judge has ever been removed this way.
Answer: proven misbehaviour or incapacity

qs.q: What is the distance of the penalty mark from the midpoint of the goal post in football?
qs.e:
In football the penalty mark is 11 m (12 yards) from the midpoint between the goalposts.
The penalty area itself extends 16.5 m (18 yards) from the goal line.
Answer: 11 m

qs.q: Three candidates P, Q and R participated in an election. P got 35% more votes than Q, and R got 15% more votes than Q. P overtook R by 2,412 votes. If 90% voters voted and no invalid or illegal votes were cast, then what was the number of voters in the voting list?
qs.e:
Take Q = 100 parts: P = 135, R = 115.
P − R = 20 parts = 2412 → 1 part = 120.6.
Total votes = 135 + 100 + 115 = 350 parts = 350 × 120.6 = 42,210.
This is 90% of the voting list → voters = 42210 ÷ 0.9 = 46,900.
Answer: 46,900

qs.q: A dealer sells his goods at a profit of 20%, but uses a weight of 800 g in place of a kg weight. Find his real gain percentage.
qs.e:
He charges 20% above the cost of 1 kg but hands over only 800 g.
Real gain factor = 1.20 × 1000/800 = 1.20 × 1.25 = 1.50.
Real gain = 50%.
Answer: 50%

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I could not sleep because I was too eager, so I got up early and dressed.
qs.e:
Eager = full of keen, excited desire for something. E.g. The children were eager to open their gifts.
Too eager to sleep suggests excitement - exhilarated (very excited and thrilled) fits best.
Apathetic = uninterested (antonym); tensed = anxious; satisfied = contented - none show excited longing.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The heavy and abundant rainfall has a major role to play in the production of crops.
qs.e:
Abundant = existing in large quantity; plentiful. E.g. The region has abundant water.
Ample = more than enough, plentiful - the synonym.
Cyclonic = of a cyclone; intermittent = stopping and starting; prolonged = lasting long - they describe type or duration, not quantity.
Answer: Ample

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Truth can never be concealed from anyone.
qs.e:
Conceal = hide; keep from being seen or known. E.g. He concealed the letter in a drawer.
Disguised = hidden by changing its appearance - the closest synonym.
Separated = set apart; borrowed = taken to return; snatched = grabbed.
Answer: Disguised

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. I begged him to reconsider my application, but he put his foot down.
qs.e:
'To put one's foot down' means to be firm and refuse to allow or change something.
He firmly refused to reconsider the application.
'Stamped his foot' is literal; 'agreed to reconsider' is the opposite; 'did not run' is unrelated.
Answer: refused to yield

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the mother of B, A – B means that A is the father of B, A ÷ B means that A is the sister of B, then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal grandmother of R?

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 3, 13, 53, 213, ?, 3413

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NMR, QFZ, TYH, WRP, ?

qs.q: A & B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A % B means ‘A is the father of B’ If S & T % R @ P # Q , then how is S related to P?
qs.e:
S & T: S is T's wife. T % R: T is R's father. R @ P: R is P's husband. (P # Q is not needed.)
S is the wife of R's father, so S is R's mother.
R is P's husband, so S is P's husband's mother → mother-in-law.
Answer: Mother-in-law

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Indian Constitution as a Fundamental Duty?

"To respect elders" is not among the 11 Fundamental Duties in Article 51A.
The others are duties: promoting harmony and brotherhood (51A(e)), safeguarding public property (51A(i)) and defending the country (51A(d)).
Answer: To respect elders

qs.q: Which of the following cities did not hosted matches of FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2022 in India?

The 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in India was played at Bhubaneswar (Kalinga Stadium), Goa (Margao) and Navi Mumbai (DY Patil Stadium).
New Delhi hosted no matches.

qs.q: Which of the following commissions recommended that “the appointment of Governor should be non-partisan”?
qs.e:
The Sarkaria Commission (1983–88) on Centre–State relations recommended that the Governor be an eminent, detached person from outside the State, not closely tied to active politics – that is, a non-partisan appointment.
Others: Fazal Ali – States Reorganisation; Rajamannar – Tamil Nadu's Centre–State committee (1969); Mandal – backward classes.
Answer: Sarkaria commission

qs.q: The T-20 Cricket World Cup for women was held in which country in 2020?
qs.e:
The 2020 ICC Women's T20 World Cup was held in Australia, which won it by beating India in the final at the MCG, Melbourne.
The final drew a crowd of over 86,000.
Answer: Australia

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers a cash discount of ₹ 85 first and then two successive discounts of 10% and 2% on the marked price of a fan. If the marked price of the fan is ₹ 1,285, what is its selling price (in ₹ )?
qs.e:
Apply the discounts in the order given: first the flat ₹85, then 10% and 2%.
1285 − 85 = 1200; 1200 × 0.90 = 1080; 1080 × 0.98 = 1058.4.
Answer: 1058.4

qs.q: Sofia sold an iPhone at the cost of Rs.46,068 at a loss of 12%. At what cost will she have to sell it to get a profit of 18%?

In an election contested between two candidates, 15% of the total voters did not cast their votes and 100 votes got disqualified. The candidate who won the election won it by securing 45% of the total votes and won by a margin of 400 votes. Find the total number of voters?
qs.e:
Let N = total voters. Votes cast = 0.85N; valid = 0.85N − 100.
Winner = 45% of N = 0.45N; loser = 0.85N − 100 − 0.45N = 0.40N − 100.
Margin = 0.45N − (0.40N − 100) = 0.05N + 100 = 400 → 0.05N = 300 → N = 6000.
Check: winner 2700, loser 2300, invalid 100, total cast 5100 = 85% of 6000.
Answer: 6,000

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Try to be frugal with your hard-earned money.
qs.e:
Frugal = careful and sparing with money. E.g. A frugal family saves a lot every month.
Economical = using money carefully without waste - the synonym.
Imprudent = unwise, careless (antonym); negligent = careless in duty; honest = truthful.
Answer: Economical

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. No one was prepared for the environmental calamity that hit the town in the middle of the night.
qs.e:
Calamity = a sudden event causing great damage or suffering. E.g. The flood was a calamity for the farmers.
Catastrophe = a sudden great disaster - the synonym.
Damage = harm (a result, not the event); degradation = gradual decline; stress = strain.
Answer: Catastrophe

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Fair-weather friends
o: A person who is friends with you during the night
A person who is friends with you every day
A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in times
A person who is friends with you in difficult times
qs.e:
'Fair-weather friends' are people whose friendship cannot be relied on in difficult times; they stay only when things go well.
Example: When he lost his money, his fair-weather friends vanished.
Option 4 describes a true friend (the opposite); options 1 and 2 are literal or vague.
Answer: A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in times

qs.q: Select the sentence that uses the idiom correctly.
o: Ranita was not selected for the job as she got cold feet.
Walking bare feet on grass gave him cold feet.
After too much cycling Arun got cold feet.
One can swim easily with cold feet.
qs.e:
'To get cold feet' means to become nervous and lose courage just before doing something.
Sentence 1 uses it correctly: Ranita lost her nerve (at the interview) and so was not selected.
Sentences 2–4 use 'cold feet' literally (grass, cycling, swimming), which is not the idiom.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Demolish
qs.e:
Demolish = pull down or destroy completely. E.g. The old bridge was demolished.
Ruin = destroy - the synonym.
Create, fabricate (make or build) and shape (form) are all about making - the antonyms.
Answer: Ruin

qs.q: A + B means ‘A is the father of B’ A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A % B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A & B means ‘A is the son of B’ If P – Q % R & S + T, then how is P related to T?
qs.e:

So P is T's mother.

So the next cluster is SA.
Answer: SA

qs.q: If A + B means that A is the father of B, A ÷ B means that A is the mother of B, A × B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the sister of P?
qs.e:
We need Q female and a sibling of P (+ = father, ÷ = mother, × = brother).
P × Q ÷ R: P is Q's brother and Q is R's mother, so Q is female → Q is P's sister.
P × Q + R makes Q male (brother); P + R × Q makes P Q's father; Q × P ÷ R makes Q a brother.
Answer: P × Q ÷ R

qs.q: Which of the following number will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 137, 114, ?, 91, 183
qs.e:
The steps are multiples of 23 with alternating signs: −23, +46, −69, +92.
137 − 23 = 114; 114 + 46 = 160; 160 − 69 = 91; 91 + 92 = 183 ✓.
So the missing term is 160.
Answer: 160

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. SMQ, WUZ, ACI, EKR, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: S, W, A, E (+4) → I. 2nd: M, U, C, K (+8) → K(11) + 8 = 19 = S.
3rd: Q, Z, I, R (+9) → R(18) + 9 = 27 − 26 = 1 = A.
So the next cluster is ISA.
Answer: ISA

qs.q: How many Lok Sabha constituencies are there in India?
qs.e:
The Lok Sabha has 543 elected constituencies, each returning one member.
Uttar Pradesh has the most (80). The constitutional maximum strength is 550 elected members; the two nominated Anglo-Indian seats ended with the 104th Amendment (2020).
Answer: 543

qs.q: How many rights are mentioned under “Right to Equality”?
qs.e:
The Right to Equality is made up of five Articles: 14 (equality before law), 15 (no discrimination), 16 (equal opportunity in public jobs), 17 (abolition of untouchability) and 18 (abolition of titles).
Answer: 5

qs.q: The first edition of the Common wealth Youth Games was organised in which of the following years?
qs.e:
The first Commonwealth Youth Games were held in 2000 at Edinburgh, Scotland.
The third edition was held at Pune, India, in 2008.
Answer: 2000

qs.q: Which of the following pairs of countries hosted the FIVB Volleyball Men's World Championship in 2022?
qs.e:
The 2022 FIVB Volleyball Men's World Championship was co-hosted by Poland and Slovenia after it was taken away from Russia.
Italy won the title, beating Poland in the final.
Answer: Poland and Slovenia

qs.q: A megastore is offering 20% discount on all grocery items. Sakshi bought one grocery item marked at Rs.400. What is its cost price if the store earned a profit of 25% after giving the discount?
qs.e:
SP after 20% discount = 400 × 0.8 = ₹320.
Profit 25% means SP = 1.25 × CP, so CP = 320 ÷ 1.25 = ₹256.
Answer: Rs.256

qs.q: In a certain shop, the profit is 130% of the cost. If the cost increases by 28% and the selling price remains constant, then what is the profit percentage to the nearest whole number?
qs.e:
Take CP = 100. Profit = 130, so SP = 230.
New CP = 128, SP still 230. Profit = 102.
Profit% = 102/128 × 100 = 79.69% ≈ 80%.
Answer: 80%

qs.q: During the first year, the strength of a school increased by 12%, in the second year it decreased by 12% and in the third year it increased by 10%. At the end of the third year its strength was nearly 10842. What was the strength at the beginning of the first year?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The foreign company is chary of investing in Africa.
qs.e:
Chary = cautiously unwilling; wary. E.g. Investors are chary of risky shares.
Cautious = careful to avoid risk - the synonym.
Keen = eager; fervent = passionate; confident = sure - all opposite in sense.
Answer: Cautious

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The new intern is a greenhorn and thus his superiors take advantage of him.
qs.e:
A 'greenhorn' is an inexperienced newcomer.
His seniors take advantage of the new intern because he lacks experience.
Jealous, overenthusiastic and sick are unrelated.
Answer: Inexperienced

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word from the following sentence. Encountered Many people have been experiencing the starting of heat wave and some of them have avoided going outside their homes.
qs.e:
Encounter = meet with or face something (often difficult). E.g. We encountered heavy rain on the way.
In the sentence, people are 'experiencing' the heat wave - facing it, the same idea.
Outside = exterior; starting = beginning; avoided = kept away from (nearly opposite).
Answer: Experiencing

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Anger
qs.e:
Anger = strong feeling of annoyance or rage. E.g. He could not hide his anger.
Fury = wild, intense anger - the synonym.
Pleasure and comfort = happy, easy feelings (antonyms); agony = intense pain.
Answer: Fury

qs.q: If P ÷ Q means that P is the mother of Q, P – Q means that P is the father of Q, P × Q means that P is the sister of Q, then which of the following expression shows that B is the daughter of A?
qs.e:
B must be female and A must be B's parent (÷ = mother, – = father, × = sister).
A – B ÷ C: A is B's father and B is C's mother, so B is female → B is A's daughter.
A – B × C also works: A is B's father and B is C's sister → B is A's daughter.
B – A ÷ C makes B the father; C ÷ B – A makes B a father too. The official key takes option 2.
Answer: A – B ÷ C

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’ A & B means ‘A is the wife of B’ A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’ If A % B & C # D @ E, then how is B related to E?
qs.e:
A % B: A is B's mother. B & C: B is C's wife. C # D: C is D's brother. D @ E: D is E's son.
C is D's brother, so C is also E's son.
B is the wife of E's son, so B is E's daughter-in-law.
Answer: Daughter-in-law

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 15, 4, –8, –21, –35, ?
qs.e:
Differences: −11, −12, −13, −14 — each drop is 1 bigger.
The next difference is −15.
−35 − 15 = −50.
Answer: –50

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ABCD, EVKT, IPSJ, MJAZ, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: A, E, I, M (+4) → Q. 2nd: B, V, P, J (−6) → J(10) − 6 = 4 = D.
3rd: C, K, S, A (+8) → A(1) + 8 = 9 = I. 4th: D, T, J, Z (−10) → Z(26) − 10 = 16 = P.
So the next cluster is QDIP.
Answer: QDIP

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ARC, EPF, JNI, PLL, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: A, E, J, P — gaps +4, +5, +6, so next +7: P(16) + 7 = 23 = W.
2nd letters: R, P, N, L (−2) → J. 3rd letters: C, F, I, L (+3) → O.
So the next cluster is WJO.
Answer: WJO

qs.q: The Paralympics Games - 2024 will be hosted by _______.
qs.e:
The 2024 Summer Paralympics were held in Paris, France, after the Olympics.
Paris had hosted the Olympics in 1900 and 1924 but never the Paralympics before.
Answer: France

qs.q: Which of the following terms is NOT included in the Preamble of Indian Constitution?
qs.e:
"Federalism" does not appear in the Preamble, and the word "federation" is not used anywhere in the Constitution.
"Sovereign", "Justice" (social, economic, political) and "Fraternity" all appear in the Preamble.
Answer: Federalism

qs.q: The State Finance Commission is appointed every ____ years by the _____.
qs.e:
Under Article 243I (added by the 73rd Amendment), the Governor of the State appoints a State Finance Commission every five years to review panchayat finances. Article 243Y applies the same to municipalities.
Because the Governor acts on the State government's advice, it is a State-level appointment.
Answer: 5, state government

qs.q: Which country beat India in the men's hockey semi-final event at Tokyo Olympics, 2020?
qs.e:
In the Tokyo 2020 men's hockey semi-final, Belgium beat India 5-2; Alexander Hendrickx scored a hat-trick.
India then beat Germany 5-4 for bronze, its first Olympic hockey medal since 1980.
Answer: Belgium

qs.q: A grocery shop is offering 10% discount on the purchase of Rs.500 and above. A 5% discount is given on the purchase of value above Rs.250 but below Rs.500. A discount of additional 1% is given if payment is made instantly in cash. How much would a customer have to pay by cash if he buys 25 packets of biscuits and one packet is priced at Rs.30?
qs.e:
Bill = 25 × 30 = ₹750, which is ₹500 or more, so 10% discount: 750 × 0.9 = 675.
Extra 1% for cash: 675 × 0.99 = ₹668.25.
Answer: Rs.668.25

qs.q: In an election between two candidates, a candidate who gets 64% of the votes polled is elected by a majority of 252 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
qs.e:
Winner 64%, loser 36% → majority = 28% of votes polled.
28% = 252 → total = 252 × 100/28 = 900.
Answer: 900

qs.q: A man sells two cows for Rs.15,640 each, gaining 15% on one and losing 15% on the other. Find his total gain or loss.
qs.e:
Cow 1 (gain 15%): CP = 15,640 ÷ 1.15 = ₹13,600. Cow 2 (loss 15%): CP = 15,640 ÷ 0.85 = ₹18,400.
Total CP = 32,000; total SP = 31,280.
Net loss = ₹720.
Shortcut: same SP with ±x% always gives a loss of x²/100 = 2.25% of CP; 2.25% of 32,000 = 720.
Answer: Rs.720 loss

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. After several years of cheating on his PhD work, the candidate finally had to face the music and lose the opportunity.
o: Choose another alternative that is uninteresting
qs.e:
'To face the music' means to accept the unpleasant results of one's actions.
Origin: possibly a disgraced soldier drummed out of his regiment to music.
The cheating candidate had to accept the punishment.
'Be exposed' is only part of it; accepting ignorance and choosing another option are wrong.
Answer: To accept unpleasant consequences

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The director is at the apex of the managing committee.
qs.e:
Apex = the top or highest point. E.g. The apex of the pyramid.
Pinnacle = highest point - the synonym.
Core = centre; bottom = lowest point (antonym); corner = where two sides meet.
Answer: Pinnacle

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The fraudsters hoodwinked us and took away all our valuables.
qs.e:
Hoodwink = trick or cheat someone. E.g. The conman hoodwinked the old couple.
Deceived = misled by a trick - the synonym.
Coerced = forced; threatened = warned of harm; misguided = having wrong ideas (adjective, not tricked).
Answer: Deceived

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Lose your marbles
qs.e:
'To lose one's marbles' means to go mad or lose one's mental balance.
Example: He shouted at the TV for an hour – I thought he had lost his marbles.
Handling stress, calming anger and being patient describe a calm mind – the opposite.
Answer: To go insane
