qs.q: If A × B means that A is the father of B, A ÷ B means that A is the mother of B, A + B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal grandmother of R?
qs.e:
Paternal grandmother = father's mother: P mother of Q, and Q father of R.
That is P ÷ Q × R (÷ = mother, × = father).
P ÷ R × Q makes P R's mother; P ÷ Q + R makes P R's mother; P × Q ÷ R makes P the father of R.
Answer: P ÷ Q × R

qs.q: ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the son of A’. If F & G @ H # I @ J, then how is G related to J?
qs.e:
F & G: F is G's father. G @ H: G is H's husband. H # I: I is H's son. I @ J: I is J's husband.
H is G's wife, so I is G's son.
J is the wife of G's son, so G is J's father-in-law.
Answer: Father-in-law

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series 12.8, 13.5, 14.9, 17, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 0.7, 1.4, 2.1 — multiples of 0.7 (0.7 × 1, × 2, × 3).
The next difference is 0.7 × 4 = 2.8.
17 + 2.8 = 19.8.
Answer: 19.8

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ABCD, CUKA, ENSX, GGAU, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: A, C, E, G (+2) → I. 2nd: B, U, N, G (−7) → 7 − 7 = 0 → Z.
3rd: C, K, S, A (+8) → A(1) + 8 = 9 = I. 4th: D, A, X, U (−3) → U(21) − 3 = 18 = R.
So the next cluster is IZIR.
Answer: IZIR

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? IR, BY, UF, NM, GT, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: I, B, U, N, G — each 7 back (wrapping), so next 7 − 7 = 0 → Z.
2nd letters: R, Y, F, M, T — each 7 forward, so next 20 + 7 = 27 − 26 = 1 = A.
So the next cluster is ZA.
Answer: ZA

qs.q: All the ______ countries likely to have Constitution.
qs.e:
Democratic countries are almost certain to have a constitution, because democracy needs written rules that limit the government's power and protect citizens' rights.
Totalitarian, oligarchic or communist regimes may have a constitution only in name, or none at all.
Answer: democratic

qs.q: In Tennis, what is the score when the receiver wins the next point after deuce?
qs.e:
After deuce (40-40), the player who wins the next point has 'advantage'. If the receiver wins it, the score is 'advantage out' (ad-out); if the server wins, 'advantage in'.
Winning the point after advantage wins the game; losing it returns to deuce.
Answer: Advantage out

qs.q: The 22nd Commonwealth Games are scheduled to be held in which of the following countries?
qs.e:
The 22nd Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England, in July-August 2022.
India finished fourth with 61 medals.
Answer: England

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers the following three schemes. Scheme-I: Two successive discounts of 15% and 25% Scheme-II: Buy 5, get 3 free Scheme-III: Buy 4, get 6 Which scheme is the best for customers?
qs.e:
Scheme I: 15 + 25 − (15×25)/100 = 36.25%.
Scheme II: buy 5, get 3 free → 3 free out of 8 = 37.5%.
Scheme III: pay for 4, get 6 → 2 free out of 6 = 33.33%.
Scheme II gives the biggest discount.
Answer: Scheme-II

qs.q: The ratio of the cost price and selling price of an article is 10 : 11. The gain per cent is:
qs.e:
Take CP = 10, SP = 11. Gain = 1.
Gain% = 1/10 × 100 = 10%.
Answer: 10%

qs.q: A Microwave oven is sold in Hyderabad for Rs.M. A retailer, Elahi from Hyderabad went to Madras and bought it for 25% less (when compared to the price in Hyderabad). He spends Rs.1,000 on transport to bring it from Madras to Hyderabad. He sold it in Hyderabad for Rs.M making a profit of 10%. Find the value of M (in Rs.).
qs.e:
Elahi buys at 0.75M and spends ₹1,000 more, so his cost = 0.75M + 1000.
He sells at M with 10% profit: M = 1.1 × (0.75M + 1000) = 0.825M + 1100.
0.175M = 1100 → M = 1100 ÷ 0.175 = 6,285.7.
Answer: 6,285.7

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Permeate
qs.e:
Permeate = spread throughout something. E.g. The smell of coffee permeated the room.
Diffuse = spread out over a wide area - the synonym.
Exude = give off from inside (close, but it means discharge, not spread through); continue = go on; remain = stay.
Answer: Diffuse

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. He's sitting on the fence
qs.e:
'Sitting on the fence' means being unable or unwilling to decide or take sides.
Example: He is still sitting on the fence about which college to join.
Trying hard, not being serious and hiding are not the meaning.
Answer: He can't take a decision

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ABCD, AXUR, ATMF, APET, ?
qs.e:
1st letter stays A.
2nd: B, X, T, P (−4) → P(16) − 4 = 12 = L. 3rd: C, U, M, E (−8) → 5 − 8 + 26 = 23 = W.
4th: D, R, F, T (−12) → T(20) − 12 = 8 = H.
So the next cluster is ALWH.
Answer: ALWH

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’. A & B means ‘A is the father of B’. A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’. If W @ Q % T & Y @ M % K, then how is W related to K?
qs.e:
W @ Q: W is Q's son. Q % T: Q is T's mother. T & Y: T is Y's father. Y @ M: Y is M's son. M % K: M is K's mother.
T and M are the parents of Y and K, so T is K's father.
W and T are both sons of Q, so W is the brother of K's father.
Answer: Father’s brother

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 25, 15, ?, −5, −15
qs.e:
Each term is 10 less than the one before: 25 − 15 = 10.
15 − 10 = 5; check 5 − 10 = −5 and −5 − 10 = −15 ✓.
Answer: 5

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the father of B, A – B means that A is the mother of B, A ÷ B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the paternal uncle of R?
qs.e:
A paternal uncle is the father's brother: P brother of Q, and Q father of R.
That is P ÷ Q × R (÷ = brother, × = father).
P ÷ Q – R makes P a maternal uncle; Q ÷ P × R makes P R's father; P × Q ÷ R makes P R's father.
Answer: P ÷ Q × R

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? VSNY, UQLU, ?, SMHM, RKFI
qs.e:
Each letter position moves back by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: V, U, T, S, R (−1). 2nd: S, Q, O, M, K (−2).
3rd: N, L, J, H, F (−2). 4th: Y, U, Q, M, I (−4).
So the missing cluster is TOJQ.
Answer: TOJQ

qs.q: Which of the following players is associated with billiards?
qs.e:
Pankaj Advani is India's leading cue-sports player, a multiple world champion in billiards and snooker.
Neeraj Chopra is a javelin thrower, Sankalp Gupta a chess player and Manish Narwal a para shooter.
Answer: Pankaj Advani

qs.q: Fundamental Duties are contained within which Article of the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
The Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A, the only Article in Part IV-A, added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
Article 44 is the Directive Principle on a Uniform Civil Code. Articles 50A and 492 do not exist.
Answer: Article 51A

qs.q: Which of the following cities hosted the finals of IPL 2022?
qs.e:
The IPL 2022 final was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, on 29 May 2022.
Gujarat Titans, in their first season, beat Rajasthan Royals to win the title.
Answer: Ahmedabad

qs.q: Who runs the government at the national level under the parliamentary system?
o: The President and Council of Ministers
The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
qs.e:
In a parliamentary system, the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers run the national government; they are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
The President is only the formal head and acts on their advice.
Answer: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

qs.q: A number is decreased by 20% to get another number. The number so obtained is increased by 200% to get a third number. The difference of the third number and the original number is what percentage more or less than the difference of second and the third number?
qs.e:
Take the original number = 100. Second = 100 × 0.8 = 80. Third = 80 + 200% of 80 = 240.
Third − original = 140; third − second = 160.
140 is less than 160 by 20/160 × 100 = 12.5%.
Answer: Less, 12.5 Percent

qs.q: The printed price of a TV set is ₹14,500. It is sold for ₹10,000 with two consecutive discounts. If the first discount is 10%, then what is the second discount?
qs.e:
After the first 10% discount: 14,500 × 0.9 = ₹13,050.
The second discount takes 13,050 to 10,000: discount = 3,050.
Second discount % = 3050/13050 × 100 ≈ 23.37%.
Answer: 23.37%

qs.q: A dishonest dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price but uses a false weight and thus gains 15%. For a kilogram, he uses a weight of _________ (rounded off to one digit after decimal).
qs.e:
Selling at cost price with a false weight: 1000/w = 1 + gain.
w = 1000 ÷ 1.15 = 869.57 ≈ 869.6 g.
Answer: 869.6 gm

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Irrevocable
qs.e:
Irrevocable = cannot be changed or undone. E.g. Signing the deal was an irrevocable decision.
Irreversible = cannot be turned back - the synonym.
Unmediated = without a go-between; congruent = in agreement; irresponsive = not responding (a look-alike trap).
Answer: Irreversible

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The sailor tells great tales of adventure that you should take with a grain of salt.
qs.e:
'To take (something) with a grain of salt' means not to believe it completely; to be a little sceptical.
Origin: Latin 'cum grano salis' – food is easier to swallow with a bit of salt.
The sailor's adventure tales may be exaggerated.
Admiration and patriotism are unrelated; option 4 makes no sense.
Answer: Not take too seriously
qs.u: take with a grain of salt

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The anxious duke was found strolling in the garden to and fro.
qs.e:
'To and fro' means moving forward and backward, back and forth.
The anxious duke kept walking back and forth in the garden.
North–south, west–east and up–down are fixed directions, not the meaning.
Answer: Forward and backward

qs.q: If R ÷ S means that R is the mother of S, R × S means that R is the father of S, R – S means that R is the sister of S, then which of the following expression shows that P is the father of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's father (× = father, ÷ = mother, – = sister).
P × Q – R: P is Q's father and Q is R's sister → P is R's father.
P × Q ÷ R makes P a grandfather; Q × P – R makes Q P's father; R × Q – P makes R P's father.
Answer: P × Q – R

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. COMB, GIUR, KCCH, OWKX, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: C, G, K, O (+4) → S. 2nd: O, I, C, W (−6) → W(23) − 6 = 17 = Q.
3rd: M, U, C, K (+8) → K(11) + 8 = 19 = S. 4th: B, R, H, X (−10) → X(24) − 10 = 14 = N.
So the next cluster is SQSN.
Answer: SQSN

qs.q: What should come in place of the question mark (?) to complete the following letter cluster series? RD, JF, DJ, ZP, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: R, J, D, Z — steps −8, −6, −4, so next −2: Z(26) − 2 = 24 = X.
2nd letters: D, F, J, P — steps +2, +4, +6, so next +8: P(16) + 8 = 24 = X.
So the next cluster is XX.
Answer: XX

qs.q: A & B means ‘A is the son of B’ A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A % B means ‘A is the father of B’ A − B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A * B means ‘A is the wife of B’ If C # D @ E % Z & L # M − N * P, then how is L related to P?
qs.e:
L # M: L is M's sister. M − N: M is N's daughter. N * P: N is P's wife.
L is M's sister, so L is also a daughter of N and her husband P.
So L is P's daughter.
Answer: Daughter

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 1, 4, 13, 40, ?, 364
qs.e:
Each term is three times the previous plus 1.
1 × 3 + 1 = 4; 4 × 3 + 1 = 13; 13 × 3 + 1 = 40.
Next: 40 × 3 + 1 = 121; check 121 × 3 + 1 = 364 ✓.
Answer: 121

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a way in which a batsman can get out in a game of cricket?
qs.e:
A leg bye is a run scored when the ball hits the batter's body (not the bat) and the batters run; it is an extra, not a dismissal.
Bowled, stumped and LBW are all ways of getting out.
Answer: Leg bye

qs.q: If the State government dissolves the Panchayati Raj Institutions before the end of their five-year term, fresh elections should ordinarily be held within _____.
qs.e:
Article 243E(3) says that if a panchayat is dissolved early, fresh elections must be finished within six months of the dissolution.
A normal panchayat term is five years from its first meeting.
Answer: six months

qs.q: Which of the following Articles states that a State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them?
qs.e:
Article 15(1) says the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them.
Art 25 – freedom of religion; Art 40 – village panchayats (DPSP); Art 59 – conditions of the President's office.
Answer: Article 15

qs.q: What is the duration of the lunch interval in a cricket test match?
qs.e:
In Test cricket the lunch interval is 40 minutes and the tea interval is 20 minutes.
Answer: 40 minutes

qs.q: Raghav purchased a shirt at Rs.1,500 and marked up the price of the shirt by 40%. What is the discount percentage he has to offer in order to get a profit of Rs.75?
A watch is sold at a profit of 25%. Had it been sold for Rs.120 less then, there would have been a less then of 15%. What is the cost price in rupees?
qs.e:
From 25% profit to 15% loss is a fall of 40% of CP.
That fall is ₹120, so CP = 120 ÷ 0.40 = ₹300.
Answer: Rs.300

qs.q: Out of an earning of Rs.720, Pankaj spends 65%. How much does he save?
qs.e:
If he spends 65%, he saves 35%.
Savings = 35% of 720 = 0.35 × 720 = ₹252.
Answer: Rs.252

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Eat humble pie
o: To live a life of humility
To enjoy life to the fullest
qs.e:
'To eat humble pie' means to admit one's mistake and apologise humbly.
Origin: 'umble pie' was made from the cheap inner parts (umbles) of a deer, eaten by servants.
Example: After his prediction failed, he had to eat humble pie.
Penury (poverty), a humble life and enjoying life are wrong.
Answer: To apologise humbly

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. After the government interventions, the enrolment and retention of female students have increased by leaps and bounds.
qs.e:
'By leaps and bounds' means very quickly, with rapid progress.
Enrolment and retention of girls rose swiftly after government action.
Systematically = in an orderly way; intermittently = on and off; gradually = slowly – none means rapid.
Answer: Swiftly

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in a sentence. The good weather has been a boon for many businesses located near the beach.
qs.e:
Boon = something that is very helpful or brings benefit. E.g. The new metro is a boon for commuters.
The weather was a boon = it was beneficial (helpful) for businesses, which is the key's choice.
Luck and fortune = chance/good luck (cause, not the benefit itself); signal = a sign.
Answer: beneficial

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Although Edward had noble blood, his ignoble qualities made him incapable of taking over the kingdom.
qs.e:
Ignoble = not honourable; base, mean in character. E.g. Betraying a friend is an ignoble act.
Unworthy = lacking worth or honour - the synonym, and the sentence contrasts it with 'noble blood'.
Salient = most noticeable; strange = unusual; ostentatious = showy.
Answer: Unworthy

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. MHDM, MYLC, MPTS, MGBI, ?
qs.e:
1st letter stays M.
2nd: H, Y, P, G (−9) → 7 − 9 + 26 = 24 = X. 3rd: D, L, T, B (+8) → B(2) + 8 = 10 = J.
4th: M, C, S, I (−10) → 9 − 10 + 26 = 25 = Y.
So the next cluster is MXJY.
Answer: MXJY

qs.q: ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the son of A’. If S @ T # P @ Q # R & V, then how is T related to Q?
qs.e:
S @ T: S is T's husband. T # P: P is T's son. P @ Q: P is Q's husband. (Q # R, R & V are not needed.)
T is P's mother, and Q is P's wife.
The husband's mother is the mother-in-law, so T is Q's mother-in-law.
Answer: Mother-in-law

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 5, 12, 26, ?, 110, 222
qs.e:
Each term is double the previous plus 2.
5 × 2 + 2 = 12; 12 × 2 + 2 = 26; 26 × 2 + 2 = 54.
Check: 54 × 2 + 2 = 110 and 110 × 2 + 2 = 222 ✓.
Answer: 54

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ABCD, EBCD, ?, OBCD, UBCD
qs.e:
Only the 1st letter changes; _BCD stays fixed.
The 1st letters are the vowels in order: A, E, I, O, U.
So the missing term is IBCD.
Answer: IBCD

qs.q: Which Fundamental Right was deleted by The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978?
qs.e:
The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the Fundamental Rights by deleting Articles 19(1)(f) and 31.
It is now a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII. The amendment was passed by the Janata Party government.
Answer: Right to Property

qs.q: Which of the following countries is NOT part of the three nations to host the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup?
qs.e:
The 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup was co-hosted by the Philippines, Japan and Indonesia.
Argentina was not a host; Germany won the title.
Answer: Argentina

qs.q: In cricket, if the umpire raises an index finger above the head it means__________.
qs.e:
In cricket, an umpire raising the index finger above the head signals that the batter is out.
A wide is shown with both arms stretched sideways, a no ball with one arm held out horizontally, and a dead ball by crossing and uncrossing the wrists below the waist.
Answer: batsman is out

qs.q: The 73rd amendment deals with which of the following?
qs.e:
The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 deals with the Panchayati Raj system (rural local self-government); it added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule.
Others: GST – 101st; urban local bodies – 74th; anti-defection – 52nd.
Answer: Panchayat Raj System

qs.q: Raghav went to a shopping mall to purchase clothes. He had two coupons with him, but only one can be used on a single day. Using the first coupon, a total discount of 30% could be obtained on the total amount. Using the second coupon, he will get 80% off on the price of the costliest shirt if he buys at least 3 shirts. What is the price at which Raghav can purchase 3 shirts at a minimum price if the prices of the three shirts are Rs.1,250, Rs.1,540 and Rs.1,375?
qs.e:
Total price = 1250 + 1540 + 1375 = ₹4,165.
Coupon 1: 30% off total → 4165 × 0.7 = ₹2,915.50.
Coupon 2: 80% off the costliest shirt (1540) → 4165 − 1232 = ₹2,933.
Coupon 1 is cheaper.
Answer: Rs.2,915.50

qs.q: A dishonest dealer sells the goods at 7% loss on cost price but uses 18% less weight. What is his percentage of profit? (Correct to 2 decimal places)
qs.e:
Let 1 unit of weight cost ₹1. He charges 0.93 (7% loss) but gives only 0.82 unit (18% less).
Profit% = (0.93 − 0.82)/0.82 × 100 = 11/82 × 100 = 13.41%.
Answer: 13.41%

qs.q: The expenditure on the cost of living of a man and his family is 60% of his salary. He gets two increment of 30% and 60% in his salary. If his saving increases by 250% of his initial saving, then the new cost of living expenditure is what percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the increased salary?
qs.e:
Take salary = 100: cost of living 60, savings 40.
New salary after two increments = 100 × 1.3 × 1.6 = 208.
Savings increase by 250% of 40 = 100 → new savings = 140.
New cost of living = 208 − 140 = 68 → 68/208 × 100 ≈ 32.7%.
Answer: 32.7 Percent

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word to fill in the blank. Your words seemed more like a demand rather than a _________ (request).
qs.e:
Request = politely asking for something. E.g. He made a request for leave.
Plea = an earnest appeal or request - it fits and contrasts with 'demand'.
Compromise = settlement by give and take; contract = a legal agreement; order = a command (close to 'demand', the opposite of a request).
Answer: plea

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Red tape
o: Catch someone at the moment they are doing something wrong
Official rules and bureaucracy that make it difficult to do something
Have a negative amount in your bank balance
Something unimportant that takes attention away from the main subject
qs.e:
'Red tape' means too many official rules and procedures that delay action.
Origin: official documents in Britain were tied with red ribbon.
Example: Getting a licence took months because of red tape.
Option 1 = 'catch red-handed'; option 3 = 'in the red'; option 4 = 'red herring'.
Answer: Official rules and bureaucracy that make it difficult to do something

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The young fellow was innocent and without guile.
qs.e:
Guile = sly or cunning intelligence used to deceive. E.g. The fox used guile to get the cheese.
Deceit = cheating, dishonesty - the synonym; 'innocent and without guile' means free of trickery.
Morality = sense of right; pride = self-respect; greed = desire for more.
Answer: Deceit

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. Let us know what you think in black and white.
qs.e:
'In black and white' means in writing or in print (black ink on white paper).
So: put your views down in writing.
'Verbally' is the opposite; darkness/light and paint are literal readings.
Answer: in writing

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 67, 46, 24, 1, –23, ?
qs.e:
Differences: −21, −22, −23, −24 — each drop is 1 bigger.
The next difference is −25.
−23 − 25 = −48.
Answer: –48

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A @ B means ‘A is the son of B’. A & B means ‘A is the father of B’. A % B means ‘A is the mother of B’. If W & Q # T & Y @ M % K, then how is Q related to K?
qs.e:
W & Q: W is Q's father. Q # T: Q is T's sister. T & Y: T is Y's father. Y @ M: Y is M's son. M % K: M is K's mother.
T and M are the parents of Y and K, so T is K's father.
Q is T's sister, i.e. the sister of K's father.
Answer: Father’s sister

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. NTR, TCE, ZLR, FUE, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: N, T, Z, F (+6) → F(6) + 6 = 12 = L. 2nd: T, C, L, U (+9) → 21 + 9 = 30 − 26 = 4 = D.
3rd letters alternate R, E, R, E (+13 each), so next is R.
So the next cluster is LDR.
Answer: LDR

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? DBK, GDL, JFM, MHN, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: D, G, J, M, P (+3). 2nd: B, D, F, H, J (+2). 3rd: K, L, M, N, O (+1).
So the next cluster is PJO.
Answer: PJO

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the brother of B, A – B means that A is the sister of B, A + B means that A is the father of B then which of the following expression shows that P is the father of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's father (+ = father, × = brother, – = sister).
P + Q × R: P is Q's father and Q is R's brother → P is R's father.
P × Q + R makes P a paternal uncle; P – Q × R makes P a sister; P + Q ÷ R uses a symbol not defined.
Answer: P + Q × R

qs.q: Which article of Indian constitution is related with the Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim?
qs.e:
Article 371F has special provisions for Sikkim, added by the 36th Amendment Act, 1975, when Sikkim became a full State.
Others: 371A – Nagaland; 371C – Manipur; 371 – Maharashtra and Gujarat.
Answer: Article 371F

qs.q: What should be the standard length of a tennis court according the laws of the International Tennis Federation (ITF), 2021?
qs.e:
Under ITF rules a tennis court is 23.77 m (78 ft) long; it is 8.23 m wide for singles and 10.97 m wide for doubles.
Answer: 23.77 m

qs.q: Article 20 of the Constitution of India deals with ______________.
o: protection of life and personal liberty
protection in respect of conviction for offences
qs.e:
Article 20 protects people in respect of conviction for offences: no ex-post-facto criminal law, no double jeopardy and no self-incrimination.
Art 21 – life and personal liberty; Art 17 – abolition of untouchability; Art 21A – right to education.
Answer: protection in respect of conviction for offences

qs.q: Who is the Ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog?
qs.e:
The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog. NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.
Its working head is the Vice-Chairperson, appointed by the PM.
Answer: Prime Minister

qs.q: An article costs Rs.4,000 to a shopkeeper, who marks its price at Rs.8,400. The shopkeeper sells it to a customer at a discount of 25%. The customer gets a further discount of 15% on the discounted price if the customer redeems a coupon issued by the store previously. What is the profit percentage (to the nearest integer) earned by the shopkeeper in this transaction?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Roads in villages during rainy seasons become muddy.
qs.e:
Muddy = covered with or full of mud. E.g. His shoes were muddy after the match.
Filthy = very dirty - the closest synonym.
Fuzzy and blurred = unclear (the sense 'muddy colour/thinking', not roads); unsoiled = clean (antonym).
Answer: filthy

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The poet managed to paint a vivid picture of the landscape by the river through words.
qs.e:
Vivid = producing clear, lively images in the mind. E.g. She gave a vivid account of the trip.
Evocative = bringing strong images or feelings to mind - the synonym.
Metaphoric = using metaphors; contemporary = modern; blurred = unclear (antonym).
Answer: Evocative

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Steer clear of
o: Show someone how to do a job or activity
Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you
qs.e:
'To steer clear of' means to avoid someone or something, usually because it is harmful.
Origin: a sailor steering a ship away from rocks.
Example: Steer clear of junk food before the race.
Teaching, being easy and being exhausted are other idioms ('show the ropes', 'a piece of cake', 'worn out').
Answer: Avoid someone or something because it is dangerous for you

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The efforts of the doctors came to a futile end with the death of the patient.
qs.e:
Futile = producing no useful result; useless. E.g. It was futile to argue with him.
Fruitless = without result - the synonym; the patient died, so the efforts failed.
Enriching = improving; startling = surprising; terrifying = very frightening.
Answer: Fruitless

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Marcella seemed morose and downcast when she refused to have dinner.
qs.e:
Morose = sullen, gloomy and ill-tempered. E.g. He has been morose since he lost the job.
Gloomy = sad and dark in mood - the synonym (and 'downcast' supports it).
Jocund = cheerful; excited = eager (both antonyms); liberal = open-minded or generous.
Answer: Gloomy

qs.q: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 12, 25, 51, 103, ?, 415, 831
qs.e:
Each term is double the previous plus 1.
12 × 2 + 1 = 25; 25 × 2 + 1 = 51; 51 × 2 + 1 = 103.
Next: 103 × 2 + 1 = 207; check 207 × 2 + 1 = 415 ✓.
Answer: 207

qs.q: If P × Q means that P is the mother of Q, P + Q means that P is the father of Q, P ÷ Q means that P is the sister of Q, then which of the following expression shows that A is the maternal aunt of C?
qs.e:
A maternal aunt is the mother's sister: A sister of B, and B mother of C.
That is A ÷ B × C (÷ = sister, × = mother).
A ÷ B + C makes A a paternal aunt; C × B ÷ A and B ÷ C × A put A lower in the tree.
Answer: A ÷ B × C

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? TYG, ?, PSM, NPP, LMS
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: T, R, P, N, L (−2). 2nd: Y, V, S, P, M (−3). 3rd: G, J, M, P, S (+3).
So the missing cluster is RVJ.
Answer: RVJ

qs.q: A – B means ‘A is the mother of B’ A * B means ‘A is the husband of B’ A % B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A $ B means ‘A is the sister of B’ If I * J – K % L $ M * N, then how is I related to N?
qs.e:
I * J: I is J's husband. J – K: J is K's mother. K % L: K is L's brother. L $ M: L is M's sister. M * N: M is N's husband.
K, L and M are children of J, and I is J's husband, so I is M's father.
M is N's husband, so I is N's husband's father → father-in-law.
Answer: Father-in-law

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. TTDS, VMLP, XFTM, ZYBJ, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: T, V, X, Z (+2) → 28 − 26 = 2 = B. 2nd: T, M, F, Y (−7) → Y(25) − 7 = 18 = R.
3rd: D, L, T, B (+8) → B(2) + 8 = 10 = J. 4th: S, P, M, J (−3) → J(10) − 3 = 7 = G.
So the next cluster is BRJG.
Answer: BRJG

qs.q: In hockey, what is the meaning if the umpire signals by pointing both arms horizontally toward the centre of the field?
qs.e:
In hockey, the umpire signals a goal by pointing both arms horizontally towards the centre of the field.
Both arms pointing towards the goal means a penalty corner.
Answer: Goal scored

qs.q: Which freedom is considered as the ‘Hallmark of Democracy’?
qs.e:
In the key's (NCERT-style) view, freedom of religion is the hallmark of democracy: everyone may freely profess, practise and propagate any religion, or none, under Article 25. This also protects minorities.
Freedom of speech and expression is very important too, but the official answer treats religious freedom as the hallmark.
Answer: Right to freedom of religion

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the eligibility criteria for being elected as Vice President of India?
o: He/She should be a citizen of India.
He/She should have completed 35 years of age.
He/She should not hold any office of profit under the Union Government/state government or any subordinate local authority.
He/She should be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
qs.e:
Under Article 66(3), a Vice-President candidate must be a citizen, be at least 35, hold no office of profit and be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha – not the Lok Sabha.
This is because the VP is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. For the President, the requirement is qualification for the Lok Sabha.
Answer: He/She should be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.

qs.q: In Triple Jump, white flag indicates:
qs.e:
In the jumps and throws, an official raises a white flag when a trial is valid and a red flag when it is a foul (failure).
The question means 'trial'; 'trail' is a misprint.
Answer: trail is valid

qs.q: Sita gets a discount of 20% on ₹3,000 juicer mixer machine. Since she pays cash, she gets additional 5% discount too. How much does she pay?
A girl purchases 9 mangoes for Rs.90 and sells 10 mangoes for Rs.95. Find the gain or loss percentage.
qs.e:
CP per mango = 90/9 = ₹10. SP per mango = 95/10 = ₹9.50.
Loss = 0.50 per mango; loss% = 0.5/10 × 100 = 5%.
Answer: 5% loss

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Distant
qs.e:
Distant = far away in space or time. E.g. A distant village in the hills.
Faraway = far off - the synonym.
Farsighted = planning wisely for the future (or seeing far things clearly); futuristic = of the future; forward = towards the front.
Answer: Faraway

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hold water
o: Appear to be of no value
Appear to be valid or reasonable
qs.e:
'To hold water' means to seem valid, logical or believable.
Image: a sound vessel holds water; a cracked one leaks.
Example: Your excuse doesn't hold water.
A diluted argument and 'of no value' are opposite; 'stop emphasising' is unrelated.
Answer: Appear to be valid or reasonable

qs.q: P + Q means ‘P is the father of Q’ P – Q means ‘P is the mother of Q’ P * Q means ‘P is the sister of Q’ P % Q means ‘P is the brother of Q’ If A – B % C * D + E, then how is A related to E?
qs.e:
A – B: A is B's mother. B % C: B is C's brother. C * D: C is D's sister. D + E: D is E's father.
B, C and D are siblings, so A is D's mother as well.
D is E's father, so A is E's father's mother.
Answer: Father’s mother

qs.q: Which of the following letter clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter cluster series? DW, FU, HS, JQ, LO, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: D, F, H, J, L (+2) → N.
2nd letters: W, U, S, Q, O (−2) → M.
So the next cluster is NM.
Answer: NM

qs.q: If S – T means that S is the mother of T, S × T means that S is the father of T, S + T means that S is the sister of T, then which of the following expression shows that P is the mother of R?
qs.e:
We need P to be R's mother (– = mother, × = father, + = sister).
P – Q + R: P is Q's mother and Q is R's sister → P is R's mother.
Q – P + R makes P R's sister; P × Q + R makes P the father; R + Q – P puts P at the bottom.
Answer: P – Q + R

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. ABCD, CTFZ, ELIV, GDLR, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: A, C, E, G (+2) → I. 2nd: B, T, L, D (−8) → 4 − 8 + 26 = 22 = V.
3rd: C, F, I, L (+3) → O. 4th: D, Z, V, R (−4) → R(18) − 4 = 14 = N.
So the next cluster is IVON.
Answer: IVON

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 31, ?, 40, 49, 61, 76
qs.e:
Work back from the end. Differences: 49 − 40 = 9, 61 − 49 = 12, 76 − 61 = 15 (+3 each).
So the earlier differences are 3 and 6.
31 + 3 = 34, and 34 + 6 = 40 ✓.
Answer: 34

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the jurisdiction of the High Court?
o: It controls the subordinate courts within its jurisdiction.
It has the power of judicial review.
It provides advisory opinion to the President of India.
qs.e:
Only the Supreme Court gives advisory opinions to the President (Article 143); a High Court has no such power.
High Courts do control subordinate courts (Art 235), have judicial review, and have writ jurisdiction (Art 226, wider than the Supreme Court's).
Answer: It provides advisory opinion to the President of India.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a Fundamental Right in the Constitution of India?
qs.e:
The right to property is no longer a Fundamental Right; the 44th Amendment (1978) made it a legal right under Article 300A.
The right to education (21A), right to freedom (19–22) and right against exploitation (23–24) are all Fundamental Rights.
Answer: Right to property

qs.q: Yellow card in badminton indicates:
qs.e:
In badminton a yellow card means a warning for misconduct, a red card means a fault (the opponent gets the point), and a black card means disqualification.
Answer: warning for misconduct

qs.q: Which country hosted the first ever Commonwealth Games in 1930?
qs.e:
The first Commonwealth Games, then called the British Empire Games, were held in 1930 at Hamilton, Ontario, Canada.
They are now held every four years.
Answer: Canada

qs.q: The cost price of an article is ₹800. After allowing a discount of 10%, a gain of 12.5% was made. The marked price of the article is:

Shiva’s monthly salary is Rs.75,000. He spends Rs.12,000 on household items, Rs.14,000 on LIC and mutual funds, Rs.15,000 on his children’s education, and keeps Rs.10,000 for miscellaneous expenses. His savings are Rs.21,000 per month and he donates the rest of the amount to an orphanage. The percentage of his income that he donates is:
Ram sold an item costing Rs.1,250 at a gain of 18% to Ramesh. It was again sold by Ramesh to Shyam at a loss of 10%. Find the selling price of Ramesh.
qs.e:
Ram's SP (Ramesh's CP) = 1250 × 1.18 = ₹1,475.
Ramesh sells at 10% loss: 1475 × 0.9 = ₹1,327.50.
Answer: Rs.1,327.50

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence. My mother said, “Make consistent progress for success.”
qs.e:
'Slow and steady' (wins the race) means steady, consistent progress leads to success.
Origin: Aesop's fable of the tortoise and the hare.
So: My mother said, 'Slow and steady for success.'
Make a habit = do regularly; ins and outs = all the details; do's and don'ts = rules – none means consistent progress.
Answer: slow and steady

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The intern aspired to understand the ins and outs of the operating systems of the institution.
qs.e:
'The ins and outs' means all the details of how something works.
The intern wanted to understand the system in detail.
Strict rules, prior conditions and theories are not 'all the details'.
Answer: Detailed description

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. You also worked with another eccentric genius.
qs.e:
Eccentric = unconventional and slightly strange. E.g. The eccentric scientist wore slippers to work.
Peculiar = strange, odd - the synonym.
Middle = central (from the geometric sense 'off-centre' - a trap); ecological = of the environment; elusive = hard to catch or pin down.
Answer: Peculiar

qs.q: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the underlined word. He declined the offer to join the Board of Directors.
qs.e:
Decline (an offer) = politely refuse. E.g. She declined the invitation.
Rejected = refused - the synonym.
Delayed and deferred = postponed (not refused); modified = changed.
Answer: Rejected

qs.q: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? EDIC, FGJF, ?, HMLL, IPMO
qs.e:
Each letter position moves forward by a fixed step (A=1).
1st: E, F, G, H, I (+1). 2nd: D, G, J, M, P (+3).
3rd: I, J, K, L, M (+1). 4th: C, F, I, L, O (+3).
So the missing cluster is GJKI.
Answer: GJKI

qs.q: A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. GAR, AXS, UUT, ORU, ?
qs.e:
Each letter position moves by a fixed step (A=1, wrap around).
1st: G, A, U, O (−6) → O(15) − 6 = 9 = I. 2nd: A, X, U, R (−3) → R(18) − 3 = 15 = O.
3rd: R, S, T, U (+1) → V.
So the next cluster is IOV.
Answer: IOV

qs.q: In the following question, select the missing number from the given series. 123, 125, 127, ?, 131, 133
qs.e:
Each term is 2 more than the one before: 123, 125, 127 …
127 + 2 = 129; check 129 + 2 = 131 ✓.
Answer: 129

qs.q: If A × B means that A is the father of B, A – B means that A is the mother of B, A + B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the son of P?
qs.e:
Q must be male and P must be Q's parent (× = father, – = mother, + = brother).
P × Q + R: P is Q's father and Q is R's brother → Q is P's son.
P × Q – R makes Q a mother (daughter); Q × P + R makes Q the father; P + R × Q makes P a paternal uncle.
Answer: P × Q + R

qs.q: U $ V means ‘U is the sister of V’ U @ V means ‘U is the husband of V’ U * V means ‘U is the son of V’ U ÷ V means ‘U is the mother of V’ If O $ P * B @ F, how is O related to F?
qs.e:
O $ P: O is P's sister. P * B: P is B's son. B @ F: B is F's husband.
P is the son of B, and F is B's wife, so O and P are children of B and F.
O is female (a sister), so O is F's daughter.
Answer: Daughter

qs.q: Which of the following jurisdictions of the Supreme Court allows it to settle disputes between the centre and state and amongst states?
qs.e:
Under Article 131, the Supreme Court has original (and exclusive) jurisdiction over disputes between the Centre and States or between States.
Appellate jurisdiction hears appeals; advisory gives opinions (Art 143); writ jurisdiction enforces Fundamental Rights (Art 32).
Answer: Original

qs.q: At which of the following places was the FIFA Men's World Cup, held in 2018?
qs.e:
The 2018 FIFA (men's) World Cup was held in Russia; France won, beating Croatia 4-2 in the final at Moscow.
The 2022 edition was in Qatar.
Answer: Russia

qs.q: According to Article 51 A (a) of the Constitution of India, it shall be the duty of every Indian citizen to abide by the ___________ and respect its ideals and institutions.
qs.e:
Fundamental Duty 51A(a): every citizen must abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
Answer: constitution

qs.q: By selling an article for Rs.33,000 a man gains 10%. To get a profit of 20%, he has to sell it for:
A shopkeeper allows a discount of 12% to his customers and still gains 18%. Find the marked price of an article which costs Rs.528 to the shopkeeper.(Answer to the nearest rupees)
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Isn’t knowledge supposed to make life sweeter and happier?
qs.e:
Knowledge = facts, understanding and awareness gained by learning or experience. E.g. Knowledge of history helps us understand today.
Wisdom = knowledge with good judgement - the closest synonym.
Curriculum = course of study; profession = a job; superiority = being better than others.
Answer: Wisdom

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I must tell you that it all went pear-shaped after you left the meeting in the middle.
qs.e:
'To go pear-shaped' means to go badly wrong.
Example: The plan went pear-shaped when the bus broke down.
Entertaining and 'turned out fine' are opposite; 'tragic' is too strong and not the idiom's sense.
Answer: Went terribly wrong

qs.q: Select the idiom from the given options that gives the most appropriate meaning of the highlighted text in the following sentence. A village fair is a place that contains many interesting objects. People of all age groups eagerly wait for this.
qs.e:
'Aladdin's cave' is a place full of many interesting or valuable things.
Origin: the treasure cave in the Arabian Nights story of Aladdin.
A village fair, full of attractive things, is an Aladdin's cave.
Road to Damascus = a sudden change of belief; ivory tower = a place cut off from real life; jewel in the crown = the best part of something.
Answer: Aladdin’s cave
qs.u: a place that contains many interesting objects

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Chide
qs.e:
Chide = scold mildly. E.g. The teacher chided him for coming late.
Scold = speak angrily to someone for a fault - the synonym.
Prevent = stop from happening; rescue = save; follow = go after.
Answer: Scold

qs.q: Ganesh was taking a walk with his mother’s brother’s father’s granddaughter. Who was he walking with?
qs.e:
Ganesh's mother's brother's father is his mother's father, i.e. his maternal grandfather.
The granddaughter of the maternal grandfather is a daughter of his mother's sibling: Ganesh's cousin.
Answer: Cousin

qs.q: The length of the badminton court for singles is:
qs.e:
A badminton court is 13.40 m long for both singles and doubles; the width is 5.18 m for singles and 6.10 m for doubles.
Answer: 13.40 m

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to citizenship?
qs.e:
Articles 5 to 11 in Part II deal with citizenship.
Articles 5–8 decided who was a citizen in 1950, Articles 9–10 cover loss and continuity, and Article 11 lets Parliament regulate citizenship by law (Citizenship Act, 1955).
Articles 2–4 are about new States.
Answer: Articles 5 to 11

qs.q: Who is the Administrative Head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department?
qs.e:
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (Article 148) heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
Accountants General and Principal Accountants General work under the CAG in the States.
Answer: The Comptroller and Auditor General

qs.q: The marked price of mustard oil is 25% more than its cost price. At what percentage less than the marked price should it be sold to have no profit and no loss?
qs.e:
Take CP = 100, MP = 125. For no profit, no loss, SP = 100.
Discount = 25 on 125 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%.
Answer: 20%

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers the following two discount schemes. A) Buy 3 get 4 free B) Buy 5 get 6 free Which scheme has the maximum discount percentage?
o: A does not give any discount
A and B both have the same discount percentage
qs.e:
A: buy 3, get 4 free → 4 free out of 7 = 57.14%.
B: buy 5, get 6 free → 6 free out of 11 = 54.55%.
A gives the larger discount.
Answer: A

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Lily-livered
qs.e:
'Lily-livered' means cowardly, not brave.
Origin: a pale liver (white as a lily) was once thought to show lack of courage.
Example: Only a lily-livered man would run away and leave his friends.
Brave is the opposite; comical and naughty are unrelated.
Answer: Not brave

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Pooja tried to explain the problem, but soon she tied herself up in knots.
o: Be forced to explain your actions and (probably) punished
Become very confused when you are trying to explain something
Make no progress in an argument or discussion
Won’t modify an opinion or agree to even small changes that another person wants
qs.e:
'To tie oneself (up) in knots' means to become very confused while trying to explain something.
Pooja's explanation got more and more muddled.
Option 1 = 'be called to account'; option 3 = 'go round in circles'; option 4 = 'dig one's heels in'.
Answer: Become very confused when you are trying to explain something

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Zealous
qs.e:
Zealous = full of eager devotion to a cause or task. E.g. A zealous volunteer worked through the night.
Enthusiastic = eager and keen - the synonym.
Detached, apathetic and indifferent all mean showing no interest - the antonyms.
Answer: Enthusiastic

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Feeble
qs.e:
Feeble = lacking physical strength; weak. E.g. The feeble old dog could barely walk.
Weak is the synonym.
Unheedful = not paying attention; baneful = harmful; strong = the antonym.
Answer: Weak

The son of my wife is my son; that son's brother is also my son.
Suresha is the daughter of my son, so she is my granddaughter.
The speaker has a wife, so he is male → he is Suresha's grandfather.

qs.q: Which of the following options conveys the meaning of the word ‘Republic’ in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e:
"Republic" in the Preamble means the head of state (the President) is elected – indirectly, for a fixed 5-year term – and is not a hereditary monarch.
Britain, by contrast, is a democracy with a hereditary head (the monarch), so it is not a republic.
Answer: Elected head

qs.q: KA Najeeb Vs Union of India case deals with violation of rights under____________.
qs.e:
In Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb (2021), the Supreme Court held that long imprisonment of an undertrial without a quick trial violates Article 21. So bail can be granted even under strict laws like UAPA.
Article 21 includes the right to a speedy trial.
Answer: Article 21

qs.q: The venue of the 2020 Olympic Games was _________.
qs.e:
The 2020 Summer Olympics were awarded to Tokyo, Japan; because of COVID-19 they were held in July-August 2021 but kept the name Tokyo 2020.
Rio hosted 2016, Sydney 2000, and Los Angeles gets 2028.
Answer: Tokyo

qs.q: Who holds the authority of transferring judges from one High court to another High Court?
o: The senior most judge of Supreme Court
qs.e:
Under Article 222, the President can transfer a judge from one High Court to another after consulting the Chief Justice of India.
In practice, the Supreme Court collegium led by the CJI recommends transfers, but the order is issued by the President.
Answer: The President of India

qs.q: In an election, 2% persons enrolled in the voter list did not participate and 500 votes were invalid. Two candidates A and B fought the election, and A defeated B by 200 votes. If 43% of the persons enrolled in the voter list casted their votes in favour of A, then what is the number of the total casted votes?
qs.e:
Let N = enrolled persons. 98% voted → votes cast = 0.98N; valid = 0.98N − 500.
A = 43% of N = 0.43N; B = 0.43N − 200.
Valid = A + B: 0.86N − 200 = 0.98N − 500 → 0.12N = 300 → N = 2500.
Votes cast = 0.98 × 2500 = 2450.
Answer: 2450

qs.q: An electronic store owner allows two successive discounts of 20% and 25% on each item. The store has a reward points scheme which enables a customer to get free shopping worth ₹0.10 on every 1 reward point credited to the customer’s account on previous purchases from the store. A customer decides to buy a laptop that is marked at ₹72,000. What will be its net selling price if he has 2850 reward points to his credit?
qs.e:
After successive discounts: 72,000 × 0.80 × 0.75 = ₹43,200.
Reward points worth 2850 × 0.10 = ₹285.
Net price = 43,200 − 285 = ₹42,915.
Answer: ₹42,915

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word from the sentence. Ready She was preparing dinner in an organised manner using well-equipped tools while listening to the radio.
qs.e:
Ready (as a verb) = make something ready; prepare. E.g. She readied the room for guests.
In the sentence, she 'was preparing dinner' - preparing is the synonym.
Equipped = provided with tools; organised = arranged; listening = hearing attentively.
Answer: Preparing

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hostile
qs.e:
Hostile = unfriendly and aggressive. E.g. The crowd was hostile to the visiting team.
Unfriendly is the synonym.
Hospitable = welcoming (sound-alike antonym); empathetic = understanding others' feelings; pleasant = nice - all opposite in sense.
Answer: Unfriendly

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To kick the bucket
qs.e:
'To kick the bucket' is an informal way of saying 'to die'.
Example: The old car finally kicked the bucket (here used jokingly for a machine).
Happy, ill and sad are not the meaning.
Answer: To die

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Miss the boat
o: Missing good moments of your life
qs.e:
'To miss the boat' means to miss a good opportunity by being too slow.
Example: I didn't apply in time and missed the boat on that job.
'Being too late' is only part of it; missing transport is literal; 'good moments of life' is vague.
Answer: Missing a good opportunity

qs.q: ‘P @ Q’ means ‘P is the wife of Q’. ‘P # Q’ means ‘P is the brother of Q’. ‘P $ Q’ means ‘P is the father of Q’. ‘P – Q’ means ‘P is the daughter of Q’. If Z – B $ D $ G, then how is Z related to G?
o: Z is the sister of G
Z is the daughter of G
Z  is the father’s sister of G
Z is the mother of G
qs.e:
Z – B: Z is B's daughter. B $ D: B is D's father. D $ G: D is G's father.
Z and D are both B's children, so Z is D's sister.
D is G's father, so Z is G's father's sister.
Answer: Z  is the father’s sister of G

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 15, ?, 27, 39, 55, 75

So the earlier differences are 4 and 8.
15 + 4 = 19, and 19 + 8 = 27 ✓.
Answer: 19

qs.q: 'Penalty Corner' is related to which of the following sports?
qs.e:
A penalty corner is awarded in field hockey for certain fouls by defenders inside their shooting circle; the ball is pushed from the back line and the attackers try to score.
It is not used in tennis, chess or badminton.
Answer: Hockey

qs.q: Thomas Cup is a/an______.
qs.e:
The Thomas Cup (men's world team badminton championship) is held every two years, i.e. a biennial event.
It was started in 1949 and India won it for the first time in 2022.
Answer: biennial event

qs.q: Which Constitutional Amendment added Fundamental Duties in the Constitution?
qs.e:
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added ten Fundamental Duties in Part IV-A (Article 51A), on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.
The 86th Amendment (2002) later added the 11th duty.
Answer: Forty-Second Amendment Act, 1976

qs.q: How many nominated members are there in the Legislative Assembly of Telangana?
qs.e:
Under the old Article 333, Telangana's Assembly had 119 elected members plus one nominated Anglo-Indian member.
The 104th Amendment (2020) ended Anglo-Indian nominations from January 2020, but the answer expected here is the original provision: one.
Answer: One

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The salesman yielded to the demands of his corrupt boss.
qs.e:
Yield (to) = give way under pressure; give in. E.g. The government yielded to public demand.
Conceded = admitted defeat or gave in - the synonym.
Trended = followed a trend; courted = tried to win favour; hounded = pursued or harassed.
Answer: Conceded

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Vennela made a big fuss about a small problem.
o: Get a taste of your own medicine
qs.e:
Idiom: "a storm in a teacup" means a lot of anger or worry about a very small matter.
"Barking up the wrong tree" means blaming or pursuing the wrong thing; "Add insult to injury" means making a bad situation worse; "Get a taste of your own medicine" means being treated as badly as you treated others.
Answer: A storm in a teacup
qs.u: made a big fuss about a small problem

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Matching
qs.e:
Matching = corresponding or similar to something. E.g. She wore a matching scarf and bag.
Resembling = looking like or similar to - the synonym.
Appointing = naming for a job; distinguishing = showing difference (antonym); adoring = loving deeply.
Answer: Resembling

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Peruse
qs.e:
Peruse = read or examine carefully. E.g. He perused the contract before signing.
Check = examine closely - the synonym.
Narrate = tell a story; pursue = chase or follow (a look-alike trap); draw = sketch or pull.
Answer: Check

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. He was offered a __________(moderate) price for his bungalow.
qs.e:
Moderate (price) = not too high, fair. E.g. The hotel charges moderate rates.
Reasonable = fair and sensible, not excessive - the synonym.
Respectable = decent; sustainable = able to be maintained; considerable = large in amount (nearly the opposite).
Answer: reasonable

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Sharp practice
qs.e:
'Sharp practice' means dishonest or barely legal dealing, especially in business.
Example: The shopkeeper was accused of sharp practice for using false weights.
Nearby, frequently and briefly are unrelated.
Answer: Dishonesty

qs.q: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is brother of B’ ‘A – B’ means ‘A is mother of B’ ‘A × B’ means ‘A is husband of B’ ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is sister of B’ If C ÷ B – E + A × F − D, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: D is the daughter of B.
C is the sister of the mother of A.
B is the mother of A.
F is the wife of the son of B.
qs.e:
Decode: C is B's sister; B is E's mother; E is A's brother; A is F's husband; F is D's mother.
So B is the mother of E and A; F is A's wife; D is the child of A and F, i.e. B's grandchild.
C is the sister of A's mother (true); B is A's mother (true); F is the wife of B's son A (true).
D is B's grandchild, not daughter, so that statement is wrong.
Answer: D is the daughter of B.

qs.q: Which of the following countries never hosted the Paralympic games ?
qs.e:
Paralympics hosts include Israel (Tel Aviv 1968), Japan (Tokyo 1964 and 2020) and South Korea (Seoul 1988).
India has never hosted the Paralympic Games.
Answer: India

qs.q: The pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Supreme Court are charged upon _______.
qs.e:
Under Article 146(3), the administrative expenses of the Supreme Court, including the salaries, allowances and pensions of its officers and servants, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Charged expenditure is not put to a vote in Parliament, which protects the Court's independence.
Answer: Consolidated Fund of India

qs.q: When did the Drafting Committee publish the first draft of the Indian Constitution?
qs.e:
The Drafting Committee published the first Draft Constitution in February 1948. People were given 8 months to discuss it and suggest changes.
A second draft was published in October 1948, and the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
Answer: February 1948

qs.q: On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down certain provisions of part IX B of the Constitution of India. Part IX B was related to:
qs.e:
Part IX-B (Articles 243ZH–243ZT), added by the 97th Amendment (2011), deals with Co-operative Societies.
On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down the parts of it that dealt with State co-operatives, because Parliament had not got the States to ratify the amendment.
Answer: Co-operative Societies

qs.q: A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers on an article: i. Two successive discounts of 15% each ii. A discount of 25% followed by a discount of 5% iii. Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% iv. A discount of 30% Under which scheme will the selling price be maximum?
qs.e:
SP is highest where the total discount is lowest. Use a + b − ab/100.
i: 15 + 15 − 2.25 = 27.75%. ii: 25 + 5 − 1.25 = 28.75%. iii: 20 + 10 − 2 = 28%. iv: 30%.
Scheme i has the least discount, so the highest SP.
Answer: Scheme i

Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word given in the sentence. The efforts will be _______________ (vain) if we do not submit the project report on time.

Delightful = pleasing; sensible = wise; careless = without care.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Keep someone at arm’s length
qs.e:
'Keep someone at arm's length' means to avoid becoming too friendly or close with someone.
Example: She keeps salesmen at arm's length.
It does not make the person an enemy, and it is not about playing or bitterness.
Answer: Avoid becoming friendly with someone

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Consent
qs.e:
Consent = permission or agreement. E.g. They married with their parents' consent.
Assent = approval, agreement - the synonym.
Disturb = interrupt; avert = turn away or prevent; dissent = disagreement (the antonym).

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence. Today, the country's nationalists rule the roost and hand out the jobs.
qs.e:
'To rule the roost' means to be in charge, the person in control.
Image: the rooster that dominates the hens' roost.
The nationalists are in control and decide who gets jobs.
Prejudice, exploitation and saving criminals are not the meaning.
Answer: To be in charge

qs.q: ‘P @ Q’ means ‘P is the brother of Q’ ‘P & Q’ means ‘P is the father of Q’ ‘P # Q’ means ‘P is the daughter of Q’ If ‘A # B @ C & D # E’, then how is B related to E?
qs.e:

qs.q: Looking at a picture of a woman Vineeta said, “She is the wife of my father’s brother’s father.” How is the woman in the picture related to Vineeta?
qs.e:
Vineeta's father's brother's father is her father's father (paternal grandfather).
His wife is Vineeta's paternal grandmother, i.e. her father's mother.
Answer: Father’s mother

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 80, 73, 64, 53, 40, ?
qs.e:
Differences: 80−73 = 7, 73−64 = 9, 64−53 = 11, 53−40 = 13 — odd numbers increasing by 2.
Next difference is 15: 40 − 15 = 25.
Answer: 25

qs.q: Fundamental duties were not placed in Part III of the Indian Constitution because Part III is ____________.
qs.e:
Part III (Fundamental Rights) is justiciable: a citizen can go to court to enforce these rights.
Fundamental Duties cannot be enforced by courts, so they were placed separately in Part IV-A, next to the non-justiciable Directive Principles.
Answer: justiciable

qs.q: What was India's rank in Paralympic 2020?
qs.e:
At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, India won 19 medals (5 gold, 8 silver, 6 bronze) and finished 24th in the medal table, its best ever then.
Answer: 24

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
qs.e:
Article 79 says Parliament consists of the President and two Houses – the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha). So Parliament is bicameral.
Art 59 – conditions of the President's office; Art 89 – Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Answer: Article 79

qs.q: On 28 June 2021, the Supreme Court held that persons with disabilities have a right to reservation in promotion under Article 16(4) of the Constitution of India, 1950, in the case of:
o: State of Kerala v. N.M. Thomas
State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
qs.e:
In State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph (28 June 2021), the Supreme Court held that persons with disabilities are entitled to reservation in promotion. It relied on Article 16(4) and the disability law.
Indra Sawhney (1992) is the Mandal case on OBC reservation; N.M. Thomas (1975) dealt with relaxation for SC/ST employees.
Answer: State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph

qs.q: In the Olympic flag, the total number of rings are ________.
qs.e:
The Olympic flag has 5 interlocking rings (blue, yellow, black, green, red) on a white background, standing for the five inhabited continents united by sport.
It was designed by Pierre de Coubertin in 1913.
Answer: 5

qs.q: In a constituency, 90% of the total number of people on the electoral roll cast their votes during an election. 15% of the votes cast were declared invalid. Jeeta secured 60% of the valid votes. If Jeeta secured 91,800 valid votes, what was the total number of people on the electoral roll?
qs.e:
Work backwards. Valid votes = 91800 ÷ 0.60 = 1,53,000.
Votes cast = 153000 ÷ 0.85 = 1,80,000 (since 15% were invalid).
Electoral roll = 180000 ÷ 0.90 = 2,00,000.
Answer: 2,00,000

qs.q: After allowing a discount of 15%, the value of a washing machine is ₹29,750. If no discount is allowed, then the shopkeeper gains 12%. The cost price of the washing machine is:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Do not beat about the bush when you have anything to say.

'Beat about the bush' means to avoid coming to the point or giving a clear answer.

So: say directly what you have to say.
Influencing, shifting blame and arguing are different behaviours.
Answer: To avoid giving a definite answer or position

‘A + B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’. If H + I – J × K × L – M ÷ N, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: H is the husband of the sister of K.
J is the wife of the son of M.
H is the husband of the daughter of M.
H is the husband of the sister of L.
qs.e:
Decode: H is I's father; I is J's son; J is K's sister; K is L's sister; L is M's son; M is N's wife.
So H and J are I's parents (J is H's wife); J, K and L are siblings, children of M.
H is the husband of J, the sister of K and L and the daughter of M, so options 1, 3 and 4 are true.
J is M's daughter, not the wife of M's son, so that statement is wrong.
Answer: J is the wife of the son of M.

qs.q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Centre-State Relations pertaining to the three lists of the Indian Constitution? A.The subjects which are not included in any of the three lists are called Residuary subjects. B.If there is any conflict between the Union List and the State List, then the former prevails. C.When the Parliament enacts a law on the request of two or more states, then that law made by the Parliament on the State List is applicable to all the states.
qs.e:
A is correct: subjects not in any list are residuary subjects, and Parliament can make laws on them (Art 248).
B is correct: if the Union List and State List conflict, the Union List prevails (Art 246).
C is wrong: under Article 252, a law Parliament makes at the request of two or more States applies only to those States and to any others that later adopt it by resolution.
Answer: A and B only

qs.q: Which country will host the 2031 Cricket World Cup ?

qs.q: The number of on-field umpires in cricket matches is _______.
qs.e:
A cricket match has 2 on-field umpires: one at the bowler's end and one at square leg.
A third (TV) umpire and a fourth umpire help off the field, and a match referee oversees conduct.
Answer: 2

qs.q: The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Constitution of India, upon the recommendations of which of the following committees?
qs.e:

Kelkar and Raja Chelliah dealt with tax reforms, and Santhanam with the prevention of corruption.
Answer: Swaran Singh Committee

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The case of Vanuatu in 2020 is a clear example of the constant and complex challenges faced by SIDS. qs.q: Read the given sentence and select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘Vigilant’ from the following options. The burglar was very cautious, so he avoided the security perfectly as they didn’t find any proof.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Harangue

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Back against the wall
o: Be in an easy situation from where escape is difficult
Be in a difficult situation from where escape is difficult
Be in a difficult situation from where escape is easy
Be in a relationship which one wants to escape

Option 1 calls it easy; option 3 says escape is easy; option 4 is about relationships.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To prime the pump

qs.q: In India The State election Commissioner is appointed by the _________ .
qs.e:

He can be removed only like a High Court judge, which protects his independence.

qs.q: Maximum how many overs can a bowler bowl in ODI cricket matches?
qs.e:
In a 50-over ODI, a bowler may bowl at most one-fifth of the overs, i.e. 50 ÷ 5 = 10 overs.
In a T20 the limit is 4 overs.
Answer: 10

qs.q: According to Article _________of the Constitution of India, it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
qs.e:

All 11 duties are in Article 51A (Part IV-A). Articles 49A, 50A and 52A do not exist.

qs.q: How many points are there in the 4th set in volleyball?
qs.e:
In volleyball, sets 1 to 4 are played to 25 points (with a 2-point lead), and only the deciding 5th set is played to 15.
So the 4th set is played to 25 points.

qs.q: The percentage profit earned by selling an article for ₹2,000 is the same as the percentage loss incurred by selling the same article for ₹1,200. At what price should that article be sold to make a profit of 20%?

qs.q: The difference (in ₹) between a discount of 35% on ₹3,600 and two successive discounts of 30% and 5% on the same amount is:

qs.q: The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State shall NOT exceed ________ of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State.

qs.q: Sports Authority of India, the apex body for sports promotion, was set up in the year _______.

The Sports Authority of India (SAI) was set up in 1984 under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, following the 1982 Asian Games in Delhi.

qs.q: The origin of Directive Principles of State Policy can be traced to which of the following?
qs.e:
The Directive Principles trace back to the Karachi Resolution of the Congress (1931). It set out fundamental rights together with an economic programme – living wages, free primary education, State control of key industries.
It was drafted by Nehru and adopted under Sardar Patel's presidency. The detailed DPSP text itself was modelled on the Irish Constitution.

qs.q: ‘We have wings' is associated with which of the following sports events?
qs.e:
'We Have Wings' was the theme of the opening ceremony of the Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games (held in 2021).
It showed a one-winged plane learning to fly, a symbol of the courage of para-athletes.
Answer: Paralympic 2020

qs.q: The marked price of a ceiling fan is ₹4,200 and the shopkeeper allows a discount of 5% on it. If his profit is 14%, then the cost price of the fan is:
By selling a watch for ₹2,000, a shopkeeper loses 20%. How much would he gain or lose by selling it for ₹3,000?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Consequence
qs.e:
Consequence = a result or effect of an action. E.g. Failing was the consequence of not studying.
Outcome = result - the synonym.
Start, origin and begin all refer to the beginning - the opposite end.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. It turns out to be a blessing in disguise.

Has a very good effect on a situation or a thing
When a simple solution solves a problem very well
When things get better and better when least expecting it

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The committee wanted us to explain this in detail.
qs.e:
Explain (in detail) = make clear by describing fully. E.g. Please explain the rules.
Elaborate = explain in more detail - the synonym.
Collect = gather; trouble = difficulty; keen = eager.
Answer: Elaborate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Through thick and thin
o: In good times and in bad times
qs.e:
'Through thick and thin' means in good times and bad times, under all conditions.
Example: They have supported their team through thick and thin.
Option 1 covers only hard times, option 2 only good times; option 4 is unrelated.
Answer: In good times and in bad times

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The outcome document of the Rio+20 Conference, the Future We Want, underscores climate change as “an inevitable and urgent global challenge with long-term implications for the sustainable development of all countries”. Through the document, Member States express their concern about the continuous rising of emissions of greenhouse gases and the vulnerability of all countries, particularly developing countries, to the adverse impacts of climate change.
qs.e:
Inevitable = certain to happen; impossible to avoid or deny. E.g. Change is inevitable.
Undeniable = certain, cannot be denied - the closest synonym given.
Escapable = can be avoided (antonym); adventurous = daring; immemorable = not memorable.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Unbiased
qs.e:
Unbiased = fair, not influenced by personal opinion. E.g. A judge must be unbiased.
Objective = based on facts, not feelings - the synonym.
Organisational = of an organisation; subjective = based on personal feelings (antonym); definitive = final.
Answer: Objective

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the highlighted word. The government’s utilitarian stance was appreciated by all.
qs.e:
Utilitarian = designed to be useful and practical. E.g. The building has a plain, utilitarian design.
Useful is the synonym.
Thrust = push; fanciful = imaginative, unrealistic (opposite of practical); distasteful = unpleasant.
Answer: useful

qs.q: Which of the following states has won the 2022 Santosh Trophy?
qs.e:
Kerala won the 76th Santosh Trophy (the 2021-22 edition, played in 2022), beating West Bengal in the final on penalties at Malappuram.
The Santosh Trophy is India's national football championship between state teams; it was Kerala's 7th title.
West Bengal is the tempting option: they hold the most titles, but they were the losing finalists this time.

qs.q: In which of the following Sessions of the IOC Executive Board Meeting was Brisbane voted to host the 2032 Olympics and Paralympics?

Brisbane (Australia) was elected host of the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games at the 138th IOC Session in Tokyo on 21 July 2021, just before the Tokyo Games opened.

qs.q: Which part of the Constitution of India incorporates the Directive Principles of State Policy?
qs.e:
The Directive Principles of State Policy are in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution.
Part III has the Fundamental Rights; Part V deals with the Union and Part VI with the States.
Answer: Part IV

qs.q: During a division, Suhas mistakenly took as the dividend a number that was 10% less than the original dividend. He also mistakenly took as the divisor a number that was 20% less than the original divisor. If the correct quotient of the original division problem was 24 and the remainder was 0, what was the quotient that Suhas obtained, assuming his calculations had no error?
qs.e:
Correct quotient = dividend ÷ divisor = 24.
Wrong quotient = (0.9 × dividend) ÷ (0.8 × divisor) = 24 × 0.9/0.8.
= 24 × 1.125 = 27.
Answer: 27

qs.q: A dealer purchased a washing machine for ₹9,000. He allows a discount of 10% on its marked price and still gains 10%. Find the marked price of the machine.

(N+18) persons, each working for 7.5 hours a day, can complete 48% of a work in 20 days. (N+12) persons can complete the remaining work in 30 days, if each of them works for 6.5 hours per day. Determine the value of N.
qs.e:
Work done ∝ persons × hours per day × days. Both groups must give the same work per unit of man-hours.
(N + 18) × 7.5 × 20 / 48 = (N + 12) × 6.5 × 30 / 52 (remaining work = 52%).
150(N + 18)/48 = 195(N + 12)/52 → 3.125(N + 18) = 3.75(N + 12).
3.125N + 56.25 = 3.75N + 45 → 0.625N = 11.25 → N = 18.
Answer: 18

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. He is very ___________ (Eager) to join the Air Force.

Unconcerned = not worried or interested (antonym); dubious = doubtful; irksome = annoying.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get into a scrape

qs.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ‘Habitual’ may be replaced by ‘_________’.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The benevolent gesture of the rich merchant was appreciated by all.

Benevolent = kind and generous. E.g. A benevolent donor funded the school.

Sober = serious, calm; numb = without feeling; sombre = dark or gloomy.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tedious
qs.e:
Tedious = too long, slow or dull; tiring. E.g. Copying the list by hand was tedious.
Tiresome = boring and tiring - the synonym.
Threescore = sixty; repetitive = repeating (a cause of tedium, not the same meaning); wholesome = healthy, good.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Gift of the gab
qs.e:
'Gift of the gab' means a natural ability to speak fluently and persuasively.
Example: With his gift of the gab, he is a born salesman.
