qs.e:
L is M's sister, M is N's sister, N is O's wife, O is P's father and P is Q's brother.
So M is the sister of O's wife N, P (a male) is N's son, and O is also Q's father: these are all true.
L is N's sister, not her daughter, so that statement is false.
Answer: L is the daughter of N.

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 2, 4, 12, 48, 240, ?
Looking at Suraj's picture, Gaurav said, "He is the son of my grandfather's only son." How is Gaurav related to Suraj, the boy in the picture?
qs.e:
Gaurav's grandfather's only son is Gaurav's father.
Suraj is a son of Gaurav's father, and he is a different person from Gaurav.
So Gaurav and Suraj are brothers.
Answer: Brother

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
qs.e:
Equality (Art. 14-18), Freedom (Art. 19-22) and Freedom of Religion (Art. 25-28) are Fundamental Rights in Part III.
The right to vote comes from Article 326 and the election laws, so it is a constitutional and statutory right, not a Fundamental Right.
Answer: Right to Vote

qs.q: The National Sports University is located in which of the following states?
qs.e:
India's first National Sports University was set up in Imphal, Manipur, under the National Sports University Act, 2018.
Answer: Manipur

qs.q:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the removal of the President of India?
A. Impeachment proceedings can be started in either House of Parliament.
B. The impeachment charges must be signed by one-third of the members of the House in which the proceedings begin.
C. The President must be given 30 days' notice in the impeachment proceedings.
D. The impeachment resolution is passed by a majority of two-thirds of the total membership of that House.
qs.e:
Under Article 61, either House can start impeachment, and each House must pass it by two-thirds of its total membership, so A and D are true.
The charges must be signed by one-fourth of the members (not one-third), and the President gets 14 days' notice (not 30), so B and C are false.
Answer: Only A and D

qs.q: The case 'State of Kerala vs Leesamma Joseph' is related to which of the following?
qs.e:
In State of Kerala v. Leesamma Joseph (2021), the Supreme Court held that persons with disabilities are entitled to reservation in promotion, not only at entry.
The case had nothing to do with dowry, education or the EWS quota.
Answer: Persons with disabilities

qs.q: Singhraj Adhana is associated with which of the following sports?
qs.e:
Singhraj Adhana is an Indian para-shooter.
He won bronze in the P1 10 m air pistol and silver in the P4 50 m pistol at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.
Answer: Shooting

qs.q: A saree bought for ₹500 is marked at 16% profit and later on sold at a sales discount of x% on the marked price. If the selling price of the saree is ₹493, find the value of x.

The monthly income of a person was Rs.80,000 and his monthly expenditure was Rs.45,000. Next year, his income increased by 16% and his expenditure increased by 8%. Find the percentage increase in his savings (correct to 2 decimal places).
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given idiom. She is an awful bore; she is always blowing her own saxophone.
qs.e:
Idiom: "blow one's own trumpet" means to praise oneself or boast, which is why she is a bore.
"violin", "lyre" and "flute" do not form this idiom (and a violin or lyre is not blown).
Answer: trumpet

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vendetta
qs.e:
Vendetta = a long, bitter quarrel or feud. E.g. The two families carried on a vendetta for years.
Disagreement (a strong quarrel) is the closest option.
Dilemma = a hard choice; vacillation = wavering; passion = strong emotion.
Answer: Disagreement

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Incredible
qs.e:
Incredible = impossible or hard to believe. E.g. His story of escape sounded incredible.
Unbelievable is the synonym.
Reasonable and realistic = sensible, believable (antonyms); unachievable = impossible to achieve (about doing, not believing).
Answer: Unbelievable

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Blow something out of (all) proportion.
o: Make things difficult for someone without reason
Behave as if something that has happened is much worse than it really is
Leave someone at a time when they need you to stay and help them
Control the level of something in order to stop it increasing
qs.e:
'To blow something out of (all) proportion' means to treat something as much more serious than it really is.
Example: It was a small scratch, but she blew it out of proportion.
Option 1 = 'make life difficult'; option 3 = 'leave in the lurch'; option 4 = 'keep a lid on'.
Answer: Behave as if something that has happened is much worse than it really is

qs.q: If, ‘B % D’ means ‘B is the brother of D’, ‘B & D’ means ‘B is the mother of D’, 'B × D’ means ‘B is the husband of D’, ‘B # D’ means ‘B is the sister of D’, ‘B $ D’ means ‘B is the son of D’, ‘B @ D’ means ‘B is the father of D’, then which of the given options is correct regarding the following expression? S & Z $ F % B % E @ G
o: Z is the son of E’s brother
B is the maternal uncle of Z.
S is the mother of G.
E is the sister of F.
qs.e:
S & Z: S is Z's mother. Z $ F: Z is F's son. F % B: F is B's brother. B % E: B is E's brother. E @ G: E is G's father.
F is male and Z's parent, so F is Z's father; F, B and E are brothers.
So Z is the son of E's brother F (option 1 true). B is Z's paternal uncle, not maternal; S is Z's mother, not G's; E is a father, so not a sister.
Answer: Z is the son of E’s brother

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 17, 24, 38, 59, 87, ?
qs.e:
Differences are multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, then 35.
87 + 35 = 122.
Answer: 122

qs.q: Which of the given letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? DMHR, AJEO, XGBL, ?, RAVF
qs.e:
Every letter moves 3 places back from one term to the next.
XGBL → X−3 = U, G−3 = D, B−3 = Y, L−3 = I → UDYI; check UDYI −3 → RAVF.
Answer: UDYI

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ _ SRDAT _ _ DA _ SR _ _ TS _ D
qs.e:
The repeating block is ATSRD (5 letters).
ATSRD ATSRD ATSRD ATSRD fills the blanks with A, T, S, R, T, D, A, R.
Answer: ATSRTDAR

qs.q: P, M, Z, A and L are part of a five-member family and all except L are females. Z and L are in a marital relationship and P, M and A are their children. How is M related to Z?
qs.e:
Generation 1: Z and L are a married couple. L is the only male, so L is the husband and Z is the wife (mother).
Generation 2: P, M and A are their children, and all of them are female.
So M is a female child of Z.
Answer: Daughter

qs.q: Which number should replace the question mark (?) in the following number series? 5475, 1100, 225, 50, ?, 8, 6.6
The 36th National games was organised by____.
qs.e:
Gujarat hosted the 36th National Games from 29 September to 12 October 2022, with events in Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot and Bhavnagar.
These were the first National Games after a 7-year gap (the 35th were in Kerala in 2015). Services topped the medal table.
Answer: Gujarat

qs.q: In case an Indian citizen is arrested and denied the right to be defended, then in such a situation, which Article of the Indian Constitution can provide a relief?
qs.e:
Article 22(1) says an arrested person must be told the grounds of arrest and cannot be denied the right to consult and be defended by a lawyer of his choice.
It also requires production before a magistrate within 24 hours. Art 23–24 deal with exploitation and Art 25 with religion.
Answer: Article 22

qs.q: Who among the following became the first Indian female sailor to qualify for the Olympics when she qualified for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics?
qs.e:
Nethra Kumanan of Tamil Nadu became the first Indian woman sailor to qualify for the Olympics. She earned her Tokyo 2020 place in the Laser Radial class in 2021.
The others: Maana Patel is a swimmer, Manu Bhaker is a shooter and Bhavani Devi is a fencer (she was India's first Olympic fencer).
Answer: Nethra Kumanan

qs.q: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission can be removed by the order of the ____________.
qs.e:
Under Article 317, the Chairman or a member of a State Public Service Commission is appointed by the Governor but can be removed only by the President.
Grounds include misbehaviour (after a Supreme Court inquiry), insolvency, outside paid work or infirmity.
Answer: President

qs.q: In February 2022, the Delhi High Court reserved judgement on a series of Public Interest Litigations (PILs) challenging which exception in Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC)?
qs.e:
The PILs challenged Exception 2 to Section 375 of the IPC (the marital rape exception), which said sex by a man with his wife (not under 15) is not rape.
In May 2022 the Delhi High Court gave a split verdict, and the matter went to the Supreme Court.
Answer: Marital rape

qs.q: Where were the 35th National Games held in the year 2015?
qs.e:
Kerala hosted the 35th National Games from 31 January to 14 February 2015, with Thiruvananthapuram as the main venue.
Services finished top of the medal table. The next edition (the 36th) came only in 2022, in Gujarat.
Answer: Kerala

qs.q: Select the option that is similar in meaning to the given word. Hapless
qs.e:
Hapless = unlucky. E.g. The hapless traveller lost his bag twice.
Unfortunate = having bad luck - the synonym.
Distasteful = unpleasant; fortunate = lucky (antonym); happy = joyful (a sound-alike trap).
Answer: Unfortunate

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. She had the temerity to call her teacher a liar.
qs.e:
Temerity = excessive boldness; rude nerve. E.g. He had the temerity to question the judge.
Impudence = rude, disrespectful boldness - the synonym.
Tedious = boring; trenchant = sharp, forceful; taciturn = quiet, reserved.
Answer: impudence

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. It is raining cats and dogs means:
o: something that does not upset you
qs.e:
'It is raining cats and dogs' means it is raining very heavily.
Example: Take an umbrella; it's raining cats and dogs.
Drizzling and showers mean light rain – the opposite; option 3 is unrelated.
Answer: it is raining very heavily

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Taking a bull by the horns
o: To decapitate a bull for beef
To make a stupid decision thinking it to be daring
To deal with a difficult situation in a very direct or confident way
qs.e:
'Take the bull by the horns' means to face a difficult situation directly and confidently.
Example: She took the bull by the horns and confronted the manager about the delay.
The other options are literal or wrongly call it a stupid decision.
Answer: To deal with a difficult situation in a very direct or confident way

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ _ D C D _ _ C D _ D _
o: D C C D C C
C D D C C D
D C D C D D
C D C D C C
qs.e:
The series is just DC repeated: DC DC DC DC DC DC.
Blanks are filled by D, C, C, D, C, C.
Answer: D C C D C C

qs.q: A # B means ‘A is the father of B’ A @ B means ‘A is the brother of B’ A & B means ‘A is the son of B’ If H & I @ J # K @ L, then how is J related to L?
qs.e:
H & I: H is I's son. I @ J: I is J's brother. J # K: J is K's father. K @ L: K is L's brother.
K and L are siblings, so J, the father of K, is also L's father.
Answer: Father

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BFZV, EIXT, HLVR, ?, NRRN
qs.e:
1st letters: B, E, H, K, N (+3). 2nd: F, I, L, O, R (+3).
3rd: Z, X, V, T, R (−2). 4th: V, T, R, P, N (−2).
Missing term: K, O, T, P.
Answer: KOTP

qs.q: Which number would replace the question mark (?) in the following number series? 131, 132, 141, 166, 215, ?, 417
qs.e:
Differences are squares of odd numbers: 1², 3², 5², 7², 9², 11² = 1, 9, 25, 49, 81, 121.
215 + 81 = 296; check 296 + 121 = 417.
Answer: 296

qs.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Finance Commission of India? A. The Finance Commission consist of a Chairman and four other members. B. The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are binding on the government and government needs to grant funds according to the advice of the Commission. C. Article 280 of the Indian Constitution talks about the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
qs.e:
A is correct: under Article 280 the Finance Commission has a Chairman and four other members, appointed by the President every five years.
B is wrong: its recommendations are only advisory and do not bind the government.
C is treated as wrong: Article 280 sets up the Commission and its duties, while Article 281 deals with its recommendations (laid before Parliament with an action-taken memo).
Answer: A only

qs.q: Which of the following Amendment Acts added four new subjects (Article 39, 39A, 43A, 48A) in the Directive Principles of State Policy?
qs.e:
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added new Directive Principles: Article 39(f) (healthy development of children), 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), 43A (workers' participation in management) and 48A (protection of environment, forests and wildlife).
Answer: 42nd Amendment Act, 1976

qs.q: When were the Commonwealth Games-2022 conducted?
qs.e:
The 2022 Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022.
India won 61 medals (22 gold) and finished 4th. Shooting was left out of this edition.
Answer: From 28 July 2022 to 8 August 2022

qs.q: The colours of the squares used in a chessboard are ________.
qs.e:
A chessboard has 64 squares (8 × 8) in two alternating colours, light and dark, and these are called white and black.
Each player sets up the board with a white (light) square in the right-hand corner nearest to them.
Answer: white and black

qs.q: Pass percentage of an examination is 35%. If a student who got 210 marks, failed by 14 marks, then what are the maximum marks of the examination?
qs.e:
He failed by 14 marks, so pass marks = 210 + 14 = 224.
224 = 35% of maximum → maximum = 224 × 100/35 = 640.
Answer: 640

qs.q: A dealer’s cost price for each fan he would like to sell is ₹2,000. After allowing a discount of 20% on its marked price, he gains 20%. His marked price of the fan is:

The cost price and selling price of rice are the same. Due to a faulty weighing machine, the seller earns a 15% profit. If Rs. x is the cost price of 1000 gm rice and the machine is changed which shows 1000 gm instead of 950 gm, what should be the selling price (in ₹) now to get the same percentage of profit?
qs.e:
The new machine shows 1000 g but gives only 950 g, whose cost is 0.95x.
To keep a 15% profit: SP = 0.95x × 1.15 = 1.0925x.
Answer: 1.0925x

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. From the outset of the pandemic, the United Nations system mobilised early and comprehensively. It led on the global health response, provided life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable, established instruments for rapid responses to the socio-economic impact and laid out a broad policy agenda for action on all fronts.
qs.e:
Vulnerable = exposed to harm or attack. E.g. Children are vulnerable to infections.
At risk is the synonym - the most vulnerable are those most exposed to harm.
Adaptable = able to adjust; arrogant = proud; poor = without money (often vulnerable, but not the meaning).
Answer: at risk

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Immerse
qs.e:
Immerse = dip into a liquid; deeply involve oneself in something. E.g. She immersed herself in her studies.
Involve (deeply) is the synonym.
Emerge = come out (antonym); uncover = reveal; distant = far away.
Answer: Involve

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The peasants worked the whole day in the fields and stopped working in the evening and went to their homes.
qs.e:
Idiom: "call it a day" means to stop working for the day.
So: "The peasants worked the whole day in the fields and called it a day and went to their homes."
"gave it a whirl" means tried something; "put ice on it" is not an idiom for stopping; "ran around in circles" means being busy without progress.
Answer: called it a day

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 245, 212, ?, 146, 113, 80
qs.e:
Each term is 33 less than the previous one.
212 − 33 = 179; check 179 − 33 = 146, 146 − 33 = 113, 113 − 33 = 80.
Answer: 179

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? EJCK, GMDO, IPES, ?, MVGA
qs.e:
1st letters: E, G, I, K, M (+2). 2nd: J, M, P, S, V (+3).
3rd: C, D, E, F, G (+1). 4th: K, O, S, W, A (+4).
Missing term: KSFW.
Answer: KSFW

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ R Q _ P R _ S _ _ Q S P R Q _
o: P R Q S P S
P S R Q P S
P Q R S P R
P S Q P R S
qs.e:
The repeating block is PRQS (4 letters).
PRQS PRQS PRQS PRQS fills the blanks with P, S, Q, P, R, S.
Answer: P S Q P R S

qs.q: Amil points towards a girl and says she is his only daughter’s father’s paternal grandfather’s granddaughter. Amil’s father has no siblings. How is the girl related to Amil?
qs.e:
Amil's only daughter's father is Amil himself.
Amil's paternal grandfather's granddaughters are the daughters of his sons; Amil's father has no siblings, so the only son is Amil's father.
So the girl is a daughter of Amil's father, i.e. Amil's sister.
Answer: Sister

qs.q: Which of the following countries will host the para badminton championship in 2023?
qs.e:
Thailand was given the 2023 BWF Para-Badminton World Championships. The event went to Pattaya and was finally played in February 2024.
The previous edition (2022) was in Tokyo. Indian para shuttlers such as Pramod Bhagat and Krishna Nagar compete in these championships.
Answer: Thailand

qs.q: In February 2021, In which of the following cases did the Court observe that Consent of a family is not needed once two adults decide to marry?
o: Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh
Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana
Rahul Sharma v. National Insurance Company Ltd.
Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka
qs.e:
In Laxmibai Chandaragi v. State of Karnataka (February 2021), the Supreme Court said that when two adults decide to marry, the consent of the family or community is not needed.
The Court tied this to the right to choose a partner under Article 21.
Answer: Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka

qs.q: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with fundamental rights?
qs.e:
Part III (Articles 12–35) contains the Fundamental Rights.
Part VI – the States; Part IX – Panchayats; Part XI – relations between the Union and the States.
Answer: Part III

qs.q: The finance commission of India is required to make recommendations to the ___________.
qs.e:
Under Article 280(3), the Finance Commission makes its recommendations to the President of India, for example on sharing taxes between the Centre and the States.
The President then lays the report before Parliament under Article 281.
Answer: President of India

qs.q: FTX Crypto Cup is associated with which of the following sports events?
qs.e:
The FTX Crypto Cup is a chess event: it was the final of the Meltwater Champions Chess Tour, held in Miami in August 2022.
Magnus Carlsen won it, and India's teenage grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa came second after beating Carlsen in their match.
Answer: Chess

qs.q: If successive discounts of 5%, 10% and p% are equivalent to a single discount of 31.6%, then the value of p is:
Identify the sentence that provides the meaning of the given idiom. Under the cloud
o: The classmates were dancing together under the rain.
The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car.
The Red fort looks beautiful amidst the cloudy weather and cold atmosphere.
It was the best place to sit under the sky with hands full of food.
qs.e:
'Under a cloud' means under suspicion or in disgrace.
Sentence 2 uses this sense: the driver was under suspicion after blood was found on his car.
Sentences 1, 3 and 4 refer to actual rain, clouds or sky, not suspicion.
Answer: The driver was under suspicion after the police found blood on his car.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. She looked ___________(luminous) in the diamond necklace.
qs.e:
Luminous = shining, giving off light. E.g. The luminous moon lit the path.
Resplendent = dazzling, splendid in appearance - it fits a woman in a diamond necklace.
Strident = loud and harsh; transcendent = going beyond normal limits; impudent = rude.
Answer: resplendent

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Once in a blue moon
qs.e:
'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely.
Origin: a 'blue moon' – an extra full moon – comes only every two or three years.
Example: My brother calls home once in a blue moon.
High, colourful and ancient are unrelated.
Answer: Very rare

qs.q: ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’. If D @ N @ H & Y @ F % V, then how is V related to H?
qs.e:
D @ N: D is N's daughter. N @ H: N is H's daughter. H & Y: H is Y's husband. Y @ F: Y is F's daughter. F % V: F is V's wife.
F and V are Y's parents, so V is Y's father.
Y is H's wife, so V is H's wife's father.
Answer: Wife’s father

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? WUS, QOM, KIG, ?
qs.e:
Each letter moves 6 places back from one term to the next.
K−6 = E, I−6 = C, G−6 = A.
Answer: ECA

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 6, ?, 54, 162, 486
qs.e:
Each term is 3 times the previous one.
6 × 3 = 18; check 18 × 3 = 54, 54 × 3 = 162.
Answer: 18

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the following blanks, will complete the letter-series. A S D F _ A _ _ F G _ U D _ G A _ _ F G
o: G T D A F V D
F T D A F V D
F T E A F W D
G T E A G X E
qs.e:
Groups of five: A?DFG, where the 2nd letter goes S, T, U, V.
ASDFG ATDFG AUDFG AVDFG → blanks G, T, D, A, F, V, D.
Answer: G T D A F V D

qs.q: A % B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A $ B means ‘A is the son of B’ A * B means ‘A is the sister of B’ If H % I $ J $ K * L, then how is H related to J?
qs.e:
H % I: H is I's daughter. I $ J: I is J's son. (J $ K, K * L are not needed.)
H is the daughter of J's son.
Answer: Son’s daughter

qs.q: The first modern Olympic Games was held in the year ______.
qs.e:
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
They were revived by Pierre de Coubertin, whose efforts led to the IOC being set up in 1894. The 1900 Games (Paris) were the second edition.
Answer: 1896

qs.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Parliamentary Committees? A. A minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee. B. The members of the Estimates Committee are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. C. A minister can be a member of the Estimates Committee if he is nominated by the Speaker. D. A member of the Committee on Public Undertakings will have tenure of 2 years.
qs.e:
A is correct: a minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee.
B is wrong: Estimates Committee members are elected by the Lok Sabha by proportional representation, not nominated by the Speaker.
C is wrong: a minister cannot be on the Estimates Committee either. D is wrong: committee members serve one year, not two.
Answer: A only

qs.q: In December 2021, who among the following became the first-ever Indian male shuttler to play in the final of the BWF World Championship Final?
qs.e:
Kidambi Srikanth became the first Indian man to reach the final of the BWF World Championships, at Huelva (Spain) in December 2021.
He lost the final to Loh Kean Yew of Singapore and took silver. Lakshya Sen won bronze at the same event.
B Sai Praneeth had won bronze in 2019, and Chirag Shetty is a doubles player.
Answer: Kidambi Srikanth

qs.q: During which of the following periods was the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup held in 2022?
qs.e:
India hosted the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup from 11 to 30 October 2022, with matches in Bhubaneswar, Goa and Navi Mumbai.
Spain won the title by beating Colombia in the final. It was India's first time hosting a FIFA women's tournament.
Answer: 11-30 October

qs.q: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India enshrines to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture?
qs.e:
Fundamental Duty 51A(f) asks every citizen to value and preserve the rich heritage of India's composite culture.
Others: Art 48A – protecting the environment (DPSP); Art 43A – workers in management (DPSP); Art 124A – the National Judicial Appointments Commission (struck down in 2015).
Answer: Article 51 (A)

qs.q: John got 20% marks in an examination and failed by 10 marks. In the same examination, Jack got 35% marks which were 20 more than the minimum passing marks. Find the percentage of minimum marks required to pass.
qs.e:
Let M = maximum marks. Passing marks = 20% of M + 10 = 35% of M − 20.
15% of M = 30 → M = 200.
Passing marks = 40 + 10 = 50 → 50/200 × 100 = 25%.
Answer: 25

qs.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods in such a way that after allowing a discount of 22% he gains 20%. If the cost price of the article is ₹650, then its marked price is:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fierce
qs.e:
Fierce = violent, aggressive or intense. E.g. A fierce dog guarded the gate.
Aggressive is the synonym.
Fanatic = an extreme follower; fraud = a cheat; gentle = mild (antonym).
Answer: Aggressive

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the following sentence. During the wedding ceremony, the bride seemed even quieter and more diffident than usual.
o: Shy due to lack of confidence.
Giving a false or misleading impression
qs.e:
Diffident = shy and lacking confidence. E.g. The diffident boy never spoke in class.
So 'shy due to lack of confidence' is the meaning; 'quieter' supports it.
Bold in others' company = confident (antonym); lack of interest = indifferent; false impression = misleading.
Answer: Shy due to lack of confidence.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Your career is now completely obsolete.
qs.e:
Idiom: "as dead as a doornail" means completely dead, finished or no longer useful — a career that is completely obsolete.
"moving like a worm" is not an idiom for this; "dead even" means exactly equal; "hanging by a thread" means in great danger but not yet finished.
Answer: as dead as a doornail

qs.q: Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. My business partners thought that I would simply accept their cheating, but they will soon realise that I am more powerful than what they expected.
qs.e:
'To catch a Tartar' means to deal with someone who proves far stronger or tougher than expected.
Origin: soldiers who tried to capture a Tartar warrior found themselves captured.
The cheating partners will find the speaker much more powerful than they thought – they caught a tartar.
Casting pearls before swine = offering good things to those who cannot value them; damsel in distress = a woman needing rescue; cutting a cloth is not the idiom here.
Answer: they caught a tartar
qs.u: I am more powerful than what they expected

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Jargon
qs.e:
Jargon = special words used by a profession or group, hard for others to understand. E.g. Legal jargon confuses ordinary readers.
Slang = informal words used by a particular group - the closest option.
Eloquence = fluent, persuasive speech; formality = strict correctness; verboseness = wordiness.
Answer: Slang

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. Arthur has some strange ideas, but on this occasion, I am inclined to agree with him.
qs.e:
Inclined (to) = tending or willing to do something. E.g. I am inclined to believe him.
Tended is the synonym - leaning towards agreeing.
Conflicted = torn between choices; refused = said no (antonym); conspired = plotted secretly.
Answer: tended

qs.q: A % B means ‘A is the daughter of B’ A = B means ‘A is the sister of B’ A $ B means ‘A is the father of B’ If E = F = G $ H = I, then how is G related to E?
qs.e:

E, F and G are siblings, and G is a father, so G is male.
So G is E's brother.
Answer: Brother

qs.q: The feature of fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution is adopted from which of the following countries?
qs.e:
India's Fundamental Duties were modelled on the Constitution of the former Soviet Union (USSR), which listed citizens' duties alongside their rights.
The USSR also inspired the ideals of justice (social, economic and political) in the Preamble.
Answer: Soviet Union (USSR)

qs.q: The Nehru trophy boat race was organised by which of the following states?
qs.e:
The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is a snake-boat race (chundan vallam) held every year on Punnamada Lake near Alappuzha, Kerala.
It began in 1952 after Jawaharlal Nehru visited and was thrilled by a race. It is usually held on the second Saturday of August.
Answer: Kerala

qs.q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the State Executive? A. Article 152 of the Indian Constitution states ‘Unless the context otherwise requires, the expression ‘State’ does not include Jammu and Kashmir’. B. The 7th Constitutional Amendment Act has provided for the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more states. C. The Supreme Court clearly mentioned that the office of the Governor is under the control of the Central Government.
qs.e:
A is correct (for the text at the time): Article 152 said "State" did not include Jammu and Kashmir, which had its own constitution. This changed when Article 370 was effectively removed in 2019.
B is correct: the 7th Amendment, 1956 added the proviso to Article 153 allowing one person to be Governor of two or more States.
C is wrong: in Hargovind Pant v. Raghukul Tilak (1979), the Supreme Court held that the Governor's office is an independent constitutional office, not under the control of the Central Government.
Answer: A and B only

qs.q: When did India first win the first World Cup title in Hockey?
qs.e:
India won its only men's Hockey World Cup in 1975 at Kuala Lumpur, beating Pakistan 2-1 in the final under captain Ajit Pal Singh.
Ashok Kumar scored the winning goal. India had won bronze in 1971 and silver in 1973.
Answer: 1975

qs.q: Rima spends 35% of her monthly income on food articles and 15% of the remaining on clothes. She saves 40% of the remaining income. If her monthly salary is ₹27,500, how much does she save (in ₹) every month?

In an examination a candidate had to sit for three papers A, B, and C. The candidate secured 75% marks in Paper A, 80% marks in Paper B, and 60% marks in Paper C. If the weightage assigned to Papers A, B, and C were 40%, 50% and 10%, respectively, then find the weighted percentage of marks obtained by the candidate, when all the three papers were taken together.
qs.e:
Weighted percentage = Σ (marks % × weight).
= 75 × 0.4 + 80 × 0.5 + 60 × 0.1 = 30 + 40 + 6 = 76%.
Answer: 76%

qs.q: Select the correct idiom to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence. Harry always speaks his eye but he is not always very diplomatic!
qs.e:
Idiom: "speak one's mind" means to say openly what one thinks, which fits the remark that he is not always diplomatic.
"speaks his tongue", "listens his ear" and "reads his heart" are not idioms with this meaning.
Answer: speaks his mind

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. We have always been told retaliation is not the key to resolving problems.
qs.e:
Retaliation = paying back a harm with harm. E.g. The attack was in retaliation for the insult.
Revenge is the synonym.
Realisation = understanding; outcome = result; pamper = indulge (a verb, unrelated).
Answer: revenge

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. The hot sun enervated the labourer to the extent that he collapsed.
qs.e:
Enervate = drain of energy; weaken. E.g. The long illness enervated him.
Weaken is the synonym - the labourer collapsed.
Elevate = raise; alleviate = ease pain; energise = give energy (the antonym and a sound-alike trap).
Answer: weaken

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exuberance
qs.e:
Exuberance = lively, energetic cheerfulness. E.g. The exuberance of the children filled the room.
Vibrancy = energy and liveliness - the synonym.
Impartiality = fairness; laziness = lack of energy (antonym); sympathy = feeling for others.
Answer: Vibrancy

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pass the buck
qs.e:
'To pass the buck' means to shift blame or responsibility to someone else.
Origin: in poker, a marker (buck) was passed to the next dealer.
Example: The manager passed the buck to his team for the delay.
Saying unpleasant things, providing services and calming down are not the meaning.
Answer: Blaming another person

qs.q: How many silver medals was won by India in Tokyo Paralympic 2020?
qs.e:
At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics India won 19 medals: 5 gold, 8 silver and 6 bronze. This is India's best ever Paralympic result.
Silver medallists included Bhavina Patel (table tennis), Nishad Kumar (high jump) and Devendra Jhajharia (javelin).
Check: 5 + 8 + 6 = 19.
Answer: 8

qs.q: __________ became India’s first sports unicorn with its market cap having touched a high of Rs.7,600 crores as of 30 January 2022.
qs.e:
Chennai Super Kings became India's first 'sports unicorn' (a company valued at over US$1 billion). Its unlisted shares took its market value to about ₹7,600 crore in early 2022.
CSK, captained by MS Dhoni, is one of the most successful IPL franchises.
Answer: Chennai Super Kings

qs.q: India borrowed the DPSP from the _______ Constitution.
qs.e:
India borrowed the Directive Principles of State Policy from the Irish Constitution (Ireland had taken the idea from Spain).
Ireland also gave India the method of electing the President and nominating members to the Rajya Sabha.
Answer: Irish

qs.q: Commonwealth Games 2022 was held in _______.
qs.e:
The 22nd Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022.
India finished 4th with 61 medals. Tokyo hosted the 2020 Olympics, Beijing the 2022 Winter Olympics, and New Delhi the 2010 Commonwealth Games.
Answer: Birmingham

qs.q: Which among the following statements about judicial review in India are correct? A. Judicial review means that the courts of law have the power of testing the validity of legislative as well as other governmental action with reference to the provisions of the Constitution. B. Under Article 23 of the Indian Constitution, the compulsion of judicial review was described in the Fundamental Rights in Part III. C. The power of judicial review is significantly vested upon the High Courts and the Supreme Court of India.
qs.e:
A is correct: judicial review is the power of courts to test legislative and executive actions against the Constitution.
B is wrong: the basis in Part III is Article 13 (laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void), not Article 23, which bans forced labour.
C is correct: judicial review is mainly exercised by the High Courts (Art 226) and the Supreme Court (Art 32).
Answer: A and C only

qs.q: A shopkeeper bought certain number of apples for Rs.3,600. He sold one-fifth of them at a loss of 10%, one-fourth of the remaining apples at a loss of 5%, and two-third of the rest at a profit of 15%. At what price (in Rs.) should he sell the remaining apples to earn a profit of 27% overall?
qs.e:
Total CP 3600. 1/5 (CP 720) at 10% loss → 648.
Of the remaining 2880, 1/4 (CP 720) at 5% loss → 684.
Of the remaining 2160, 2/3 (CP 1440) at 15% profit → 1656. Left: CP 720.
Target SP = 3600 × 1.27 = 4572; still needed = 4572 − (648 + 684 + 1656) = 4572 − 2988 = ₹1,584.
Answer: 1,584

Apple of discord = cause of a quarrel; apple of one's eye = a dearly loved person; 'alley apple' is slang for a stone.

qs.q: Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. Shelley has been contemplating for a few days but still has not decided to quit the job.

Image: a cow slowly re-chewing its food.
Shelley has been thinking it over but has not decided.
Biting the dust = failing or dying; cooling one's heels = being kept waiting; getting into hot water = getting into trouble.
Answer: chewing the cud

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Judicious
qs.e:
Judicious = showing good judgement; wise. E.g. A judicious use of funds.
Sensible is the synonym.
Imprudent, careless and short-sighted all mean unwise - the antonyms.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Extol
qs.e:
Extol = praise highly. E.g. The critics extolled the film.
Praise is the synonym.
Reward = give something for merit (not the same as praise); punish = penalise; dismay = discourage, alarm.
Answer: Praise

qs.q: How many elected members are there in the Legislative Assembly of Telangana till December 2022?

The Telangana Legislative Assembly has 119 elected members.
Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014. Earlier it also had one nominated Anglo-Indian member, a provision that ended in 2020.
Answer: 119

qs.q: As the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces, who takes the salute of the various regiments of the armed forces during the march past on Republic Day?
qs.e:
Article 53(2) vests the supreme command of the Defence Forces in the President.
So the President takes the salute at the Republic Day parade on Kartavya Path.
Answer: President of India

qs.q: Where and when were the first Khelo India University Games held?

The first Khelo India University Games were held in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, from February to March 2020, hosted by KIIT University.
Panjab University topped the medal table. The second edition was in Bengaluru (Karnataka) in 2022.
Answer: Odisha, 2020

qs.q: Who among the following was India's second Grandmaster after Viswanathan Anand?
qs.e:
Viswanathan Anand became India's first Grandmaster in 1988.
Dibyendu Barua of West Bengal became the second in 1991, followed by Pravin Thipsay as the third.
Answer: Dibyendu Barua

qs.q: The Indian Constitution originally consisted of ______ Articles.
qs.e:
When adopted in 1949, the Constitution had 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
New Articles were later inserted with letters (21A, 243A, etc.), so the last Article is still numbered 395.
Answer: 395

qs.q: The marked price of an article is ₹50,000. Of three shopkeepers, the first one allows two successive discounts of 25% and 15%.The second one allows two successive discounts 20% and 20%. The third shopkeeper allows two successive discounts of 30% and 10%. From which shopkeeper does the customer get more profit?
qs.e:
Equivalent discount = a + b − ab/100.
First: 25 + 15 − 3.75 = 36.25%. Second: 20 + 20 − 4 = 36%. Third: 30 + 10 − 3 = 37%.
The third gives the largest discount, so the customer gains most there.
Answer: Third

qs.q: Mona purchased two sets of jewellery for ₹4,000 each. She sold these sets of jewellery, gaining 8% on one and loosing 6% on the other. Calculate her total loss or gain in this whole transaction.
qs.e:
Gain on first set = 8% of 4000 = ₹320. Loss on second = 6% of 4000 = ₹240.
Net = 320 − 240 = ₹80 gain.
Answer: ₹80 gain

qs.q: A family income is ₹35,000 in a month. The family spends the income on various expenditures, viz., food, health, education, entertainment, and rent. After incurring all the expenditures, 8% is saved every month. The expenditure on health is 50% more than that of food. While food is three times of the expenditure on entertainment, the expenditure on health is half of the expenditure on education. The expenditure on rent is one-third of the combined expenditure on food, health and education. How much expenditure (in ₹) is incurred on education?
qs.e:
Savings 8% → expenditure = 92% of 35000 = ₹32,200.
Let entertainment = E: food = 3E, health = 1.5 × 3E = 4.5E, education = 2 × 4.5E = 9E.
Rent = (3E + 4.5E + 9E)/3 = 5.5E.
Total = E + 3E + 4.5E + 9E + 5.5E = 23E = 32200 → E = 1400.
Education = 9 × 1400 = ₹12,600.
Answer: 12600

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Gentle
qs.e:
Gentle = kind, mild and tender. E.g. She is gentle with animals.
Sympathetic = kind and caring - the closest synonym.
Fierce, ferocious and cruel all mean violent or harsh - the antonyms.
Answer: Sympathetic

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. At cross purposes
qs.e:
'At cross purposes' means misunderstanding each other or having aims that clash, so people work against each other.
Example: The two departments were at cross purposes, so the project stalled.
Developing ideas, finalising plans and blindly following each other suggest agreement – the opposite.
Answer: Disagreeing with each other’s ideas

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The Department of Educational Policy is committed to the study of educational policy, analyse, and evaluate educational programmes, to identify trends, understand outcomes and guide policy and practice, towards finding solutions to current problems in educational governance and management.
qs.e:
Committed (to) = dedicated, pledged to a cause or task. E.g. She is committed to helping the poor.
Dedicated is the synonym.
Affiliated = officially connected; inclined = tending towards; apathetic = uninterested (antonym).
Answer: dedicated

qs.q: Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. You must not participate in the marathon this year without any training. It is an unreal hope on your part!
qs.e:
'A pipe dream' is a hope or plan that is unrealistic and will never come true.
Running a marathon with no training is an unreal hope – a pipe dream.
Carrying coals to Newcastle = doing something pointless; will-o'-the-wisp = something hard to catch; losing one's temper = getting angry.
Answer: a pipe dream

qs.q: In a family of four persons there is only one child. B is A's wife and D's daughter. If C is A's daughter, how is C related to D?

So C is the daughter of D's daughter.

qs.q: In which of the following sports, apart from volleyball, do players make use of the Screen technique?
qs.e:
A screen (also called a pick) is a legal block: an attacking player stands in a defender's path so a teammate can get free. It is a basic move in basketball.
In volleyball, a screen means players hiding the server from the receiving team. Cricket, baseball and handball do not use this term.
Answer: Basketball

qs.q: Which player led India at the women's Hockey Asia Cup in Muscat, which was held in January 2022?
qs.e:
Goalkeeper Savita Punia captained India at the Women's Hockey Asia Cup in Muscat, Oman, in January 2022. India won bronze.
Regular captain Rani Rampal missed the event through injury, so Savita led the side.

qs.q: Who among the following was the flag bearer of the Indian contingent at the opening ceremony of the Asian Games 2018?
qs.e:
Javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra carried India's flag at the opening ceremony of the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta-Palembang.
He then won gold in the javelin at those Games, and three years later took Olympic gold at Tokyo 2020.
Answer: Neeraj Chopra

qs.q: What do you understand by ‘dual citizenship’ as in the case of the US?
o: Citizenship of two states simultaneously with two countries
Citizenship of a country alongwith that of a constituent State, where one resides/born
Citizenship of two states alongwith two countries
qs.e:
Dual citizenship in the USA means a person is a citizen of the country (USA) and also of the constituent State where he lives or was born.
India has single citizenship – only Indian, with no separate State citizenship – a feature taken from Britain.
Answer: Citizenship of a country alongwith that of a constituent State, where one resides/born

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders?
qs.e:
Article 137 lets the Supreme Court review any judgment it has given or order it has made, subject to laws by Parliament and the Court's own rules.
Art 136 – special leave to appeal; Art 138 – enlargement of jurisdiction; Art 135 – powers of the Federal Court.
Answer: Article 137

qs.q: The difference between a discount of 40% and two successive discounts of 30% on a certain bill was ₹220. Find the amount of the bill (in ₹).
qs.e:
Two successive 30% discounts = 30 + 30 − (30×30)/100 = 51%.
Difference from a single 40% discount = 51 − 40 = 11% of the bill.
11% of bill = 220 → bill = 220 × 100/11 = ₹2,000.
Answer: 2000

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. I just went to Bali on a backpacking trip and did everything by the ear without any itinerary.

Spreading rumours, criticising and asking are not the meaning.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Predicament

Predicament = a difficult, unpleasant situation. E.g. Missing the last train left us in a predicament.
Quandary = a state of difficulty or uncertainty - the synonym.
Ease = comfort; blessing = something good; solution = a way out - all opposite in sense.

qs.q: Which of the following pairs of countries are going to host 2022 FIVA Volleyball Women’s World Championship?
qs.e:
Poland and the Netherlands co-hosted the 2022 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship (23 September – 15 October 2022). Serbia won the title.
('FIVA' in the question is a misprint for FIVB.) The men's championship the same year was co-hosted by Poland and Slovenia, which is why that option is tempting.
Answer: Poland and Netherlands

qs.q: The Governor of an Indian state before entering upon his office takes an oath or affirmation before ________.
o: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
the Chief Minister of the concerned state
qs.e:
Under Article 159, a Governor takes the oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court of that State, or in his absence the senior-most judge available.
The President takes the oath before the Chief Justice of India.
Answer: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State

qs.q: In hockey, ________ is awarded if the ball goes over the back line after last being touched by a defender.
qs.e:
In hockey, if the ball goes over the back line and a defender touched it last without meaning to, the attacking side gets a long corner. Play restarts from the 23-metre line, level with where the ball went out.
If the defender sent it over the back line on purpose, a penalty corner is given instead.
Answer: long corner

qs.q: ________of the Constitution of India says that the State shall take steps to organise panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
qs.e:
Article 40, a Directive Principle, asks the State to organise village panchayats and give them the powers needed to work as units of self-government.
This Gandhian principle got constitutional backing through the 73rd Amendment (1992).
Art 32 – constitutional remedies; Art 38 – social order for welfare.
Answer: Article 40

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. You snooze, you lose
o: If you oversleep, you are likely to lose a job
You may lose your money if snoozing is not stopped
If you are not alert, you are likely to miss opportunities.
qs.e:
'You snooze, you lose' means if you are not alert or quick, you will miss opportunities.
Example: The sale ended at noon – you snooze, you lose.
Options 1–3 take 'snooze' literally (oversleeping, laziness, money).
Answer: If you are not alert, you are likely to miss opportunities.

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Extinct
qs.e:
Extinct = no longer existing. E.g. The dodo is an extinct bird.
Vanished = disappeared completely - the synonym.
Vibrant, active and living all mean alive and present - the antonyms.
Answer: Vanished

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Glorify
qs.e:
Glorify = praise and honour highly. E.g. Poems glorify the brave soldiers.
Praise is the synonym.
Simplify = make easier; stupefy = stun or daze; strengthen = make stronger.
Answer: Praise

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Out of the blue
qs.e:
'Out of the blue' means suddenly and unexpectedly.
Image: like a bolt from a clear blue sky.
Example: Out of the blue, my old school friend called me.
Undoubtedly, unbelievably and unconcerned do not mean unexpected.
Answer: Unexpectedly

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The boxer showed audacity by agreeing to fight the champion.
qs.e:
Audacity = bold willingness to take risks. E.g. She had the audacity to climb alone.
Courage = bravery - the synonym here.
Honesty = truthfulness; desperation = hopeless urgency; reparation = making amends.
Answer: Courage

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 8, 14, ? , 44, 68, 98, 134
qs.e:
Differences are multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36.
14 + 12 = 26; check 26 + 18 = 44, 44 + 24 = 68.
Answer: 26

qs.q: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? ZXV, TRP, NLJ, HFD, ?
qs.e:
Each letter moves 6 places back from one term to the next.
H−6 = B, F−6 = Z, D−6 = X (counting back past A to Z).
Answer: BZX

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. BUP_ESH_UPL_SHB_PLES_BU_LE_H
qs.e:
The repeating block is BUPLESH (7 letters).
Writing it 4 times — BUPLESH BUPLESH BUPLESH BUPLESH — fills the blanks with L, B, E, U, H, P, S.
Answer: LBEUHPS

qs.q: Mishka says she is looking for the only child of her brother’s maternal grandmother. Who is she looking for?
qs.e:
Mishka's brother's maternal grandmother is Mishka's own maternal grandmother.
Her only child must be Mishka's mother.
Answer: Mother

qs.q: Part 3 of the Indian Constitution enlists how many groups of Fundamental Rights?
qs.e:
Part III now has six groups of Fundamental Rights: Equality (14–18), Freedom (19–22), Against Exploitation (23–24), Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational (29–30) and Constitutional Remedies (32).
Originally there were seven; the Right to Property was removed in 1978.
Answer: 6

qs.q: Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was formed in the year ______.
qs.e:
The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was formed in 1927, with Sir Dorabji Tata as its first president.
It organises India's participation in the Olympics, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games. India had first sent athletes to the Olympics in 1900.
Answer: 1927

qs.q: The first Paralympic games were held in:
qs.e:
The first Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960, right after that year's Summer Olympics. About 400 athletes took part.
They grew out of the Stoke Mandeville Games started by Dr Ludwig Guttmann in England in 1948.
Answer: Rome

qs.q: Which of the following can make provisions for Ancillary powers of the Supreme Court?
qs.e:
Under Article 140, Parliament can by law give the Supreme Court supplementary (ancillary) powers so that it can use its jurisdiction more effectively.
The Law Commission only advises, and the President and Law Minister cannot add to the Court's powers.
Answer: Parliament of India

qs.q: Which of the following is the least? 12% of 625 15% of 555 10% of 720 9% of 845
qs.e:
Compute each: 12% of 625 = 75; 15% of 555 = 83.25; 10% of 720 = 72; 9% of 845 = 76.05.
The smallest is 72.
Answer: 10% of 720

qs.q: R’s weighing machine shows 400 gm when the actual weight is 350 gm. The cost price of almonds is ₹880 per kg and packets of 200 gm are made using the faulty machine. What should be the selling price (in ₹) of each packet to get a profit of 25%?
qs.e:
The machine shows 400 g for an actual 350 g, so a "200 g" packet really holds 175 g.
Cost of 175 g = 0.175 × 880 = ₹154.
For 25% profit: SP = 154 × 1.25 = ₹192.50.
Answer: 192.50

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression to fill in the blank. Anita keeps on repeating that she is innocent, but there is ___________.
o: no pulling up of the socks
qs.e:
'(There is) no smoke without fire' means a rumour usually has some basis of truth.
Though Anita says she is innocent, people think there must be some truth behind the accusation.
Pulling up socks = improving; rubbing shoulders = mixing with; no love lost = mutual dislike – none fits.
Answer: no smoke without fire

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the highlighted word in the given sentence. A strong man is a mediator between divine and mortal fate.
qs.e:
Mortal has two senses: subject to death (human), and causing death (a mortal wound).
Of the options only Lethal (deadly, causing death) matches a sense of mortal, so it is the answer.
Delightful = pleasing; sincere = honest; overjoyed = very happy - none relate to death.
Answer: Lethal

qs.q: Select the option that can substitute the underlined segment with the correct idiom. After finishing this assignment, the employees make it a day.
qs.e:
Idiom: "call it a day" means to stop working for the day.
So: "After finishing this assignment, the employees call it a day."
"consider it", "stop it" and "ring it" a day are not idioms.
Answer: call it a day

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. C _ _ UP _ EX _ PC _ XU _ _ E _ UP
qs.e:
The repeating block is CEXUP (5 letters).
Writing it 4 times — CEXUP CEXUP CEXUP CEXUP — fills the blanks with E, X, C, U, E, P, C, X.
Answer: EXCUEPCX

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 10, 40, 120, 240, ?
Looking at a picture of a woman Samuel said, “She is the mother of my father’s brother’s daughter.” How is Samuel related to the woman in the picture?
qs.e:
Samuel's father's brother's daughter's mother is the wife of Samuel's father's brother (his aunt).
The woman's husband is Samuel's father's brother, and Samuel is that brother's son.
So Samuel is her husband's brother's son.
Answer: Husband’s brother’s son

qs.q: Who was the winner of ICC Men’s T20 World Cup– 2021?
qs.e:
Australia won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021 (played in the UAE and Oman), beating New Zealand by 8 wickets in the Dubai final.
It was Australia's first T20 World Cup title. Mitchell Marsh was player of the match and David Warner player of the tournament.
Answer: Australia

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right against Exploitation?
qs.e:
Articles 23 and 24 make up the Right against Exploitation. Article 23 bans human trafficking and forced labour (begar), and Article 24 bans child labour below 14 in hazardous work.
Art 20 – protection in respect of conviction; Art 21 – life and liberty; Art 22 – protection against arrest.
Answer: Article 23

qs.q: Deepika Pallikal is associated with ______.
qs.e:
Deepika Pallikal is a squash player. She was the first Indian woman to enter the world top 10 and is an Arjuna Award winner.
She won Commonwealth Games gold in women's doubles (2014) with Joshna Chinappa and has Asian Games medals. She is married to cricketer Dinesh Karthik.
Answer: squash

qs.q: Which state had the first female Governor in independent India?
qs.e:
Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor in independent India. She became Governor of the United Provinces (Uttar Pradesh) in August 1947.
Sucheta Kripalani, also in Uttar Pradesh, was India's first woman Chief Minister (1963).
Answer: Uttar Pradesh

qs.q: By which of the following acts was a bicameral legislature introduced in India at the centre level?
qs.e:
The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms) first created a bicameral central legislature: the Central Legislative Assembly and the Council of State.
It also brought dyarchy to the provinces. The 1935 Act later added bicameralism in some provinces.
Answer: Government of India Act of 1919

qs.q: Which of the following will yield maximum discount on ₹7,500? 1. Two successive discounts of 5% and 5% 2. Single discount of 10% 3. Two successive discounts of 8% and 2%
o: All will yield the same discount
qs.e:
Use a + b − ab/100 for successive discounts.
1: 5 + 5 − 0.25 = 9.75%. 2: 10%. 3: 8 + 2 − 0.16 = 9.84%.
A single 10% discount is the largest (successive discounts always total a bit less than their sum).
Answer: 2

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the highlighted word. His modest nature made all the difference.
qs.e:
Modest = humble, not boastful; also reserved or bashful. E.g. Despite his fame, he remained modest.
Shy = reserved, not putting oneself forward - the closest option.
Horrific = terrible; courageous = brave; dry = without moisture or dull.
Answer: shy

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. Though very rich, Alexander always saves for a rainy day.
qs.e:
'To save for a rainy day' means to save money for a future time of need.
Even though he is rich, Alexander keeps money aside for later.
Miserliness, accumulating less and spending too much do not match.
Answer: Saves money for later

qs.q: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. His voice gets on my nerves.
qs.e:
'To get on someone's nerves' means to irritate or annoy them.
Example: The dripping tap gets on my nerves.
Sad, ill and painful are not the meaning.
Answer: Irritates me

qs.q: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? GTCL, KWEM, OZGN, SCIO, ?

Answer: WFKP

qs.q: Looking at a photograph, Reema says, “This boy’s father is the father of my daughter”. How is the boy related to Reema’s daughter?
qs.e:
The father of Reema's daughter is Reema's husband, and he is the boy's father.
So the boy and Reema's daughter share the same father: the boy is her brother.
Answer: Brother

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 214, 207, 193, ? , 144, 109
Under which Constitutional Amendment, the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children from the age of six to fourteen years?.
qs.e:
The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 a Fundamental Right.
It also rewrote Article 45 (early childhood care below 6) and added Fundamental Duty 51A(k).
Answer: 86th

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to establish additional courts for better administration of laws made by it?
qs.e:
Article 247 lets Parliament establish additional courts for the better administration of laws it makes or of existing laws on Union List matters.
Art 246 – distribution of subjects among the lists; Art 248 – residuary powers; Art 253 – laws to implement international agreements.
Answer: Article 247

qs.q: Who among the following became the first fast bowler to take up captaincy of the Australian men’s Test side full-time in November 2021?
qs.e:
Pat Cummins became Australia's full-time Test captain in November 2021 after Tim Paine stepped down. He was the first fast bowler to hold the job full-time.
He later led Australia to the 2023 World Test Championship and the 2023 ODI World Cup.
Answer: Pat Cummins

qs.q: The number of flights in a 110 m hurdle race is _______.
qs.e:
The 110 m hurdles (men) has 10 flights of hurdles, each 1.067 m high.
The first hurdle is 13.72 m from the start, the hurdles are 9.14 m apart, and the run-in to the finish is 14.02 m: 13.72 + 9 × 9.14 + 14.02 = 110 m.
Answer: 10

qs.q: Which of the following countries won the highest number of golds in Paralympic-2020?
qs.e:
China topped the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics medal table with 96 gold (207 medals in all), well ahead of Great Britain (41 gold) and the USA (37 gold).
China has topped every Summer Paralympics medal table since 2004.
Answer: China

qs.q: Which State Assembly passed a resolution to create a Legislative Council in 2021?
qs.e:
In July 2021 the West Bengal Assembly passed a resolution to create a Legislative Council. Under Article 169, Parliament must then pass a law to create it.
West Bengal had abolished its Council in 1969. Andhra Pradesh, in contrast, passed a resolution in 2020 to abolish its Council.
Answer: West Bengal

qs.q: Sita sold a whiteboard marker set at 10% profit. On selling it for Rs.20 more, she would have earned a profit of 15%. What is the cost price of the whiteboard marker set?
qs.e:
Moving from 10% to 15% profit adds 5% of CP to the price.
5% of CP = ₹20, so CP = 20 × 20 = ₹400.
Answer: Rs.400

qs.q: A father gives 8% of his monthly income to both his sons as pocket money. The elder son gets 85% of the total amount given to both the sons. He spend 90% of the amount and saves ₹17. What is the monthly income of father?
qs.e:
Let the income be I. Both sons get 8% of I; the elder gets 85% of that = 0.068I.
He spends 90%, so saves 10% = 0.0068I = 17 → I = 17 ÷ 0.0068 = 2500.
Answer: ₹2,500

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In a soup
qs.e:
'In a soup' means in trouble or a difficult situation.
Example: He forgot his hall ticket and was in a soup on exam day.
Being short of money, cowardice and getting nothing are not the meaning.
Answer: In trouble

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase that can substitute the given group of words. The better you know someone the less you like him.
qs.e:
'Familiarity breeds contempt' means the better you know someone, the more you notice their faults and the less you respect them.
Save for a rainy day = save for the future; spill the beans = reveal a secret; the elephant in the room = an obvious problem everyone avoids.
Answer: Familiarity breeds contempt

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The internationally agreed Declaration of the Small Island Developing States (SIDS) Accelerated Modalities of Action, the so-called S.A.M.O.A Pathway, recognises that SIDS remains a special case for sustainable development in view of their unique and particular vulnerabilities.

qs.q: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. If P ÷ Q – R + S – K × L, then which of the following statements is correct?.
qs.e:
Decode: P is Q's sister; Q is R's mother; R is S's brother; S is K's mother; K is L's husband.
S is K's mother and R is S's brother, so R is K's mother's brother (true).
Q is K's grandmother, not L's mother; Q is S's mother, not sister; R is K's uncle, not K's brother.
Answer: R is K’s mother’s brother

qs.q: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 2, 6, 9, 27, 30, 90, ?
qs.e:
The operations alternate: ×3, then +3.
2×3 = 6, 6+3 = 9, 9×3 = 27, 27+3 = 30, 30×3 = 90, so next is 90 + 3 = 93.
Answer: 93

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. L _ N N N _ _ M N N N N _ M N N N _
qs.e:
The repeating block is LMNNNN (6 letters).
Writing it 3 times — LMNNNN LMNNNN LMNNNN — fills the blanks with M, N, L, L, N.
Answer: M N L L N

qs.q: Following an order of 16 July 2021, the Supreme Court of India introduced an electronic system named ____________, in November 2021, through which its crucial decisions can be communicated electronically to prison authorities and investigating agencies.
qs.e:
FASTER (Fast and Secured Transmission of Electronic Records) was started by the Supreme Court in 2021 to send bail and other orders electronically to jails and investigating agencies.
It came after reports that prisoners stayed in jail even after getting bail because paper orders arrived late.
Answer: FASTER

qs.q: In which of the following years did the Indian Premier League begin?
qs.e:
The Indian Premier League began in 2008. It was set up by the BCCI, with Lalit Modi as its founder-commissioner.
Rajasthan Royals, led by Shane Warne, won the first season. The 2007 option is the year India won the first T20 World Cup, which led to the IPL.
Answer: 2008

qs.q: Which state ranked first among the 18 large and mid-sized states (with population of over one crore each) in justice delivery in India as per the second edition of the India Justice Report?
qs.e:
In the second India Justice Report (2020), Maharashtra ranked first among the 18 large and mid-sized States (population above one crore) in justice delivery. It was followed by Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
The report ranks States on police, judiciary, prisons and legal aid.
Answer: Maharashtra

qs.q: What is the duty of the Chief Minister, as mentioned under Article 167 of the Indian Constitution?
o: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
Appointment and removal of Council of the Ministers.
Appointment of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
Appointment of Advocate General of the state in consultation with Attorney general.
qs.e:
Under Article 167, the Chief Minister must communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers about State administration and proposed laws, and give any information the Governor asks for.
Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the CM's advice; the Speaker is elected by the Assembly; the Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.
Answer: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.

qs.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits religious instructions in any state- funded educational institution?
qs.e:
Article 28(1) says no religious instruction shall be given in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
Article 27 bars taxes for promoting a religion; Articles 29–30 protect minorities' cultural and educational rights.
Answer: Article 28

qs.q: Three successive discounts of 10% are available on the sale of a washing machine with a marked price of ₹55,000. Find the final selling price (in ₹) of the washing machine.
qs.e:
Each 10% discount multiplies the price by 0.9.
SP = 55,000 × 0.9³ = 55,000 × 0.729 = ₹40,095.
Answer: 40095

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. I really don’t want to pour cold water on your theory but it cannot be applied to real life situations.
o: To destroy someone’s written piece of work
To take revenge on someone by destroying their lives’ work under the pretext of bad quality
To be critical or doubtful of a plan that someone is excited about
To give goosebumps by showing a prospect
qs.e:
'To pour cold water on' an idea means to criticise or discourage a plan someone is excited about.
The speaker doubts the theory will work in real life.
Destroying written work, taking revenge and giving goosebumps are wrong.
Answer: To be critical or doubtful of a plan that someone is excited about

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the italicised word in the given sentence. In most organisations there are predators who take advantage over the meek ones.
qs.e:
Predator = an animal that hunts others; (figuratively) a person who exploits weaker people. E.g. Online predators target children.
Exploiters = those who take unfair advantage of others - the synonym.
Supporters, philanthropists (lovers of mankind who donate) and benefactors (helpers) are all opposites in sense.
Answer: exploiters

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fragile
qs.e:
Fragile = easily broken or damaged. E.g. Handle the glass vase carefully; it is fragile.
Delicate = easily damaged - the synonym.
Firm = solid (antonym); composed = calm; fanatic = an extreme follower.
Answer: Delicate

qs.q: Looking at the family picture, Sneha said, “She is my brother’s wife’s son’s father’s mother-in-law’s only daughter.’ How is the girl in the photo related to Sneha?
qs.e:
Sneha's brother's wife's son's father is her brother himself.
Her brother's mother-in-law is his wife's mother; her only daughter is his wife.
So the girl is Sneha's brother's wife.
Answer: Brother’s wife

qs.q: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the following blanks, will complete the letter-series. G _ A R E G L _ R _ G _ C _ E G L _ _ E
o: L B E L R D R

qs.q: Which of the following is mentioned in the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
o: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
qs.e:
The Preamble promises "Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship".
The other options are misquoted: the Preamble says Justice – social, economic and political (not administrative); Equality of status and of opportunity (not employment); and Fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation.
Answer: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship

qs.q: In T20 cricket matches, a bowler can bowl a maximum of _______.
qs.e:
A T20 innings has 20 overs, and no bowler may bowl more than one-fifth of them: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 overs.
The same one-fifth rule gives 10 overs per bowler in a 50-over ODI.
Answer: 4 overs

qs.q: Who among the following served the shortest tenure as the Prime Minister of India?
qs.e:
Chandra Shekhar was PM for only about 7 months (10 November 1990 – 21 June 1991), the shortest of these four.
H.D. Deve Gowda, I.K. Gujral and V.P. Singh each served roughly 11 months.
Among all regular PMs, Charan Singh (1979) had an even shorter term.
Answer: Chandra Shekhar

qs.q: In which year India won gold in men’s hockey in the Olympic games?
qs.e:
India won the men's hockey gold at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, beating Spain 4-3 in the final, with V Bhaskaran as captain.
It was India's 8th and most recent Olympic hockey gold. India's next hockey medal was the bronze at Tokyo 2020.
Answer: 1980

qs.q: On selling a painting at Rs.1,498, the gain is 25% more than the loss incurred on selling it at Rs.1,300. In order to gain 25%, the selling price will be:

A shopkeeper gives a 12% additional discount on the discounted price, after giving an initial discount of 25% on the labelled price of a radio. If the final selling price of the radio is ₹792, then what is its labelled price (in ₹)?
Select the most appropriate idiom for the given underlined segment in the sentence. Riya always considers sincerity, devotion and dedication as the highest priority of a good employee.
qs.e:
Idiom: "first and foremost" means most important of all, i.e. the highest priority.
"Free and easy" means relaxed; "Fair and square" means honestly; "Ever and anon" means now and then.
Answer: First and foremost

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym for the highlighted word. This is credible information provided by the informer.
qs.e:
Credible = able to be believed; trustworthy. E.g. The police found a credible witness.
Dependable = reliable - the synonym.
Detachable = removable; commendable = praiseworthy; digestible = easy to digest.
Answer: dependable

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hard nut to crack
o: A situation that can be altered
qs.e:
'A hard nut to crack' is a problem (or person) that is difficult to solve or deal with.
Example: This puzzle is a hard nut to crack.
Leaving an effect, saying goodbye and an alterable situation are unrelated.
Answer: A problem difficult to solve

qs.q: Pointing to a man, Rocky (a man) said, “He is the father of the daughter of my daughter-in-law.” How Rocky is related to that man?
qs.e:
The daughter of Rocky's daughter-in-law has her father = the daughter-in-law's husband = Rocky's son.
So the man is Rocky's son, and Rocky is his father.
Answer: Father

qs.q: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? CM, EP, GO, IS, KQ, MV, OS, ?
qs.e:
1st letters: C, E, G, I, K, M, O → +2 → Q.
2nd letters alternate: M, O, Q, S (+2) and P, S, V (+3); the 8th belongs to the second chain → V + 3 = Y.
Answer: QY

qs.q: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 232, 221, 199, ? , 122, 67
Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ T M _ P T _ R _ _ M R P _ _ R
o: P R M P T T M
M P T R M T T
M T P R T M R
P M T R R M T
qs.e:
The repeating block is PTMR (4 letters).
Writing it 4 times — PTMR PTMR PTMR PTMR — fills the blanks with P, R, M, P, T, T, M.
Answer: P R M P T T M

qs.q: Pointing to a picture, Azad says that it is the picture of the only brother of the only daughter's daughter of his mother's father. How is Azad related to the person in the picture?
qs.e:
The daughter of Azad's mother's father is Azad's mother, so the only daughter's daughter is Azad's sister.
The only brother of Azad's sister is Azad himself.
Answer: Azad himself

qs.q: Fundamental duties are ___________ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
qs.e:
The key's wording: Fundamental Duties are statutory duties – written into the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment – but courts cannot enforce them directly.
Courts can still use them when judging whether a law is reasonable, and Parliament can enforce them through ordinary laws (e.g. laws against insulting the National Flag).
Answer: statutory

qs.q: The word 'direct free kick' is related to which of the following sports?
qs.e:
A 'direct free kick' belongs to football. The kicker may score straight from it, without anyone else touching the ball.
It is given for fouls such as tripping, pushing or handball. If the foul happens inside the penalty area, a penalty kick is given instead.
Answer: Football

qs.q: Till which year did the High Court of Delhi continue to exercise jurisdiction over Himachal Pradesh?
qs.e:
Himachal Pradesh was under the Delhi High Court's jurisdiction until 1971.
It got its own High Court when it became a full State on 25 January 1971.
Answer: 1971

qs.q: The FIFA World Cup 2026 will be hosted by _______.
qs.e:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup is co-hosted by Canada, the USA and Mexico, the first World Cup with three host nations.
It is also the first with 48 teams (up from 32). Mexico becomes the first country to host three World Cups (1970, 1986, 2026).
Answer: Canada, USA and Mexico

qs.q: A laptop is sold for ₹54,000 after giving a discount of 20%. What is the list price (in ₹) of the laptop?
qs.e:
SP = 80% of list price.
List price = 54,000 ÷ 0.8 = ₹67,500.
Answer: 67500

qs.q: A dishonest dealer sells articles at 15% loss on cost price but uses the weight of 20 g instead of 25 g. What is his profit or loss percentage?
qs.e:
Let 1 g cost ₹1. He charges for 25 g at 15% loss: 25 × 0.85 = ₹21.25.
He gives only 20 g, costing ₹20.
Profit = 1.25; profit% = 1.25/20 × 100 = 6.25%.
Answer: 6.25% Profit

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. A wide-ranging effort is being made to safeguard lives and livelihoods by addressing the devastating near-term socio-economic, humanitarian, and human rights aspects of the crisis with attention to those hit the hardest.
qs.e:
Devastating = causing great damage or destruction. E.g. A devastating earthquake hit the city.
Destructive is the synonym.
Fortunate = lucky; emerging = coming into view; flourishing = thriving - all positive, the opposite idea.
Answer: destructive

qs.q: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Treading on thin ice
o: To be in a dangerous risky position
Skating on ice fallen in a hailstorm
qs.e:
'Treading (skating) on thin ice' means being in a risky or dangerous position.
Image: thin ice may crack under your weight at any moment.
Example: You are treading on thin ice by arguing with the boss again.
The other options take 'ice' literally.
Answer: To be in a dangerous risky position

qs.q: Select the synonym of the word ‘reproduce’ from the sentence. Many scientific researches have proved that DNA replicates itself in the human body and is an enzyme based catalyst reaction.
qs.e:
Reproduce = make a copy of; produce again. E.g. Cells reproduce by dividing.
In the sentence, DNA 'replicates' itself - makes an exact copy, the synonym.
Proved = shown to be true; researches = studies; reaction = a chemical change or response.
Answer: Replicates

qs.q: Select the most appropriate idiom or phrase to fill in the blank in the given sentence. He is rich and famous and expects everyone to _________ on him.
qs.e:
'To dance attendance on' someone means to serve them eagerly and attend to their every need.
The rich, famous man expects everyone to wait on him.
Give a song and dance = make excuses; dead duck = a failure; tap dance like mad = desperately try to escape blame.
Answer: dance attendance

qs.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Connote
qs.e:
Connote = imply or suggest a meaning beyond the literal one. E.g. 'Home' connotes warmth and safety.
Convey = communicate or express an idea - the closest synonym.
Comment = remark; criticise = find fault; care = look after.
Answer: Convey
